Conrad Singapore Marina Bay is going all out for the season with its Lights by the Bay festive programme, which includes a life-sized gingerbread house, a German-inspired market in the hotel lobby and a line-up of festive feasts running from late November into January.
The German-inspired Festive Market (Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay)
Festive Gingerbread Gift Shop and German-inspired market
The Festive Gingerbread Gift Shop runs from 23 November to 6 January. The centrepiece is a life-sized gingerbread house handcrafted from real gingerbread, stocked with festive treats from the hotel’s pastry team.
The Festive Market follows from 30 November to 26 December, set up as a German-inspired market in the hotel lobby. It opens with a festive light-up on 30 November at 6.30pm, complete with welcome drinks, the lighting of the lobby and carols.
Festive feasts at Conrad Singapore Marina Bay
The festive dining offerings all run from 25 November to 6 January.
Oscar’s Festive Buffets
Oscar’s lays out fresh seafood, festive roasts and desserts, from S$70++ per adult.
Oscar’s festive buffet setting (Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay)
Oscar’s festive buffet spread (Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay)
Lobby Lounge Festive Afternoon Tea
The Lobby Lounge serves a weekday tiered afternoon tea from S$55++ and a weekend high tea buffet from S$68++.
Lobby Lounge Festive Afternoon Tea (Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay)
Golden Peony Festive Set Menu
For something more Cantonese, Golden Peony offers a festive twist on its classics, with set menus from S$68++ per person.
Golden Peony Festive Set Menu (Image: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay)
Our take
With dining across a buffet, afternoon tea and Cantonese set menus, plus a free-to-browse lobby market, the programme gives families and office teams plenty of options for a Marina Bay Christmas outing. Prices are subject to service charge and prevailing taxes, so check the hotel before you book.
Looking for more festive dining? See The Orchard Cafe’s Christmas buffet , Mister Donut’s KitKat Christmas donuts and Sushi Express’s tree-shaped sushi platters .
Details: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay, Two Temasek Boulevard, Singapore 038982. More at Conrad Singapore Marina Bay .
summary: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay's Lights by the Bay brings a life-sized gingerbread house, a German-inspired lobby market and festive feasts from 23 November.
title: Conrad Singapore Marina Bay Lights by the Bay: gingerbread house, German-style market and festive feasts

Sushi Express Christmas platters are coming to Singapore from 7 to 31 December 2026, and this year the festive spread is shaped like a tree. The conveyor-belt sushi chain is rolling out three tree-shaped sushi platters, priced from S$19, along with a plush mascot eco bag for app members.
The three Sushi Express Christmas tree platters (Image: Sushi Express)
Three Sushi Express Christmas tree platters
The platters are the star of the festive menu, each served in a Christmas tree-shaped tray. They scale up in size and price, so you can pick one for a solo treat or a family spread.
Twinkle Delight Platter (S$19)
The smallest of the trio features Hana Maki Sushi topped with three star-shaped tamago, which gives the tray its twinkling look.
Twinkle Delight Platter (Image: Sushi Express)
Joyful Noel Platter (S$25)
Made for sharing, the Joyful Noel Platter has Grilled Salmon perched at the peak of the tree.
Joyful Noel Platter (Image: Sushi Express)
Merry Forest Platter (S$30)
The biggest of the three is topped with salmon sashimi and offers the widest selection, so it is the one to order if you are feeding a crowd.
Merry Forest Platter (Image: Sushi Express)
Eco Bag Plush for app members
App members also get an exclusive Eco Bag Plush: a recyclable bag tucked inside a soft plush of mascot Shimizu Salmon-kun. It is a cute, practical keepsake that doubles as a reusable shopping bag.
The Eco Bag for app members (Image: Sushi Express)
Shimizu Salmon-kun Eco Bag Plush (Image: Sushi Express)
Where and when to get them
The Christmas offerings are available from 7 to 31 December 2026 at Sushi Express, Sushi Plus and 争鲜gogo outlets. They are for takeaway only, so plan to pick them up and bring them home for the party. Prices are as provided by the brand; check outlets or the Sushi Express app for availability.
It is a pocket-friendly alternative if you are planning a festive gathering on a budget. If you are collecting festive eats this season, you may also like The Orchard Cafe’s Christmas buffet and Mister Donut’s KitKat Christmas donuts . We also covered the chain’s earlier Minions-themed sushi menu .
summary: Sushi Express launches three Christmas tree sushi platters from S$19 and an Eco Bag Plush for app members, from 7 to 31 December 2026.
title: Sushi Express Christmas platters: three tree-shaped sushi trays from S$19, 7 to 31 December

body:
Things to do in Munich
Mention Munich and most people picture 2 things: beer halls and Oktoberfest. That’s a shame, because Bavaria’s capital is arguably the best base in Germany for the Alps. With castles straight out of a storybook, emerald lakes, and painted mountain villages all a mere day trip away, the city itself changes completely with the seasons, from beer gardens in spring, to Christmas markets come winter.
If you’re looking for some inspo, here are 14 things to do in Munich, no matter which season you fly in.
The current exchange rate is S$1 = €0.70 as of 11th November 2026 , and prices in the article are accurate as of 11th November 2026 .
1. Neuschwanstein Castle
Real-life fairytale castle that inspired Disney
I mage credit: @visitbayern via Instagram
No Munich trip is complete without the castle you’ve seen on a thousand postcards. Neuschwanstein Castle was commissioned in 1869 by King Ludwig II, who was nicknamed “fairytale king”. Sadly, he never got to see this ambitious project finished before he passed away, and the castle was opened to the public in 1886, mere weeks after that.
Visits are by timed guided tour only, and each tour takes around 30 minutes, bringing you through rooms that pay homage to composer Richard Wagner’s operas. Tickets cost €21 (~S$31) plus a €2.50 (~S$3.70) online booking fee, and it’s recommended that you book your tickets online ahead of your intended visit date, as they do sell out.
Image credit: @europewithlily via Instagram
The castle sits about 2.5 hours by train from Munich, near the town of Füssen. You should note that the walk to the castle is approximately 40 minutes, winding up a steep hill. Alternatively, you can take a shuttle bus or horse-drawn carriage, though there is a final 10-minute uphill walk after that.
Pro tip: go in autumn for red-golden forests, or hold out till winter to catch a snowy scene that’s straight out of a fairytale.
Season to visit: All seasons
Address: Neuschwansteinstraße 20, 87645 Schwangau, Germany
Opening hours: 28th Mar-15th Oct 9am-6pm | 16th Oct-27th Mar 10am-4pm (Closed on 1st Jan, 24th, 25th & 31st Dec)
Contact: +49 8362 9398877 | Neuschwanstein Castle website
2. Linderhof Palace
The only palace that Ludwig II finished, with an underground grotto lake
Image credit: @la.lidija via Instagram
Ludwig II never got to see Neuschwanstein Castle completed, but he did stay somewhere else just as spectacular – Linderhof Palace – AKA one of the palaces that was completed in his lifetime.
Image credit: @steven2759 via Instagram
It was here that he spent more time than any of his other palaces, and if you see the Venus Grotto , you might just understand why. The artificial dripstone cave, 90m long and 14m tall, was the largest of its kind in the 19th century, and had an interactive stage which allowed Ludwig II to feel like he was in Wagner’s opera, Tannhäuser .
Fun fact: the stage was designed to Wagner’s exact stage directions, and also inspired by the Blue Grotto in Capri, which Ludwig II never visited, but was fascinated with. It was also Bavaria’s first permanent electric lighting system back in Ludwig II’s day, with lamps that had exchangeable colored glass discs to shift the mood of the artificial lake and waterfall!
Palace tours at Linderhof Palace run every 5 to 10 minutes, each lasting around 25 minutes. Grotto tours only take place from April to October each year, when the Venus Grotto and other ancillary buildings in Linderhof are open.
A palace-only ticket costs €11 (~S$16) , or €18 (~S$27) with the Venus Grotto added.
Season to visit: All seasons, but the Venus Grotto and ancillary buildings are not open in autumn and winter.
Address: Linderhof 12, 82488 Ettal, Germany
Opening hours: 15th Apr-15th Oct 9am-6pm | 16th Oct-14th Apr 10am-4.30pm (Venus Grotto is closed in winter)
Contact: +49 8822 9203-0 | Linderhof Palace website
3. Herrenchiemsee Palace
Palace on an island in Bavaria’s largest lake, modelled after Versailles
Image credit: @schloesserverwaltung.bayern via Instagram
Another of Ludwig II’s names is Mad King Ludwig, thanks to his history of paranoia, extreme reclusiveness, and how he drained the royal treasury to build his extravagant, impractical castles. Today, Herrenchiemsee Palace stands as the 3rd of his fantasy castles, built on Herreninsel, an island in Bavaria’s largest lake.
Image credit: @schloesserverwaltung.bayern via Instagram
It’s so big, Chiemsee is also affectionately known as the Bavarian Sea. But its location is not the only fantastical part of this palace – it was modelled after Versailles in France, with its very own Hall of Mirrors that’s even longer and grander than the OG!
Then, there’s the magnificent marble State Staircase, and Tischlein-deck-dich , or “little table serve dinner”, a mechanical, lowerable dining table inspired by a Brothers Grimm fairytale.
Image credit: @schloesserverwaltung.bayern via Instagram

Monster Curry is putting chocolate in its curry for Christmas. A Meiji collaboration menu runs at Monster Curry outlets from 16 November 2026 to 3 January 2027, led by a S$16.90 Meiji Black Choco Katsu Curry.
The Japanese curry chain is known for its demi-glace curry. For the festive run it has paired up with Meiji, the Japanese confectionery maker, and built six items around Meiji Black Chocolate, Hello Panda, Chocorooms and Uproll.
The Meiji menu and prices
• Meiji Black Choco Katsu Curry, S$16.90: the classic katsu curry with Monster Curry’s demi-glace sauce, with Meiji Black Chocolate mixed in for a hint of sweetness. Pork or chicken katsu.
• Meiji Black Choco Curry Fries, S$8.90: thick-cut fries with the same chocolate curry sauce.
• Choco Noel Honey Toast, S$14.50: buttery toast with Meiji Black Chocolate ganache, toasted marshmallows, Chocorooms and fresh strawberries, topped with vanilla ice cream and a small Santa.
• Choco Cone Milkshake, S$6.90: a chocolate milkshake topped with Uproll.
• Strawberry Cone Milkshake, S$6.90: a strawberry milkshake, also topped with Uproll.
• Deck-the-Toast, S$13.90: a make-your-own honey toast with honey-buttered toast cubes, Meiji Black Chocolate ganache, Hello Panda, strawberries and sprinkles. Ice cream is a S$2 top-up.
Choco Noel Honey Toast, S$14.50. Image: Monster Curry Singapore
The menu photo shows the chocolate poured over the curry from a small jug, and Monster Curry pitches it as a richer curry with a touch of sweetness rather than a dessert. The fries get the same chocolate curry sauce, at S$8.90, if you want a side for the table.
Meiji Black Choco Curry Fries, S$8.90. Image: Monster Curry Singapore
Dine-in only, plus service charge
The festive menu is for dine-in only and runs while stocks last. Prices are subject to a 10 per cent service charge and GST, so the S$16.90 katsu curry is not the bill total.
The Meiji Christmas table menu: dine-in only, prices subject to 10 per cent service charge and GST. Image: Monster Curry Singapore
Monster Curry also runs a Meiji Holiday Toast Workshop for families on selected weekends at selected outlets, with limited spots and booking required. Monster Curry has not published session dates or a price yet; bookings go through its workshop page .
Deck-the-Toast, S$13.90, with a S$2 ice cream top-up. Image: Monster Curry Singapore
Where to find it
All nine Monster Curry outlets serve the menu: ION Orchard (#B4-52), Jurong Point 2 (#03-57), NEX (#B1-08), Northpoint City (#B1-102), Novena Square (#02-78/79), Suntec City (#02-377/378), Jewel Changi Airport (#03-200), VivoCity (#02-126/127 and 129) and Waterway Point (#02-25). Most open from 11am to 10pm; Waterway Point opens from 11.30am to 9pm.
summary: Monster Curry's Meiji Christmas menu runs from 16 November 2026 to 3 January 2027 at nine outlets, with a S$16.90 Black Choco Katsu Curry, S$8.90 curry fries and S$14.50 honey toast.
title: Monster Curry puts Meiji chocolate on a S$16.90 katsu curry for Christmas, 16 November to 3 January

body:
You no longer have to fly to the Land of Smiles to get your Thai food fix. Soi Stories , opening in Dec 2026 at The Centrepoint , will be Singapore’s first Thai food street . It will bring together 11 food concepts curated by Michelin-starred Chef Thitid “Ton” Tassanakajohn . It will open daily, 7.30am – 11pm.
The stars of this new dining spot are the 2 award-winning Bangkok hawkers alongside 9 other concepts developed under Chef Ton’s culinary direction. There will also be additional dessert and drink stalls, along with a lifestyle goods stall. Altogether, that’s a total of 13 stalls under one roof !
The dining experience will go beyond just tasting delicious Thai meals; the space itself will make you feel as though you’ve been transported to Thailand. Inspired by Bangkok’s neighbourhood streets, Soi Stories will feature layered shopfronts, vintage colours, aged finishes and greenery. Plus, the dining space will have 270 seats, including a communal Thai Pavilion that will accommodate groups of up to 10.
The 2 award-winning hawker stalls will be: Khun Chui Kapow and Kua Kai Ai Khao . The former is Chef Ton’s personal favourite, and it will specialise in a familiar favourite — Kaprow . With the aromatic holy basil as its star ingredient, you can expect dishes such as Minced Pork Krapow with Rice and Fried Egg and Beef Krapow . They will prepare all their dishes to order — yum!
The other Bangkok export, Kua Kai Ai Khao , will focus on G uay Tiew Kua Gai . The dish consists of wok-fried wide rice noodles with chicken and egg. You can choose from 3 variations: Classic, Crispy and Heritage.
Original Thai stalls will include Mor Khao Mor Gaeng (curry and rice), Siam Beef Co. (beef noodles), Phad Thai Arai ( Phad Thai ), Jok Thong (congee), Talad Guay Jub ( kway chap ), Heng Dee Fishball (fishball noodles), and BKK Fried Chicken . For beverages, head over to Khao Chao for coffee and toast or Nam Jai for drinks and tipples. Plus, Nam Jai will feature Singapore’s first 6-tap Chang beer system.
Want to finish your meal with a sweet treat? Mae Ka-Nom will have you covered with colourful Thai desserts. Lastly, you will also be able to bring some goodies home when you shop at Sarapad Thai . This will be their lifestyle goods stall, featuring specially curated, Thai-made goods.
10 Thai SELECT-certified restaurants in Singapore for an authentic taste of Thailand
summary: Soi Stories at The Centrepoint is set to become Singapore’s first Thai food street when it opens in Dec 2026, bringing 13 food, drink and lifestyle concepts together under one roof. Curated by Michelin-starred Chef Ton, the 270-seat dining destination features 2 award-winning Bangkok hawker stalls, 9 other Thai food concepts, dessert and beverage stalls, making it a convenient option for those seeking a variety of Thai street food in Orchard Road.
title: Soi Stories – Michelin-starred chef curated Thai food street with 13 stalls

Are you the kind of person who likes a no-frills meal in the midst of a busy work or school day, as long as it’s tasty and filling? Tsui Wah might have the answer for you – its new limited-time menu that embodies that spirit of a simple, delicious meal from a Hong Kong cha chaan teng .
Credit: Tsui Wah
The highlight is a series of new hearty rice meals for one , starting at S$13.80 , featuring generous portions of familiar ingredients for the perfect comfort meal . This includes the Baked Pork and Corn with Fried Rice in Cream Sauce (S$14.80) , affectionately known as “Show Me Your Love” for its Cantonese pronunciation.
Another timeless cha chaan teng staple in the new menu is Minced Beef with Pasteurised Egg and Steamed Rice (S$14.80) . The steamed rice is topped off with a golden-orange egg yolk, symbolising “Overflowing Love”.
Credit: Tsui Wah
Looking for a drink to complete your meal? There is also a selection of refreshing drinks, including the popular Red Bean and Green Tea/Vanilla Ice-Cream Float ($6.80) , and the new 7UP with Salted Lime ($5.80) and 7UP with Vanilla Ice-Cream ($5.80) .
If you noticed a little ‘love’ theme here, that’s because Tsui Wah launched the new menu items in conjunction with Singles’ Day (11.11) ! But whether you’re dining alone or with a special someone, you’ll probably find a meal that brightens your day.
Drop by your nearest Tsui Wah outlet and find out for yourself.

body:
Monster Curry launches Christmas collab with Meiji
Bizarre flavour combinations have been on the rise lately, with mala peanut gelato and even bougie chocolate pasta . As a chocolate and spicy food lover, I never would have thought to pair chocolate with curry, but Monster Curry did. The Japanese curry chain has put a festive spin on its menu, releasing a Christmas Chocolate series in collaboration with Meiji . Despite our initial scepticism, my colleague and I headed down to the VivoCity outlet to see if the new series is worth a try.
Available islandwide at all Monster Curry outlets from 16 November 2026 to 3 January 2027, the menu features your Monster Curry favourites with a chocolate twist, including Singapore’s very first chocolate curry, as well as an array of sides and desserts. Fun fact: the chocolate used in all dishes is none other than Meiji’s Black Chocolate —the brand’s dark chocolate bar.
We first dug into the Meiji Black Choco Curry Fries ($8.90++) . The thick-cut fries were fried to a crisp, and we were surprised at how long each one was.
What sets this side apart is, of course, the sauce, which combines Monster Curry’s signature demi-glace curry sauce with the Meiji Black Chocolate.
Taste wise, we found that the chocolate overpowered the curry flavour in the sauce, leaning more towards the sweet side. Though it was a tad too sweet for us, this would be great if you love sweet and salty combinations.
Moving on to the star of the show: the Meiji Black Choco Curry ($16.90++) , sporting the usual massive portion that Monster Curry is known for. We opted for the pork katsu, but you can go for chicken if that’s what you prefer. It comes with the usual curry katsu fixings, this time served alongside melted Meiji Black Chocolate sauce.
We poured in a good amount of chocolate straight into the curry. Upon first impressions, the chocolate added a subtle sweetness to the dish, giving it a slight depth of flavour. Similar to the fries, we found the pairing slightly too sweet, so it’s best to pour the sauce one bit at a time before committing to the entire jug. This combo was slightly too funky for us, though we do think it’s an interesting addition to the lineup.
We also recommend pouring the chocolate in ASAP before it hardens and giving everything a good mix to marry the flavours together. Katsu wise, each slice was perfectly crisp with tender and juicy meat.
Now would be a good time to wash all that food down with their milkshakes. Choose between the Choco Cone Milkshake or Strawberry Cone Milkshake , both priced at $6.90++ each and topped with Meiji uproll strawberry chocolates .
The former had a strong chocolate flavour that was rich and decadent. The latter was my personal favourite as it was refreshing and less heavy. It tasted nostalgic and familiar, with the strawberry chocolates being the ones I used to snack on as a kid.
There’s no better way to enjoy chocolate than in a dessert, and the Chocolate Noel Honey Toast ($14.50++) that was doused in a rich chocolate ganache instantly satisfied our sweet tooth. Accompanying the dessert is the iconic Chocorooms snack, adding a nice crunch in each bite. The toast was also topped with vanilla ice cream, strawberries, and toasted marshmallows for an ultimate indulgent sweet treat.
Each toast had a buttery aroma, with a crunchy exterior and a soft, pillowy centre. The Meiji chocolate ganache stole the show, pairing well with the toast.
To add to the festive cheer, get your hands on exciting prizes when you try the new chocolate series. Receive one stamp on the Christmas Stamp Card with every $25 spent, plus a bonus stamp with a purchase of the Meiji Black Choco Katsu Curry or Chocolate Noel Honey Toast.
Image credit: @monstercurry.sg
What’s more: spot the upcycled Meiji Christmas trees at Jewel, Suntec, and VivoCity and guess how many boxes were used to build them for a chance to win a free Super Monster Combo, featuring made-to-order yaki beef or pork alongside yakiniku sauce, red wine, fried pork katsu, and an omelette.
Overall, we found that chocolate and curry definitely made for a unique pairing, though we’d still stick to the regular one for now. Do drop by any outlet when it officially launches in-stores to try it out for yourselves!
On the topic of collabs, check out our KFC x Avengers: Doomsday feature for the latest scoop on their limited-time menu. For more spicy food, read our Mala Mia feature for halal mala with over 60 ingredients at Changi Airport.

Monster Curry is not halal-certified.

body:
Best crab bee hoon in Singapore
If you are a fan of all things crab, then you’ve got to try crab bee hoon at least once in your life. Served with either white vermicelli noodles (bee hoon) or Chinese vermicelli (dong fen), crab bee hoon is usually cooked in two styles: braised and soupy. Find out where you can get a taste of both with our list of the 10 best crab bee hoon spots in Singapore !
1. Crab at Bay
Tucked in the corner of Macpherson Road is Crab At Bay , which serves delicious and fresh-tasting crabs. Get a taste of this sweet flesh in the Crab Bee Hoon (seasonal price) where these crustaceans are cooked to perfection along with bee hoon that absorbs the crab’s delicious flavour. The restaurant frequently offers promotional deals, such as 1-for-1 crabs, so do check out their Facebook page to get more bang for your buck!
Address: 540 MacPherson Road, Singapore 368223
Opening hours: Daily 10:30am to 2:30pm, 4:30pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 6743 8366
Website
Crab at Bay is not halal-certified.
2. Long Ji Zi Char
Image credit: @xineats
Avid fans of crab bee hoon would be well-acquainted with Long Ji Zi Char . Their signature Crab Bee Hoon (seasonal price) is on the slightly wetter side with thick oyster sauce, and features strong and flavourful wok hei notes with a slightly peppery taste. The crabs themselves are said to be fresh, juicy, and reasonably meaty. They tend to be on the pricier side, however, so you’ll have to be prepared to pay a hefty price for this excellent dish.
Address: 253 Outram Road, Singapore 169049
Opening hours: Daily 5pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 9790 5682
Website
Long Ji Zi Char is not halal-certified.
3. Chicken Pie Kitchen & Don Signature Crab
Chicken Pie Kitchen & Don Signature Crab is, as the name suggests, home to superb pies and crab dishes, with their crab bee hoon being a clear standout. Their crab Beehoon Sou p (from $39.80++) is served in a broth which has a splash of Shaoxing Chinese White Wine, dang gui, and an aromatic hint of ginger. This is topped off with some milk cabbage, yam, and evaporated milk to give it some creaminess. The combination of these ingredients results in a really sweet and tasty soup dish.
Address: 39 Tyrwhitt Road, Singapore 207538
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 10am to 9pm, Fri-Sat 10am to 10:30pm
Tel: 6993 3333
Website
Chicken Pie Kitchen & Don Signature Crab is not halal-certified.
4. Kelly Jie
Image credit: @minmin_tabemon
Formerly known as Melben Seafood (Toa Payoh), Kelly Jie Seafood rebranded and named themselves after one of their vivacious managers. The famous Claypot Crab Vermicelli Soup (seasonal price) is highly recommended, but be patient with the long wait which is at least 45 minutes. A whole crab is cooked in a milky broth, giving it a rich, umami flavour. It’s not too jelak, and almost feels like you can drink it all day long.
Address: 211 Toa Payoh Lorong 8, #01-11/15, Singapore 310221
Opening hours: Daily 12pm to 2:30pm, 4:30pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 8123 4156
Website
Kelly Jie Seafood is not halal-certified.
5. De Golden Spoon Seafood
Image credit: @valswc
De Golden Spoon Seafood is well known for their Golden Spoon Bee Hoon Crab (seasonal price) . The crab sits in a thick, umami-rich gravy, which is best appreciated when slurped up with the accompanying al dente noodles. The huge crab is packed with succulent and sweet-tasting meat, with hints of wok hei notes that elevate the robust sauce. The Salted Egg Crab (seasonal price) here also comes highly recommended.
Address: 62 Seng Poh Lane, #01-11, Singapore 160062
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 2:30pm, 5pm to 10:30pm
Tel: 9118 5544
Website
De Golden Spoon Seafood is not halal-certified.
6. Sin Huat Eating House
Image credit: @amap1014
Some consider Sin Huat Eating House one of the best places to get crab bee hoon in the country. However, the exorbitant prices they charge and long waiting times have made them highly controversial—it wasn’t too long ago that a food blogger’s $1,127 meal here sparked discussion about the place online. Their Crab Bee Hoon ( seasonal price) , features a fresh-tasting crab that is packed with meat. Each strand of springy bee hoon is said to be soft and springy, and well-coated in the wok hei-filled gravy.
Address: 659-661 Lorong 35 Geylang, Singapore 389589
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 1pm
Tel: 6744 9755
Website
Sin Huat Eating House is not halal-certified.
7. Keng Eng Kee Seafood
Image credit: Keng Eng Kee Seafood @ Alexandra Village
Keng Eng Kee Seafood is a legendary zi char restaurant that has achieved significant recognition over the course of its 50-year history, with a Michelin Plate award and a recommendation from the late Anthony Bourdain. Their Stir Fried Thin Beehoon With Cr ab (seasonal price) is as good as the other hits at this restaurant, featuring bee hoon noodles, chunky crabs, and plenty of wok hei.
Website | Full list of outlets
Keng Eng Kee Seafood is not halal-certified.
8. Uncle Leong Seafood
Image credit: @uncleleongseafood

body:
When it comes to briyani , I’d like to think that I have a refined palate for it. Every briyani that I have eaten while writing for SethLui.com has been nothing short of mind-blowing. It’s come to the point where I’d compare every briyani that I eat to the very best ones. And yes, nothing comes close. So, I came to Bismi Biryani , located at Yishun Park Hawker Centre , with an open mind.
Admittedly, it’s better known for its near-absurd briyani platter than its actual briyani , which prompted me to give it a go. Bismi Biryani was founded by 26-year-old Sheik Mohammad. When the day came to sign the agreement to open his stall, it was also the same day that PM Lee Hsien Loong announced the start of the circuit breaker.
He didn’t let that deter him as he continued operations from his flat, but even that had to cease when there was a temporary ban on home-based businesses. He then focused his attention on perfecting his recipe and was finally able to start renovations for his hawker stall when Phase 2 began.
What I tried at Bismi Biryani
Despite having an eating buddy with me, we listened to our arteries and opted out of their many different biryani platter sets, such as Combo Platter ($39) , Seafood Platter ($52) and Lamb Shank Platter ($70) . Instead, we had the Lambchop Biryani ($8) and Grilled Chicken Kabsa ($7) . Other solo-eating friendly items include Lambshank Mandhi ($18) and Fried Chicken Sambal B iryani ($7) .
I was somewhat disappointed that Bismi Biryani didn’t have the classic mutton biryani . Also missing was the chicken biryani, which is usually cooked along with basmati rice.
First off was the Lambchop Biryani, which came with a bowl of goat curry and a side of onion and cucumber salad. The rice definitely has a milder look to it as compared to the overly vibrant orange and yellow hue that we often associate with briyani . I also appreciated the fact that the rice only used spices, saffron and rose water without any artificial colouring involved.
Unfortunately, mild could also be used to describe the flavours of the rice. Imagine your standard briyani flavours of turmeric, masala powder and cloves, but watered down twice — that was exactly how it tasted. It was also quite dry, and frankly, I’m not even sure how you can make rice dry without being undercooked (which it wasn’t). I found myself sipping on my drink after nearly every spoonful of rice.
Thankfully, the lamb chop was tender and easy to cut through, but it wasn’t fall-of-the-bone tender like some online reviews suggested. As far as flavours go, it tasted mostly of the gravy that it was covered with. Well, at least it wasn’t gamey.
For the price, I felt that the portion was slightly on the low side, as the piece I received had a ‘T’ shaped bone that took up maybe 30% of the lamb. I found myself rationing the pieces to last my entire plate.
Up next was the Grilled Chicken Kabsa . My expectation was quite low the minute I ordered the dish, as the chicken had already been grilled and was left in a heated pan of sorts. My sixth sense told me that the grilled chicken was going to be a really dry affair. It came with a watery curry and the same onion & cucumber salad.
The kabsa rice was made using 5 spices, ghee , saffron and rose water — something I was only aware of when I wrote this review, as it almost tasted like ordinary rice with just a hint of smokiness. And really, it shouldn’t be the case, as our plate had a piece of a cinnamon stick in the rice.
The biggest letdown of the afternoon had to be the grilled chicken, and to cut a long story short, it was as dry as it looked. Usually, I could ignore an overcooked dish if the flavours were at least decent, but the chicken tasted entirely of turmeric and salt. I’m not sure where the marination that consisted of a variety of spices and masala went.
In fairness, I thought the portion of the grilled chicken leg was quite generous — if only I could say the same thing about its seasoning.
Both the curries were quite average. It tasted like fish curry, the kind you usually get along with your prata . It did help us down our meals better, which was a godsend. The only difference between the two curries was that one was thicker and the other was watery, but they tasted quite similar to one another.
Another condiment that we had was green chilli sauce. It had a pretty potent kick, though I felt that the raw chilli taste was too prominent, and served as a distraction from the little flavours the rice already had.
Final thoughts
To be clear, it wasn’t the worst thing I’ve eaten despite being critical about it. It just fell short as a briyani dish. The rice, which was supposed to be the highlight of the dish, didn’t live up to expectations, even when compared to your run-of-the-mill briyani spots.
At least social eaters and mukbangers have a unique spot for their huge food platter cravings.

Where do I get the best affordable lunch in the CBD in Singapore?
…
summary: Bismi Biryani at Yishun Park Hawker Centre is known more for its large briyani platters ($39 to $70) than for its rice, with solo dishes such as Lambchop Biryani ($8) and Grilled Chicken Kabsa ($7). The rice and chicken tasted mild and dry, and the portions were modest. Best suited to groups wanting a platter rather than diners seeking a strong briyani.
title: Bismi Biryani: XXL briyani platters & grilled chicken kabsa rice with generous portions

body:
If you venture into the basement of Golden Mile Tower , you’ll find yourself surrounded by several small Thai eateries, each serving its own regional specialities. Amongst these, Somtam Saklai stands out as the most prominent, boasting ample seating and a giant khrok sak (traditional Thai mortar and pestle) dedicated to pounding out their namesake dish.
Unlike the more conventional Central or Southern Thai dishes commonly found in Singapore, Somtam Saklai specialises in Northeastern Isan cuisine. Isan cooking places heavy emphasis on bold, punchy, and fiery flavours achieved by use of pungent fermented ingredients — contrasting the tangier, citrus-forward profiles of the south. With its completely unpretentious atmosphere, the eatery immediately exudes an authentic vibe that made me all the more excited to dive in.
What to order at Somtam Saklai
Of course, I had to try their namesake dish: the Fish Crab Papaya Salad (S$8) , aka somtam . The dish arrives piled with crisp papaya strips, a quarter of a tomato, and raw garlic, all adorned with smashed pieces of traditional Thai salted crab ( poo khem ) and dressed in lime juice. I requested just a mild kick with a bit of chilli padi, but you can fully customise the spice level to your liking.
Unlike standard Central-style papaya salads that rely on palm sugar and regular fish sauce ( nam pla ) for a sweeter finish, this Isan variation gets its deep, complex, and pungent profile from pla ra . Despite also being made by fermenting freshwater fish with salt, this traditional alternative instead boasts a strong, deeply briny aroma and an intense savoury umami depth.
Save your time and don’t bother trying to pry any meat out of the small salted crabs like I did! Their role is to be pounded directly with the mortar to release a sharp, mineral-rich saltiness and a distinct fermented fragrance that builds the dish’s complexity.
However, I wish the salad had a touch more lime juice for a sharper, tangier kick to cut through all that rich savouriness. I recommend pairing it with some of their house-made sauces for that extra punch.
Next up was the Tom Yum Seafood Noodle (S$8) , which came chock-full of squid rings and prawns, sitting atop a heaping pile of glass noodles and vibrant, red broth. This dish proved to be a very pleasant surprise for me, as I usually avoid tom yum because the aggressive sourness tends to hit the back of my throat, but this soup base was remarkably balanced. Neither overly sweet nor cloyingly sour, it remained incredibly refreshing while maintaining a rich depth of flavour.
The soup carried pleasant, citrusy notes of makrut lime and lime juice, complementing the deeply savoury foundation of the broth, which I didn’t find to be as rich and creamy as other tom yum soups I’ve had in the past, instead leaning more towards being light and drinkable. It wasn’t very spicy either, with the heat building slowly as I ate, rather than being outright spicy from the start.
For just S$8, I was genuinely shocked by the generous spread of ingredients, which included tender squid and fresh prawns — offering fantastic value for money. I probably had a piece of seafood in every other mouthful, which is honestly a rare find today, especially at this price point.
11 authentic Thai restaurants in Singapore with the prestigious Thai SELECT award
The glass noodles had a delightful chewiness to them initially, though they do absorb the broth quickly and turn a bit soggy over time, so you’ll want to tuck in fast!
As a staple Thai comfort food, Pad See Ew Seafood (S$8) arrives steaming hot with a generous amount of ingredients. This classic stir-fried noodle dish features a heap of thick, flat noodles tossed with crunchy kailan , scrambled egg, and a remarkably large portion of seafood — most notably 2 plump prawns and pieces of tender squid.
The fresh seafood was cooked perfectly and wasn’t rubbery or tough, instead being perfectly tender with a nice bite. The scrambled egg pieces absorb all the savoury seasonings and add rich bursts of flavour throughout the dish, while the kailan stalks lend a fresh, natural sweetness and a satisfying crunch that contrasts beautifully against the bouncy, chewy noodles.
I’d liken the noodles themselves to the thick, flat rice noodles used in char kway teow , cooked to perfection with a great chew. Tossed over high heat, they boast a smoky wok-hei aroma that infuses every bite. Overall, the dish is well-balanced without leaning too sweet or overly salty; it delivers a deeply savoury, comforting finish that makes every mouthful immensely enjoyable.
Who is Somtam Saklai best for?
Somtam Saklai is ideal for anyone hunting for a genuinely authentic, no-frills (and no GST) Thai meal that doesn’t pinch the wallet. It’s a fantastic spot if you’re eager to venture beyond standard Central and Southern styles to explore regional Isan specialities that are hard to find in Singapore.
…
summary: Somtam Saklai in the basement of Golden Mile Tower offers affordable, authentic Northeastern Isan Thai cuisine in a comfortable, air-conditioned setting. The menu features fiery fermented papaya salads along with generous S$8 seafood noodle dishes like balanced tom yum and smoky pad see ew. Free of GST and service charges, this unpretentious spot is best suited for diners seeking bold regional Thai flavours and hearty portions on a budget.
title: Somtam Saklai: No-GST Thai gem in Golden Mile with loaded $8 plates

Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge
The next Olympics might not be till 2028, but this end-of-year school holidays, you and the fam can take part in Mandai Wildlife Reserve ’s very own Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge , happening from 7th November 2026 to 3rd January 2027 .
This challenge follows the recently concluded Stars of Mandai Autograph Trail , starring the same animal celebrities, with a festive twist. Here’s what you can look forward to at Zoolympix:
Take part in 10 wildlife-inspired challenges
Each designed to showcase the Stars of Mandai’s unique skills
The highlight of these Zoolympix is a set of 10 challenges , inspired by the unique abilities of the Stars of Mandai. Head to the Zoolympix Village at Mandai Wildlife EAST Lawn , where you can take them on from 10am to 7pm daily .
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group
The Mandai Wildlife Reserve comprises 5 parks: Singapore Zoo, Bird Paradise, River Wonders, Night Safari, and Rainforest Wild Adventure. Each park is repped by 2 Stars of Mandai, with the challenges designed around their distinctive traits.
Take, for example, the Agility challenge, where you’ll have to pick up durians, and swing, balance, and get across the faux forest canopy a la Ah Meng to complete the task.
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group
Over at the challenge inspired by king penguins, the mission is to waddle your way to the finish line in giant flippers, while keeping your egg balanced on your feet – just like Arlo the king penguin.
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group
Then, the next challenge sees you emulate Bayu the Malayan tapir, dashing through the rain zone to look for his favourite foods to pass the test.
Every challenge has been designed with 2 difficulty levels – one for participants aged 3 to 7, and the other for challengers aged 8 to 12, and above.
Pass all 10 challenges to win a medal
Besides discovering how we can help protect the animals and habitats we share together, you and the kids can also walk away with a little something to remember the experience by.
Each completed challenge earns you a stamp on your activity card. Collect all 10 stamps to redeem an exclusive Zoolympian medal .
Every finisher is a podium finisher at Zoolympix too, so don’t forget to snap a photo on the Zoolympix Podium to commemorate your achievement!
Image credit: Mandai Wildlife Group
Cop a Zoolympian trophy plush
That’s not all – bring your completed activity card to The Mandai Shop, River Wonders Shop and Night Safari Shop, and you can bring home an uber cute Zoolympian Trophy Plush at $9 , instead of the usual $12.
Check out the Partner Zone
There’s more to explore beyond the main challenge course. While you’re at the Zoolympix Village, drop by the Partner Zone to check out booths from participating partners including AIA , Anywheel , POSB , and Families for Life .
Spot the bonus Zoolympix Outposts
The fun doesn’t stop at Zoolympix Village. Head into the wildlife parks to discover 1 Zoolympix Outpost per park , where you can learn more about the Stars of Mandai, complete the activities, then strike your best pose with the photo ops there.
Of course, you’ll want to cop a shot with the Stars of Mandai IRL before carrying on with the rest of the park.
Perks for local residents & Friends of Mandai
If you’re a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, you’re in luck: sign up for WildPass and you’ll enjoy access to the Zoolympix Village, along with a $10 Retail and F&B voucher with any purchase of selected admission tickets.
Friends of Mandai can look forward to special deals during Members’ Wild Weekend , taking place on 14th to 15th November . On these dates, Zoolympix Village tickets will be available for $8 (U.P. $20) each, inclusive of an exclusive members-only gift.
Catch the festive decor around the parks
Stick around to enjoy the festive atmosphere across Mandai Wildlife Reserve, where Christmas decor and photo opportunities bring the holiday season to life. Join the Ranger Buddies in spreading festive cheer by sending Christmas wishes, creating handmade ornaments and taking part in fun seasonal activities at Curiosity Cove .
From festive crafts to interactive experiences, there are plenty of ways for little ones to celebrate, connect and make special holiday memories. Don’t forget to stop by the Ranger Buddies Outposts to discover what other surprises they’ve got!
Challenge yourself at Mandai Wildlife Reserve’s Zoolympix
Learning through play is a fun way to bring classroom lessons to life while keeping the little ones entertained, sans screens. With activities that encourage kids to get moving and learn about wildlife and conservation, Zoolympix makes for a great family outing this EOY hols.
So, bring the kids down to Zoolympix: Stars of Mandai Festive Challenge this December, and who knows? You might find yourself joining in on the challenges right alongside them!
Find out more about Mandai Zoolympix

Singapore Art Week 2027
January isn’t only about making new year resolutions or gearing up for CNY. Singapore Art Week (SAW) is back for its 15th edition from 21st to 31st January 2027 , bringing over 100 exhibitions, installations, tours, and parties to different parts of the island.
With Singapore taking on the ASEAN Chairmanship and ASEAN celebrating its 60th anniversary next year, this edition puts the spotlight on Southeast Asian art. Expect building-sized projections at Raffles Place, a former rice warehouse transformed into a living artwork, and giant inflatables towering over the Padang.
We’ve rounded up the key things to know about this year’s edition, along with the highlights worth adding to your calendar.
What is Singapore Art Week?
Organised by the National Arts Council (NAC), SAW is Singapore’s biggest visual arts season . Most programmes are spread across art precincts such as the Civic District, Tanjong Pagar Distripark, Gillman Barracks , and Marina Bay, though you’ll also find installations in everyday spaces, including MRT stations and Clarke Quay .
View this post on Instagram
There are a few handy additions to look out for this year:
• A SAW app: Plan your own itinerary across the 100+ events without having to juggle multiple browser tabs.
• SG Culture Pass : Use your credits for selected ticketed programmes, including ART SG, S.E.A. Focus, and the SAW Forum.
• Free and ticketed events: Many exhibitions and public installations are free to visit, while art fairs, tours, and talks require tickets.
We also checked out Singapore Art Week 2026 last year, and one tip still stands: wear comfortable shoes. With events happening across the island, you’ll probably be clocking quite a few steps.
What to expect at Singapore Art Week 2027
1. The Last Sunset by Dawn Ng
1-night-only live cinema show at Golden Mile Tower, narrated by a global cast including Tilda Swinton
Image credit: Dawn Ng Studio
Singaporean artist Dawn Ng is bringing the world premiere of 4 chapters from The Last Sunset to Golden Mile Tower , one of Singapore’s last remaining brutalist landmarks. The 30-minute performance takes place for 1 night only, making this one of the more exclusive experiences at SAW 2027.
At its centre is a giant moving-image work of a sun made from frozen pigment, which slowly melts and collapses throughout the show. A live choir will sing from within the audience, accompanied by an original score by Welsh composer Alex Mills that blends heartbeats, lullabies, gamelan degung, and even NASA recordings.
The stories of endings are narrated by an international cast that includes Oscar-winning actress Tilda Swinton. This is one to keep an eye on when tickets are released.
Venue: Golden Mile Tower, 6001 Beach Road, #05-00, Singapore 199589
Date: 22nd January 2027
2. Pop after Pop: Art around Us & Light to Night 2027
Warhol & Lichtenstein at SEA’s largest Pop Art exhibition
Roy Lichtenstein. Reflections on Crash. 1990.
Image credit: Singapore Art Museum
National Gallery Singapore is teaming up with New York’s Guggenheim to present Pop after Pop: Art around Us , the largest group exhibition of Pop Art ever staged in Southeast Asia. The showcase brings together over 200 artworks by more than 100 artists.
Alongside familiar names like Andy Warhol and Roy Lichtenstein, you’ll also get to see works by regional artists such as Singapore’s Ming Wong and the Philippines’ Ronald Ventura. So there’s plenty more to explore beyond the iconic Campbell’s soup cans.
The Pop Art theme will spill out of the gallery and into the Civic District through Light to Night Singapore 2027: POP. POWER. PLAY. . Look out for interactive installations, performances, and a facade projection by local design collective PHUNK, featuring creatures and floral motifs from its mythological universe.
Pop after Pop: Art around Us
Venue: National Gallery Singapore
Date: 11th December 2026-4th April 2027
Light to Night Singapore 2027: POP. POWER. PLAY.
Venue: Civic District
Date: 15th-31st January 2027
3. Rollie Pollie Art Park & BYOR at the Padang
2.7m-tall inflatables, artist merch, & a sculpture playground where you bring your own racket
Image credit: weareSuper
The Padang is getting a colourful makeover with Rollie Pollie Art Park by weareSuper. Taking inspiration from the traditional wobbly toy, the installation features 3 patterned inflatables standing 2.7m tall, alongside collectible merch, creative retail, and public workshops.
Local artists involved include Robert Zhao, Ruben Pang, and Vincent Leow, as well as artists from MINDS. The inflatables will also light up at night as part of Light to Night, making this a fun spot to swing by after dinner.
Right next to it, BYOR: Where Play Takes Shape by Aaron Lim and Quek Jia Qi turns sports equipment and urban infrastructure into sculptures that visitors can actually play with. The name stands for bring your own racket, so remember to pack one if you fancy getting a game in.
Venue: The Padang
…
summary: Plan your SAW itinerary!
title: Singapore Art Week 2027: SEA’s Largest Pop Art Exhibition, Art Rave At SAM & A Live Cinema Show Narrated By Tilda Swinton

Food options at AEON Mall Tebrau City in JB are getting more variety, with several new eateries joining its line-up. From crispy British-style fish and chips and comforting Hong Kong noodles to Korean fried chicken and Singapore-style min jiang kueh , there’s plenty to look forward to on your next mall visit.
Here are 7 new F&B openings to check out at AEON Mall Tebrau City , JB .
1. BatterCatch (Now open – S23, Level 2)
Credit – BatterCatch
Seafood lovers can get their fix at BatterCatch , a Singaporean fish and chips chain with MUIS Halal certification . Specialising in British-style comfort food, its menu features golden-battered fish made with choices such as halibut, haddock and barramundi, served with fries, mushy peas and house-made sauces.
Beyond its signature fish and chips, you can also tuck into other mains like pasta, burgers, and pies.
2. Zok Noodle House (Now open – S26, Level 2)
Established in 2011, Zok Noodle House brings Hong Kong and Macau-inspired comfort food to the table, with an emphasis on quality ingredients and house recipes. Its signature dumpling noodles are a good starting point, alongside pork bone broth noodles in spicy or milky soup.
The extensive menu also covers curry noodles, spicy chilli rice noodles, wonton noodles and steamed dim sum , including shrimp dumplings, crab roe siu mai and golden custard buns. Rice dishes and other pork-based noodle combinations round out the selection.
3. Nasi Lemak Shop (Nov 2026)
KL’s popular Nasi Lemak Shop is expected to arrive in November, bringing its familiar nasi lemak fix to Johor Bahru. Look out for its Nasi Lemak Ayam Goreng Berempah , alongside sides such as Sambal Kerang . The menu also includes local favourites like Mee Siam , giving diners more than one reason to drop by.
4. NakNak (Dec 2026)
Credit – NakNak
Korean fast food fans can look forward to NakNak , which combines 100% beef burgers, fried chicken and loaded fries. Its Nak Dak Boneless Thigh comes coated in your choice of Soy Garlic, Spicy Gochujang or Cheese Sauce, while wings and drumettes offer more saucy options.
Burger choices include Cheeseburger , Spicy Double Cheeseburger and Mushroom Swiss , as well as chicken burgers. For a more indulgent bite, try the Spicy Gochujang Mozzarella NakDak Burger .
5. Munchi Pancakes (Dec 2026)
Credit – Munchi Pancakes
Singapore’s Munchi Pancakes is bringing over 20 flavours of min jiang kueh , or apam balik , to the mall. What started as a hawker stall in Yishun has grown into a brand with over 42 outlets across Singapore.
Alongside familiar fillings like Peanut , Coconut , Red Bean and Kaya , expect creative options such as Biscoff , Milo Dinosaur , Matcha , Thai Milk Tea and Pistachio Kunafa . Mini Munchi boxes come with 6 pieces , making it easier to sample a few flavours in one go.
6. Subway (Dec 2026)
Credit – Subway Malaysia
For a quick, customisable meal, Subway is also expected to open in December. Its menu spans 6-inch and footlong subs, wraps and salads, with familiar picks including Chicken Teriyaki , Roasted Chicken , Italian B.M.T. , Steak & Cheese , Meatball Marinara and Tuna . Egg Mayo and Veggie Delite are available for those after something simpler.
7. Pepper Lunch (Jan 2027)
Credit – Chonky the Shiba Woofer via Google Reviews
Sizzling hotplate meals are coming to AEON Mall Tebrau City with Pepper Lunch , the Japanese fast-casual chain known for its signature iron plates. Meals arrive piping hot, allowing diners to mix their ingredients and sauces as the meat continues cooking at the table.
Its popular Beef Pepper Rice combines thinly sliced beef, rice, sweet corn and black pepper, while other options include steak platters, chicken and salmon sets, hotplate pasta and Japanese curry.
This new Initial D-inspired Fujiwara Tofu Shop cafe in JB serves unique tau fu fah, matcha & cocktails
summary: AEON Mall Tebrau City in Johor Bahru is welcoming 7 new F&B outlets between November 2026 and January 2027, spanning British-style fish and chips, Hong Kong noodles, Korean fried chicken, min jiang kueh and sizzling Japanese hotplate meals. The openings include halal-certified BatterCatch and familiar Singaporean and Malaysian brands, making this a useful overview for shoppers planning meals around their next mall visit.
title: New food spots opening at AEON Mall Tebrau City JB including Nasi Lemak Shop & NakNak

Family-friendly activities for the December holidays
The spooky season is finally behind us, which means the year-end holidays are closing in fast. As the school break approaches, your kids will soon have plenty of free time and energy to burn. But keeping them entertained throughout the holidays might be a challenge, especially when they’re eager to get out of the house.
Thankfully, there’s no shortage of things happening around Singapore when school’s out to add to your family calendar. We’ve rounded up a list of family-friendly activities worth checking out, including limited-time Christmas pop-ups, interactive exhibitions, and fun-filled camps.
1. Defence Collective Festival 2026
14th-15th Nov
The Defence Collective Festival (DCF) is back this year, celebrating all things Singapore Armed Forces, and the men and women keeping our country safe. This edition runs from 14th to 15th November 2026 at the Singapore Discovery Centre , Singapore Navy Museum , and Singapore Air Force Museum .
Admission to the festival is free, but you can purchase a Premium: Exclusive Passport ($10) , which you can use across all 3 museums to access the Premium activities. All Exclusive Passport holders also get a free DCF tote bag. Complete activities to collect stamps in the passport, and pick up museum-exclusive iron-on patches to personalise your tote bag!
Some premium activities you can look forward to include target shooting , drone-flying , and even turning into a human claw machine . There will be interactive gallery walks across all 3 locations, and there will also be historical characters coming to life at each museum whom you’ll get to meet as you solve riddles to collect stamps.
The free fringe activities are a ball too, with Morse code signal relays, bridge-building, giant battleship games, and more. There will be free, hourly shuttle buses operating from Jurong Point to Singapore Discovery Centre and back, as well as Expo MRT Station Exit B and Our Tampines Hub (Festive Walk), to the Singapore Navy Museum.
Book your Defence Collective Festival Premium: Exclusive Passport .
Admission: Free | Premium: Exclusive Passport $10/pax
Venue: Singapore Discovery Centre | Singapore Navy Museum | Singapore Air Force Museum
Date: 14th-15th November 2026
Time: 10am-6pm, Daily
2. The Story of Studio Ghibli
12 sets based on fan-favourite Studio Ghibli flicks
Image credit: Klook
Every kid who grew up watching Studio Ghibli films has probably imagined stepping into their fantastical worlds. That childhood dream can now become reality at The Story of Studio Ghibli exhibition coming to Gardens by the Bay on 18th November 2026 . Spanning 3,500sqm , the exhibition will feature 12 immersive sets inspired by some of the studio’s classics.
Get up close to an 8-metre-tall recreation of the famous bathhouse from Spirited Away , or join Totoro in the rain while waiting for the Cat Bus. It’s a chance for longtime fans to revisit indelible scenes, while introducing younger ones to the magic of Studio Ghibli. It’ll take around 60-75 minutes to finish the exhibition, though you’re welcome to take your time at each set.
Image credit: Klook
Early bird tickets starting at $29 are available from now till 17th December , with every adult ticket coming with an exclusive gift. Fans can also get the No Face Fortune Coin Bundle ($48) for a keepsake inspired by the iconic character. The exhibition will run until 4th July 2027 , so there’s no rush in squeezing this into your holiday plans.
Get your tickets to The Story of Studio Ghibli .
Admission: From $29/pax
Date: 18th December 2026 to 4th July 2027
Time: 10am-7pm, Daily
Venue: 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Gardens by the Bay, The West Lawn, Singapore 018953
3. PokéXciting!
Themed lounges & Pokémon meet-and-greets
Image credit: Changi Airport Group
Rounding off the Pokémon 30th anniversary celebrations this year is PokéXciting! , a special Asia tour inviting fans and trainers to step into an immersive Pokémon world. It’s making a stop in Singapore, so there’s plenty of Pokémon-themed festivities and pop-ups happening around Changi Airport and Jewel Changi Airport for fans to look out for.
One of the highlights is the PokéXciting First Partner Pokémon Parade , featuring all 27 starter Pokémon alongside 2 Pikachus, bringing some of the franchise’s most recognisable characters to life. There’s also the chance to catch familiar faces like Eevee, Gengar, and Snorlax in person at the free meet-and-greet sessions happening on selected dates.
Head to the Pokémon Experience Lounge to try out games on the Nintendo Switch 2, learn how to play the Pokémon TCG, and put your skills to the test with friendly battles. You can even drop by the Pokémon Personalisation Station to customise your own cap or Poké Ball bag with your name and charms.
…
summary: School’s out, so why not swap out the screen time with some family fun.
title: 18 Family-Friendly Things To Do During The December Holidays 2026 – Interactive Musical Shows & Festive Markets

body:
One festive event we all look forward to is the annual Christmas Wonderland in Singapore. From dazzling light displays and magical snowfall to hearty feasts and carnival games, the Yuletide fair is popular with families, friends, and couples for date nights. This year, it returns with more than 40 attractions across an expanded 30,000 sqm fairground. Want more festive cheer? Check out the best Christmas events in Singapore or Christmas markets in Singapore .
Tip: visit between 27 November and 10 December 2026 to get Merry Deals coupons with deals like free carnival games, rides, and discounts to participating lifestyle booths (T&Cs apply).
Christmas Wonderland 2026: Details at a glance
Best for: Family Christmas adventures, festive group gatherings, and romantic date nights
Date: 27 November 2026 to 3 January 2027
Time: 6.30pm to 11pm; session times at 6.30pm, 7.30pm, 8.30pm and 9.30pm, last entry at 10.15pm
Price: (Advance purchase) Adults $9 to $13, children aged three to 12 $7; (Same-day purchase) Adults $11 to $15; children aged three to 12 $7
Address: Christmas Wonderland , Supertree Grove and Meadow at Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Gardens Drive, Singapore 018953
Things to do at Christmas Wonderland
1. Enter the immersive Santa Mission Control
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
The all-new attraction to Christmas Wonderland is Santa Mission Control, a new immersive experience bringing Santa’s workshop to life. For one night, you get to be one of Santa’s helpers! Go behind the scenes at his gift factory and explore woodworking and gift-wrapping stations, the command centre overseeing delivery operations, and you can even visit Mr Claus himself in his executive office space. So swanky of you, Santa.
2. The return of Flying Santa
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
If you made it on the Nice List this year, here’s a special treat for you: catch Santa soaring above The Meadow at Gardens by the Bay to deliver presents! Additional show timings have been added too, thanks to popular demand. The enhanced show starts with Santa’s First Flight, a prelude following a toy maker’s journey to becoming Santa Claus.
Flying Santa sessions start at 7.55pm, 8.25pm, 8.55pm, and 9.25pm. Additional shows at 7.25pm and 9.55pm are only on weekends and in the lead-up to Christmas Day.
3. A new 20-metre Spalliera and snowfall
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
We all know and love the Spalliera , aka that magnificent light display handcrafted by one of Italy’s oldest artisan families that everyone posts on their social media accounts. Fun fact: the installation is roughly the height of five double-decker buses!
Families, look forward to the popular Garden Rhapsody light and sound show with Christmas tunes, and Blizzard Time , where little ones can experience snow in the tropics. Stand under the twinkling lights, catch snowflakes on your palm, and immerse yourself in the joyous occasion.
Garden Rhapsody and Blizzard Time occur three times a day, with timings at 7.45pm, 8.45pm, and 9.35pm. An additional show happens at 10.15pm, between 18 and 27 December 2026.
4. Fresh and festive light displays
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
Did someone say more light? As with past years, Christmas Wonderland promises plenty of light installations (and photo opportunities) dotted around Gardens by the Bay.
This year’s display includes the Elf Treehouse , a 20-metre-tall digital mixed-media installation that lets you peek into the lives of Santa’s merry elves and woodland creatures as they prepare for Christmas.
Other photo opportunities with dazzling lights include the Merry Lane by Trip.com , Snowball Lane, Jingle Grove , and many more!
5. Solace Studios’ festive photobooth
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
For the first time ever, Solace Studios will be bringing its popular Korean-style photobooths to the fairgrounds! There’ll be eight Christmas-themed rooms available with signature camera angles and shooting styles. Pick from backdrops like the Phone Booth to North Pole, Gift Room, or Gingerbread Shop and snap away. Queues for Solace Studios photo booths can be long, so be prepared for a wait. But it’s so worth it for those holiday memories.
6. Get your game on at the Grab Village
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
If you’re up for Christmas fun, swing by the Grab Village for festive huts and interactive activities. Plenty of prizes to be won, so put your best face forward and try your hand at the games! You can even take a break and enjoy drinks at the Grab Holiday Lodge , snap photos at the Chill Out Snowglobe , or try your luck at the Wishing Christmas Tree .
7. Eat, drink, and shop to your heart’s content
Photography: Christmas Wonderland
Even more festive dining and shopping options have been added this year, so this is your sign to prepare your wallets! Make it a special memory and build your own bear at the TinkerBox vending machine or shop food-inspired novelty gifts by Kids21 at Mistletoe Alley.

body:
Christmas afternoon tea in Singapore is a splendid way to get into the festive spirit without committing to a full-blown Christmas brunch or Christmas dinner . You won’t have to jostle with the crowds or loosen your pants after one too many trips to the buffet table. Instead, settle in with a loved one, tuck into an assortment of sweet and savoury bites, and perhaps enjoy a glass of bubbly or two. We’ve rounded up a few spots in Singapore serving Christmas afternoon tea this year – be sure to book ahead before the festive rush!
Why trust this guide
We’ve done the festive homework for you, comparing festive menus, prices, locations and experiences to help you find the spot for your ideal Christmas afternoon tea in Singapore. Details are checked against the latest available information from the venues.
Christmas afternoon tea in Singapore
1. The Marmalade Pantry
Photography: The Marmalade Pantry
We can always count on The Marmalade Pantry to ring in the festive season. Its Festive Moments Afternoon Tea is a lovely pick for those who enjoy the traditional afternoon tea experience, with a Christmas-inspired spread. Sink your teeth into the petite orange ginger cupcake and caramelised cashew nut tart for a touch of sweetness, or get adventurous with the fig garden tart and roasted zucchini sandwich. Wash everything down with two pots of Gryphon tea or a refreshing cucumber, pomegranate and sparkling fizz concoction.
Best for: A leisurely festive catch-up with your favourite tea companion
How much: $58++ for two people (additional wine pairing of $20++ for two glasses)
When: 2 November 2026 to 31 January 2027
Timings: Daily, 2pm to 6pm
Address: Multiple locations in Singapore including Ion Orchard, Peck Seah Street and Novena
Visit The Marmalade Pantry
2. The Lobby Lounge at Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
Photography: Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore
Take a seat beneath soaring ceilings and stately columns, and indulge in a refined festive afternoon tea at The Lobby Lounge, Frasers House, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Singapore. Executive pastry chef Jason Goh presents an elegant daytime affair inspired by the warmth and spirit of the holidays.
Served on a Christmas-themed three-tier stand, the menu includes seasonal savouries, delicate pastries, and freshly baked scones in English buttermilk, and rum and raisin renditions. Nibble on unique creations such as winter black truffle and foie gras parfait, mini Christmas gammon pie, strawberry mint yogurt cake and Sicilian pistachio brownie. Enjoy these with a daily selection of sorbet and gelato, alongside a choice of coffee or loose-leaf tea. Want to take your celebrations up a boozy notch? Top up from $16 to enjoy a glass of Saicho Single-Origin sparkling tea, champagne, and festive cocktails – featuring refreshing options like Mulled Wine Sour and Mistletoe Blush.
Little ones are also welcome to join the festivities with an afternoon tea menu curated for them. On the savoury front, they’ve got roasted turkey and cranberry cream cheese pinwheel, and smoked salmon tartare cone. Meanwhile, the whimsical sweet line-up includes Christmas tree cheesecake, mini gingerbread house and reindeer macaron. To top off the experience, the kiddos can enjoy a daily selection of sorbet and gelato from the ice cream trolley, as well as a choice of beverage.

Photography: 1-Group
Looking to make your Christmas date a little more special? Swing by Arden Bar & Lounge at 1-Arden for its Festive High Tea, where you can enjoy indulgent bites alongside gorgeous city views. Tuck into moreish offerings such as wood-smoked kamo kushiyaki, as well as the tarabagani and ise ebi sarada tartlet before moving to the sweet stuff. The matcha-kuri mont blanc will be a hit with matcha lovers, mark our words! The high tea set also comes with two festive cocktails with adorable names. We can’t wait to sip on the Winter Slay!
Best for: A Yuletide treat with skyline views and festive cocktails

body:
St Rosyam Mart is a new 24-hour supermarket in Tampoi
Image credit: Dina Din via Google Maps
The first activities that probably come to mind when you think of Johor Bahru are cafe-hopping , hearty zi char meals , and a massage sesh to end the day. However, if you really want to maximise your JB trip, here’s a tip from a fellow kiasu Singaporean: do your weekly grocery shopping here. St Rosyam Mart is a 24-hour mart in JB, so you can shop whenever you want.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~SS$0.32 as of 12 November 2026.
15 New JB Cafes To Visit In 2026: Sausage Dog Cafe, Free Boardgames And More
For the uninitiated, ST Rosyam Mart is a Malaysian supermarket chain by Sri Ternak Group. It has over 10 outlets around the nation, with its newest outlet at Paragon Market Place being its biggest yet.
There are over 40,000 products stocked here, from fresh produce to household essentials, so you’ll find what you need. Better yet, everything’s said to be priced at wholesale prices. All of the items in ST Rosyam Mart are also halal-certified, meaning Muslim patrons can also get their grocery shopping in.
The standout is the fresh fish and meat section, which feels like a proper wet market. There are fishmongers stationed round the clock to expertly prepare your chosen fish.
Their meat section is not lacking either. There are butchers around to help break down chicken and other poultry into different parts for easy cooking. If you’re worried about your seafood and meat going bad, the store even offers free ice packs.
I initially imagined the space to have a pungent fishy smell; there’s surprisingly little to no odour, as the mart is pretty well-ventilated.
Don’t skip their frozen seafood and meat section, as there are some good deals to be snagged. We found a whole King Crab priced at RM148 per kg , a steal for an extravagant seafood dinner, in our opinion.
Otherwise, a more affordable option is the pack of four Three-spot Swimming Crabs going for RM22.49 per kg . According to online reviews, they’re best eaten cooked in a spiced coconut gravy or in a soy sauce marinade.
Steak lovers will be glad to know that they sell Tomahawk Steaks (from RM188 per kg) too. The size was something else, too; I was genuinely struggling to lift it at first.
There’s also Wagyu Steak (from RM73 per kg) that’s basically the size of my whole torso—perfect for a steak dinner with your friends.
Before you make your haul, do note that SFA’s list doesn’t allow meat products to be brought back into Singapore, and seafood products have a 5kg weight limit. So, cook up and eat any meat you’ve purchased in JB before heading back.
You can also get the TikTok-viral Nims Crispy Choco Tub (RM15.59) here. Try their localised flavours: Onde Onde Crunch and Sirap Bandung Laici Crunch . The former is said to have the distinct ondeh ondeh flavours of coconut, pandan, and gula melaka, while the latter has a subtle fragrance of rose and lychee.
ST Rosyam Mart is located in Tampoi, a 17-minute drive from CIQ Jalan Jim Quee .
Once you’re done with your groceries, head to 365 Bakery , a TikTok-viral spot with over 100 handmade bakes, for your next morning’s fix. If you’re after something heartier, check out our guide to the best JB breakfast spots .
Address: Lot G.01, Paragon Market Place, 135, Jalan Tampoi, Kawasan Perindustrian Majidee, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 24 hours
Website
ST Rosyam Mart is halal-certified.
20 JB Breakfast Spots To Eat At The Next Time You Cross The Causeway Early
Photos taken by Nivian Chiang.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.
summary: ST Rosyam Mart is a 24-hour mart selling over 40,000 items, including wagyu steaks, king crabs and more!

body:
Best Food at Paya Lebar Square and PLQ Mall
With malls popping up one after another at Paya Lebar , you don’t even have to leave the comfort of the aircon to access some good food. As the newest and largest mall in the area, Paya Lebar Quarter (PLQ) has a whopping 160 F&B stores. Together, the Paya Lebar Square and PLQ food spots add up to a long, intimidating list.
If you suffer from serious indecision when it comes to what to eat, this list of the best food places at Paya Lebar Square and PLQ Mall will point you in the right direction.
What to eat at PLQ
From popular drink chains like Tomoro Coffee to trendy cafes and restaurants , this PLQ food guide will help you choose what to eat within the mall.
1. COLLIN’S
Image credit: COLLIN’S
For family-friendly meals that’ll please the crowd and not break the bank, pay a visit to COLLIN’S. The casual Western grill house’s menu features hearty Western staples and all-new fusion classics, as well as a specially curated wine menu. Start off the meal with their Garlic Prawns ($18++) , where tiger prawns are simmered in a rich seafood broth, served with freshly baked Sourdough bread. For mains, choose between pastas, seafood dishes, and their grilled meats, including their famed Signature Roasted BBQ Pork Ribs ($20++ for half a slab), starring fall-off-the-bone tender pork ribs brushed with a smoky barbecue sauce. Additionally, for the festive season, COLLIN’S is offering a discount of up to 50% on selected signature dishes, including Seafood Laksa ($16++) and Seafood Risotto ($19.90++) , from now till 30 November 2026 .
Unit number: #B1-01
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 10pm
Tel: 6970 2195
Website
COLLIN’S is not halal-certified.
2. Yakiniku Like
Enjoying Japanese yakiniku doesn’t always need to be a group activity or carry a hefty price tag. If you’re looking for affordable, quick, and solo dining at PLQ , Yakiniku Like has got you covered.
For the budget-conscious, I recommend getting their set meals, which start from under $10. Each meal comes with a protein of your choice, rice, soup, and a salad. While the set menu is value for money, check out their a la carte items for more premium meat options such as the Karubi 100g ($4.90) beef that is beautifully juicy and melty. If you’re a fan of barbecue but dislike the fuss, head to Yakiniku Like at PLQ for a speedy yakiniku fix!
Check out our Yakiniku Like review.
Unit number: #B1-28
Opening hours: Daily 11 am to 10pm
Website
Yakiniku Like is not halal-certified.
3 . NeNe Neko
NeNe Neko is a new addition to the PLQ restaurant scene that offers an all-day izakaya-style menu. You can find donburi and noodle dishes in the day, such as the Unagi Don ($20) and the Cold Truffle Somen ($28) . At night, indulge with your drinking buddies and choose from an assortment of kushiyaki, such as Mentaiko Yakitori ($3) , Bacon Asparagus ($5) and Minced Chicken Tsukune ($6) . Order some drinks to wash it all down—you can order a full 300ml bottle of Asahi Beer for $10 .
Read our NeNe Neko feature .
Unit number: #01-K7, PLQ Plaza, Level 1
Opening hours: Sun-Thurs 11am to 10pm, Fri-Sat 11am to 12am
Website
NeNe Neko is not halal-certified.
This New Japanese Cafe Has Mains Under $20++, Get Mentaiko Shokupan And Goma Latte Here
4. Tipsy Bird Gastrobar
Image credit: Tipsy Bird
At Tipsy Bird Gastrobar , expect live music entertainment next to your platter of juicy well-aged steaks or fancy chai tow kway, with cocktails on the side. This restaurant and bar serves up a selection of high-end Western fare such as Beef Tomahawk ($100++) and Lobster Bisque Ravioli ($24++) . Seafood lovers will be delighted to know that they offer Oysters for just $1.90 per piece on Tuesdays, with a minimum order of one dozen.
Also on the menu are elevated local favourites such as the Moonlight Truffle Beef Hor Fun ($26++) which is a dish perfumed with the aroma of truffle, and topped with slices of Wagyu striploin beef. They even have a lunch promo from 12pm to 3pm from $7.90++ , where you can pick a main and add a drink and side for $3 .
Unit number: #01-08
Opening hours: Mon-Sat 12pm to 1am, Sun 12pm to 11pm
Tel: 8879 6057
Website
Tipsy Bird Gastrobar is not halal-certified.
5. Fong Sheng Hao
Hailing from Taipei’s Shilin Market, Fong Sheng Hao has opened its first local outlet at Paya Lebar Quarter , bringing traditional Taiwanese breakfast food like charcoal-grilled toast to Singapore. Get a hearty breakfast fix with their toast sets, such as the popular Pork and Egg Cheese ($8.60) , which features a thick cut of minced pork patty and a generous helping of melty cheese, sandwiched between two pillowy slices of grilled milk toast.
If you’re just dropping by for drinks, try their Fong Sheng Signature Milk Tea ($6.50) which has a smooth, roasted black tea flavour. It’s only slightly sweetened to allow the tea’s aroma to shine through.
Read our Fong Sheng Hao review .
Unit number: #B2-04
Opening hours: Daily 7:30am to 9pm
Website

body:
Niko Niko Onigiri is a goldfish-themed cafe in JB
Animal cafes are all the rage, with cat cafes, dog cafes, and even alpaca cafes popping up. So when we heard of Niko Niko Onigiri in Johor Bahru, a goldfish-themed cafe serving Japanese rice balls, we had to check it out.
The cafe is popular among Gen Z and locals for its themed concept, made-to-order onigiri, and affordable pricing. However, since it’s a 20- to 30-minute drive from customs, we wanted to decide for ourselves if it’s worth the trip.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.31 as of 13 November 2026.
The space had a cute, Japanese-inspired aesthetic, with natural light filtering in, colourful mosaic tiles, and adorable goldfish and onigiri motifs throughout the cafe.
However, the standout was an entire wall with built-in aquariums filled with goldfish, keeping you company as you eat. It also doubles as a unique photo backdrop, perfect for your IG feed.
Moving on to the food, we got three of their signatures and two drinks: Avocado Salmon Onigiri (RM 6.90) , Beef Bacon & Egg (RM 5.50) , Fresh Salmon Ochazuke (RM 26.90) , Matcha Latte (RM 14.90) , and There’s Orange Beneath The Blue (RM 15.90).
The two onigiri were served on a cute rattan tray.
The Avocado Salmon Onigiri features mashed avocado and fresh salmon sashimi encased in rice and wrapped with sheets of seaweed. The creamy avocado paired nicely with the salmon’s natural sweetness, complementing its richness so it didn’t get too jelak.
The Beef Bacon & Egg comes with tamago salad and beef bacon. The beef bacon was slightly sweet and chewy, which paired well with the creamy, mayo-based tamago salad.
We did note that both onigiri fell apart rather easily, so be prepared to get messy if you order them.
Next, the Fresh Salmon Ochazuke features a bowl of rice topped with raw salmon slices, wasabi, and bonito flakes, served with hot green tea and a side of potato salad.
The dashi broth comes in a teapot, so you can pour it yourself for a warm, comforting dish perfect for rainy days.
It had a clean, delicate flavour, with the savoury, umami-rich dashi broth carrying a subtle sweetness. The salmon tasted fresh and had a pleasant, springy texture that paired well with the broth.
Our only gripe was the portion of salmon, as we would have preferred a few more slices or thicker cuts, considering the price.
Lastly, the drinks—given how popular matcha latte is, we had to give theirs a try. Meanwhile, There’s Orange Beneath The Blue is a lime soda layered over peach syrup, garnished with two Goldfish gummies.
The glasses were also amusingly on theme, decorated with the graphics of an onigiri marvelling at a goldfish.
The Matcha Latte was milky and slightly sweet, with a siap-siap mouthfeel followed by earthy matcha notes. It wasn’t overly bitter, making it a good choice for those who prefer a milder matcha flavour.
The lime soda tasted similar to Sprite, with the peach syrup adding extra fruity flavour and sweetness. The goldfish gummies were chewy and slightly sour, a fun addition to the drink.
Overall, Niko Niko Onigiri has a unique concept that’s just as well-executed. With its adorable graphics, goldfish wall, and affordable Japanese fare, it’s worth a visit if you’re a fan of cute, quirky cafes.
If you’re spending a full day or more in JB, here are some of the best Johor Bahru cafes within a 30-minute drive from customs, including a seaside cafe and more. And if you’ve thoroughly explored JB, check out this Melaka food itinerary for other cool food spots worth visiting in Malaysia.

Opening hours: Daily 9am to 8:30pm
Website
Niko Niko Onigiri is Muslim-friendly.

This was an independent feature by Eatbook.sg.
