Best dim sum in Singapore
Dim sum is always a good idea, not just for breakfast, lunch, or dinner , but also for afternoon tea or even a quick supper fix . That’s why we curated a list of the best dim sum places in Singapore , including dim sum buffets and halal dim sum that cater to every budget. Whether you’re broke or looking to splurge, our list has got your dim sum cravings covered.
1. 126 Dim Sum Wen Dao Shi
If you want dim sum for supper, chances are you’ll find yourself at 126 Dim Sum Wen Dao Shi . This late-night dining institution is famous for its wallet-friendly fare, ranging from steamed to fried yum cha classics, as well as congee and noodle dishes. Fan favourites here include the Shrimp Dumplings ($4.80) , AKA har gao, Ebiko Siew Mai ($5.30) , and their Fried Prawn Rolls ($6.20) .
Image credit: @thefluffypao
Seafood lovers should save some space for the Signature Crab Vermicelli , where wok-fried glass noodles are served with a whole crab for just $28 !
Both their Sims Avenue and Serangoon Road outlets feature comfortable air-conditioned dining areas with tables suitable for intimate gatherings or larger groups. Open past midnight on weekdays, 126 Dim Sum is an ideal dining pick, whether you’re satisfying a midday craving or looking for a post-clubbing supper spot.
Geylang outlet
Address: 126 Sims Avenue, Singapore 387449
Opening hours: Mon 12am to 5:30am, 11am to 12am, Tue-Thurs 11am to 5:30am, Fri 11am to 12am, Sat-Sun 24 hours
Boon Keng outlet
Address: 1086 Serangoon Road, Singapore 328187
Opening hours: Daily 5:30pm to 2:30am
Website
126 Dim Sum Wen Dao Shi is not halal-certified.
2. Ji Tuo Hong Kong Style Dim Sum
Image credit: Jas o n Ng
Tucked away in an industrial area, Ji Tuo Hong Kong Style Dim Sum has a rather small menu, with only 14 items to choose from. But that’s not to say their offerings aren’t worth a try; the Fried Carrot Cake is touted as soft on the inside and crispy on the outside, affordably priced at $3.50 for three . Other value-for-money items include the Beijing Style Dumplings ($3.50 for five) and Custard Buns ($3.50 for three) .

Tel: 8150 8784
Website

3. Xin Cuisine
Image credit: Xin Cuisine
Located at Holiday Inn Singapore Atrium is Xin Cuisine , an award-winning Chinese restaurant known for its contemporary takes on traditional Cantonese cuisine, including dim sum. Start your meal with familiar favourites such as the Barbecued Pork Buns ( $8.80++ for three) , Shrimp and Fish Roe Har Gao ($10.80++ for three) , and Custard Bun with Salted Egg Yolk ( $8.80++ for three) . Then, supplement these classics with their elevated counterparts: the Chicken Feet with Black Pepper Sauce ($7.80++ for one portion) , for instance, is unlike your traditional chicken feet with black bean sauce; the one at Xin Cusine is served dry with a rich, peppery sauce coating each piece.
Image credit: Xin Cuisine
Enjoy a selection of delicious dim sum and more on special occasions—get a complimentary “Shao Tao” Longevity Bun if you dine in on your birthday, or check out their stunning private dining rooms available for reservation if you prefer a more intimate setting.

Tel: 3138 2531
Website
Xin Cuisine is not halal-certified.
4. Hua Ji Bao Dang
Hua Ji Bao Dang doesn’t have the most extensive menu on this list, but that doesn’t mean their dim sum offerings are any less superb. Their renowned buns, such as the Red Bean Bao , Char Siew Bao , and Lotus Paste Bao , go for just $1.30 a pop. Other dim sum classics are really affordable as well—the Siew Mai ( $1.30 ) and Glutinous Rice ( $2.40) certainly won’t make a dent in your wallet, so try and see if it’s to your liking!
Check out our Hua Ji Bao Dang review .

Tel: 9675 1628

Hua Ji Bao Dang is not halal-certified.
5. Nian Nian Fa Dim Sum
The low prices belie the excellent dim sum at Nian Nian Fa Dim Sum, a hawker stall run by a former Hong Kong chef. Try their Turnip Cake ($1.50) and Shrimp Dumpling ($1.20 each) —the former has a strong radish fragrance made better by the house-made chilli, and for the latter, you can expect fresh and succulent diced prawn enveloped in a crispy wonton skin.

body:
Age.3, the Japanese fried sando shop that drew queues of up to two hours in Ginza, opens its first Singapore store at ION Orchard today, Friday 13 November 2026. Doors open at 10am, and the shop on the mall’s fourth basement level, at #B4-64/65, keeps ION’s hours of 10am to 10pm daily.
The draw is the bread. Age.3 takes a coarse-textured shokupan, dries it, then fries it, so the outside turns crisp while the inside stays soft and chewy. Each sando is fried when you order and filled by hand at the counter, from plain whipped cream to egg salad.
Where Age.3 comes from
The brand grew out of FRUITS SAND THREE, a fruit sandwich business set up in 2020 in Kama, a small city in Fukuoka. The fried sando came in 2023, and the first Age.3 shop opened in Ginza, Tokyo, that December. Japanese television picked it up, including Nippon TV’s ZIP! and TBS’s Lovit!.
Shops in Shanghai, Sydney, Manila and Dubai followed, then Bangkok and Hanoi in October 2026. Singapore makes it eight countries and regions, Japan included, in about three years. By June 2026, Age.3 had sold 580,000 fried sandos.
An Age.3 counter, pictured in the brand’s announcement of its Singapore opening. Image: Age.3 / ANCHOR
What is on the Singapore menu
The ION Orchard shop sells sweet and savoury sandos. The main items, under their Singapore names:
• Creme Brulee: a crackly caramelised top over smooth cream, the most popular item at every Age.3 shop in Japan and overseas
• Whipped Cream: fried bread and cream, nothing else
• Jam Strawberry: strawberry jam with whipped cream
• Chocolate Strawberry: strawberries with chocolate sauce
• Egg Salad: a generous filling of fluffy egg
• Beef Yakiniku + Egg: grilled beef in a sweet and savoury sauce with a soft-boiled egg
• Chicken Nanban: fried chicken with plenty of tartare sauce
Fillings can change with supply. Age.3 also swaps its fruit sandos with the seasons, and the range differs from shop to shop.
The Creme Brulee sando, Age.3’s most popular item, shown as served in Japan. Image: Age.3
Age.3’s head chef is Kohei Matsushita, a senior managing director of operator ANCHOR, who trained at Hotel Okura in Tokyo, Kyoto and Fukuoka. He and the Japan team went to Singapore ahead of the opening to train local staff, from frying the bread to finishing each sando.
Whipped Cream and Chocolate Strawberry sandos, shown as served in Japan. Image: Age.3
Getting there
Age.3 Singapore ION Orchard is at 2 Orchard Turn, #B4-64/65, Singapore 238801, on the B4 level of the mall, which sits next to Orchard MRT station (NS22/TE14). It is open daily from 10am to 10pm, with no rest day. Sandos are sold over the counter only, fried and filled fresh.
summary: Age.3, the Ginza fried sando shop, opens its first Singapore store at ION Orchard #B4-64/65 on Friday 13 November 2026 at 10am, with Creme Brulee, Egg Salad and Beef Yakiniku + Egg sandos fried to order, daily 10am to 10pm.
title: Age.3, Japan’s fried sando shop, opens its first Singapore store at ION Orchard on 13 November

Out with the old and in with the new — Tampines Mall has just completed its S$24 million Asset Enhancement Initiative (AEI). That’s essentially a revamp, and you can look forward to 21 new brands , refreshed retail spaces and upgraded facilities during your next visit. I believe more is more when it comes to a shopping mall, so these new shops will definitely give shoppers greater choice and a more rounded experience.
Credit – CapitaLand
Of the 21 brands introduced, 15 are new to the East. Additionally, with 14 beauty retail stores, Tampines Mall is now home to the biggest beauty cluster in the East. This includes well-known, premium brands and more accessible, everyday beauty names. The 8 new beauty brands are: CHANEL, DIOR, ELEMIS, Judydoll, Rituals, Sephora, SHISEIDO, and YSL Beauty. Besides the newbies on the block, the brands with refreshed looks are Bath & Body Works, Kiehl’s, L’Occitane, Laneige and The Body Shop.
Credit – CapitaLand
Beyond shopping until you drop, standalone boutiques on Level 1 offer distinctive personalised services . For example, SHISEIDO offers a personalised skin analysis for the best skincare and makeup recommendations.
A trip to Tampines Mall isn’t complete without having a meal; there are also 8 new F&B concepts . These dining spaces include Alchemist, Casa Vostra, Ging Sun Ho King of Bun, IM QALB by Pun Im, LONGJING, RUXU, YEAH Gelato and Charlie’s Tea. Don’t miss out on IM QALB’s Tampines Mall-exclusive menu. Plus, Charlie’s Tea’s Tampines Mall outlet is their first-ever in Singapore.
Credit – CapitaLand
Shop for a new wardrobe at 5 new fashion, sports and watch stores — Asics, Boarding Gate, Braun Buffel, Meileur Moment and CC Primos. Brands that have had a store makeover include Decathlon, Running Lab, Goldheart, SK Gold and Vincent Watch. Decathlon’s 18,000-square-foot store has more than 6,000 sporting essentials across over 60 different sports. You can try out various gear at dedicated test zones before committing to a purchase. Post-purchase services such as basic bicycle maintenance, racket restringing and re-gripping are also available.
I know where I’m heading this weekend, and I hope you do too!

body:
Designer furniture in Singapore
Most of us spend the workday parked on a chair, elbows on a desk, under a lamp we never think twice about. But some designer furniture in Singapore offices, cafes, and hotel lobbies comes with better stories than office gossip.
Equate , a homegrown commercial furniture company founded by 3 industry veterans, invites you to dig into these pieces from their range. Featuring a chair made of plastic bottles and a table folded from a single 1mm sheet of steel, plus where to see them all in person.
1. Arper Catifa 53
The chair inspired by a carpet caught in the wind
Image credit: Equate
Arper Catifa 53 is one of the most recognisable chairs in modern offices. Designed in 2001 by Spanish studio Lievore Altherr Molina, Catifa 53 is the most iconic product in Arper’s catalogue.
The idea was simple: a single wavy shell that supports your body. Designer Alberto Lievore compared it to a carpet blowing in the wind, just starting to curl up and take off. It proved so popular that it has since grown into a whole family of collections.
2. Arper Kata
The cosy lounge chair made from old plastic bottles
Image adapted from: Equate
Kata looks like the wood-and-woven-straw armchair at your grandparents’ place. Look closer, and the woven part is actually a 3D-knitted fabric made from recycled plastic bottles.
The yarn is spun from post-consumer plastic waste, producing 1kg of yarn for every 1kg of PET waste. The 3D-knitting method also cuts production waste by 30-50%. It was designed by Barcelona studio Altherr Désile Park and launched in 2021 as Arper’s first solid wood lounge chair.
3. Arper Juno 02
The plastic chair that’s 70% recycled
Image credit: @hello_equate via Instagram
Plastic chairs get a bad rap, but Juno 02 is out to change that. The slim, stackable chair was first designed by British designer James Irvine in 2012, and Studio Irvine gave it a refresh in 2022.
The new version is made from 70% recycled plastic from industrial waste. The mould was also redesigned so each chair uses less material without losing strength. It comes in 6 colours and works indoors and outdoors, which makes it handy for everything from offices to restaurants.
4. Arper Onemm
The table folded from a single 1mm sheet of steel
Image credit: @hello_equate via Instagram
The name says it all. Onemm’s tabletop is made from one sheet of steel just 1mm thick, folded like origami into a slim but sturdy table.
Swiss architect Peter Kunz designed it in 2022, taking inspiration from the monocoque technique used in Formula 1 cars. The whole table is made of just 5 parts that can be put together without tools and taken apart for recycling at the end of its life.
5. Lumina Daphine lamp
The desk lamp that started a whole company
Image credit: @lumina_italia via Instagram
That slim, bendy desk lamp you’ve probably spotted in design-savvy offices just turned 50. Tommaso Cimini, a mechanical engineering whiz, built the first Daphine prototype in 1975 in a small workshop near Milan, using machines he had modified himself.
His design rule was lots of light, not much lamp. The lamp did so well that he founded the lighting company Lumina in 1980 on the back of it. To mark the 50th birthday, Lumina released special editions in green, orange and mustard, colours taken from the 1970s.
Where to see these designer office furniture pieces in Singapore?
Try them out at Equate’s Kallang Bahru showroom
Image credit: @hello_equate via Instagram
Furniture is one of those things you need to sit on, lean on and fiddle with before you commit, especially when you’re kitting out a whole office or a new F&B spot. Equate’s showroom in Kallang Bahru puts these pieces in one place, so you can test the chairs and tables for yourself.
The team handles the whole process, from helping you pick the furniture to shipping, delivery, and installation. That’s handy if you’re setting up a new space and don’t want to juggle a different supplier for every item.
Your office furniture can have interesting stories too
The next time you sink into a meeting room chair or flick on a desk lamp, take a second to look at it. There’s a good chance it has a better backstory than your last team-building session.
And if you’re planning an office refresh or opening a new F&B spot, swing by Equate in Kallang Bahru to see these pieces in person before you commit.
Browse Equate’s full furniture collection
Address: 219 Kallang Bahru, #03-01, Singapore 339348
Contact: Equate Furniture Instagram | Equate Furniture Facebook

body:
The Ultimate Holiday Playdate at Suntec City
We’ve still got a little over a month left before Christmas officially hits, but take a look around, and you’ll realise that the jingle bells are tolling ahead of time. Malls all over the Little Red Dot are already wreathed in gold and green, and Suntec City is no exception, as they celebrate merry moments with The Ultimate Holiday Playdate .
With the help of The Powerpuff Girls and We Bare Bears , they’ve transformed the mall into an oversized playground that promises much holiday cheer; best of all, it’s even free to enter. Here’s all you need to know about the family-friendly affair, from fun installations to character meet & greets and themed goodies.
What is Suntec City’s The Ultimate Holiday Playdate?
Suntec City’s The Ultimate Holiday Playdate is a mall-wide event that runs from now till 27th December 2026 . At the heart of the festivities is the A Beary Fun Playdate installation, which can be found at Suntec City’s North Atrium, Tower 1 and 2, Level 1. Open from 11am to 9.30pm daily , 2 giant inflatable play zones await, along with a thrilling floor is lava game, carnival game booths, and a retail area.
Admission to A Beary Fun Playdate is free . However, entry is exclusive to Suntec+ Members ; you can sign up as one for free by downloading the Suntec+ app ( App Store | Google Play ). Each account admits up to 2 children and 1 parent , and the play zones here are suitable for little ones aged 4 to 12 who are at least 100cm tall .
Each time slot grants 30 minutes of play at the Mega Claw Machine and Super Slide, while those at the Lava Arena run for 20 minutes . Simply make your way to the registration counter to redeem your time slots, and you’re good to go.
What to expect at Suntec City’s The Ultimate Holiday Playdate?
If you don’t already know, Suntec City does not pull any punches when it comes to putting together grand holiday activations, and this year’s no different.
View this post on Instagram
For The Ultimate Holiday Playdate, they’ve decided to tap into the charm of the crime-fighting trio that is The Powerpuff Girls and the band of furry brothers from We Bare Bears ; iconic animated series that are bound to resonate with the young and old alike. But it’s the children who’re coming out on top here, as the mall will be packed with kid-friendly attractions that’ll have them squealing in delight, for instance:
Mega Claw Machine, Super Slide & Lava Arena
Families heading to Suntec City during the festive season with kids in tow, you’ll want to make a beeline for A Beary Fun Playdate. Found on Level 1 of the mall’s North Atrium, what stands out immediately is the event space’s 2 massive inflatable play spaces: the Mega Claw Machine and Super Slide .
Themed after the arcade staple, the Mega Claw Machine is essentially a ball pit filled with oversized balls where the kids can let loose and toss them around, while imagining themselves as the prizes within.
Right next door is the Super Slide, and like its name suggests, it’s a giant inflatable slide that young’uns can whoosh down. But they’ll have to work for it though, as they’ll have to scale a small wall before reaching the apex. Don’t forget to strike a pose with Grizzly first, as he’s all decked out in a new getup for the occasion, but do watch your step as the slope leading up to the top is especially slippery.
Another main attraction of A Beary Fun Playdate is the Lava Arena . It’s one of those Floor is Lava -esque games that have been getting popular as of late, which surprisingly requires a decent level of athleticism to clear. There are a whole host of levels that get progressively harder, but the premise remains the same – step on the green tiles and avoid the red ones.
Carnival games, claw machines, photo booth & retail area
Once the rowdy little ones have had their fun at the inflatables, head over to the carnival game booths nearby to try your hand at winning PPG and We Bare Bears-themed prizes . Games here cost 5 tokens a pop, and you can convert tokens at the following rates:
• $10: 5 tokens
• $20: 10 tokens
• $50: 30 tokens
• $120: 75 tokens + exclusive pin mat
If you’ve noticed, an additional event-exclusive pin mat will be given as a freebie when you spend $120 on tokens. As for filling it up, special PPG and We Bare Bear pins are up for grabs as consolation prizes at the various game booths here, so you’ll definitely be walking home with a memento when you have a go at them.
Speaking of, there are 4 different game booths to hit up. At Cyclone Rescue , you’ll have to stick your hand into a transparent sphere and grab little gachapon capsules as they fly about. You’ll then be awarded points based on what’s inside them; rack up at least 12 points, and you can win a small prize.
…
summary: Christmas is starting a little earlier this year.
title: Suntec City Has A Powerpuff Girls x We Bare Bears Makeover With Fun Play Zones & Meet & Greets

body:
Craft workshops & activities in Singapore
If one of your new year’s resolutions is to try something new, you might’ve considered picking up a cool hobby with a friend. Well, what about getting chaotically creative with balloon splatter paintings? Or reduce wastage by turning used eggshells into coasters?
We’ve rounded up a list of 12 unique craft activities you can dip your toes – or fingers – into this year. Try them out and who knows? You might just find something that intrigues you.
1. Paper-making workshop at Print N Matters
Make unlimited sheets of handmade paper & get a $5 store vouchers
Image credit: Print N Matters
Writing cards to your besties may be your love language – but get this, instead of purchasing coloured paper for your cards, why not make your own? At Print N Matters , you can learn to make paper from scratch and customise its colour and design.
The process involves using paper pulp from unused scraps of paper – then, you can try mixing your own colour combination, adding pressed leaves, or sprinkling bits of flowers. There’s no limit to how many sheets of paper you can make within the hour-long workshop, so let your creativity shine through and don’t hold back.
Image credit: @printnmatters
Besides taking home a stack of unique handmade paper, you’ll also get a $5 store voucher. You can use it to purchase paper made by the experienced staff, notebooks, or stickers from the Print N Matters store.
Book a paper making workshop session at Print N Matters .
Rate: $38/pax
Address: 3011 Bedok Industrial Park E, #03-2014, Singapore 489977
Operating hours: 10am-6pm, Daily
Contact: 8800 3563 | Print N Matters website
2. Balloon splatter painting workshopat Art Pop Studio
Pop balloons to make art
It’s a creative way to blow off some steam as you fling darts at the balloons filled with paint.
Image credit: @artpop. sg
If you watched the first The Princess Diaries movie, you’ll remember a scene where Mia did balloon splatter art with her mum. Well, you can do that irl and be the main character at Art Pop Studio . Throw darts at paint-filled balloons attached to a canvas and watch the colours explode on it.
Before you enter the splash zone, instructors will share some art techniques like colour-mixing and layering. With the knowledge gained, you won’t be as clueless about the process and will have more ways to spice up your masterpiece.
Image credit: @ nadiahartista
If you have kids aged 5 years or older, bring them along to have some family fun. For once, they can have their fun and make a mess without you having to worry about cleaning it up. As darts are involved, parental supervision is strongly encouraged.
The paint will need a few days to dry – you can come back and pick it up or have it delivered at an additional fee. The balloon splatter workshop can also be booked with your SG Culture Pass credits .
Rates: $83-85/pax
Group rates : $85/pax for groups of 1-3 | $83/pax for groups of 4 or more
Address: 3007 Ubi Road 1, #06-446, Singapore 408701
Opening hours : Wed-Fri 11am-7pm | Sat-Sun 11am-5pm (Closed on Mondays & Tuesdays)
Contact: 9663 6864 | Art Pop website
3. Beeswax wrap workshop at The Sustainability Project
Make 2-3 reusable food wraps in 45 minutes, in-studio or online
Have some fun while reducing your impact on the environment.
Image credit: @thesustainabilityproject_
If you bake or cook at home, you probably tend to use lots of plastic cling wrap. A more sustainable option is to replace them with reusable beeswax wraps . Instead of buying one, consider making your very own and find out what goes into making one with The Sustainability Project .
In this 45-minute workshop, you’ll get to make 2-3 beeswax wraps that can last 6 months each. The best part is that they are non-toxic and reusable, perfect for wrapping your food.
You get to pick out your desired design for your handmade beeswax wrap.
Image credit: The Sustainability Project
Both physical and virtual workshops are available, so even couch potatoes can take up this hobby from home. Materials will be provided for both – all you need to bring is an open mind and eagerness to learn.
Book a beeswax wrap-making workshop .
Rates:
Virtual workshop: $45/pax
Physical workshop: $50/pax | $87.50/2 pax
Address: 21 Bukit Batok Crescent, #06-78 WCEGA Tower, Singapore 658065
Opening hours: Mon-Wed & Fri 11am-6.30pm | Sat-Sun 11am-4pm (Closed on Thursdays)
Contact: 8316 0845 | The Sustainability Project website
4. Ukulele painting workshop at SmallGiant Music
Paint your own ukulele & learn to play a tune in 3 hours
Image credit: @smallgiant.musicsg
If your New Year’s resolution is to pick up a new instrument, consider Ukulele Paint & Play at SmallGiant Music Singapore . You get to flex 2 talents here – learn the basics of playing the ukulele and painting it to reflect your personality.
…
summary: If your new year resolution is to try something new, consider trying out these craft workshops and activities with loved ones.
title: 12 Unique Craft Workshops & Activities In Singapore From $28/Pax If You Need A New Hobby

body:
This place had been sitting on my must-try list for quite some time, though I never quite managed to drop by due to the long queues. The crowd hasn’t let up even after months of buzz, and for good reason, it seems.
So, after hearing fellow foodies sing its praises for nearly a year, I decided to start my morning a little earlier than usual to finally experience what makes DONKAI such a darling among Malaysians .
Those expecting a calm, candlelit setting may want to look elsewhere. DONKAI’s charm lies in its casual, energetic atmosphere. Think narrow stools lined up along an open kitchen, much like the snug izakayas peppered throughout Tokyo ’s backstreets.
From your seat, you can watch the chefs prepare the hamburg patties, which are served sizzling on individual hot plates at 50% or 70% doneness — left to you to finish cooking to your liking.
The menu is expectedly limited. You’ll choose between an Angus beef or A5 Wagyu beef hamburg rice bowl , both served with a pasteurised egg yolk , unlimited refills of vegetables , and a comforting bowl of miso soup steeped with mushrooms and konbu . There are a few side offerings too like chicken karaage and ebi tempura .
What I tried at DONKAI
Truthfully, walking into DONKAI for the first time was a little disorienting. There’s no clear guide on how to order or what to expect except for a single deliberate sheet, and the stuffy and loud atmosphere doesn’t exactly lend itself to asking too many questions. It’s the kind of place where you learn by watching. A glance around at how seasoned diners navigate their trays and hot plates can be more helpful than anything you’ll hear.
For my order, I went with what seemed like the safest bet, or perhaps the most budget-friendly: the Angus Beef Hamburg (RM34) , paired with a side of Truffle Sauce (RM5) . Once it landed on my personal hot plate, the server politely asked if I wanted the patty sliced up. I said yes, and from there, the rest was a hands-on affair.
I gave the beef a bit more time to sizzle alongside the broccoli and carrots, then transferred everything into the bowl of short-grain rice. On the side, a condiment tray featuring an eclectic mix of chilli sauce, a Thousand Island-esque mayo, soy sauce, black pepper, red chilli flakes, and kimchi awaited. I also couldn’t resist adding a stick of A5 Wagyu Skewer (RM22) , just to see what the fuss was about.
10 best Japanese restaurants in JB [Sep 2026]
The Angus beef on its own was well-seasoned, but once dipped into that truffle sauce, it became something else entirely. The sauce had the creamy tang of a bold tartar, laced with the punch of black pepper and earthy mushroom.
The rice, once mixed with the molten egg yolk and a generous spoonful of truffle sauce, was rich, comforting, and deeply satisfying. Surprisingly, the kimchi was above average, giving a clean, well-balanced bite that cut beautifully through the richness of the dish without overpowering it.
As for the wagyu skewer, it was pleasant, but not especially memorable. It melted away so quickly on the tongue that it barely registered — a wisp of umami before disappearing altogether. A luxurious bite, perhaps, but one that left me wanting something a little more tangible.
If you’re planning a visit to DONKAI, let me gently nudge you toward the Japanese Wagyu Beef Hamburg (RM44) — an upgrade well worth the few extra ringgit. Compared to the Angus patty I had earlier, the difference was night and day. If I may create a metaphor: it felt like comparing my best scribbles to Shakespeare’s sonnets.
Even though my dining partner accidentally left it on the hot plate a little too long which resulted in some crispy edges, the patty still managed to taste heavenly. It melted effortlessly on the tongue, each bite rich with umami and luxurious fattiness. Remarkably, it didn’t need any condiment to make it better.
Final thoughts
Given that my main meal was the Angus Beef Hamburg rather than the Japanese Wagyu , I can see why some diners might find DONKAI a little underwhelming. The Angus option, while decent, may feel a tad mediocre to those expecting something more life-changing, especially considering the portion-to-price ratio.
That said, the wagyu is where DONKAI truly shines. If you’re not an ardent beef lover, this spot may not be for you. But if you are, and you’re willing to splurge a little, go for the wagyu . That’s where the magic happens. You can thank me later.
People also read:
What to eat at Ombak KLCC?
Where to go for yummy Mediterranean food in PJ?
summary: DONKAI serves Japanese-style beef hamburg rice bowls in a casual, open-kitchen setting, with Angus and A5 Wagyu patties cooked on individual hot plates. Priced from RM34, each set includes egg yolk, unlimited vegetable refills and miso soup, making it suited to beef lovers willing to spend more for the richer Wagyu option, though queues and a lively, cramped dining space may be less appealing to some.
title: DONKAI: Halal-certified Angus & A5 Wagyu Hamburg on sizzling hot plates — overrated hype or splurge-worthy?

body:
Attention Westies! 505 Jurong West Market & Food Centre has just welcomed a new Korean addition to its hawkers. In the sea of stalls serving up traditional local fare, Busan Pork Soup ‘s unmistakable red signage stands out immediately. At the time of writing, Busan Pork Soup has yet to even be added to Google Maps, so we’ve got the full lowdown for you right here.
Credit – Busan Pork Soup via IG
As per the name, Busan Pork Soup specialises in Korean pork soup, otherwise known as dwaeji-gukbap . The stall is from the same team behind OMMA Chicken Soup, which operates multiple outlets islandwide. Similar to their sister brand, the soup recipes served at Busan Pork Soup are crafted by the same 2 chefs who formerly worked in a Michelin-starred Korean restaurant before bringing their signature Korean fare to the Singaporean hawker scene.
The menu centres around unbelievably tender pork slices and their signature 10-hour slow-simmered broth. No MSG is added to the broth, so all the rich and savoury flavours are extracted solely from the pork itself.
Each bowl comes in 3 sizes, with varying amounts of pork slices. Small gets you 3 slices, while medium gets 4 and large gets 5.
Credit – Busan Pork Soup
Menu highlights include their bestselling Tomato Busan (S$6.90 for small) , which comes with 3 slices of melt-in-your-mouth pork and steaming-hot savoury tomato and pork broth.
For kimchi lovers, order the Kimchi Busan (S$7.30 for small) to hit that spicy-sour craving. If you prefer something on the milder side, go for the Collagen Busan (S$6.50 for small) for a comforting, milky-white broth.
Sides and add-ons like Kimchi (S$1.50) , Short Grain Rice (S$0.80) and Quail Egg (S$1.50) are also available amongst others.
If you’re looking to get your soupy Korean fix, consider supporting this brand-new stall down in Jurong!
Ex-Michelin star restaurant chefs sell Korean samgyetang from $6.80 at hawker stalls
summary: Busan Pork Soup is a new hawker stall at 505 Jurong West Market & Food Centre specialising in Korean pork soup (dwaeji-gukbap) created by former Michelin-starred restaurant chefs. The stall serves MSG-free, 10-hour slow-simmered broths in varieties like Tomato, Kimchi, and Collagen starting from S$6.50, alongside sides from S$0.80. It is best suited for diners in western Singapore seeking affordable, authentic Korean comfort food at a hawker centre.
title: Busan Pork Soup – New ex-Michelin chef hawker stall has $6.50 broth bowls

body:
Christmas Vinterland at IKEA
If your dream European Christmas market vacay involves a 13-hour flight and a winter jacket you’ll wear exactly once, here’s a version much closer to home, and only requires a trip to Tampines.
IKEA Singapore is holding its first-ever Christmas market at IKEA Tampines as part of Christmas Vinterland , a festive takeover that will happen on 3 weekends in December: 4th to 6th , 11th to 13th , and 18th to 20th December 2026 .
Think: a massive Christmas tree, 20+ homegrown vendors, “snowfall”, and a Swedish Christmas buffet. While IKEA Tampines is the main event, IKEA Alexandra and IKEA Jurong are getting their own activities too. Here’s everything you can look forward to:
Christmas market with 20+ homegrown brands
Image credit: IKEA
Christmas Vinterland is set to transform Level 3 of IKEA Tampines into a Christmas market – the brand’s first-ever in Singapore – with more than 20 homegrown brands setting up shop.
These include children’s clothing brand Sea Apple alongside The Toy Folks , The Weekend Florists , and The Everyday Club .
On the F&B side, you can look forward to bites and drinks from 1925 Brewing Co. , Dapiku Sweets , and even Le Matin Patisserie .
Do note that some vendors are only popping up on selected weekends:
• The Cheese Shop : 4th to 6th, 11th to 13th December
• Sake Street : 18th to 20th December
P.S. IKEA Family members can enjoy special deals from selected vendors on the first weekend!
“Snowfall” at Level 1 store entrance
Image credit: IKEA
There’s no Christmas like a white Christmas, and IKEA Tampines is bringing this to life with a “snowfall” experience that will take place at the store’s Level 1 outdoor store entrance .
This will run from 6pm to 8.45pm on 4th to 6th December , as well as 11th to 13th December , and everyone’s invited.
Each session is 15 minutes long , and takes place every half hour.
Christmas movie screenings, sticker trail & Santa’s cabin
Image credit: IKEA
To really get you into the mood, IKEA Tampines is running weekend Christmas movie screenings from 1pm to 3.30pm .
These are only screening on Saturdays and Sundays at Level 4 in the Living Room set, on a first-come, first-served basis. Children need to be accompanied by a parent or guardian at all times.
Image credit: IKEA
Kids aged 5 to 12 can also join the Vinterland Sticker Trail to collect 8 limited-edition “Vinter pals” stickers, from 1pm to 9pm on all 3 market weekends, except on 4th December, when it runs from 5pm to 9pm.
Each child gets one sticker per visit, and different designs are given out on different dates. Stickers are available while stocks last.
There’ll even be a Santa’s cabin set up across all 3 IKEA stores, and Santa meet-and-greets at selected stores and times. Check out the IKEA Christmas page for more details.
Kids’ Christmas workshops & gingerbread cookie party
Image credit: IKEA
That’s not all – IKEA has also organised Christmas craft workshops for kids aged 4 to 12, where they can make snow globes , candy jars , or even snowflake decorations with IKEA products.
Alternatively, check out the Joyful Cookie Party , where kids can decorate their own VINTERSAGA gingerbread cookies with icing, candies, and jellies.
Slots for these workshops are limited, and you’ll have to register to join via the IKEA Christmas page . Here’s where and when these workshops will be held:

Julbord is a traditional Swedish Christmas buffet, and you don’t have to fly to the Nordic country to get your fill of this feast, because IKEA is organising one right here for IKEA Family members.
There’s beef goulash, Swedish meatballs – of course – and salmon with Hollandaise sauce, plus smoked salmon starters, mushroom cream soup, even cinnamon buns and Belgian chocolate log cake to look forward to.
This buffet is happening on 11th December at IKEA Alexandra and 18th December at IKEA Tampines .
It’s priced at $29.90 for adults and $15.90 for kids aged 5 to 12 , and you’ll have to get your tickets at the Swedish Restaurant counter, available from 12th November at Alexandra and 17th November at Tampines.

Pinduoduo Singapore guide
If there’s one thing Singaporeans love, it’s scoring a good bargain, whether it’s hunting down cheap household essentials on Shopee or spending hours scrolling through Taobao .
Enter Pinduoduo (拼多多) , an online shopping platform where you can snag everything from phone cases to home decor at wallet-friendly prices. And here’s the cherry on top: eligible items come with free shipping to Singapore , even without a minimum spend.
So, if you’re curious about giving the app a shot but aren’t sure where to start, we’ve put together a beginner’s guide to Pinduoduo, including how to download the app, navigate its Chinese interface, swap it to English, and avoid dodgy sellers.
What is Pinduoduo & why is everyone talking about the app?
Image credit: InvestorPlace
For those unfamiliar, Pinduoduo is a Chinese e-commerce platform launched in 2015 and operated by PDD Holdings, the same company behind Temu. Like Taobao, it offers a huge variety of products, from clothing and beauty accessories to homeware and everyday necessities.
Pinduoduo initially made a name for itself through its group-buying feature, which allowed shoppers to enjoy discounts when purchasing items together. However, this feature is no longer consistently visible on the updated app, and some listings display the same prices regardless of whether you’re buying individually or as part of a group.
The good news is that you can still find plenty of affordable products without having to rope your friends into a group purchase. Eligible products can be shipped to Singapore for free, even if you’re buying just a single item; previously, shoppers had to meet a minimum spend of ¥99 (~S$19).
How to download Pinduoduo in Singapore on iPhone & Android
Screenshot from: App Store
For iPhone users , it’s fairly straightforward. Simply search for Pinduoduo or 拼多多 on the App Store and install the app.
Android users have a little more to consider. Pinduoduo was suspended from Google Play in March 2023 following malware-related security concerns involving certain versions of the app.
While APK files may be available through Pinduoduo’s official website, installing apps outside Google Play can expose your device to additional security risks. We’d recommend exercising caution and avoiding downloads from unfamiliar third-party websites.
How to switch Pinduoduo to English
Screenshots from: Pinduoduo
One thing that might put many Singaporeans off Pinduoduo is its predominantly Chinese interface. Thankfully, an English-language mode has been added to the app, although certain product descriptions and menu options may still appear in Chinese.
Here’s how to find it:
• Update Pinduoduo to the latest version.
• Open your profile, or 个人中心 , at the bottom-right corner.
• Tap 设置 (Settings) at the top-right corner.
• Look for 国家与地区/语言 (Country/Region and Language) .
• Select Singapore and English.
• Reopen the app if the changes don’t appear immediately.
That said, if you’re looking for something very specific, we’d still recommend searching in Chinese, as you may get more relevant results.
Another handy trick is to use Google Lens or your phone’s translation feature to decipher product descriptions, customer reviews, and unfamiliar menu options.
How to shop on Pinduoduo in Chinese & ship to Singapore?
Step 1: Create an account
First, register for an account using your Singapore mobile number (+65). You’ll receive an SMS verification code to confirm your registration.
Alternatively, you can sign in using your WeChat account if you have one.
Step 2: Add your delivery address
Image credit: blog.csdn.net
After creating your account, you’ll be able to find 收货地址 (Delivery Address) where you can enter details, including your name, Singapore phone number, postal code, and full delivery address.
Make sure you’ve selected Singapore as your delivery destination so that the app can display the relevant shipping options.
Step 3: Search for products
Screenshot from: Pinduoduo
With your account set up, you’re ready to start browsing. You can type relevant Chinese keywords into the search bar at the top of the homepage, or tap the camera icon to search using an uploaded photo.
Our advice: don’t jump on the first listing you see. Compare a few sellers, check the product specifications, and read customer reviews before making your purchase.
Step 4: Select your item
Screenshot from: Pinduoduo
If you’ve found something you fancy, tap on the listing and select your preferred colour, size, or product variation. Pay close attention to the options before checking out, especially if you’re shopping for clothing or accessories with multiple designs.
Step 5: Pay for your order
Screenshot from: Pinduoduo
Once you’ve selected your item, tap 提交订单 (Place Order) to proceed to checkout.
Select from the payment methods available to your account, which may include card payments or supported Chinese payment services.
…
summary: Here’s your beginner’s guide to shopping on Pinduoduo in Singapore.
title: Guide To Pinduoduo, The Up-And-Coming Chinese Shopping App That’s Cheap & Also Ships To Singapore

视野Live – Free 3D concert seat map
With an exciting lineup of upcoming concerts in Singapore , there’s no better time to start planning for your next gig. But while scoring tickets to your favourite artist’s show is already a challenge, choosing the right seats can be just as stressful. After all, nobody wants to spend hundreds of dollars on tickets, only to end up with a blocked view or a stage that looks miles away.
Thankfully, there’s a free 3D concert seat map that lets you preview the view from your chosen seat before buying tickets. Covering major concert venues across the world, including 8 venues in Singapore, 视野Live is a handy tool that could help you snag the best possible view at your next concert without leaving things to chance.
What can I do through this map?
Preview your concert seat view at 8 Singapore venues
Singapore Indoor Stadium.
Image credit: Trip.com
If you’ve ever found yourself frantically comparing seating plans before a concert ticket sale, the 视野Live website might just become your new best friend. The interactive 3D concert seat map allows you to explore different seating positions and see what the stage could look like from your preferred spot.
The website currently features 311 venues across 19 countries , including but not limited to China , Thailand , Malaysia , Japan , Australia , France , Italy , and the United States . This makes it especially handy for concertgoers who are planning to catch their favourite artists overseas.
Image adapted from: Capitol Theatre, Tripadvisor, Ticketmaster SG
For those attending concerts in Singapore, the platform features 8 local venues , including the Singapore National Stadium , Singapore Indoor Stadium , Starry Sky Performing Arts Center , Mediacorp Theatre , Singapore Arena @ Expo , Capitol Theatre , Sands Grand Ballroom , and OCBC Arena Hall 1 .
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
Simply select your preferred concert venue from the website’s directory to get started.
Select your seat to see the stage from your perspective
The website’s default language is Chinese. So before you start, toggle the top-right button to switch the interface to English.
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
Once you’ve chosen a venue, you’ll be presented with an interactive seating map. From there, you can click on the section and specific seat you’re considering to get a preview of your concert view.
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
The best part is, you can even choose the exact upcoming concert you are going for since some artists have different stage set-ups from the standard set-up.
View from selected seat in section 2 12 .
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
The website’s Audience Perspective feature then generates a simulated view of the stage from your selected seat. This gives you a better idea of how far you’ll be from the performance area and what your viewing angle might look like.
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
Beyond the 3D simulation, the website also features actual concert photos taken by other attendees from the same seats or nearby seating positions. You can compare these real-life images with the simulated perspective to get a more realistic idea of what to expect.
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
If you’re unable to select a particular seat directly on the map, there’s also a Choose A Location feature. Simply select your preferred seating section, then manually enter the row and seat number to preview the view.
See what your concert photos might look like with up to 30x zoom
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
For those who love recording concert fancams, the website has another nifty feature worth checking out. Its Mobile Phone Viewfinder lets you simulate what the stage might look like through your phone’s camera from your selected seat.
You can even toggle between different zoom levels, ranging from 1x to 30x zoom , to see how much closer your favourite artist might appear on your phone screen.
Horizontal view.
Screenshot from: shijiao.xingpaste
You can even choose whether you want the view on your phone to be vertical or horizontal, allowing multiple different simulations.
This is particularly useful if you’re planning to get seats further away from the stage but still want to capture decent videos and photos of the performance.
Of course, the actual results will depend on your phone’s camera capabilities, but the simulation provides a helpful reference before you decide on your seats.
Check your concert seat view on 视野Live before buying tickets
With concert tickets often costing a pretty penny, it’s worth doing a little research before deciding where to sit. This free 3D concert seat map on 视野Live makes it easier to compare seating options, explore different viewing angles, and get a better sense of what to expect on concert day.
Plus, with hundreds of venues around the world covered, it’s a useful tool to bookmark for your next concert, especially if you’re travelling overseas to catch an artist who isn’t stopping by Singapore.
…
summary: Use this handy tool before splurging on concert tickets.
title: This Free 3D Seat Map Shows Your Exact View At 8 Concert Venues In SG, Plus A Phone Camera Perspective

Best food places to use CDC Vouchers
With over 24,000 local establishments accepting CDC Vouchers as of June 2026, you’re spoiled for choice when it comes to deciding where to makan. But don’t worry, we’ve curated a bunch of the best food places for you, be it cafes, restaurants, fruit stalls, or bakeries to spend your SG60 and CDC Vouchers. There’s something on this list for every tastebud.
Cafes
1. Hello Arigato
Hello Arigato is best known for its stacked Japanese-inspired sando, including the crowd-favourite Gyu Sando ($28++) , which stars a thick slab of beef tenderloin katsu and house-made caramelised onion jam. The Pork Katsu Sando ($24++) is another hearty pick that’s equally satisfying. Wash it all down with their Strawberry Matcha Cloud ($6.50++) , a light and refreshing drink that hits the spot on a sweltering day.
They’ve got five outlets in Singapore, but to use your CDC Vouchers, head to the Everton Park , Joo Chiat , and Tiong Bahru ones.
Read our Hello Arigato feature .

Hello Arigato Opens In Tiong Bahru With Orh Nee Coffee, Cai Poh Egg Sando And More
2. Bag Me Up Bagel House
Bag Me Up Bagel House has quickly become a neighbourhood favourite since opening in Everton Park in late 2022, drawing crowds with their house-made bagels. Their menu features eight different bagels: four signature creations (from $10.50) and four lighter options ($6.50) for smaller appetites.
Top picks include the cheekily named Can’t Trust Chick ($14.50) , stuffed with grilled teriyaki chicken, sautéed mushrooms, truffle schmear, and melty mozzarella, and the breakfast-inspired Brekkie ($12.50) , layered with caramelised beef bacon, scrambled eggs, torched cheddar, pickles, and their house sauce. Pair your bagel with one of their protein smoothies ($11.90) for a satisfying meal that’ll fuel your day.
Read our Bag Me Up Bagel House review .
Address: 2 Everton Park, #01-59B, Singapore 081002
Opening hours: Tue, Sat-Sun 9am to 3pm, Wed-Fri 9:30am to 3pm
Website
Bag Me Up is not halal-certified.
Bag Me Up Review: Unagi And Wagyu Beef Bagels At This Under HDB Bagel Shop Near Outram Park
3. Cafe Fufu
Tucked away under an HDB block in Redhill, Cafe Fufu isn’t just your usual minimalist brunch spot—it’s actually a wood-fired pizzeria. There are plenty of options on the menu, but if you need a recommendation, try their signature Pizza Fufu ($20+ for personal, $30+ for sharing) . It swaps out the usual tomato base for a fragrant coriander pesto, and comes topped with fresh tiger prawns, semi-dried tomatoes, and a dusting of chilli flakes for a subtle kick.
Read our Cafe Fufu feature .

4. Dearborn
Image: @dearborn.granola
Dearborn has only a few items on their menu—and that’s how you know they’re doing it well. This quiet little granola cafe tucked away in Everton Park whips up granola bowls (from $7) , served with your choice of dairy-free Raglan Coconut Vanilla Bean Yogurt , Delta Greek Yogurt, or Oatside Oat Milk. Flavours rotate between classics such as Strawberry Macadamia , Dark Chocolate Hazelnut Sea Salt , and a flavour of the day.
If you’re not feeling like a bowl, their house-made Sourdough with Dearborn butter (from $5) is worth a try too, with options including country or smoked cheddar and chilli. Swing by on a Saturday for a slightly expanded menu with off-menu specials.
Address: 1 Everton Park, #01-29, Singapore 081001

Website

5. Cafe Wabi Sabi
Another gem in Everton Park is Cafe Wabi Sabi , a cosy Japanese cafe that’s just a 10-minute walk from Outram Park MRT Station . The menu leans into comfort food, with sando, soba, and donburi on rotation.
A must-try is the Pork Katsu Sando ($13.90++) , their bestseller. It features house-made shokupan stuffed with a thick slab of pork katsu, crisp salad, tomato, and cucumber. If you’re in the mood for a rice bowl, the Buta Don ($18.90++) is another solid pick, served with braised Iberico pork, caramelised onions, shimeji mushrooms, and tangy pickles.

1. Summer Folk Cafe & Steakhouse
Within Guoco Midtown on Beach Road is this lovely cafe filled with warmth. Summer Folk Cafe & Steakhouse is the perfect spot for a friend group or family to hang out and enjoy a lovely meal.
By the cashier, they even give out free Pokémon cards! They have all sorts of yummy drinks, cakes and awesome snacks to try out. But after 5pm, like a princess in a Disney movie, it transforms into a steakhouse.
Some dishes I’d recommend are the Cold Crab Angel Pasta (S$16.80) and the SF Meat Platter (S$118.80). With how hot Singapore normally is, you probably want something cold and refreshing, perfect for the SG climate.
Now, while the SF meat platter is a bit pricey, its portions and flavours will easily leave 3 people satisfied. Trust me, my friends and I have put it to the test. If you’re looking to treat yourself, the SF meat platter will definitely fit the bill.
Signature highlights: Cold Crab Angel Pasta, SF Meat Platter
Price range: S$16.80 – S$25 per pax
124 Beach Road, Guoco Midtown, #01-06 Singapore 189771
+65 8810 1239

Facebook | Instagram | Website
2. Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant
Perhaps you’re looking for something with more gravitas. A bit of history with a splash of style. Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant at Marina Square is one such place. With an interior that screams fancy and views that will leave your jaw on the glossy floors. The outdoor eating area even has a view of Marina Bay Sands and The Esplanade . Talk about a double feature.
When I went there with my friends, it literally felt like going to that one rich family during visiting on Hari Raya. Beautiful tables with a deep brown varnish, colourful tablecloths with intricate Turkish art, and even couches that might knock you out the moment you take a seat. Luckily, their coffee and tea will prevent that from happening.
Now, let’s talk food. I can recommend 2 classics: Chicken Shish Kebab (S$22.50) and Baklava (S$9.80) . What better to judge than the fundamentals? The chicken shish kebab was balanced, nicely seasoned and filling. With the amount of different things on your plate, every bite is slightly different from the last.
The baklava is also something special. Layers of buttery, thin filo pastry that stack together and bond into a rich, buttery bite. The pistachio filling is also extremely nutty and evenly distributed throughout. The syrup is then soaked into each layer, making it a decadent affair. The perfect end to an arguably healthy meal.
Signature highlights: Chicken Shish Kebab, Baklava

body:
Tanoto Foundation is a philanthropic partner supporting research into Asia’s most pressing health challenges. It recognises that Type 2 Diabetes affects a significant number of Singaporeans, especially the younger generation — over 400,000 to be exact. It’s one of the leading causes of death and sounds alarming when 1 in 4 Singaporeans will be affected by this disease by 2050 .
I saw first-hand how this condition affected my late grandmother’s daily life. Terrified of needles, she had to summon the courage to inject insulin into her stomach every morning. The terror in her eyes still haunts me, but so does the immense pride I felt seeing her push right past it.
Healthier eating habits are crucial and necessary to not just people with diabetes, but to Singaporeans in general. Small, sustainable lifestyle changes such as the food we consume can vastly improve our health in the long run. Thankfully, Tanoto Foundation has teamed up with National Healthcare Group (NHG) to launch a Diabetes Reversal Programme , taking a more proactive approach to tackling this life-threatening condition.
One of the initiatives was to publish a book called ‘ I Can’t Believe It Tastes So Good! ’, featuring 100 delicious diabetes-friendly recipes that are not only easy and accessible for the masses, but also backed by NHG experts. With the motto, ‘ Choose healthier; keep the flavour ’, this book was written to make a statement: healthy cooking methods can still taste good.
They include Breakfast Dishes , One-Pot Meals , Snacks , and even Desserts . With clear, step-by-step instructions, the book also features a dedicated Quick Tips section offering advice on flawless execution and flavor enhancement. The recipes focus on utilising lesser oil, salt and sugar.
Now, I can already guess what thoughts are running through your head: healthy recipes are bland, boring and never taste like the actual dish. Trust me, I’ve had the same reservations!
Well, it was up to MasterChef Singapore season 2 winner, Derek Cheong , to prove us wrong.
He conducted a cooking class for a group of 48 aunties and uncles at Toa Payoh West Community Centre across 2 sessions, guiding them through 2 featured recipes from the book — Chicken Curry and Fruit Chaat .
We watched as the cheerful aunties and uncles split into groups of 3, eagerly following Chef Derek’s instructions and having a blast along the way. If they could breeze through the lesson, I’m sure you’ll have no trouble getting the hang of it, too!
Trust me, the culinary studio was filled with the irresistible aroma of curry spices, and my stomach couldn’t stop rumbling. In the end, the session was a success, with Chef Derek pleased by both the overall experience and, most importantly, the taste of the 2 dishes.
To further test the theory on whether healthier recipes do indeed taste better, we bought a regular chicken curry from a local kopitiam and compared it against the healthier recipe. And guess what? More than half of us actually preferred the healthier version. HOW WAS THAT EVEN POSSIBLE? I was genuinely impressed!
The spices in the healthier chicken curry had more layers of flavour and depth, as compared to the coffeeshop’s version which was rather one-dimensional and had no character.
Well, Tanoto Foundation’s recipe book proved a point — healthy cooking methods can still taste great. If we can adopt healthier recipes in our diet while still retaining all that delicious flavour, I don’t see why this book can’t be placed in every kitchen.
To download the book online, click here .
Since World Diabetes Day is falling on 14 Nov 2026 , let us all play a part in taking care of ourselves and adopt better eating habits to reduce the risk of developing diabetes.
* This post is brought to you in partnership with Tanoto Foundation.

summary: Tanoto Foundation and National Healthcare Group’s Diabetes Reversal Programme promotes healthier eating through a recipe book featuring 100 diabetes-friendly dishes, from breakfast and one-pot meals to snacks and desserts. Using less oil, salt and sugar, the NHG-backed recipes come with step-by-step instructions and practical cooking tips, making them useful for Singaporeans looking to adopt healthier eating habits without compromising on flavour.

We’ll say it – chocolate advent calendars in Singapore are superior. Sure, you can find some unique advent calendars in Singapore that feature coffee, tea, liquor, and even gym equipment or jewellery. But there’s something about popping open that little window and treating yourself to a holiday bon bon that just hits different. If you’re a chocolate lover who wants to get into the festive spirit or you’re on the lookout for a holiday gift, read on to find out where you can buy chocolate advent calendars in Singapore.
Where to buy chocolate advent calendars in Singapore
1. Pierre Herme
Photography: Pierre Herme
The macaron maestro is back at it with a whimsical new chocolate advent calendar. This year’s Pierre Herme Christmas collection is themed around the circus, bringing the wonder of the big top across its various desserts. Everything is encased in beautifully designed boxes illustrated by Paris-based artist Dimitri Rybaltchenko, who has designed for Hermes, Dior, and Saint Laurent. While its Singapore location is currently undergoing refurbishment, you can grab your advent calendars at the pop-up within the Resorts World Convention Centre.

Photography: Janice Wong

BBQ Pits in Singapore
Having a BBQ at East Coast Park (ECP) is pretty much a rite of passage for Singaporeans. With over 70 BBQ pits along its beachfront and rates that won’t break the bank, it’s no surprise that ECP has become the go-to spot for birthday celebrations and gatherings. And with the year coming to a close, you might already be planning a get-together with friends and family to ring in the New Year.
But you don’t have to travel to the East Coast just to grill a few chicken wings. There are several underrated spots around Singapore that’ll make for an equally good grill sesh . From poolside pits to private rooms with karaoke, here are some public BBQ pits in Singapore worth considering for your next big function.
1. Pasir Ris Park
$20 per booking, from 12pm to 10.30pm
Image credit: Tom hum via Facebook
With 65 BBQ pits across 4 areas, Pasir Ris Park is a popular spot to host a coastal cookout. Its sprawling 70ha grounds offer plenty to explore while your chicken wings and otah cook, so you won’t have to hover around the pit.
View this post on Instagram
Nature-lovers can take a stroll through the 6ha mangrove forest , where you’ll find a boardwalk and a 3-storey birdwatching tower . Head to the top to spot birds like the Oriental Pied Hornbill and Stork-billed Kingfisher roosting and flying through the canopy.
Make the most of the morning before your feast by joining one of the free mangrove guided tours . These take place on selected days during the school holidays from 9.30am to 11am ; just remember to register a slot beforehand on the NParks website .
Image credit: Andrea Goh via Google Maps
Families with younger children can head over to Area 3’s Adventure Playground , recognised as Singapore’s largest playground. It’s fully decked out with swings, climbing structures, and ziplines that are sure to keep the little ones entertained. Meanwhile, the nearby beach is a nice spot to unwind after your meal, whether you’re building sandcastles or going for a swim.
Image credit: Evangeline Yumen Pacheco via Facebook
Those who want to extend their outing can also stay overnight at one of Pasir Ris Park’s 2 designated camping zones . Camping is free with a permit , which can be applied for online before your visit.

Its 10 BBQ pits along the coast make it a quieter alternative compared to ECP, especially for those living in the North. Image credit: Chee Siong Cheng (CS) via Google Maps

Take in the sea breeze and get close to the water’s edge if you manage to catch the low tide.

Super Mario Holiday Power-Up at VivoCity
Nintendo has certainly been on a roll lately. Between PokéXciting! at Changi Airport and the McDonald’s x Pokémon collab , the gaming giant has been giving fans plenty of reasons to geek out over their favourite pocket monsters.
While Pokémon seems to be Nintendo’s favourite child, it isn’t the only one getting love. Its flagship mascot, Mario, and his crew will be getting the spotlight as part of VivoCity ’s 20th anniversary celebrations with the Super Mario Holiday Power-Up , running from now till 27th December 2026 . Here’s what you should know so you don’t miss out on the fun.
What is the Super Mario Holiday Power-Up all about?
Image credit: VivoCity
Rounding off its 20th anniversary celebrations, VivoCity has teamed up with Nintendo to bring the Mushroom Kingdom to life for its year-end festivities. Expect familiar faces, iconic Mario power-ups, and all the little details long-time fans are sure to clock instantly.
Beyond the nostalgia, there’s plenty to keep everybody busy: immersive play areas , character meet-and-greets , and enough decorative photo ops to fill your camera roll twice over.
What to expect from the Super Mario Holiday Power-Up
Go on a holiday adventure through 6 themed zones
Image credit: VivoCity
Take on the Super Mario Holiday Adventure , located at the Outdoor Plaza right outside of VivoCity. The space has been turned into a larger-than-life festive playground with 6 discovery zones to explore, each inspired by different parts of the Mario universe.
Start at the Pipe Discovery Walk , where you’ll find the classic Warp Pipes Mario uses to zip around the Mushroom Kingdom. From there, head over to the Power-Up Block Wall to pose with props and stages lifted straight from the games.
Image credit: Universal Studios Japan
Keep an eye out for some of Mario’s friends along the way too, including Yoshi and Princess Peach , who’ll be making appearances at selected zones. We’ll leave the rest for you to discover as the zones progressively open in phases throughout the celebrations.
Stand before a 10-metre-tall inflatable Mario
Image credit: VivoCity
And at the centre of it all stands Singapore’s first-ever 10m-tall Mario inflatable . You won’t need a Super Mushroom to spot him; he towers over the plaza while striking his signature fist-raised pose.
VivoCity’s nightly snowfall sessions will also take place here every Tuesday to Sunday , at 7.30pm and 8.30pm . Watch the wintry spectacle with the iconic moustachioed plumber filling up the backdrop.
Location: Outdoor Plaza, Level 1
Get pop-up exclusive merchandise straight from Japan
Image for illustrative purposes only.
Image credit: VivoCity
Within the mall itself, you’ll find the Nintendo POP-UP STORE , taking up the Central Court on Level 1 . Running from 1st to 27th December 2026 from 10am to 10pm , Singapore’s latest Nintendo pop-up is stocked with official Nintendo merchandise brought in directly from Japan .
Image credit: VivoCity
Get your hands on the pop-up exclusive Super Mario Winter Collection Plushies , featuring characters like Mario, Luigi, and Yoshi as snowmen, dressed in cosy scarves and winter accessories. There are even mini ornament versions to hang on your Christmas trees at home.
Image credit: VivoCity
You can also pick up some of the Singapore-exclusive T-shirts that are making their debut, featuring a range of fun and minimalist designs. They’re a fun addition to the wardrobe, especially if you consider yourself a hardcore fan of the franchise.
Image credit: VivoCity
Even if Mario isn’t your go-to Nintendo series, don’t write yourself off just yet. The pop-up store will also feature a selection of collectables from other popular Nintendo games. Some notable trinkets that fans might recognise include the Ocarina of Time from The Legend of Zelda franchise and the Bell Bags found in Animal Crossing .
Location: Central Court, Level 1
Opening hours: 1st to 27th Dec, 10am to 10pm
Try your hand at game demos on the Nintendo Switch 2
Image credit: VivoCity
Of course, you can’t have a Nintendo-themed celebration without the games themselves, and boy, are there a lot of them. Get in on the action starting from 20th November 2026 , with free game demos on the Nintendo Switch 2s available right beside MLB . Some of the titles featured include Pokémon Pokopia , Pikmin 4 , and Splatoon Raiders , just to name a few.
If you have memories of grinding on Wii Sports as a child, then you’ll be pleased to know that the newly released Nintendo Switch Sports Resort is also available to try out here. Relive your childhood of playing sports with a joystick in hand with this spiritual successor.
For those with a competitive streak, the Mario Kart World Challenge could be worth checking out. Spanning 2 weekends, from 5th to 6th and 19th to 20th December , you’ll be able to race against other players through iconic tracks like Rainbow Road for the chance to win exciting prizes, and it’s free to join .

Si Yan Teochew Dining opened on Friday, 13 November 2026, in the basement of Palais Renaissance on Orchard Road. The restaurant takes units #B1-01 to #B1-03 and builds its menu around Teochew seafood, from marinated crab to oyster omelette, with dim sum at lunch.
For the opening, Si Yan members pay soft-opening prices on three signature dishes, which the restaurant calls the Si Yan Signature Trio, until 3 January 2027. Membership is free to join.
The members’ prices, dish by dish
• Signature Teochew Style Shark’s Fin in Supreme Broth, served in a Japanese stone pot: S$38, down from S$58
• Braised 3-Head Australian Abalone in Abalone Sauce: S$38 a piece, down from S$62
• Alaskan King Crab Steamed with Chinese Wine: S$14 per 100g, down from S$28 per 100g, by advance order only
The prices run daily at lunch and dinner, for dine-in in the main dining hall only. Membership is required, the offer cannot be combined with other promotions, vouchers or membership benefits, and the dishes are subject to availability. GST and service charge come on top.
How membership works
Anyone aged 18 and above can sign up for Si Yan membership online at no cost, with one account per person. It lasts 12 months and renews for S$3 a year, paid in person at the restaurant. Members show their membership before paying.
New members get a S$10 welcome voucher that activates 24 hours after sign-up and lasts 90 days, and earn SY$1 for every S$10 spent on regular-priced à la carte food. The voucher cannot be used together with the opening prices, since those exclude vouchers.
Double-Boiled Pineapple Kampong Chicken Soup with Pig Stomach, an advance-order dish. Photo: Si Yan Teochew Dining
What else is on the menu
The kitchen leans on an aged ingredient: 15-year vintage preserved turnip, or chai poh. It goes into a stir-fried XO carrot cake at S$16 and a wok-fried hor fun with crispy pork lard and XO sauce at S$28.
The oyster omelette is pan-fried whole into one crisp golden sheet rather than served loose, at S$24, with a prawn version at S$26. The kitchen asks for at least 40 minutes for either.
For a group, the Teochew Style Fresh Prawn Poached Rice with Crispy Rice comes in a claypot for four at S$58, and a whole roasted suckling pig is S$338 by advance order. The braised section covers duck, pork belly, trotters and beef shank, with a braised duo platter from S$32.
Teochew Style Fresh Prawn Poached Rice with Crispy Rice, S$58 for four. Photo: Si Yan Teochew Dining
Advance orders also cover the Teochew Marinated Red Cream Mud Crab, steeped in a house sauce for more than eight hours, and a double-boiled soup of pineapple enzyme-fed kampong chicken with a whole pig stomach cooked inside the bird.
Teochew Marinated Red Cream Mud Crab, marinated for more than eight hours. Photo: Si Yan Teochew Dining
Dim sum at lunch
Lunchtime dim sum starts at S$8.80 a basket, for items such as the Teochew glutinous rice roll, deep-fried taro puffs and BBQ honey pork buns. Prawn ha kao and siew mai are S$9.80. Teochew porridge with oyster and minced meat, or with dried scallop, is S$11.80 a person.
Until 30 November, members who spend at least S$50 on à la carte food at lunch (11am to 3pm) get 50% off all dim sum, with no limit on how many baskets they order. Dim sum and drinks do not count towards the S$50.

Italian food has long been called the GOAT of cuisines. Whether you agree with that statement or not, it is undoubtedly sad to lose a spot that represents the cuisine in its most authentic form. That spot is Porta Porta Italian Restaurant at Simpang Bedok, and it is closing after a 33-year run.
Their last day of business is on 31 Dec 2026 ; what a sad way to end the year. Before they officially close, I intend to visit them, with my only regret that I didn’t visit them sooner.
Credit – Google
The restaurant itself feels like those Italian movies, those romantic, down-to-earth productions that make it feel like you’re visiting your grandma’s house. Pastel colours fade into the background and the walls are busy with stunning paintings, instruments and other souvenirs that add character to the home.
And that’s exactly what it is. The entire restaurant feels more like home than anything else. And there’s nothing sadder than when your home is no longer there.
Credit – Google
You are probably wondering why they are closing in the first place. Co-founder Rozianah Baharudin Laino — known as Rozi — wants to spend more time with her family, and her son, Danesh Laino , has established a career outside of F&B. That led to her decision to close after 33 long years.
Credit – Google
What makes this spot so remarkable to me is the story. Rozi founded Porta Porta with her late husband, Antonino Laino , or Nino, who passed away in 2012. They began as an Italian cooking school before deciding to serve instead of teach. Their first spot was a small kitchen in Changi, and after years of hard work, they moved to their current home in 2019 .
This restaurant is also Muslim-owned, which made it accessible to almost everyone. They take pride in their ability to be a home for all, and even their name represents this admirable mission. The name Porta Porta means “door to door” in Italian. With the name came the idea that the door would always be open for anyone hungry. Unfortunately, every door has to close.
While they’re still operating, I implore my fellow foodies to show them the support they deserve. I’m happy Rozi and her family managed to have a business that lasted as long as it did, in an F&B scene as cutthroat as Singapore’s. I wish them the best in their future endeavours.
Trovato: Hidden Italian restaurant with an incredible brick-fire oven charcoal pizza and Italian delights in the North-East of SG
summary: Porta Porta Italian Restaurant, a Muslim-owned Italian restaurant at Jalan Pari Burong in Simpang Bedok, closes on 31 Dec 2026 after 33 years, following the retirement of co-founder Rozianah Baharudin Laino. The restaurant is known for homely dishes such as squid ink tagliatelle and meat lasagna. The family has no plans to relocate but remains open to a takeover, so the restaurant is best suited to regulars planning a final visit.
title: Porta Porta – 33y.o. Italian restaurant in Bedok says goodbye on 31 Dec 2026

body:
Raffles City is one of Singapore’s most central malls. Conveniently linked to City Hall MRT , this bustling shopping centre is frequented by folks from all walks of life: white-collar workers from nearby offices, tourists on city walks, families on weekend shopping sprees and even millennials looking to grab quick bites before heading to the nearby museums.
How I chose these best food spots in Raffles City
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which eateries to recommend:
• Variety : I picked eateries which offer a range of cuisines so you can pick what you feel like when you are there.
• Wide price range : From affordable to premium eats, there’s something for everyone.
• Independent businesses : I included brands with a smaller presence as well as big chains widely available around Singapore.
It’s home to more than 200 shops, half of which are eateries to curb any cravings. From Michelin-recognised restaurants and stalls to casual eateries, Raffles City has it all. Here are 12 best food spots in Raffles City to fill up your tummy .

1. Gyukatsu Kyoto Katsugyu (#B1-63/64)
If you’ve ever drooled over one too many Instagram stories of sizzling gyukatsu in Japan, save that plane ticket and get it right at Gyukatsu Kyoto Katsugyu . This Kyoto-born brand found its way to our shores in 2024, adding to an arsenal of 60 outlets in Japan and nearly 20 more worldwide.
In case you’re not already familiar, gyukatsu is a Japanese dish of beef cutlet that’s breaded with panko , deep-fried until golden and typically served rare inside. Part of the fun is searing the meat to your preferred doneness on a small tabletop hot stone, then customising each bite with seasonings of your choice.
Gyukatsu Kyoto Katsugyu offers 5 indulgent cuts: Sirloin (from S$25) , Tenderloin (from S$32) , Chuck Tail Flap (from S$32) , Tongue (from S$37) and the crown jewel — A5 Miyazaki Wagyu Beef Sirloin (from S$55) . The Wagyu , naturally, steals the spotlight with its melt-in-your-mouth tenderness enveloped in an impeccable crunch.
Each set meal comes with a generous tray of sides for a wholesome meal: fluffy rice, onsen egg, miso soup and a trio of condiments — dashi soy sauce, sansho pepper salt and their signature gyukatsu sauce — to elevate the cutlet however you like.
Daily: 11am – 10pm
Facebook | Instagram | Website
2. Spicy Noodle 销魂面铺 (#B1-38)
Hankering for a slurpin’ good time? Look no further than Spicy Noodle 销魂面铺 . This famed restaurant boasts 18 outlets across Taiwan, with its Raffles City branch being the only overseas outpost. 销魂 ( xiao hun ) translates to “selling one’s soul”. Aptly so, as Singaporeans have been quick to fall in love with their soul-stirring noodles. Don’t believe me? Let its queues do the talking.
Spicy Noodle holds its roots dear, with its handmade Xiao Hun noodles, master chilli sauce, noodle sauce and chilli oil flown in directly from China. Take your pick between the Mild Beef Soup Set (from S$18.80) or the Spicy Beef Soup Set (from S$18.80) , each of which includes the noodles, braised tau pok , soft-boiled egg and a rich bowl of beef broth packed with meat and vegetables.
While you can’t go wrong with either soup, we must say the Mild variation took us by surprise. Simmered with pure beef bones for over 6 hours, it has a robust yet clean profile that’s easy on even ardent spice lovers’ palates.
Equally impressive are the noodles, which effortlessly epitomise the words “springy and QQ”. And don’t forget to add a dash of Spicy Noodle’s signature Soul Chilli Oil — sparingly, though. Stir-fried by hand for a whopping 8 hours, this fiery elixir has been dubbed “the Hermès of chilli oil”. A drop or two is all it takes to kick the whole bowl up several notches.
…
summary: Raffles City offers a diverse range of dining options, from Michelin-recognised food court stalls and affordable noodle shops to Japanese-Western fusion restaurants, bakeries and cafes. Conveniently located near City Hall MRT, these food spots cater to CBD workers, shoppers, tourists and families, with options for quick budget meals, casual dining and more substantial sit-down meals.
title: 12 best food spots in Raffles City that’ll fill up your tummy [Nov 2026]

body:
You know what they say about mending a broken heart: there are plenty of fish in the sea. I like mine served fresh, straight from the ocean and onto a bed of Japanese rice, with a little soy sauce and wasabi on the side. If that sounds like your kind of comfort food, Shinmatto Fish Market at Bangunan Mun Nang in Pudu is worth adding to your list.
Shinmatto has been getting quite a bit of attention lately, particularly among sashimi enthusiasts, so don’t be surprised if you find yourself waiting for a table. My little tip is to visit between 5pm and 6pm , when the crowd tends to be more manageable.
Once you arrive, the staff will give you a queue number. When it’s your turn, place your order at the kiosk, collect your table number and make yourself comfortable while they bring your food over.
What to order at Shinmatto
There’s a fair bit to choose from here, including fresh fish, clams, uni and prawns. Seasonal fish selections are also available, so do check with the staff to see what’s in stock. For our visit, we decided to stick to the regular menu.
We started with the Shinmatto Don (RM32) , their signature bowl of hamachi , salmon and yuko tai sashimi served over steamed Japanese rice, with wasabi , pickled ginger, ebiko and a sprinkle of chopped turmeric leaves.
The first thing I noticed was how fresh the fish tasted. Each had its own character, although the yuko tai (sea bream) was probably my favourite of the three for its clean, delicate sweetness. The hamachi (yellowtail) had a little more flavour while remaining pleasantly clean, whereas the salmon was decent but didn’t quite stand out as much as the other cuts.
Surprisingly, I found myself paying just as much attention to the rice. It was soft, fluffy and nicely seasoned, to the point where I wouldn’t mind eating it on its own. The wasabi was also pleasant, without being too overpowering. Soy sauce and green tea are available free-flow at the self-service station, too.
Mezze Mazi: This cosy Levantine eatery in PJ gets its hummus, falafel & spring chicken right
Next was the Tekka Ebi Don (RM33) , which comes with raw akami (lean bluefin tuna) and amaebi (sweet shrimp). I’ll admit that I’m usually not too fond of lean tuna, as I sometimes find its fishiness a little distracting. I’m generally more inclined towards fatty tuna, so I wasn’t expecting much going into this bowl.
Well, I stand corrected. This was genuinely some of the best lean tuna I’ve tasted, even compared to a few more established sashimi restaurants I’ve visited (not naming names, soz ). It had a lovely firm yet tender texture, was pleasantly juicy and carried just a subtle taste of the ocean without the fishiness I usually associate with it.
The amaebi was another favourite. Fatty, tender and naturally sweet, it was every bit as enjoyable as the sea bream from our first bowl. Between the two, I honestly had a hard time picking a favourite.
As for the portions, they’re not particularly generous, but considering the prices, I wouldn’t say they’re unreasonable either. Plus, there were much cheaper options than what we ordered. We were surprisingly comfortable after the meal, and my dining companion couldn’t even finish her rice, so it was enough for us.
Who is Shinmatto best for?
Sashimi lovers who enjoy fresh seafood without spending too much will appreciate the selection here. Just note that the dining area is rather compact, which might not be the most comfortable for older diners.
How to get there?
Driving is your best option, as there’s no convenient public transport nearby. Parking is available, but spaces can fill up quickly during peak hours.
Do we recommend Shinmatto?
I’d say it’s worth a visit if you’re in the mood for sashimi . The freshness was consistent across the bowls we tried, and the akami and amaebi were particularly memorable. I also like that there’s a selection of seasonal fish to look forward to, giving me a reason to see what’s available on another visit. It’s not a particularly fancy dining experience, but sometimes all you really want is a good bowl of fresh seafood and rice.
