What to eat at Solaris, Mont Kiara?
Which Korean food spot in KL is worth the drive?
summary: Shinmatto Fish Market in Pudu, Kuala Lumpur, serves fresh sashimi and seafood donburi at affordable prices, with seasonal fish selections alongside its regular menu. It is suited to sashimi lovers seeking quality seafood without spending too much, though the compact dining area, queue system and limited public transport access are worth considering. Visiting between 5pm and 6pm may mean shorter waits.
title: Shinmatto: Pudu’s viral sashimi spot serves fresh seafood donburi from RM20

body:
Tucked away in an industrial estate right next to the MRT tracks in Aljunied is An La Ghien -5 , a low-key spot serving genuine, home-style Vietnamese fare from 11am all the way to 5am, making it the perfect late-night supper spot.
Founded in 2019 by Yuki, a Vietnamese immigrant in Singapore who missed the taste of home, An La Ghien -5 has since been sharing authentic Vietnamese flavours with expatriates and locals alike.
Unlike Singapore’s more commercialised Vietnamese chains, the focus here is squarely on comforting, traditional cooking. Even better, they offer a wide variety of free-flow fresh herbs to customise your meal — a Vietnamese dining touch rarely seen anywhere else on the island. I mean, look at that fridgeful of greens!
What to order at An La Ghien -5
I came here specifically for the Sliced Beef Pho (S$3.90++) . While it is a fairly standard rendition, you get a remarkably generous portion of sliced beef for the price.
The clear beef broth is clean-tasting with a subtle sweetness, paired with flat white noodles that lean slightly softer than I would prefer.
Most of the beef slices were tender, though a few pieces turned out a touch dry and firm. Tossing in the fresh herbs really helped to elevate the bowl — I went with sprigs of basil and sawtooth coriander, which added a bright, almost peppery lift to the soup.
10 best Vietnamese food places in Singapore that will blow your mind
Next I dug into the Grilled Pork Chop and Vegetables with Rice Vermicelli (S$12.90++) . This turned out to be my favourite dish here, just for how fresh and light it was, thanks to the abundance of vegetables and herbs.
The pork chop in this dish was well-seasoned and had a nice char to it, adding just a hint of smokiness. It was moist and tender throughout and wasn’t dry or tough at any point. I found it to be a little salty on its own, but when enjoyed together with the noodles and vegetables, the saltiness is just right.
The small pile of pickled water spinach added a slight tang to the bowl and paired well with the grilled pork by helping to cut through its richness.
The noodles in this dish were similarly soft, though tossing them with the crisp lettuce created a great textural contrast that made every bite much more addictive. I particularly liked the accompanying sweet chilli sauce. Infused with fish sauce, it delivered a savoury umami depth alongside a gentle spicy kick without ever leaning overly sweet.
The menu also featured less common Vietnamese dishes such as Pan-Seared Goat Ribs (S$29.90) and Fried Frog Feet with Fish Sauce (S$14.90) that I’d definitely be interested in trying next time. They also specialise in hotpot and BBQ sets, making it ideal for communal meals or family dinners.
Who is An La Ghien -5 best for?
An La Ghien -5 is ideal for anyone craving authentic, home-style Vietnamese fare. And with doors staying open until 5am, it also doubles as a perfect supper spot in the East, offering a comforting meal after hours. Plus, if you love fresh herbs, the generous free-flow spread makes it easy to customise every bowl just the way you like it.
How to get to An La Ghien -5
An La Ghien -5 is located along Lorong 23 Geylang, which is just a 2-minute walk from Aljunied MRT station (EW9) . The station connects to the East-West line of the MRT. Use Exit A and cross Aljunied Road before continuing toward Lorong 23 Geylang.
If you prefer to travel by bus, you can stop at bus stop Opp Aljunied Stn (81081) and walk towards Lorong 23 Geylang. Do note that buses 158A and 125A only operate on weekdays.
Do we recommend An La Ghien -5 ?
The free-flow herbs are a massive plus if you enjoy bright, herbaceous flavours as much as I do. Coupled with an air-conditioned dining space, it makes for a comfortable meal. While the rest of the menu is priced slightly higher than the wallet-friendly S$3.90 pho , it remains a solid spot I would likely revisit whenever I am in the area, or craving a late-night supper.

summary: An La Ghien -5 is an air-conditioned Vietnamese eatery along Lorong 23 Geylang in Aljunied, serving home-style dishes from 11am to 5am daily. Highlights include S$3.90++ Sliced Beef Pho, grilled pork chop vermicelli, hotpot, and rare free-flow fresh herbs, though other menu items carry higher prices. It is best suited for late-night supper diners in the East, herb lovers, and groups seeking communal meals near Aljunied MRT.
title: An La Ghien -5: $3.90 beef pho with free-flow herbs, open until 5am

Casa Vostra’s fourth Singapore restaurant is open on level two of Wisma Atria, and it is the first of the chain’s outlets to take reservations. Opening hours are 11.30am to 10pm daily.
A limited number of tables can be booked online , opening 14 days ahead, and most tables are kept for walk-ins. The other three outlets, at Raffles City, Jem and Tampines Mall, take walk-ins only.
The dining room at Casa Vostra Wisma Atria, #02-02/03. Photo: Casa Vostra
Casa Vostra belongs to the Mission Group and is led by chef Antonio Miscellaneo, the chef-owner behind La Bottega Enoteca in Joo Chiat. The restaurant says La Bottega was named Asia’s No. 1 pizzeria in 2023 and 2024 by 50 Top Pizza. The house pizza is the Newpolitan, made with dough cold-fermented for 36 hours and fired at 450°C.
What is only at Wisma Atria
The Wisma Atria menu marks 13 dishes as exclusive to this address. The biggest is SquareCrunch, toppings baked on long-fermented, high-hydration dough with a crisp base and served by the square. The Doublecrunch sandwiches sold at Raffles City are not on the Wisma Atria menu. There are three, each S$15: Tomato Tarte Tatin with roasted heirloom cherry tomatoes; Zucchini and Sakura-Ebi with zucchini cream and chips; and Potato, Leek and Speck with ricotta and rosemary. A counter sells SquareCrunch and desserts for dine-in or takeaway.
Two white pizzas are new here too. Anchovy 2.0 is S$22, with fiordilatte, anchovies, pizzutello tomatoes and olive dust. Carbonara 2.0 is S$24, with Parmigiano Reggiano, pancetta, egg yolk and black pepper.
A Newpolitan pizza, made with 36-hour cold-fermented dough. Photo: Casa Vostra
The Wisma-only pastas are Orecchiette Salsiccia e Broccoli at S$22 and Spaghetti alla Nerano, with zucchini and Parmigiano Reggiano, at S$19. Two mains join them at S$30 each: a breaded Pluma Iberica “Milanese” with lemon burnt butter and capers, and Ossobuco, a slow-cooked veal shank with potato purée and gremolata.
Gelato with Petra
The gelato, also exclusive to Wisma Atria, is a collaboration between Casa Vostra and Petra, a Mediterranean-Levantine restaurant. It pairs housemade mascarpone gelato with a crisp housemade za’atar cone, eaten plain or with toppings. The Original is S$9. Tiramisù, with savoiardi, coffee and cocoa, and Blue Forest, with mixed berries, are S$10 each. Dubai Chocolate, with pistachio and chocolate ganache and pistachios, is S$12.
Prices against the other outlets
Dishes that appear on both menus cost the same as at Raffles City. A Margherita is S$17 at both Wisma Atria and Raffles City, Carbonara with rigatoni is S$21 at both, and the Gamberi pizza with Argentinian prawns is S$28 at both. The priciest food at Wisma Atria is S$30: the Tartufo e Funghi pizza with fresh black truffle, and all three mains, including the Guazzetto del Pescatore seafood stew also served at Raffles City. Prices are subject to GST and service charge.
Carbonara with rigatoni, S$21 at Wisma Atria and Raffles City. Photo: Casa Vostra
The menu includes pork across several dishes, including speck, pancetta, guanciale and salame, so this is not a halal option.
Margherita, S$17 at Wisma Atria. Photo: Casa Vostra
Details
• Casa Vostra Wisma Atria, 435 Orchard Road, #02-02/03, Singapore 238877
• Open daily, 11.30am to 10pm, last order 9.30pm
• Nearest MRT: Orchard (NS22/TE14)
• Reservations: book online up to 14 days ahead; limited tables, most are walk-in
• Menu: Wisma Atria menu (PDF)
• Contact: wisma@casavostra.sg
• Prices exclude GST and service charge
summary: Casa Vostra's fourth outlet, at Wisma Atria #02-02/03, is the first to take bookings. Wisma-only dishes include three S$15 SquareCrunch squares, Anchovy 2.0 and Carbonara 2.0 pizzas, and a mascarpone gelato made with Petra, from S$9 to S$12.
title: Casa Vostra is now open at Wisma Atria, with reservations, S$15 SquareCrunch and a Petra gelato collaboration

Pavilion KL in Bukit Bintang has been welcoming a fresh mix of names to its retail lineup. The latest additions span artisan sourdough pastries, Michelin-starred Sichuan cuisine, niche fragrances and international fashion labels, with several highly anticipated brands also preparing to make their Malaysian debut.
Here are 18 new openings at Pavilion KL worth knowing about , including those arriving in the coming months.
Now open
1. adough (Level 3)
Credit – adough
Sourdough enthusiasts have another reason to visit Pavilion KL, as adough has opened its third bakery and cafe outlet here. Known for its artisan sourdough bakes, the menu features treats such as Pistachio Frangipane Croissants , Honey Butter Shio Pan , Pistachio Pain Suisse and seasonal fruit tarts.
There are savoury options too, including Spring Onion & Cheese Croissants , Jalapeño Seaweed Rolls and Chicken Pot Pies . Look out for its sourdough loaves, including Marmite & Cheese and Garlic , Rosemary & Sea Salt Focaccia , alongside cafe favourites like Matcha Brownies and Banana Chocolate Cake .
2. Burberry Beauty (Level 3)
Credit – Burberry
Burberry Beauty has opened its first flagship in Malaysia, bringing the British fashion house’s signature aesthetic into fragrance and make-up. Inspired by London’s character and the brand’s heritage, its collection features sophisticated scents and make-up essentials that balance classic elegance with a contemporary edge.
3. TROVE (Level 3)
Credit – TROVE
Beauty enthusiasts looking beyond mainstream labels can explore TROVE , a curated beauty and lifestyle store carrying niche fragrances, skincare, haircare and home essentials. Its fragrance selection includes Essential Parfums , Chasing Scents , D’Annam , The House of Oud and Ormonde Jayne , with full-sized bottles, discovery sets and travel-sized options available.
You can also browse premium skincare from Cellcosmet and La Colline , hair treatments by Miriam Quevedo , bodycare from Neal’s Yard Remedies , as well as Ichendorf Milano glassware and home fragrances.
4. SK-II (Level 3)
Credit – SK-II
Japanese skincare brand SK-II has also opened its doors at Pavilion KL. Best known for its signature PITERA ingredient, discovered through sake fermentation, the brand offers skincare formulations designed to improve skin texture, clarity and radiance.
5. Diptyque (Level 3)
Credit – Diptyque
Parisian fragrance house Diptyque brings its distinctive collection of personal fragrances, bodycare and home scents to Pavilion KL. Founded in 1961, the brand is known for its carefully crafted fragrances and distinctive olfactory signatures.
Selected Pavilion Lifestyle, Priority and Luxe members can also enjoy complimentary personalisation services with candle and fragrance purchases, including Make A Wish and The Capsule.
6. Weekend Max Mara (Level 3)
Credit – Weekend Max Mara
For relaxed Italian dressing, Weekend Max Mara offers a wardrobe of versatile pieces that balance practicality with understated sophistication. Originally created as a casual lifestyle line under Max Mara, it has since expanded into a full-fledged collection of everyday fashion, including its distinctive designer collaborations and seasonal capsule collections.
7. Sandro (Level 3)
Credit – Sandro
French fashion label Sandro has added another shopping destination to its lineup at Pavilion KL. Its latest collections include womenswear inspired by 1970s silhouettes, fluid fabrics and modern tailoring, alongside menswear that leans towards understated sophistication.
8. Sam Edelman (Level 3)
Credit – Sam Edelman
American lifestyle brand Sam Edelman brings its footwear, handbags, apparel and accessories to Pavilion KL. Founded in 2004, the label combines timeless American influences with contemporary trends. Travellers can also enjoy 10% off regular-priced items through its tourist privilege offer.
9. JNBY (Level 2)
Credit – JNBY
Chinese fashion label JNBY , short for Just Naturally Be Yourself, brings an artistic approach to contemporary womenswear. Expect unconventional silhouettes, architectural cuts and bold prints, with collections built around the brand’s philosophy of modernity, vitality, meaning and serenity.
Opening soon
10. Cioccolatitaliani (Dec 2026)
Credit – Cioccolatitaliani
Chocolate lovers can look forward to Cioccolatitaliani , a first-in-Malaysia arrival scheduled for December 2026. Founded by the Ferrieri family in 2009, the Italian brand revolves around its concept of Chocology , combining chocolate with ice cream, pastries and coffee.
11. Xu’s Cuisine (Jan 2027)
Credit – Xu’s Cuisine
Xu’s Cuisine will make its Malaysian debut at Pavilion KL in January 2027, bringing its Michelin-starred Sichuan cooking to Level 3. Established in Chengdu, China, in 2011, the restaurant is known for giving traditional Sichuan specialities a contemporary touch while staying true to seasonal ingredients and regional flavours.
12. Puyi Optical (Mar 2027)
Credit – Puyi Optical
…
summary: Pavilion KL in Bukit Bintang has welcomed new food, beauty, fragrance and fashion retailers, with openings either now operating or planned for the coming months. Highlights include artisan bakery adough, niche fragrance store TROVE and Burberry Beauty, alongside upcoming first-in-Malaysia arrivals such as Cioccolatitaliani and Michelin-starred Xu’s Cuisine, making it a useful update for shoppers planning a visit through 2027.
title: 18 new openings at Pavilion KL to check out, from adough to Michelin-starred Xu’s Cuisine

Most of us are always glued to our screens , be it phones, laptops or the television, so why not try out Virtual Reality (VR) experiences? It’s also a type of screen, just that it allows you to explore worlds and situations that are normally extraordinary, such as diving deep into an underwater world or exploring the past. Whether you enjoy interactive storytelling, adventures and games or simulations, there’s a VR experience for you on this list.
If you’re wondering where to experience such fun, here are 10 of the best immersive VR experiences in Singapore for a digital getaway .
How I chose these best VR experiences
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which VR experiences to recommend:
• Variety : The experiences on this list are varied, from flight simulators to VR escape rooms.
• Immersion : These experiences use VR headsets to create realistic virtual environments for great immersion.
• Accessibility : I included venues that cater to experienced VR players and also welcome first-time VR users.
This isn’t a ranked best-to-worst list, but a collection of the most enjoyable VR experiences overall. Get ready to head out to experience some fun!

1. Horizon of Khufu: A Journey in Ancient Egypt by GROUNDSEESAW Singapore
Tired of your mundane daily life? Travel back more than 4,500 years to the golden age of Egypt with Horizon of Khufu: Journey in Ancient Egypt . Developed in collaboration with Egyptologist Peter Der Manuelian and his team from the Giza Project at Harvard University, this immersive VR adventure is carefully curated. Each session lasts approximately 45 minutes and accommodates groups of up to 4 people . The VR space is shared, and you’ll be able to roam around and interact with the surroundings. Do note that this experience is available until 2 Apr 2027 . Fret not, GROUNDSEESAW switches up their exhibitions to keep things fresh, so there’ll be more to come.
You’ll get to wander around and explore all the hidden nooks and crannies of the pyramids and even peer into the Queen’s chamber. This experience was equal parts thrilling and educational; there’s a section where you get to witness the embalming of Pharaoh Khufu. I’ve always read about their techniques and reasoning behind their traditions, but seeing it come to life was really on another level. The illusion of movement and height successfully tricks your brain into feeling you’ve actually gone back in time.
Get your tickets from S$29 for kids below 8 and S$35 for adults on FEVER
600 North Bridge Road, Parkview Square, Level 3, Singapore 188778
+65 6911 0851
Daily: 10am – 6pm [until 2 Apr 2027]
Facebook | Instagram | Website
2. Science Centre Singapore
Credit – Science Centre Singapore
Located in Jurong East , don’t be mistaken in thinking Science Centre Singapore only offers traditional science exhibits. Science Centre Hall C is home to E-mmersive Experiential Environments (E3) . This is an immersive exhibition that combines virtual reality with large-scale 360 ° visual projections that cover the room from floor to ceiling. These features will transport you into their unique digitally recreated environment. Tickets for E3 are Complimentary with Science Centre admission.
Credit – Science Centre Singapore
You can expect to explore larger-than-life landscapes when you step into their virtual forest. The experience is brought to life through real-time 3D rendering technology and the Unreal game engine . What’s unique here is the dynamic setting with day and night transitions and realistic weather changes. E3 also features interactive elements; for example, you can play with the fish along the forest’s central river.
…
summary: Singapore’s VR experiences span educational virtual exhibitions, flight simulators, free-roam adventures, arcade games and escape rooms, with options across locations such as Orchard, Jurong East and Marina Bay. From complimentary exhibits to paid sessions starting at S$5, these venues cater to both first-time visitors and experienced players, making them useful for anyone seeking interactive activities, group outings or a change from conventional entertainment.
title: Best immersive VR experiences for a digital getaway

To be the first of anything is a coveted title. The first man on the moon, the first to reach the summit of a mountain or, in this case, the first ayam gepok in Singapore. Ayam Gepok Anakmak has been around since 2020 , when it began as a home-based business. In 2025 , they finally settled at Ang Mo Kio , where they often serve hundreds of plates a day to a crowd of regulars, students and curious foodies.
Something I noticed right off the bat was their serving area. They had 2 gigantic mortar and pestle sets, one filled with their signature cashew sauce and another with their spicy chilli or sambal. It’s not often businesses have the time to hand-grind their sauces, so this immediately impressed me.
The thing is, ayam gepok is nothing new around Southeast Asia. Countries like Indonesia and Malaysia have so many spots that serve ayam gepok with even more variations, like cheesy ayam gepok and matcha ayam gepok. Luckily for us, Ayam Gepok Anakmak chose to stick to the classics. Now that they’ve found their home at Sinfoodie Kopitiam , it looks like their stall is here to stay.
What to order at Ayam Gepok Anakmak
For those of you who are familiar, ayam gepok is very similar to ayam penyet , a dish that is much more common in Singapore. The only difference is how violently you treat the chicken. Ayam penyet is crushed, giving the meat an almost flaky quality, and the skin is noticeably crisper, whereas ayam gepok is flattened, so the meat is tenderised without losing its juiciness.
My friend and I have wanted to try this dish for a long time. We never got around to it, what with life getting in the way. So believe me when I tell you, I literally jumped at the chance to eat there. To make the most of our experience, we ordered both the Ayam Gepok Original Supersized (S$12.40) and Ayam Gepok Berempah Supersized (S$13.90) .
If you couldn’t tell, we were hungry. And the supersized option includes all the bonus sides that I feel are essential to ayam gepok. Though I will say they did run out of the fried kangkong, so that was a bit of a bummer.
Pondok Pantai Timur: Beautifully presented ayam penyet with sambal-filled plates in Ubi
Let’s start with the Ayam Gepok Original Supersized (S$12.40). I can tell out of the gate that this is exactly how ayam gepok should be. The chicken was juicy and extra tender from the flattening. The marinade has seeped into every fibre of the chicken. The skin has that happy balance between chewy and crisp.
And then came the big brother, Ayam Gepok Berempah Supersized (S$13.90). The chicken is one big flavour bomb. The krisik (fried crispy seasoning), when mixed with the rice, changes the dish completely. The rice becomes so much more flavourful, filled with the taste of garlic, onion and a slightly bitter fragrance of lemongrass. The chicken was slightly drier due to how intensely it’s fried, but that made the skin extra crispy — definitely my preference of the 2.
Now come the real stars, the sides. The cashew and chilli combo was completely unexpected. Before trying ayam gepok, the only similar experience I can draw from is the sambal kacang , dipped with satay. Let me tell you, it was nothing like that. The sauce was almost buttery. Mixed with the chilli, it added a unique depth to the dish. It was the perfect balance of richness and spice. And boy, was it spicy. My spice tolerance is relatively high, and even I felt a pretty harsh kick, so I suggest ordering the Level 3 at most.
Lastly, the trio. Bergedil, fried cabbage and a fried egg. I would love to go into detail about each item, but this article would end up a novel. A romance novel, because the addition of these sides can only be described as romantic — the luscious runny egg, the fluffy and delicate bergedil and my personal favourite, the fried cabbage.
At first glance, the cabbage looked burnt, harsh and rough around the edges. But when I committed myself to a bite, it completely took me by surprise. It was soft, with a slight crunch. It had a lingering sweetness that made me come back to it over and over. Part of me even wondered if the entire dish would be better if it were just the chicken and the fried cabbage. After tasting all these sides along with the rice, I am even sadder that I couldn’t taste the fried kangkong.
Who is Ayam Gepok Anakmak best for?
Ayam Gepok Anakmak is perfect for someone who wants to explore popular Indonesian dishes made the authentic way. Sometimes you just want something more grounded and familiar, but unique in its own way without being gimmicky. You will find very similar flavours across Southeast Asia, but the way it is slightly different here makes every bite interesting.
This spot is perfect for those of you in need of something heavy and hearty. The food court is also just opposite a school, so you’d see students rushing and lining up for a huge plate of ayam gepok. I genuinely envy them. I wish I had something this good close by as a kid.
How to get to Ayam Gepok Anakmak
…
summary: Ayam Gepok Anakmak is a stall at Sinfoodie Kopitiam in Ang Mo Kio serving ayam gepok, an Indonesian-style flattened fried chicken, with hand-ground cashew sauce and sambal. The Original and Berempah supersized sets cost S$12.40 and S$13.90, with sides included. Best suited to those after a hearty, traditional plate, though some items sell out by around 3pm.

PastaMania has put four Christmas dishes on its menu from 16 November to 31 December 2026, and the cheapest of them is a dessert: a S$9.90 Pistachio Kunafa Pizza.
The line-up runs under the name Holly Jolly Pasta Christmas! and covers one pasta, two pizzas and a bake. Prices run from S$9.90 to S$16.
The kunafa pizza
Kunafa is the Middle Eastern dessert built on fine shredded pastry, and PastaMania turns it into a sweet pizza. The Pistachio Kunafa Pizza is topped with katifi, the shredded pastry strands, plus pistachio nuts, pistachio sauce and chocolate sauce, and costs S$9.90.
Pistachio Kunafa Pizza, S$9.90. Image: PastaMania
The savoury three
The Smoked Chicken Sausage Pasta, at S$13, comes with baby potato and broccoli in a shallot mustard cream sauce and is finished with a smoked chicken sausage.
The Black Truffle Honey Chicken Pizza is the only dish in two sizes: S$13 for a 7-inch and S$16 for a 10-inch. It carries fried chicken bites, pineapple, cranberry and baby rocket, finished with smoked aioli and truffle honey.
The Chicken Sausage Shepherd’s Pie, at S$16, layers minced chicken under creamy potato, then adds smoked chicken sausage, smoky pizza sauce and melted mozzarella. PastaMania frames it as a festive spin on a family classic.
Where you can order it
The festive menu is not available at the PastaMania Pronto outlets at Pioneer Mall, Toa Payoh and Changi Airport Terminal 2.
The dishes cannot be combined with other discounts, privileges or reward redemptions, and that includes the TriplePlus programme.
PastaMania keeps the right to change the terms without notice.
Details
• Holly Jolly Pasta Christmas!, 16 November to 31 December 2026
• Pistachio Kunafa Pizza, S$9.90
• Smoked Chicken Sausage Pasta, S$13
• Black Truffle Honey Chicken Pizza, S$13 (7-inch) or S$16 (10-inch)
• Chicken Sausage Shepherd’s Pie, S$16
• Not available at PastaMania Pronto at Pioneer Mall, Toa Payoh and Changi Airport Terminal 2
• Not valid with other discounts or TriplePlus rewards
summary: PastaMania's Holly Jolly Pasta Christmas! menu runs from 16 November to 31 December 2026 with four dishes from S$9.90 to S$16, led by a Pistachio Kunafa Pizza. Three Pronto outlets are left out.

Whenever I visit Queensway Shopping Centre , I always pass by Hei Lun Shi Tang , an old-school food stall on the 2nd floor of the shopping centre. With Taiwanese food being one of my favourite cuisines, I do wonder why I didn’t patronise this shop sooner.
Hei Lun Shi Tang’s unique selling point is the fact that its rice dishes are served in metal bento boxes, adding an extra layer of nostalgia to the stall. They offer a range of classic Taiwanese dishes like braised pork rice, scallion oil noodles and even curry rice!
Hei Lun Shi Tang operates within a shared space as another cafe, so you can choose to sit outside next to the main kitchen, or opt to sit inside. I ordered a few dishes and got ready to tuck into my meal.
What I tried at Hei Lun Shi Tang
Unlike many other Taiwanese places that only offer braised pork rice, Hei Lun Shi Tang gives diners the option to choose from 5 types of meat: braised pork, stewed pork belly, pork cutlet, fried chicken and braised chicken. Each option is available at S$7 for a small portion and S$8 for a large portion . I wanted to try all the meats, so I got the Signature Mixed (S$10) , which came topped with all 5 of Hei Lun Shi Tang’s meat options.
I started off with the braised pork, which was tender and incredibly flavourful. There was an adequate ratio of meat to fat, and the marination and sauce made the braised pork both sweet and savoury.
The pork cutlet came as a moderately-sized pork slice. It tasted similar to the braised pork, just that texture-wise, it was a little firmer and chewier.
The stewed pork belly was delightful, as the fat portion of the belly slice had a lovely melt-in-the-mouth texture. The meat portion was flavourful and well-marinated, albeit slightly dry. However, it wasn’t tough at all. The fried chicken was yet another great element, with a crispy and umami skin and tender meat. The fried chicken was seasoned very well, with a good dispersion of flavour all throughout.
The final element, the braised chicken, was my favourite of all 5 meats. The texture was what made it stand out, as it was incredibly tender and fell apart easily. It was also very flavourful as the marination soaked all the way through the meat, making every part of the chicken as tasty.
The Signature Mixed rice also came with a side of stewed cabbage and preserved vegetables for some added fibre. The preserved vegetables gave the dish a bit of saltiness, balancing out the sweetness and savouriness of the rest of the dish. I enjoyed Hei Lun Shi Tang’s Signature Mixed rice, though I did find the price to be a bit on the higher end.
Next up, I had Hei Lun Shi Tang’s Curry Braised Pork Rice available in an S$9 or S$10 portion. I opted for the S$9 portion, which came with an adequate amount of rice and meat. Half of the rice was topped with braised pork while the other half was covered in curry, chicken, potatoes and carrots.
Like the braised pork in the Signature Mixed , this braised pork in the Curry Braised Pork Rice was tender and flavourful. I found the amount of braised pork served on the rice to be quite generous.
The curry reminded me of Japanese curry, and it made the rice a little mushier. The curry wasn’t very spicy and wasn’t too salty either. I liked the softness of the potatoes and carrots served on the dish, and the curry chicken pieces were a little firmer than the chicken on the Signature Mixed , but was tender nonetheless.
Taiwan Fan Bao: Taiwanese-style cai fan with saba fish, chicken thigh & $3.50 pork belly buns
I didn’t find this dish to be all that outstanding, but it definitely satisfied both my braised pork rice and curry rice cravings at the same time.
Hei Lun Shi Tang offers Scallion Oil Noodles (S$4.50) as one of its noodle dishes, and you could also opt to get a meat topping. I ordered the Fried Chicken Noodles (S$6.50) and was served a bowl of scallion oil noodles topped with fried chicken pieces, scallions and a half-boiled egg.
The noodles had a bouncy yet soft texture, which I adored. I could taste the slight fragrance of the scallion oil throughout the noodles, though the flavour was slightly too mild for my preferences. The fried chicken was crispy and well-seasoned just like the ones in the Signature Mixed . I liked the pairing of the chicken and the noodles, though parts of the chicken became a little less crunchy from being in contact with the slightly wet noodles. Definitely consume this dish a little faster to avoid the chicken from getting soggy!
Finally, I tried Hei Lun Shi Tang’s Daily Soup and Braised Pork Rice Set (S$7) . The stall’s daily soup changes based on the day of the week: I visited on a Sunday, so I got to enjoy the Snow Pear Pork Rib Soup . Other days offer soups like Watercress Pork Rib Soup and Herbal Chicken Soup !
The Snow Pear Pork Rib Soup had a clear and refreshing taste, with a light sweetness emerging from the snow pears. The pork ribs were tender and soft and the soup as a whole was comforting and homely.
…
summary: Hei Lun Shi Tang in Queensway Shopping Centre serves old-school Taiwanese rice and noodle dishes, including nostalgic bento box meals and daily home-style soups. While prices sit slightly higher than typical hawker fare, the stall delivers generous portions and tender, well-marinated meats across a broad menu. It is best suited for shoppers and nearby visitors seeking comforting, authentic Taiwanese comfort food rather than a standalone dining trip.
title: Hei Lun Shi Tang: Comforting Taiwanese dishes served in metal bento boxes in Queensway Shopping Centre

Step into the world of Disney’s Frozen , where Arendelle comes alive. Experience the Orchestra of the Music Makers performing composer Christophe Beck’s GRAMMY-nominated score live to the film, accompanied by live vocal performances of the film’s beloved songs, including “Let It Go” performed by Idina Menzel .
Calling all Frozen fans: Only on 3 April 2027 , with 2 showtimes at 2.30pm and 7.30pm , this is a film with a live orchestra you wouldn’t want to miss at the Esplanade Concert Hall .
Credit: SISTIC Singapore
Olaf is awaiting! Bring your family and journey to Arendelle with Princess Anna, Olaf, Kristoff, and his loyal reindeer Sven to find Elsa and save the Kingdom from eternal winter. Come dressed in your best winter look, or step out as Elsa or Anna!
Do note that this concert doesn’t permit admission for infants in arms and children under 3 years old. Children aged 3 and above must purchase an admission ticket .
Prices & Seats
Credit: SISTIC Singapore
Standard tickets (Cat 1 to 4) start from S$78 , with Premier and Esplanade Box tickets at S$138 each, and Restricted View (Cat 2 and 3) from S$98 . Guests are strongly encouraged to be seated at least half an hour before the performance start time, as admission may not be granted once the performance has begun. Tickets can be purchased here !
Do note that photography and videography are not permitted during the show, and the performance runs for 135 minutes , with one intermission . Gather your friends and family, secure the tickets, and see you on 3 April next year !

Romantic bus routes in Singapore
For the partners scratching their heads for date ideas that won’t break the bank, look no further than our humble buses for a dose of inspiration. Besides being the perfect excuse to share earbuds and listen to a curated playlist, these scenic bus routes also double as an effortless date itinerary.
From waterfront views that look like a scene from Spirited Away to misty open fields straight out of Pride & Prejudice , our list of romantic bus routes is perfect for cosying up with your partner and pretending you’re in a music video .
1. Bus 14
An Insta-worthy trip to the east
With candy-coloured Peranakan Houses and 101 Insta-worthy cafes to explore around Katong, Bus 14 is the one to take for a date straight out of a Wes Anderson film.
Starting from Clementi Interchange, you’ll cruise past nostalgic HDB estates, historic landmarks like CHIJMES and Raffles Hotel , and postcard-worthy views of the Singapore River as you make your way through the city centre.
Image adapted from: Syaqil Sarafian via Facebook
Get your camera ready for a quick wefie as the bus crosses over the Merdeka Bridge , with a picture-perfect backdrop of the Kallang River and Marina Bay skyline.
Image credit: Tricia Teong
Once you’re in the east, alight at the Opp Roxy Sq (92111) bus stop along East Coast Road and cross over to get a hearty bowl of laksa from the famous 328 Katong Laksa . Explore the charming Katong neighbourhood as you take an 11-minute stroll towards Cafe Wabi Sabi for some afternoon tea in a retro shophouse.
Image credit: Katie Platt Willes via Facebook
Strike a pose at the iconic Peranakan Houses just around the corner, or spice up your scenic stroll with a colour-hunting challenge and piece together a collage of the neighbourhood’s most aesthetic corners to post on your socials.
Add a little more whimsy to your trip by popping by the Heartware Store and Gallery , just a 3-minute walk away from the Peranakan Houses. You’ll find pop-up exhibitions featuring international artists and adorable prints and trinkets to take home as matching souvenirs.
From now till 22nd November 2026 , the gallery is hosting the Henshin Atomic Daydream exhibition by Jakarta-born illustrator Ardhira Putra. Inspired by a combination of superheroes and retro-pop nostalgia, the exhibition features several artworks done by the artist, alongside a merch store with exclusive collectables.
Route: From Clementi Interchange to Bedok Interchange
Total stops: 75
Total duration: 140 minutes
2. Bus 51
A nature trail made for Strava-obsessed couples
Singapore may be tiny, but our abundance of green spaces makes hiking and jogging some of the most convenient and wallet-friendly date ideas. After all, nothing says “I love you” quite like suffering through a sweaty hike in this relentless humidity and making it out side-by-side.
Hop on Bus 51 and kick off your journey through the west, with Pandan Reservoir being one of the first few stops you’ll want to hit. When you reach the Blk 408 (20149) bus stop, hop off and continue your adventure on foot. An 8-minute walk later, and you’ll arrive at the reservoir.
Image credit: Hongbin via Google Maps
Start off strong with a 6km jog along the well-paved trail that follows the edge of the water, and you might even spot a few otters if you’re lucky.
For a fun side-quest, rent a double open-deck kayak from Pandan Lodge and enjoy a leisurely ride together.
Image credit: @cheng_lyoh via Instagram
Give your legs a break and hop back on the bus until you reach the Opp Labrador Pk Stn (15149) stop. You’ll find yourself at Labrador Nature Reserve after a 12-minute trek. Soak in the sea breeze, and saunter along the 330m-long Bukit Chermin Boardwalk . On one side of the boardwalk, you’ll spot conserved colonial bungalows and rocky shores, and sweeping views of the sea on the other.
If a 330m stroll sounds too easy, the coastal boardwalk makes up just one section of the full 2.1km Labrador Nature & Coastal Walk , so you can still close those rings.
Once you’ve soaked in the view, get back on the bus and head to your final stop, Alexandra Retail Centre (15041) . From there, it’s a 16-minute hike to HortPark , one of the more underrated gems along the Southern Ridges trail . The 23ha park is the perfect resting spot for a picnic or casual stroll around, with over 10 themed gardens to explore.
Image credit: NParks
The Therapeutic Garden , designed in line with the principles of horticultural therapy, features a romantic gazebo where you’ll get to slow down and enjoy some uninterrupted quality time. It may not be the iconic glass gazebo from the Sixteen Going on Seventeen duet scene, but it has all the romantic, whimsical charm of a setting straight out of The Sound of Music .
Turn the romance up a notch at the Butterfly Garden , where the winged residents are sure to get your heart fluttering.
…
summary: AKA the perfect excuse to share earbuds and lean on their shoulder.
title: 10 Most Romantic Bus Routes In SG – Scenic Views, Best Pit Stops & Budget-Friendly Activities

body:
IKEA’s Christmas buffet is returning in December
Image credit: IKEA
IKEA Singapore is part of some of my fondest memories. Growing up, it’s been my family’s favourite weekend dinner spot, and their meatballs are still one of my favourite childhood bites. If you’re an IKEA meatball enthusiast like me, I come bearing good news: IKEA’s buffet is back in anticipation of the Christmas season, featuring a spread of traditional Swedish Christmas buffet dishes.
The standout this time round is the Beef Goulash With Carrots and Potatoes , a hearty Hungarian stew made by simmering beef, carrots, potatoes, onions, and other aromatics, such as paprika, in a tomato-based broth. The result is a comforting, slightly smoky soup that’s best eaten with bread.
Image credit: IKEA
Europe’s long been known for its cheeses, and Sweden is no exception, so it’s only right to try IKEA’s Hushallsost Cheese , a traditional Swedish cow’s-milk cheese. For the uninitiated, it’s a semi-hard cheese made from cow’s whole milk, with a mild taste and subtle flavours of clear salt and fresh acidity. Due to its creamy texture and high fat content, it’s best savoured with Rye & Multigrain Crispbread .
Of course, you can’t leave without a plate of their iconic Swedish meatballs with Cream Sauce , made from a blend of beef and pork, and served with their signature cream sauce and lingonberry jam. For those who can’t eat pork or beef, get their Plant Balls with Cream Sauce instead, a vegetarian option with the same garnishes. From my years of experience at IKEA Food Market, both are best enjoyed with the Mashed Potatoes and Penne Pasta with Tomato Sauce .
Image credit: IKEA
To round off the meal, get their new festive desserts: the Belgium Chocolate Log Cake and Lingonberry Vanilla Log Cake . The former is a fan favourite, featuring a soft, fluffy sponge cake filled with indulgent chocolate buttercream, while the other is a fruity variant, with prominent notes of lingonberry and vanilla.
IKEA Singapore’s Christmas buffet is available at their three outlets for just $29.90++ per adult . Unfortunately, tickets for their Jurong and Alexandra outlets have sold out. However, ticket sales for their Tampines outlet will start on 17 November 2026 , so set your alarms if you wish to snag some of those prized tickets.
Image credit: IKEA
If you’ve missed the date, fret not; IKEA is also introducing some new festive dishes on their regular menu. From now till 3 January 2027 , you can order their Rosemary Chicken Set ($18.70++) : a whole chicken leg seasoned with rosemary, and served with a vegetable medley of broccoli, carrots, and edamame, plus mashed potatoes and cream sauce. The set also comes with a bowl of mushroom soup and a mini Christmas log cake. Then there’s the Boneless Pork Knuckle Set ($27.70++) , which features a roasted pork knuckle served with mashed potatoes and cream sauce. The pork is said to be tender on the inside, with a satisfyingly crunchy exterior. There is also the aforementioned Mini Christmas Log Cake ($4.90++) and a Christmas Cold Plate ($7.90++) , the latter comprising slices of smoked salmon, honey-baked ham, shrimp, and more.
If you’re looking for more buffets for this coming holiday season, read our guide to 1-for-1 buffet deals in 2026 . Otherwise, check out Cedele’s new Christmas menu for a Nordic-inspired Christmas spread.
Website | Full list of outlets
IKEA is not halal-certified.

Feature image adapted from IKEA.

Best catering companies in Singapore
Every year for Chinese New Year , my family and relatives come together for a gathering, a tradition that we started many years ago. As all of us are huge foodies, we typically hire different catering companies each year for a change. After many years of such gatherings, we compiled a list of catering companies that met our expectations. Together with recommendations from some of my peers, here are 17 catering companies that can help ease the burden of your party-hosting journey.
P.S.: If you’re still looking to impress your ah ma for a weeknight dinner out, our guide to the best porridge buffets has you covered.
Best catering companies in Singapore, in a nutshell:
• For family dinners: Chilli Manis – Award-winning Peranakan cuisine with a modern twist
• For weddings and atas events: Charlie’s Catering – Highly rated buffets by hotel-trained chefs
• For casual tea time sesh: Delifrance – Wide variety of French pastries and refreshing drinks
• For affordable office parties: Deli Hub Catering – Affordable bentos from just $4.50+
1. Lavish Catering
Image credit: Lavish Catering
Planning an event comes with plenty of moving parts, which is why having a dependable catering partner can make all the difference. Halal-certified Lavish Catering specialises in delivering professional, end-to-end catering services for a wide variety of occasions, ranging from corporate functions to family celebrations and milestone occasions, like a birthday. Alongside chef-crafted menus, clients can expect polished presentation, timely delivery, attentive service, and optional cleanup support, helping events run smoothly from start to finish.
Lavish Catering has flexible dining solutions to suit different event formats and guest counts. Their Premium Buffet Spreads (from $26+ per person) are ideal for large-scale gatherings and VIP events, featuring dishes designed to impress. For cocktail receptions and networking events, the Canapés & Cocktail Catering (from $25+ per person) menu provides elegant bite-sized selections that are easy to enjoy while mingling. Corporate teams can also opt for Executive Bento Boxes (from $18+ per set) for meetings and seminars, while Mini Buffet Sets (from $398+) with self-heating functionality offer a fuss-free option for smaller gatherings and home celebrations.
Plan your next event via the Lavish Dine Catering website or WhatsApp them at 9776 3071 .
Lavish Catering is halal-certified.
2. Rasel Catering Singapore
Image credit: Rasel Catering Singapore
Rasel Catering Singapore is a trusted corporate caterer that covers everything from networking sessions and launch events to social gatherings, with quality cuisine, professional service, and seamless execution. That leaves you free to focus on your guests instead of the logistics.
Rasel’s buffet spread has also been refreshed with a number of new dishes, so there’s more variety at every gathering. New additions include Sous Vide Duck Breast with Orange Cinnamon Sauce , Gambas Al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Prawns) , and Baked Fish with Roasted Garlic Aioli & Burnt Onion Cream. There’s also a bold Roasted Peri-Peri Chicken with Tangy Pepper Sauce and a comforting Pasta Al Funghi . Save room for handcrafted desserts such as the Pistachio Kunafa Tart too.
The festive menus change every season, with new dishes inspired by the latest food trends and contemporary flavours, so regulars always have something new to try. Whatever the occasion, there’s a package to suit it. Choose from Buffet Catering (from $19.90+ per person) , a High Tea Cocktail Reception (from $15.90+ per person) , or a Canapes Reception (from $30+ per person) . Running a workshop? The Half Day Seminar Packages start from $24+ per person , and you can add Interactive Live Stations (from $6+ per person) to liven things up.
Order from Rasel Catering Singapore via their website .
Rasel Catering Singapore is halal-certified.
3. Deli Hub Catering
Image credit: Deli Hub Catering
Those looking for a halal corporate caterer ought to consider Deli Hub Catering , one of Singapore’s foremost. Their offerings comprise buffets, catering for corporate events and seminars, trendy live stations, high tea selections, and bentos, all tailored to suit a variety of different occasions and needs. What’s more, their menus include both local and international dishes that cater to different preferences and dietary requirements—you get to pick from the likes of Sambal Fried Rice, Spring Onion Fish, Honey Glazed Chicken and plenty more. Plus, they have Healthier Choice menus, which are Health Promotion Board-approved!
Their regular buffet catering menus start at $13.99+ per person . Bentos, on the other hand, start from an extremely affordable $4.50+ per person . Having been in the industry for nearly two decades, they understand the nuances of your events. All dishes and set-ups are handled by pro chefs and caterers, so there’s absolutely no fuss for the organisers involved.
…

Coalfields Retail Mall is quickly becoming a spot worth checking out for shopping and good food in Sungai Buloh. Beyond the familiar names, this neighbourhood mall has a growing mix of cafes, restaurants, and eateries serving everything from comforting local favourites to hearty Western fare and sweet treats.
Here are 10 of the best food spots at Coalfields Retail Mall to add to your next makan plans .

1. Andra by Gula Cakery (UG-09 & 10)
Andra by Gula Cakery is a cosy spot for good, hearty food and, of course, a little something sweet afterwards. The menu covers a good mix of Western and local favourites, so there’s more to it than just dropping by for the cakes Gula Cakery is known for.
For a proper meal, you can tuck into Grilled Chicken Chop , Grilled Lamb , Creamy Cajun Pasta , Chicken & Mushroom Carbonara , or Swedish Meatballs . Those who prefer local flavours can go for Nasi Daging Dendeng , Gula’s Signature Nasi Goreng , and local platters.
If you’re visiting around lunchtime, the sets are worth a look too, with options such as Aglio Olio Crispy Chicken , Mee Goreng , Breaded Chicken Chop , and Grilled Chicken Chop with Rice , priced at around RM25 .
Of course, saving room for dessert is almost a given here. Gula Cakery has over 200 cake flavours in its repertoire, with choices ranging from Chocolate Cheesecake to its signature GC Matilda Chocolate Cake . You can also find Tiramisu in a Jar , Panna Cotta , and fruit pavlovas like Berry Pavlova .
+6016 216 0977
Daily: 10am – 10pm
Instagram | Website
2. The Social (GF-03)
Credit – The Social
If you’re looking for somewhere to settle in for a long lunch, catch up over drinks, or enjoy a proper dinner, The Social is a familiar name worth knowing. With several established outlets across the Klang Valley, including Bangsar, 163 Retail Park, and Desa ParkCity, the neighbourhood favourite brings its extensive food and drinks menu to Coalfields Retail Mall.
Credit – The Social
The menu is a little bit of everything, spanning local comfort food, Asian favourites, and Western classics. You can start with small bites like Chiew Yim Squid , Mantou With Marinated Lamb , Chicken 65 , or KFC Korean Fried Chicken , before moving on to heartier options.
Local staples include Nasi Lemak , Nasi Goreng , Nyonya Curry Laksa , and Crab Kway Teow , while those craving Western fare can opt for Hainanese Chicken Chop , Traditional Fish & Chips , Shepherd’s Pie , or The Social Air Flown Ribeye Steak . There are also burgers, pastas, salads, sandwiches, and Japanese-inspired rolls to choose from.
A couple of house specialities are worth looking out for, too. The Aromatic Crispy Duck comes with mandarin pancakes, sweet plum sauce, chilli oil, and fresh cucumber and spring onions, while the The Social Oriental Sharing Platter brings together spring rolls, chicken otak-otak Muar, chicken karaage , and Chicken 65.
+603 7732 9225
Daily: 11.30am – 12am
Instagram | Website
3. Lisette’s Cafe & Bakery (GF-03A)
Credit – Lisette’s
A familiar name among cafe-goers, Lisette’s Cafe & Bakery has built a following with its neighbourhood outlets in Bangsar, Mont Kiara and Coalfields Retail Park. Known for its artisan bakes, hearty brunch fare and generous selection of vegetarian and vegan dishes, the cafe offers plenty of reasons to linger over a meal.
Credit – Gee Gee, Will i am & Resh Rayan via Google Reviews
The menu is considerably more extensive than your usual café spread, covering everything from small bites and salads to burgers, local favourites and Western mains. For something a little different, try the Black Rice Nasi Lemak (RM30) , which pairs organic black rice with chicken curry, prawn sambal and the usual condiments.
Other options include Johor Laksa (RM30) , Kimchee Fried Rice (RM32) and Katsu Curry (RM35) . Those after lighter fare can opt for the Greenest Green Salad (RM28) or the vegan-friendly Power Bowl (RM34) , packed with quinoa, avocado, edamame and curried chickpeas.

I get FOMO. Badly. Hearing a few of my friends talk about how amazing Chinese noodle soup is makes my mouth water and my heart ache because it’s usually not halal. So when I set my sights on Afanti Chinese Halal Food on Arab Street , I was focused on their authentic beef lamian.
Afanti is owned and operated by Muslims from Xinjiang, China. And they didn’t arrive empty-handed; they brought their recipes, training, and even some spices that originate from Xinjiang. I honestly can’t think of a more authentic experience apart from booking a flight and heading to Xinjiang myself.
When my sister and I entered the restaurant, we were flooded by warmth. The lighting was so orange, it looked like the surface of the sun. The walls were painted and sculpted with arches that you’d see in a mosque.
Colourful decorative wall plates contrasted nicely against the beige background. There were tapestries, too, with slight imperfections that made them look hand-stitched. From the interior alone, we knew this place was the real deal.
What to order at Afanti Chinese Halal Food
Their menu is extensive, to say the least. There were many interesting, new and also familiar items across their many categories of dishes. But my sister and I were locked in. Probably melodramatic, but I looked at her and said, “We know what we’re here for,” with a smouldering intensity.
In less than 5 minutes, we had ordered the Beef Lamian Set Meal A (S$14.80) and a Chinese Hamburger (S$7.80) . It arrived surprisingly quickly, considering the number of people in that small restaurant.
Let’s start with the Chinese Hamburger. This was one of the items on the menu with which I was familiar. Chinese roti has been very popular lately but this style is quite different.
The pastry was very reminiscent of an American biscuit, the kind you find at Popeyes. Instead of being flaky, it is more dense and buttery. And much like the biscuits at Popeyes, the pastry was quite dry. It was also rather bland on its own.
Fortunately, there was the beef filling, which can only be described one way: meaty. The savoury, meaty flavour was extremely tasty.
After every bite, I could feel a slight numbing sensation on my tongue but the chilli was also surprisingly sweet, giving the dish a sweet-and-savoury balance that made it very satisfying.
Malaysian Hup Kee Fishball Noodle: Stellar handmade yellowtail fishballs & must-try Malaysian-style noodles in AMK
And now, for the dish we’ve all been waiting for, the Beef Lamian Set Meal A. As we looked around at our neighbours, we noticed that almost every table had ordered this. Perhaps it’s the combination of reasonable pricing and popularity?
When it arrived, we were first surprised by how large the bowl was. The photo really doesn’t do it justice; it was huge . I watched the sheen of fat particles dance across the surface of the soup, looking like a live mosaic. It felt like a shame to disturb the performance.
But I was hungry, so I got to work. When the chopstick broke the surface of the fatty soup, I was met with heavy resistance. They are generous with the noodles. While I wish there were more beef slices, I really can’t complain.
Honestly, the star of the show is the soup. For most of my life, I’ve had very rich soups, often caked with spices and flavour. Because of that, I never understood when someone described soup as ‘clean’. Well, this soup is clean .
The chilli added a peppery note to an overall very beefy broth. It was perfectly seasoned, and not too salty or herby in any way. The coriander added a freshness that made the soup even brighter. I genuinely could drink it like water. It also clings to and coats the noodles, which was another delight.
This bowl is served with hand-pulled noodles. The main difference is the texture but it also had a lovely bounce and chew that reminded me of mochi, of all things. The sides of the noodles were curled and thinner than the centre.
This was so fun to eat; I felt like a child playing around. The noodles also carried the soup very well; every bite was seasoned with the numbing spice and beefy richness. My only qualms with this dish are the intense numbing and the beef slices themselves.
The beef, when compared to the rest of the dish, might not be to most people’s liking. The meat was rather chewy with a surprising lack of flavour. I found myself ignoring the beef after a while to have more of the soup and noodles.
Personally, I like the texture. I prefer a slight chew to the protein, but I understand most prefer the meat to be more tender. To each their own, I suppose.
Who is Afanti Chinese Halal Food best for?
…
summary: Afanti Chinese Halal Food is a Muslim-owned Xinjiang restaurant at 39 Arab Street, known for hand-pulled beef lamian in a clean, beefy broth. The Beef Lamian Set Meal A costs S$14.80 and the Chinese Hamburger S$7.80, though the beef slices were chewy and the dining room runs warm and tight. It suits diners after an authentic Xinjiang bowl near Bugis who can wait around 15 minutes for a table.
title: Afanti Chinese Halal Food: Xinjiang chefs serve authentic hand-pulled lamian & Chinese hamburgers

Home Team Festival 2026
What is the Home Team ? If HomeTeamNS comes to mind, you’re on the right track – but only partly. Behind that familiar name sits 11 Home Team Departments, including the Singapore Police Force (SPF) under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), each playing a distinct role in keeping Singapore safe and secure.
No shame if you didn’t, but here’s your chance to find out more about what the Home Team is all about at the upcoming Home Team Festival 2026 , which rolls around every 3 years. Everyone’s invited to this free event!
Note: All images for illustrative purposes only.
When & where is Home Team Festival 2026 taking place?
Image credit: Singapore Police Force
This year’s festival runs from 20th to 22nd November 2026 at Halls 401-406 , Suntec Convention Centre .
Here are the festival hours:
• 20th Nov: 11am-9pm
• 21st Nov: 1pm-9pm
• 22nd Nov: 9am-9pm
As mentioned, this festival only takes place once every 3 years, so you better believe this is the Home Team’s largest public showcase, where you can see a full display of its technologies, innovation, and cutting-edge capabilities in action.
Try live-firing guns at the shooting range
Image credit: HTF 2023 – Home Team Festival 2023
If you think you’ve got what it takes to be a sniper IRL, put your skills to the test at the shooting range , using non-lethal equipment, of course.
Rest assured that this is conducted under the expert supervision of officers from the Singapore Police Force (SPF) Special Operations Command and Singapore Prisons Emergency Action Response (SPEAR) Force, so put your game consoles aside and try the real deal at the Home Team Festival 2026.
There’s no age limit at this range, but you do have to be at least 1.1m tall to try it out.
Test your baton strike
Image credit: HTF 2023 – Home Team Festival 2023
For those of you who are less American Sniper , more Kung Fu Panda , you’ll be happy to know that you can unleash your inner Ryu or Chun Li at Fight the Manikin .
Try using a Straight Extendable Baton (SEB) on a training manikin to test your strike accuracy. Organised by SPS, this gives you an idea of the skills, discipline, and control required to use the SEB for self-defence and to handle prison disturbances.
This station is open to everyone of all ages, with no height restrictions.
Get up close with our K-9 unit & watch SCDF search dog demonstrations
Image credit: SPF
Think you’re good enough to take on the SPF’s canine teams and SCDF’s search dogs? See how you fare against their 4-legged colleagues in Human vs Dog , where you can compete against trained police dogs to locate contraband items, or in a Tug of War game.
Image credit: SCDF
If that’s too physical for you, let them bowl you over at the stage demonstrations , where SCDF search dogs showcase their agility navigating rubble and debris, track down hidden accelerants, and locate “missing persons”.
Escape a “building on fire” & play Overcooked , Home Teams-style
Over at SCDF’s Smoke-logged Confined Maze , you’ll find out what it takes to escape a building on fire. Think: dark, smoke-filled obstacle course that may be absolute fun in this controlled environment, but 100% a life skill to remember in case of an emergency.
Then, there’s Dayroom Dash , a la Overcooked , Singapore Prison Service edition. This fast-paced co-op game will have you and your team mate playing Correctional Unit Officers managing a busy Correctional Unit (CU), juggling operations which include facilitating inmates’ rehabilitation activities, and responding to inmates’ disputes.
Will your CU emerge unscathed, or will it be cooked? Guess you’ll have to play and find out.
Guide a humanoid robot through an obstacle course
Image credit: Home Team Festival
If game consoles are still your preferred mode of play, try your hand at guiding HTX’s humanoid robot through an obstacle-laden course to reach a post-blast site and uncover key evidence, then bring them back to your base within a specified timeframe.
Step into the shoes of a CNB officer
Image credit: Central Narcotics Bureau
The thrills don’t stop there – over at Drug Buster by the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB), there are 2 games for the entire family to join.
First, a physical search and detect game , set up in a mock HDB unit. This kid-friendly game lets you test your instincts and awareness, to see how many drug exhibits you can uncover in a limited time.
For the bigger kids aged 12 and above, there’s a VR game that puts you in the shoes of a CNB officer to conduct first-hand covert surveillance and intelligence gathering.
Catch the MHA Ops demo & the latest Home Team tech on display
Image credit: Singapore Police Force
Another stage performance that you cannot miss is the MHA Ops Demo , or Ministry of Home Affairs Operations Demo – an action-packed theatrical production that’s inspired by real-life Home Team operations, showing how different Home Team Departments work together as One Home Team.
Image credit: Singapore Police Force

Who needs to cook up a storm when you’ve got these Christmas catering services in Singapore at your fingertips? No matter how big or small your holiday party is, these professional caterers will deliver gourmet spreads – complete with seasonal specialties and decadent desserts. Take your pick from full-fledged buffets with glittering setups, ready-to-serve mini buffets for small groups, and halal-certified menus. Trust us, these top Christmas catering services in Singapore mean serious business. With the feast sorted, check out Christmas in Singapore guide so you don’t miss out on other festive must-knows.
Why trust this guide
Every year, during Christmas, our team combs through the festive menus, gift sets, hampers, and turkey and log cake offerings. We compare notes, taste menus where we can, and research everything else, so you don’t have to spend time figuring out what’s worth spending your money on. We prioritise stand-outs over exhaustive lists, we fact-check prices and availability before publishing, and we update guides as new launches come in. When in doubt, we ask around – our community is generous with its seasonal picks.
Best Christmas 2026 food catering services in Singapore
1. Elsie’s Kitchen
Photography: Elsie’s Kitchen
On the search for a halal-certified feast this Christmas? Meet Elsie’s Kitchen, one of Singapore’s pioneering caterers. These folks are known for dishing out mouthwatering Asian delicacies, and you can spot these Asian cooking influences even in the Christmas catering menu.
If you’re hosting a larger group of 25 or more, go for the full buffet packages. The Festive Wanderlust Indulgence is the most premium of the lot, featuring 12 courses and a Dubai chocolate-inspired dessert for a sweet finale. Alternatively, order the Merry Miles mini buffet sets that caters for intimate get-togethers of 10 guests or more. We’ve spotted prawn gambas al ajillo, honey and brown sugar dijon-glazed turkey, and chicken meatballs in the line-up.
Best for: Halal-certified spreads for gatherings of any size

Order from Elsie’s Kitchen
2. Rasel Catering
Photography: Rasel Catering
This Christmas, whisk your guests away to an enchanting garden with Rasel Catering’s Tinsel Gardenland menu. The award-winning halal buffet caterer joins hands with The 1872 Clipper Tea Co. to reimagine festive catering. Picture an immersive experience, where festive botanicals, tea rituals and Christmas magic come together. Whether you’re pining for a fancy afternoon tea party, a sumptuous full buffet, or a homely mini buffet, the extensive menu will deliver a feast that impresses.
Taking centre stage are four exclusive tea-infused appetisers and desserts that are thoughtfully crafted using tea blends by The 1872 Clipper Tea Co. On the savoury front, try the Winter Healing Garden poached chicken salad with maple-glazed pumpkin and citrus dill emulsion. Meanwhile, those with a sweet tooth can look forward to the Snowy Canopy Garden Tea vanilla miso log cake and more. Plus, there are non-tea infused dishes such as the salmon en papillote with winter artichoke barigoule and young asparagus, alongside a curated selection of seasonal centrepieces like honey baked turkey ham.
To sweeten the celebrations, selected Christmas buffet menus will also come with an exclusive tea gift blind box that contains either Healing Garden Tea or chamomile tea from The 1872 Clipper Tea Co. These blind boxes are available while stock lasts, so get your orders in early!
Perk alert: the first 50 orders of selected Christmas buffet menus will receive a complimentary Snowy Canopy Garden Tea miso vanilla log cake (worth $78); valid with every 50 pax order from now till 8 Dec 2026 (T&Cs apply).
Best for: A botanical-inspired festive feast with tea-infused creations
Prices: Full buffet from $28.80 per pax; high tea buffet from $23.80 per pax; mini buffet from $338 per set; bentos from $25 per pax; a la carte items from $78
When to order: Orders open from now till 31 Dec 2026; available for delivery with a minimum five-day lead time
Where to purchase: Order online
Order from Rasel Catering

Photography: Stamford Catering
Can’t decide if you’re feeling naughty or nice this Christmas? This is your sign to enjoy the best of both worlds with Stamford Catering’s halal-certified festive catering menu. Expect comforting holiday classics that everyone knows and loves, alongside sinful treats worth the annual indulgence.

Beauty World Food Centre guide
Whenever I step onto Level 4 of Beauty World Centre , the first thing that hits me is the smoky aroma drifting through the air, mingling with the unmistakable bustle of Beauty World Food Centre . Serving generations of diners since 1984, it remains one of Singapore’s most underrated hawker centres in my eyes, home to a diverse mix of cuisines, ranging from old-school stalwarts to newer names bringing fresh picks to the table. Here are the best Beauty World Food Centre stalls for those who can’t decide what to eat there.
30 Beauty World Food Gems Including DIY Okonomiyaki, Famous Eng Kee Wings And More
1. Berempah Bros
One of the newer stalls making waves at the food centre is Berempah Bros , helmed by MasterChef Singapore Season 2 finalist Derek Cheong. Best known for its creative take on ayam goreng berempah AKA spiced fried chicken with rice, the stall gives the familiar favourite a contemporary refresh while retaining its bold flavours.
You have to try their signature Ayam Berempah ($7.50) , which features a piece of deep-fried chicken with a crisp exterior that gives way to juicy, tender meat marinated in a fragrant blend of spices, with distinct notes of cumin and garlic. The chicken is topped with their signature “typhoon shelter crumbs”—a savoury mix of fried garlic, breadcrumbs, and a touch of chilli. Accompanying it is a serving of fragrant coconut rice infused with coconut milk and chicken stock, while a side of tangy achar and house-made sambal belacan rounds out the dish.
Read our Berempah Bros review .
Unit number: #04-51
Opening hours: Daily 10am to 9pm
Tel: 9058 9674
Website
Beramaph Bros is not halal-certified.
MasterChef Finalist Opens Ayam Berempah Stall At Beauty World—Here’s Our Honest Review
2. Top 1 Home Made Noodle
Image credit: @wreckmytummy
Seeing “Top 1” in its name may strike some as a little gimmicky, but Top 1 Home Made Noodle has earned its reputation over the years. The humble stall has been serving handmade noodles at the hawker centre since 1989, building a loyal following through its consistent craftsmanship.
The stall operates on a build-your-own-bowl concept, where diners begin by choosing from seven types of handmade noodles, including Mee Hoon Kueh , U-Mian , and Ban Mian . Next, pick your preferred soup base— Soup ($4.50) , Dry ($5) , Mala Soup ($5) , or Tom Yum ($5) —before customising your bowl with add-ons such as White Fish (+$1) , Salmon (+$1.50) , Fish Maw (+$2) , or Meatballs . The noodles are known for their springy, chewy texture, cooked just right with a pleasant bite without that overly doughy consistency.
Unit number: #04-51
Opening hours: Thur to Tue 11am to 5pm
Top 1 Home Made Noodle is not halal-certified.
3. Pink Candy
With the Korean wave in Singapore still going strong, you do not have to break the bank every time a craving strikes, as Pink Candy is one hawker stall worth checking out for affordable Korean fare. Established by a native Korean who has run the stall for over a decade, the eatery stands out in its corner of the hawker centre with its distinctive pink-themed decor and vibrant displays.
Diners are often spoilt for choice here with an extensive menu featuring over 40 items, many of which are your typical Korean favourites. This includes your typical Kimbap ($8.50) , Black Bean Noodles ($12.90) , Spicy Cold Beef Noodles ($14.90) , Bibimbab ($12.90) , and Spicy Rice Cake ($12.90) . If you are dining in larger groups, get their Pork Army Stew ($34.90) , Kimchi Pancake ($21.90) and Original Sweet-Spicy Fried Chicken ($36).
Unit number: #04-51
Opening hours: Wed to Mon 10:30am to 2:30pm, 5pm to 9:30pm, Tue 5pm to 9:30pm
Website
Pink Candy is not halal-certified.
4. Lao Gai Mee
Image credit: Mr Yang via Google Maps
It’s not easy to find kolo mee in Singapore, let alone a good one. Fans of the dish will likely be familiar with Lao Gai Mee , a stall run by young Malaysian hawkers serving traditional Kuching- and Sarawak-style noodles. The menu features four main options— Fish Ball Bak Chor ($5) , Kolo Mee ($5) , Char Siu Mee ($5.50) , and Sarawak Laksa ($6.50) , with a choice of Kolo Mee or thick bee hoon available for all dishes.
Their Kolo Mee comes topped with a generous serving of minced pork, char siew, crispy pork lard, and springy noodles tossed in a fragrant blend of shallot oil and rendered lard that gives the dish its signature savoury flavour. The noodles are perfectly chewy and satisfyingly QQ, all while being priced very reasonably. For an extra bite, add a side of fishballs ($1.20) , which provide a pleasant bounce to the meal.
Unit number: #04-41
Opening hours: Daily 8am to 8pm
Website
Lao Gai Mee is not halal-certified.

The year is coming to a close and it’s time to celebrate Christmas in the best way — by gathering your closest family and friends around good food . Great conversations, infectious laughter and full tummies are sure to follow. I’ve had a grand old time eating my way across Singapore in search of the best Christmas buffets, lunches and dinners , and these are my recommendations.
Every restaurant’s Christmas fare was special in its own way. With so much lovely food, so many talented chefs and such creative spins on traditional Christmas fare, it was difficult to decide what to include and in what order. I did work out a system, and here are the 3 main criteria I used:
• Taste and flavour – How delicious the dishes were, including the balance of flavours, seasoning, sauces, marinades and overall execution
• Variety and selection – The breadth of the menu, from seafood & meat to local cuisine, European specialities and traditional Christmas desserts
• Presentation & dining experience – Visual appeal of the dishes, the live stations experience, and the overall restaurant ambience
Based on my glutton’s journey, here are the best Christmas buffets, lunches and dinners for 2026 in Singapore .

1. Mandarin Oriental, Singapore
Mandarin Oriental, Singapore offers a range of festive dining experiences, whether you are planning a lively year-end gathering with friends and colleagues or a cosy family dinner.
For grand family feasts, our recommendation is the lavish embu . Their Festive Lunch and Dinner Buffets run from 23 Nov 2026 to 3 Jan 2027 showcasing a spread of seasonal favourites. Ring in the cheer with Bone-in Gammon Ham with Pineapple Glaze and Spiced Honey , carved alongside Roasted Irish Duck with Signature Sauce .
Beyond the roasts, we plan to head to the celebrated Seafood Colosseum featuring Boston lobster and seasonal oysters . Other highlights include perennial Singaporean favourite Chilli Crab with Mantou , and my personal kryptonite, the Wheel of Pasta , where you will find 5 varieties of freshly prepared pasta.
Parents will definitely appreciate the dedicated kids’ buffet corner , stocked with child-friendly savoury bites and sweet treats.
Those dining on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day can look forward to traditional confections like classic Christmas Stollen , Christmas Fruit Cake and Chocolate Log Cake . For something different, finish your meal with a delicate Chestnut Mont Blanc Tart .
Dolce Vita ’s inviting Italian warmth is perfect for an intimate festive celebration. Their Festive Set Menu begins with a delicate Sweet Corn and Basil Panna Cotta . The fork-tender Slow-braised Veal Shank in Saffron Butter Emulsion is a standout main course. Meanwhile, seafood lovers will relish the Chilean Sea Bass with Raisin Sauce and Orange-braised Endive .
Whether you’re gathering the family for a lavish buffet or enjoying a leisurely Italian meal, Mandarin Oriental, Singapore offers a warm, inviting setting for festive celebrations.
…
summary: Christmas dining in Singapore for 2026 spans hotel buffets, festive set menus, Italian family lunches and speciality restaurant offerings across areas including Marina Bay, Orchard, Clarke Quay and Chinatown. Covering 12 restaurants, the selection considers food quality, menu variety and presentation, with options for families, couples and groups seeking halal-certified, luxury or more casual celebrations.
title: Christmas 2026: Our editor’s picks of the best Xmas buffets & dinners in Singapore

body:
Six Singapore coffee shops made the 2026 Asia-Pacific top 100 from The World’s 100 Best Coffee Shops, and the one at the top of the whole region is Apartment Coffee on Selegie Road.
The list comes from the team behind The World’s 100 Best Coffee Shops, which also ranks Europe, South America, and North and Central America. The Asia-Pacific ranking runs from No 1 to No 100 across 14 countries and territories, from Australia and Japan to India and New Zealand. Singapore’s six entries sit at No 1, No 36, No 38, No 50, No 55 and No 90.
Apartment Coffee on Selegie Road, No 1 in the Asia-Pacific top 100. Photo: The World’s 100 Best Coffee Shops
How the ranking works
Scores blend two kinds of votes. An expert panel of baristas, roasters and coffee professionals carries 70 per cent of the final score, and public online votes carry the other 30 per cent. The panel judges coffee quality, barista expertise and sustainability, alongside service, atmosphere and food.
Australia has the most entries, with 18, followed by South Korea with 13, Japan and Taiwan with 11 each, and India with eight. Singapore’s six put it level with Hong Kong and the Philippines, ahead of Malaysia and Indonesia on five each.
The six Singapore entries
No 1: Apartment Coffee, Selegie
Apartment Coffee calls itself a coffee studio, and the menu leans mostly on pour-overs made with single-origin beans from places such as Costa Rica, Rwanda and Kenya. The room is sleek and minimalist. If you mostly drink lattes, this is a filter coffee bar first, so go in ready to choose a bean rather than a milk.
Address: 139 Selegie Road, #01-01, Singapore 188309.
No 36: Alchemist, Khong Guan Building
Alchemist started in 2016 as a coffee bar in the Central Business District. The ranked outlet is its roastery in the former Khong Guan Biscuit Factory in the Tai Seng area. It opened in 2019 as the brand’s first dedicated roastery, with roasting and brewing under one roof.
Address: 2 MacTaggart Road, #01-01 Khong Guan Building, Singapore 368078.
Alchemist (Khong Guan), No 36, in the former Khong Guan Biscuit Factory. Photo: The World’s 100 Best Coffee Shops
No 38: Homeground Coffee Roasters, Bukit Timah
Homeground’s whole pitch is the home brewer. The roaster wants people to understand what they buy and brew it well in their own kitchens, and the name doubles as freshly ground beans at home. That makes it the pick of the six for someone who wants to leave with beans and some know-how, not just a cup.
Address: 911 Bukit Timah Road, Singapore 589622.
No 50: The Community Coffee, Far East Plaza
The Community Coffee sits on the second floor of Far East Plaza, at the Scotts Road end of Orchard, and has been going for nine years. The fit-out is pared back and rustic. It is an easy one to fold into an Orchard errand.
Address: 14 Scotts Road, #02-94 Far East Plaza, Singapore 228213.
No 55: Cata Coffee, Joo Chiat
Cata is an independent cafe and roastery in Joo Chiat that rotates its beans by season, for both espresso and pour-over, and bakes its pastries in-house. It works as a neighbourhood cafe as much as a roastery, built for sitting down over a pastry rather than a quick takeaway.
Address: 56 Joo Chiat Place, Singapore 427780.
Cata Coffee, No 55, at 56 Joo Chiat Place. Photo: The World’s 100 Best Coffee Shops
No 90: The Populus, Neil Road
The Populus pairs competition coffee with a full brunch menu. Its coffee team’s competition record takes in the 2019 Singapore National Barista Championship, back-to-back Singapore Latte Art Championship titles and a top-four finish at the 2025 World Latte Art Championship in Geneva. The food is Australian-style brunch with Japanese and Asian touches. If someone in your group wants a proper plate and someone else wants a serious flat white, this is the compromise.
Address: 146 Neil Road, Singapore 088875.
The Populus, No 90, at 146 Neil Road. Photo: The World’s 100 Best Coffee Shops
Quick guide
• No 1, Apartment Coffee: 139 Selegie Road, #01-01, Singapore 188309. Pour-over specialist
• No 36, Alchemist (Khong Guan): 2 MacTaggart Road, #01-01, Singapore 368078. Roastery in a former biscuit factory
• No 38, Homeground Coffee Roasters: 911 Bukit Timah Road, Singapore 589622. Beans and home brewing
• No 50, The Community Coffee: 14 Scotts Road, #02-94 Far East Plaza, Singapore 228213. Orchard coffee bar
• No 55, Cata Coffee: 56 Joo Chiat Place, Singapore 427780. Seasonal roastery with in-house bakes
• No 90, The Populus: 146 Neil Road, Singapore 088875. Coffee with a full brunch menu
summary: Apartment Coffee on Selegie Road is No 1 in the Asia-Pacific top 100 from The World's 100 Best Coffee Shops. Alchemist, Homeground, The Community Coffee, Cata Coffee and The Populus also made the list. All six, with addresses.
title: Apartment Coffee is No 1 in the 2026 Top 100 Coffee Shops Asia-Pacific list, and five more Singapore cafes make the top 100
