It’s the end of an era for Assam laksa lovers. Popular regional chain D’Laksa is officially winding down operations, pulling out of Singapore after almost 10 years of serving up its signature tangy mackerel-packed Assam laksa . As a farewell treat, D’Laksa is also running a Buy-2-Get-1-Free promotion at its last outlet at Compass One before permanently shuttering on 23 Nov 2026 .
Originally hailing from Johor Bahru, D’Laksa was known for offering the less common Penang-style laksa, which forgoes the more usual coconut milk base in favour of a robust, spicy fish-based broth. The brand built a loyal following through its quick-service kiosks nestled inside neighbourhood malls and food courts (including past spots like YewTee Point and Northpoint City).
Their signature dish of Asam Laksa (S$6) comes with a generous portion of lettuce, pineapple and fish, giving the dish a tart aroma thanks to the sweet, sour and tangy flavours it packs. Their special prawn paste complements the sour tamarind sauce with its heavily umami profile. They also offer Asam Lobsterball (S$4.50) , which comes with 5 pieces of bouncy lobster balls drenched in their signature Assam sauce.
Credit – D’Laksa
Alternatively, try their Asam Pedas Stingray with Rice (S$8.90) , which features a slab of stingray meat dressed in a bold, spicy gravy. Sides and beverages such as Fruit Rojak (S$5.50) and Cendol Drink (S$2.50) are also available.
While the brand has steadily scaled back its islandwide footprint over recent months, this quiet closure marks the end of D’Laksa in Singapore, with only their Johor Bahru outlets remaining. Fans of D’Laksa should head down to Compass One before 23 Nov to enjoy the Buy-2-Get-1-Free deal and get one last bowl of their favourite Penang-style Assam Laksa; otherwise, you’ll have to trek across the border to get a taste.
Traditional Penang Food: Authentic Penang assam laksa, fried kway teow, Nyonya fried rice & chendol in Toa Payoh
summary: Malaysian chain D'Laksa is closing its final Singapore outlet at Compass One on 23 Nov 2026 after nearly a decade, ending its local presence with a Buy-2-Get-1-Free promotion. Originating from Johor Bahru, the brand specialises in Penang-style assam laksa (S$6), as well as budget-friendly dishes like Asam Pedas Stingray (S$8.90) and Fruit Rojak (S$5.50). This update is ideal for fans of tangy fish-based laksa looking to catch the farewell deal in Sengkang before future cravings require a trip across the border.
title: D’Laksa closing last SG outlet – Buy-2-Get-1-Free deal till 23 Nov

It would seem that as we approach the end of the year, even more of our favourite spots are starting to close. Ramen Keisuke Tori King has announced their closure at 100AM mall in Tanjong Pagar after 14 years .
While this is very sad news, you still have a chance to grab a bowl, as they will be closing on 29 Nov 2026 . Ramen and other Japanese dishes are popular in Singapore, mainly due to how filling and flavourful they are. This closure means that there’s one less spot for Singaporeans to enjoy.
Credit – Ramen Keisuke Tori King
This ramen spot has been around since 2012 , serving hungry students, office workers and so many others. The Keisuke Group have expressed their sadness over this closure. They have also been extremely grateful to all their loyal customers over the last 14 years, in a post on Facebook .
While it may be easy for some people to shrug it off as just another closure this month, this restaurant has undoubtedly garnered a loyal fanbase that is sure to be devastated.
Credit – Ramen Keisuke Tori King
This specific outlet is Japanese chef Keisuke Takeda ‘s third ramen concept in Singapore. For those of you who aren’t aware, Takeda is the winner of the 2011 Tokyo Ramen Championships. If you’ve never had ramen before, Ramen Keisuke Tori King is the perfect spot to make a first impression.
Credit – Ramen Keisuke Tori King
The ramen itself is known for its thick, creamy chicken broth. This is from hours and hours of cooking and stewing, drawing out as much of the chicken’s natural flavours into the stock. The collagen is also what helps with the thickness, giving that creamy and thick texture that makes the soup oh-so filling and satisfying.
Credit – Ramen Keisuke Tori King
Should you decide to visit before their closure on 29 Nov 2026, here are their signature dishes: The Tori King Ramen (S$13.90) is the standard bowl, and the Black Spicy Tori King Ramen (S $ 14.90 ) is its spicy variant. With the impending closure, I’m sure the queues will be longer than usual.
While this closure is sad, they still have 13 outlets , all of which have exclusive dishes worth exploring. If you’d like to see what else they have in store, you can check out their website to see what their other outlets have available.
Broth & Bowls Ramen: Japanese comfort food starting from $11.90 run by a solo chef
summary: Ramen Keisuke Tori King at 100AM mall in Tanjong Pagar closes permanently, with its final day of service on 29 Nov. The outlet opened in 2012 as chef Keisuke Takeda’s third ramen concept in Singapore and served a thick, creamy chicken broth for 14 years. The closure is useful to know for diners who want one last bowl of its signature chicken ramen.
title: Ramen Keisuke Tori King – Closing after 14 years; beloved ramen spot shutters end-Nov

JJAN! What does ‘jjan’ stand for? It’s an onomatopoeia. A sound effect that stands for the clinking sounds of their glasses or beer cans together, a casual way to toast with one another!
Situated along Craig Road , JJAN! is an intimate place to enjoy 30 varieties of traditional Korean rice wines and brews , and modern interpretations of Korean dishes made for sharing .
Good Pour Decisions
Credit: JJAN!
Every Korean meal has a sidekick, and it’s usually soju or beer. At JJAN!, they deliver an outstanding collection of liquors to the table. Featuring a premium Korean traditional yakju , Midam Seoktanju (S$19) , brewed in earthenware crockery for fermentation. Another distinctive option is the Suamju (S$18) , offering a crisp, dry finish with a lingering aroma of melon and Korean pear.
Gin lovers, Namul Gin 40 (S$16) is for you, with minari (Korean water dropwort) for a light and botanical flavour in your glass. Switch to Burnt Buckwheat (S$12) for deeper flavour: traditionally brewed soju with hints of roasted coffee beans, dark chocolate, and vanilla.
Sharing Bites
Credit: JJAN!
Meat is always on the menu in a Korean restaurant – expect no less from JJAN! If beef tartare is your thing, their Yukhoe (S$34) combines Australian wagyu with fermented octopus and Korean pear. Unlike the usual tartare presentation, JJAN! makes it interactive. Diners can assemble each bite with crispy fried seaweed chips , controlling the savoury depth each time.
Plates here are thoughtfully curated to complement the pours; the Chilled Crab Salad (S$26) contains king crab leg , crunchy jellyfish , and tangy vegetable strips (Dongchimi – Korean water kimchi) for a delightful mouthfeel. This dish balances well alongside a glass of makgeolli .
Continuing their salad game, the Busan Jijimi & Squid Salad (S$19) is an interpretation of vegetable pancakes and squid salad sold in Busan. Think mung bean and Singapore’s local Kueh Chye (Chwee Kueh), with cabbage and leek, with squid lathered in tangy chojang sauce for bright acidity.
Big Bites
Credit: JJAN!
There’s something about the simplicity of pork-and-rice soup that Koreans love. JJAN! delivers the same level of comfort in their Pork Gukbap (S$21) , with a broth simmered for 48 hours . It’s served with Jeju pork collar, glutinous rice, and several condiments to pimp up the heat and savouriness of your meat, your way!
No fishy business other than the Fish of the Day (S$48) , a unique twist that pairs pan-seared seasonal fish with Korean abalone and fermented white asparagus , drizzled with takju makgeolli butter sauce for a hint of subtle sweetness.
Small Bites
Credit: JJAN!
Mushrooms are a popular and versatile ingredient used in many cuisines, and JJAN! takes a playful spin with their Pyogo Jeon (S$5) , stuffed with finely ground sea bass and prawn mousse . The cooking process starts with gentle steaming before frying, coating it off with a perilla-leaf soy glaze. This bite pairs exceptionally well with My God Spring Blossom (S$19) , a sparkling yakju brewed with white magnolia petals.
Spuds in all shapes and sizes are the ultimate drinking companion . The flavourful Myeonglan and Potato (S$6) layers confit Agria potato with an aromatic lemon cream, fermented chilli, and umami salted pollack roe .
Sweeter Endings
Whoever said they are too full for a sweet treat isn’t honest with themselves. Save some stomach space for Fruit Chapssaltteok (S$8) , essentially soft fruit (strawberry, kiwi, grape, and fig) mochi, layered with delicately sweet red bean paste or a richer, cheesy mascarpone. Otherwise, cleanse your palate with their Pomegranate Sorbet (S$2) .
Intrigued? Bring your friends over to JJAN! and discover something new, with good company, superb food, and raise your glasses to ‘jjan’!

5pm–12am (Mo to Fri) & 1pm–12am (Sat to Sun)

Another viral coconut drink brand joins the Orchard crowd. Yee3 is now at ION Orchard , with over 20 fresh coconut beverages from S$4.90 ; there’s definitely a flavour for you amongst the line-up. For first-timers, we recommend trying their original Fragrant Coconut Water (S$4.90) , made with 100% natural , fresh Thai coconut water.
Cloud Coconut Water
Credit: Yee3 Singapore
Pistachio is a flavour that needs no introduction, and it is well-loved by many. The Pistachio Cloud Coconut Water (S$6.20) is a drink worth trying, followed by Oreo Storm Cloud Coconut (S$6.50) for chocolate lovers, a perfectly sweet indulgence.
Iced Coconut Water
Credit: Yee3 Singapore
If creamy goodness from the Cloud Coconut Water series isn’t your kind of beverage, fret not! You can still seek flavour without the heaviness. The Iced Coconut Water series has you covered with lighter, healthier options! Quench your thirst with their Lychee or Watermelon Coconut Water (S$5.90) , a great fun alternative to boost hydration in sunny Singapore.
Coconut Specials
Credit: Yee3 Singapore
Need more than a coconut fix? Here are some drinks that bring in the caffeine. Starting with Yee3’s Coconut Latte Frost Shake (S$7.50) and the Matcha Coconut Frost Shake (S$7.90) , both icy cold with coconut meat for extra texture. Prefer something subtle? The Coconut Americano (S$5.60) pairs a shot of espresso with coconut water, and the Matcha Coconut Milk (S$7.50) whisks matcha with coconut milk for fragrant sips. Try the Matcha Mango Coconut Milk (S$7.50) for something fruitier.
Opening Promotions
Credit: Yee3 Singapore
Snag 20% off all drinks from 16 to 19 November , and grab yourself a complimentary Yee3 Penguin Mascot when you purchase any 2 cups ! There’s also a 1-for-1 deal from 20 to 22 November , and the entire lineup is included except the Coconut Frost Shake series. Queue early to score a Free Mystery Gift Bag , made available to the first 200 customers daily .
Deals sorted. Time to jio your friends and see what the fuss is about.

16 to 22 November 2026

Capyba Pet Farm in Johor Bahru
Although we might be barreling into the holiday season, not all of us have the luxury of embarking on a cross-continental trip on a whim. Perhaps you might have run out of ALs to burn, or are already budgeting for an African safari next year, and so another trip to JB is on the books.
But if you can’t quite let go of your ambitions of getting up close to exotic animals, you’re in luck. Just under half an hour from the JB checkpoints is Capyba Pet Farm , a small zoo that’s home to a slew of adorable furry companions that you won’t see roaming around the Little Red Dot. From the Internet-famous capybara to friendly alpacas, here’s what you can expect.
How to get to Capyba Pet Farm?
Image adapted from: Rachael Tan via Google Maps
Capyba Pet Farm, not to be confused with Capyba Cafe, which operates under the same brand, is located on the outskirts of Taman Sutera Utama. It’s about a 25-minute drive from the JB checkpoints.
Although you can take the public bus to Capyba Pet Farm, we recommend hiring a private vehicle instead, as the journey takes over an hour and involves 1.8km of walking. Instead, book a Grab to get you there in a jiffy; it only costs around S$14.20 . If you’ve opted to drive there yourself, there is parking available on-site.
What to expect at Capyba Pet Farm?
Once you’ve crossed the border to Capyba Pet Farm, your first order of business is to get your admission tickets. You can buy them at the farm’s entrance; adult tickets cost RM35/pax (~S$11.01) , while children and seniors pay RM25/pax (~S$7.86) . There’s no time limit to your visit too, and you’re free to stay on as long as you’d like.
You can also purchase animal feed here for RM10 (~S$3.15) , and trust us, you’ll want to fork out the pocket change to give the lil’ critters here a treat, as they’re simply too cute to resist. Armed with your bucket of shredded carrots and greens, you’ll want to make a beeline for the animal pens; Capyba Pet Farm is home to over 50 animals , so there’s plenty of mouths to feed.
Image credit: The WestCoast Garage via Google Maps
Undoubtedly, the stars of the farm are their resident capybaras . The semi-aquatic cuties have been noted by visitors to be extremely mellow whose sole intent is to graze on veggies, so give them a handful and watch as they munch away.
Image credit: Piano girl via Google Maps
They share an enclosure with geese and ducks too, so be sure to show some love to their feathered brethren. According to videos posted online of the farm, it seems like visitors are also able to go inside some of the enclosures to pet the animals, so check in with the staff if you’d like to take a closer look at them.
Image adapted from: Siow Wai Wong & SY Yee via Google Maps
You’ll also notice that some of the animals here are left to their own devices and are allowed to roam freely around the farm . As such, don’t be shy to approach them with a leafy offering in hand; some to look forward to interacting with beyond their pens include alpacas , miniature mountain goats , and chickens .
The variety of the cast of animals doesn’t end there. While terrapins lounge lazily in their tanks and camels await their next serving of greens, make your rounds, and you’ll chance upon foxes , cows , horses , ponies , deer , raccoons , and even ostriches .
Image adapted from: threelittle peas & Siow Wai Wong via Google Maps
Meanwhile, there are also smaller set-ups where younger kids can enjoy the company of similarly pint-sized farm inhabitants, such as guinea pigs , ducklings , and rabbits .
Image credit: Pearl Aizhu via Google Maps
When you decide to call it a day, be sure to make a pit stop at the farm’s on-site cafe, the Yvonne Sweet Bakery . Housed within 2 separate shipping containers, it’s air-conditioned too, so we won’t judge you for popping by to cool off. One of them sells various bakes; in particular, buy a box of capybara macarons (RM13, ~S$4.09) for the road, that is, if you can bear to gobble them up.
Image adapted from: Nur Nabiha & April Lau via Google Maps
Within a separate shipping container nearby, famished visitors can grab a more substantial bite as the cafe also whips up hearty mains (from RM17, ~S$5.35) like Crispy Fish & Chips , Smoked Duck Aglio Olio , Mentaiko Pasta , and Chicken Katsu Sandos . Another must-try is their capybara pudding , which jiggles satisfyingly in place when you move its plate around.
Visit Capyba Pet Farm in JB this school holidays
There’s nothing more family-friendly than spending an hour or 2 mingling with the most docile of animals, and if your little one has a soft spot for wildlife, this one’s a no-brainer. So, instead of letting the kids rot away at home with their iPad in hand, take a quick road trip to JB and stop by Capyba Pet Farm for the upcoming school holidays.

When the twinkling lights, shiny baubles and jolly music hit the streets, it can only mean one thing: the holiday season is officially upon us. This year, two of our go-to lifestyle destinations – Capitol Singapore and CHIJMES – are ushering in a bedazzling, golden Christmas. With a theme of ‘Golden Splendour’, look forward to gold-themed decorations and exciting festive activities from now till 31 December 2026. Can’t wait to see the sparkle season in full swing? Scroll on for the festive highlights at Capitol Singapore and CHIJMES for Christmas 2026.
A guide to Christmas 2026 at Capitol Singapore and CHIJMES
1. A festive playland for families with little ones
Photography: Capitol Singapore
The holiday season is all about cherished reunions, so round up your loved ones for a day-out at Christmas Playland at Capitol Singapore. Both little ones and the young at heart are welcome to join in the fun at the Outdoor Plaza on 21 and 22 November 2026.
Swing by anytime from 12pm to 8pm, pick up a golden quest card, and make your rounds around the activity booths to collect points. You’ll bring home a sweet prize once you’ve completed the card. With a line-up of activities like face painting and gift box tossing, you’re in for a fun-filled time.
2. Celebrate Christmas the Swedish way
Curious how the Swedes celebrate Christmas? Consider this your invitation to join the Lucia celebration at CHIJMES, held in collaboration with The Embassy of Sweden.
To celebrate this traditional festival of light observed in Sweden and other Nordic countries, the Lucia Procession will take place on 11 December 2026. Held from 5pm onwards, the procession features an advent candle lighting ceremony, as well as performances by a highly-anticipated Swedish folk music group and local singer-songwriter Glen Wee.
Photography: The Embassy of Sweden in Singapore
More Swedish festivities await on 11 and 12 December 2026. Swing by for a curated Makers Market, a Swedish Cocktail Bar, a floorball shoot-out challenge as an ode to Sweden’s national sport, as well as a photo exhibition showcasing 60 years of diplomatic relations between Sweden and Singapore.
And get your cameras on stand-by in the evenings. From 7pm to 10pm, look out for a show-stopping light projection featuring iconic representations of Sweden, such as Nordic lights, Dala horses and more.
3. A festive atmosphere all set for merrymaking
We may not have the four seasons in Singapore, but that doesn’t mean a cosy, snowed-in Christmas is out of reach. Experience the enchantment of snowfall as Capitol Singapore and CHIJMES transform into magical winterlands from now till 31 December 2026. Every evening, from 7pm to 9pm, the Outdoor Plaza at Capitol Singapore and the Mini Lawn at CHIJMES welcome flurries of snow. Now, that’s how you celebrate winter in the tropics!
Photography: Capitol Singapore
To amp up the merrymaking mood, Capitol Singapore also brings back its iconic Singing Tree at the Outdoor Plaza. Immerse in enchanting Yuletide tunes brought to you by Voices of Singapore and other carollers. The choral performances take place from 4 to 25 Dec 2026, on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, as well as Christmas Eve and Day. Catch these 30-minute performances at 6.30pm, 7.30pm and 8.30pm.
Up for more merry tunes? Take a seat at the live carolling performances by The Crescendos on 19, 20, 24 and 25 Dec 2026. Held at the Main Lawn at CHIJMES, the immersive performances will take place from 7.30pm to 8.30pm in the evening.
Photography: CHIJMES
Of course, how can we forget about the magical festival displays? CHIJMES Hall’s facade is set to transform into a massive, golden music box. Watch as a giant key winds up the building to unveil a moving clockwork toy emporium of nutcrackers and other holiday staples. This spellbinding showcase runs every 30 minutes from 7pm to 10pm daily, from now till 31 December 2026.
4. Your chance to play Santa
Ticking off your gift shopping list will be a breeze at the Christmas markets. Capitol Singapore’s festive market beckons with stylish apparels, handmade accessories and local crafts for every giftee. Drop by the Outdoor Plaza from 27 November to 27 December 2026, anytime from 12pm to 9pm, to get shopping.
Photography: CHIJMES
Over at CHIJMES, two festive marketplaces await at the Main Lawn. On selected dates from 27 November to 25 December 2026, The Gatherry Craft Market comes alive from 3pm to 10pm with booths from homegrown and international brands. Think timeless jewellery, unique apparel, festive-themed trinkets and more.
On 26 and 27 December 2026, make a beeline for The Winery Discovery Market from 5pm to 10pm. Curated for imbibers, the market features DIY festive wine baskets and hampers, wine sampling and pairing experiences, holiday cocktails and exclusive wine flights.

Sentosa’s calling, and it’s tempting you with a next-level boozy brunch at the kitchen table at W Singapore – Sentosa Cove. This weekend brunch brings the heat with global flavours and an exciting entertainment lineup. Getting heated up? Don’t worry, you can cool down with a splash in the Wet Deck, one of Singapore’s largest outdoor pools featuring a playful water slide.
The open kitchens dish out everything from Asian street food faves to freshly grilled delights. Carnivores will love the juicy pork belly and wagyu beef. body:
BK Eating House is a 24-hour coffeeshop in AMK
Image credit: Stall.sg
Ang Mo Kio is no stranger to iconic hawker stalls; after all, it’s home to the famed Lao San Kway Chap , Dongsheng Cafe , and a slew of under-HDB coffeeshops. Adding to the mix is BK Eating House , which has recently opened a new coffeeshop at Ang Mo Kio Block 226F , offering a variety of affordable hawker eats. Better yet, it’s open 24 hours, so you can get your fill anytime.
Image credit: Kwong Fei Yee via Google Maps
The most enticing deal is from Hua Dee Hong Kong Style Roasted Delight , which is selling their plates of Soy Sauce Chicken Rice for just $1 as part of their opening promotions. Their soy sauce chicken is said to be succulent and tender, with a prominent soy sauce aroma. The rice is also said to be fragrant, savoury, and glossy. Their Char Siew Rice ($4) is another crowd-pleaser, with char siew that hits the sweet spot between fat and meat, and a satisfying smoky, charred finish.
Image credit: Heng Long Teochew Porridge via Google Maps
Heng Long Teochew Porridge is another popular stall here, serving up a plethora of side dishes alongside their signature Teochew porridge. Unlike Cantonese porridge, AKA congee, which is thick and creamy, Teochew porridge is thinner and more watery, designed to be eaten alongside stronger-flavoured side dishes.
As part of its opening promotions, you can select your preferred fish, steamed Hong Kong-style and drenched in a savoury soy-based sauce, for just $9.90 . Round it out with other side dishes, such as the Stewed Duck : tender duck slices simmered in a rich dark soy sauce base.
Image credit: Stall.sg
There’s also $6 Western , with menu items priced at $6 or less—a steal, considering Western food often goes up to $10 or more. Their Chicken Chop with Fries ($6) is a safe bet, comprising juicy, chargrilled chicken chop served alongside crispy shoestring fries, coleslaw, hamburger bun, and gravy. Their Chicken Cutlet with Pasta ($6) is also highly raved about: crispy, deep-fried chicken cutlet on a bed of pasta tossed in a tomato-based sauce, topped with a sunny-side-up egg.
Image credit: Jessie via Google Maps
If you can stomach innards, try Jalan Besar Pig’s Organ Soup ’s Pig’s Organ Soup (from $4.80) . Choose your preferred ingredients from a selection of pork slices, pork liver, meatballs, pork kidney, tofu and more. The whole medley is simmered in pork bone broth that’s best eaten with rice.
BK Eating House is located a 20-minute walk from Ang Mo Kio MRT Station .
For more eats in the area, read our Ang Mo Kio 628 Food Centre food guide . Otherwise, check out our review of Shared Table , a new garden cafe located at Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, located just a 14-minute walk away.
Address: 226F Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1, Singapore 566226
Opening hours: Daily 24 hours

body:
Bagel Chef is a new bakery at Sengkang Grand Mall
Image credit: Besharps via Google Maps
The bagel trend may have died down a little, but they’re still a pretty solid and IG-worthy treat from time to time. In the sea of good bagel spots , we’ve found another bakery that whips up the cult-favourite baked good. Bagel Chef has recently opened in Sengkang Grand Mall , giving bagel enthusiasts another spot to add to their rotation.
17 Best Sengkang Food Places For Cheap Korean Food, Popular Min Jiang Kueh And More
Image credit: SiDing Wang via Google Maps
The bakery currently offers an extensive selection of bagels, with over 20 flavours to choose from. Their Light & Wholesome range features the Plain Bagel for just $2 , alongside the Chia Protein Bagel ($2.80) and All-in-Nut Bagel ($3.80) for a healthier, guilt-free snack.
Image credit: Qing_ via Google Maps
What caught my eye is their Loaded Bagel series. As the name suggests, these are hefty bagels that are sure to fill your belly. Four flavours are up for grabs, including the must-try Pistachio Loaded Bagel ($9.80) , stuffed with pistachio cream, and the Blueberry Loaded Bagel ($8.80) for a fruity option. Matcha lovers can go for the Double Matcha Panna Cotta Bagel ($9.90) that’s filled with two kinds of matcha cream.
Image credit: Balyn Lim via Google Maps
There’s also the Rich Sweet line-up for those with a sweet tooth. Satisfy your cravings with their Milky Strawberry Bagel ($3.70) , which looks like a strawberry Pocky in bagel form. Caffeine junkies can opt for the Caramel Mocha Bagel ($4.20) or the Earl Grey Crunch Bagel ($4.80) . For something that’s not too sweet, the Sea Salt Lemon Bagel ($3.90) is worth a shot.
Locally inspired bagels are also available, such as the Pandan Coconut Crunch ($4.20) , Taro Mochi Floss ($3.90) , and Chestnut Pumpkin Bagel ($3.90) .
Image credit: jiaojiao song via Google Maps
Folks who like sweet and salty combos can go for the Raw Choco Butter ($4.20) , starring a thicc slab of butter atop a chocolate spread. If sweet bagels aren’t your thing, go for their savoury bagels instead, ranging from Seaweed Pork Floss ($4.20) to Bacon Kimchi ($4.20) for a heartier treat.
Image credit: jiaojiao song via Google Maps
Planning a potluck or party for the festive season? Consider picking up a Gift Box (price TBD) , a long box that fits around 10 bagels per box, perfect for sharing with the fam or gifting a bagel lover multiple flavours in one go.
Image credit: 博雅 via Google Maps
Their other bakes, such as toasts and buns, look just as interesting. Standouts include the Black Gold Pork Floss Toast ($8.60) , Hokkaido Pistachio Toast ($8.60) , and the Buttery Soft Bun ($3.20) . They also have the Buttery Sea Salt Roll , AKA shio pan, for $2 .
Image credit: SiDing Wang via Google Maps
Bagel Chef also offers a rotation of flavours that aren’t featured on the menu, such as Black Pepper Potato Sausage ($3.90) , Lemon Tea ($3.50) , and even Chocolate Cheese ($3.90) , so we recommend dropping by to see what’s on offer that day.
Bagel Chef is a five-minute walk away from Buangkok MRT Station .
Speaking of shio pan, check out our comprehensive ranked list of the best shio pan in Singapore . Alternatively, head to 365 Bakery in Johor Bahru for Swiss roll blind boxes and more bakes across the border.
Address: 70 Compassvale Bow, #01-73, Sengkang Grand Mall, Singapore 544692
Opening hours: Daily 10:30am to 9pm

body:
Sengkang Pasar Malam is back, and better than ever before, from 14 Nov to 15 Dec 2026 . Open 12pm – 10pm daily, it’s located at the big green field, so you can expect many, many food stalls. In fact, there are 40+ F&B stalls this time round, along with a squishy store . Complement your meal with the amusement rides and game stalls too. Best of all, there’s live music to jam out to every Fri, Sat and Sun.
With so much food available, here are some stalls you can look forward to.
Start off with drinks to quench your thirst from the heat. The drink stall we tried was Dadih Chill , which offers various colourful and creamy Pudrinks with hilarious names such as My Caramel Romance (caramel milk with chocolate) and Mango’s A Peach (peach tea with mango). We opted for the Cookies & Scream! (S$8.50) . The drink tastes as good as it looks (above, left), with aqua blue dadih at the bottom, layered with Oreo crumbles and topped with salted vanilla cold foam.
The next stall we tried was Gepuk Leh!! , which sells ayam gepuk , also known as Indonesian smashed chicken. We ordered the Ayam Gepuk Original (S$10.90) (above, right). I would say this dish was an indulgent one — from the crispy ayam gepuk to the bayam goreng (fried Chinese spinach) to the tempeh (soybean cake), everything was fried. That said, the piquant chilli definitely helps to cut through some of the greasiness, and the meal was still delicious.
For dessert, we got a set of 4 basic Putu Piring (S$5) (above, left) from Chong Pang Putu Piring . Their putu piring is freshly steamed and all flavours — gula melaka , chocolate and peanut — are made with real ingredients, not artificial seasoning . Besides putu piring , the stall also offers drinks such as Chendol (S$3.50) and Coco Shake (S$5) .
We also ordered the Milk Chocolate Cake (S$11) (above, right) from Matilda’s Puddle Cake . The cake pieces are more mid-sized than bite-sized, and the stall generously coats them with a ladle of their rich chocolate sauce. By generous, I really do mean generous; the chocolate sauce was almost spilling out! This creates moist and soft cake pieces which have soaked up all that fudgy goodness.
If you prefer heading to pasar malams for the entertainment, you’ll be glad to know there are also game booths, amusement rides and a squishy store. This is just a sneak peek of the 40+ F&B stalls available; head down to Sengkang Pasar Malam to discover even more.

Open daily from 12pm to 10pm, it also features live music every Friday to Sunday. The food selection includes drinks, ayam gepuk and local desserts, making it a useful evening outing for families and those looking for affordable pasar malam food and entertainment.

body:
Supermoons in Singapore
Mooncake season may be long over, but the moon clearly isn’t done stealing the spotlight. And honestly, we’re not complaining, because there’ll be not 1, not 2, but 3 supermoons making their grand appearance in Singapore’s skies, one each in November, December, and January.
Here’s when to catch them, including a few tips on how to spot these giants at their brightest. We’ve also thrown in a meteor shower and a Uranus sighting for the stargazers who want more bang for their late night.
What’s a supermoon?
Image credit: NASA Science
I had the same question too, and did some quick Googling so you don’t have to. NASA’s explanation can get a little science-y , but here’s the gist: a supermoon happens when the moon looks bigger and brighter than usual because it’s at its closest point to Earth in its orbit – a spot called perigee.
The moon doesn’t orbit us in a perfect circle, so sometimes it’s nearer and sometimes it’s farther away. When a full moon happens to line up with that closest point, we get a supermoon. They aren’t super rare, but they only pop up about 3 to 4 times a year, usually back-to-back.
Fun fact: “supermoon” isn’t an official astronomical term, but it’s the easiest way to describe that extra-bright, extra-large moon we all love snapping pics of.
When & what time will the supermoons appear in Singapore?
Image credit: Mervyn Soon via Facebook
According to the Observatory at Science Centre Singapore, the first of 3 consecutive supermoons, the Beaver Moon , lights up the sky on 24th November 2026 . It rises in the east-northeast at 6.34pm and becomes fully illuminated at around 10.54pm, so you can catch the moonrise after work and still have time to see it at its peak.
Next up is the Cold Moon on 23rd-24th December 2026 . This one is the closest and largest supermoon of the year, which is as good an excuse as any to slip out of Christmas Eve dinner for some moon-gazing.
The trio wraps up with the Wolf Moon on 22nd January 2027 , which turns full at around 8.17pm Singapore time. Exact rise timings for the December and January supermoons haven’t been released by the Science Centre yet, but at least you can start planning your moon-gazing sesh.
Why is November’s supermoon called the Beaver Moon?
Beaver Moon is the name given to November’s full moon. It rises around the time of year when beavers in North America retreat into their lodges , having stored enough food to last them through winter. Not exactly a Singapore problem, but we’ll take the cute name.
Other cultures have their own take on it. The Cree people of Canada and the northwestern US call it the Frost Moon, while the Tlingit people know it as the Digging Moon, a nod to animals digging and foraging for food as the ground hardens with the onset of winter.
Where to spot the supermoons in Singapore?
Image credit: @andrers2b via Reddit
You won’t need any fancy telescopes or camera gear – just a good spot with clear skies. It’s recommended to head to open spaces like Marina Barrage , East Coast Park , and the Southern Ridges for an unobstructed, elevated view of the moon in all its glory, away from the glare of city lights.
Or, visit one of Singapore’s many scenic vantage points for a moon-gazing experience that comes with a side of city views.
The good news is that a full moon this bright is hard to miss from pretty much anywhere in Singapore, so a cloudy night is really your only enemy here.
Bonus: Catch the Leonid meteor shower on 17th-18th November
Image credit: NASA Science
There’s more to be excited about, but you’ll need to act fast for this one. The Leonid meteor shower peaks on 17th-18th November 2026 , and the best time to catch it in Singapore is between 3am and 5.30am, when the constellation Leo, where the meteors appear to shoot out from, climbs high enough above the horizon.
The shooting stars are actually bits of dust left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle. When Earth ploughs through this debris trail, the particles hit our atmosphere at about 71km per second and burn up in bright streaks. Under a perfectly dark, moonless sky, you could see up to around 15 meteors an hour, though Singapore’s light pollution and clouds usually mean fewer.
The best part is this meteor shower is visible to the naked eye. Telescopes and binoculars will actually make you miss the action, so just give your eyes 20-30 minutes to adjust to the dark, put your phone away and scan the whole sky instead of staring right at Leo.
Fun fact: about every 33 years, the Leonids can erupt into a full-blown meteor storm. In 1966, observers saw thousands of meteors a minute during an intense 15-minute stretch. The last storm was in 2002, and the next spike in activity is expected in the 2030s.
Sleep through the alarm, and the Geminid meteor shower has your back, typically peaking around 13th-14th December .
Bonus: Spot Uranus at its brightest on 25th November

title: 3 Back-To-Back Supermoons Will Shine Over SG Till Jan 2027, Plus Meteor Showers & A Uranus Sighting

body:
Sagye Lite to open at VivoCity on 25 November
Good news for sotbap fans: Sagye Lite is officially opening at VivoCity on 25 November 2026 ! To celebrate, the restaurant is giving out 1-for-1 sotbap , AKA Korean pot rice, for six days only.
Image credit: Sagye VivoCity via Google Maps
Sagye Lite is a more casual, affordable spin-off of the original Sagye, which served Korean pot rice and barbecue. At Sagye’s now-closed outlet in Tanjong Pagar, their sotbap was only served at lunch, with dinner focused on Korean barbecue, so Sagye Lite puts the pot rice front and centre instead.
The prices show the budget-friendly angle too. At Sagye Lite, you can get the Grilled Chicken Pot Rice ($12.90++) and the Grilled Pork Belly Pot Rice ($13.90++) . If you want something heartier, there’s also the Beef Bulgogi Pot Rice ($18.90++) .
You can also get their viral Rose Yupdduk (price TBD) at VivoCity, which is a good chance to order it alongside your sotbap. If you want more to share, consider ordering their Korean side dishes, including Bossam ($8.90++) , Korean Pancakes (from $12.90++) , Korean fried chicken (from $14.90++) , and Rose tteokbokki ($18.90++) .
To enjoy the 1-for-1 promo, simply buy any eligible sotbap, and you’ll get a second eligible sotbap of equal or lower value free. The 1-for-1 promo runs from 25 to 30 November 2026 , with two redemption sessions every day.
A few tips before heading down: up to 300 complimentary sotbap redemptions are available daily across lunch and dinner sessions, so it’s worth going early if you can. There are also no advance reservations required for the promotion, and your redemption is only secured when you place your order in the store, so you’ll need to be there in person.
In more food news, read our Yee3 feature on the viral Chinese coconut drink brand that has opened at ION Orchard, and our Age.3 feature on the Ginza-famous fried sando brand with 35 flavours from $4.80.

Oriental Kopi and Niko Neko Matcha are teaming up for a second collaboration , following their Matcha Kaya collection in Aug 2026 .
Credit – @sinyeolsaw via Threads
This time, the two brands are introducing three new matcha -based drinks , with combinations that introduce Japanese tea flavours into Oriental Kopi’s kopitiam culture.
Credit – @sinyeolsaw via Threads & Oriental Kopi
The Nov 2026 series features Niko Neko’s YURI matcha in three variations, each paired with a different flavour profile. One of the more interesting additions is Kopi Matcha Latte (RM14.90) , which combines aromatic Malaysian kopi with Japanese matcha .
Credit – @sinyeolsaw via Threads & Oriental Kopi
For those who prefer a more straightforward matcha drink, Oriental Kopi will also be serving Classic Matcha Latte (RM13.90) — blending fragrant YURI matcha with creamy milk. It’s the simplest option of the three, but sometimes that’s all you need to satisfy your cravings.
Credit – @sinyeolsaw via Threads & Oriental Kopi
Meanwhile, Strawberry Matcha Latte (RM16.90) takes a fruitier approach, combining creamy matcha with tangy strawberry flavours. This one is a no-brainer — I mean, who doesn’t like a little strawberry in their matcha ? Not me!
Credit – Oriental Kopi
All three drinks will be available at Oriental Kopi outlets nationwide from 19 Nov 2026 . There is also a launch promotion running from 19 to 22 Nov 2026 , where customers can enjoy 30% off their second cup .
The latest menu follows the Oriental Kopi x Niko Neko Matcha’s previous collaboration, which explored Malaysian and Japanese flavours through three creations: Matcha Kaya Latte , Matcha Kaya Gelato , and Houjicha Pandan Kaya Gelato .
While the earlier lineup brought together matcha , houjicha , kaya and pandan , this newest collaboration focuses on drinks, with Kopi Matcha Latte being a particularly innovative addition to the menu.
Got your eye on any of these new drinks?

body:
Quirky road features in Singapore
Whether you’re behind the wheel or scrambling across road junctions, we all interact with roads on a daily basis. With how developed sunny Singapore is, finding a plot of land that the asphalt and pavements don’t cover is pretty dang hard. As such, it’s easy to overlook the oddities that whiz past our windscreens in a blur when we’ve got places to be.
From Joo Chiat’s trial of a crossing inspired by the busiest one in the world to a road in Upper Thomson that’s a measly 5 metres long, here are some quirky road features in Singapore to spot during your next drive or jaunt.
1. Shibuya-style scramble crossing in Joo Chiat
Image credit: Traveloka
You don’t have to hop on a plane to Japan to catch the Shibuya Crossing in action any longer. Although it’s not quite on the same scale as its Japanese counterpart, the road junction along Joo Chiat Road that’s right in front of i12 Katong now has its very own scramble crossing as we speak.
Image credit: CNA
This new scramble crossing is a 3-month trial by the Land Transport Authority (LTA) that hopes to alleviate traffic congestion in the area and improve pedestrian safety. Those who’ve been to the one near Lau Pa Sat will know the drill: when the green man on the traffic light shows, pedestrians can make their way across the junction from all sides , including diagonally , as traffic from all directions comes to a halt momentarily.
Will this become a mini tourist attraction of sorts? Perhaps, but one thing’s for sure; coffee runs at the many cafes in the neighbourhood are going to get a whole lot more lively with the increased footfall.
2. “End Of Friendly Streets” road sign
Image credit: Jacob Chin via Facebook
Don’t worry, there’s no imperial mandate that dictates you’ve got to wipe off your cheeky grin whenever you drive past the “End Of Friendly Streets” road sign. They’re there to remind you that you’re exiting a road that’s been designated as a Friendly Street .
If you don’t already know, the Friendly Streets initiative is a programme launched by the LTA that aims to make neighbourhood roads safer , especially for seniors, children, and persons with disabilities. These roads can be found in areas like Ang Mo Kio, Tampines, and Toa Payoh, and feature lower speed limits, longer crossing times at traffic lights, and special road markings and signs.
That brings us back to our ominous roadside sighting. Unless you’ve had too much to drink, you’ve got nothing to worry about when you catch the sign in your rearview mirror.
3. Overhead Rope Bridge at Old Upper Thomson Road
While we humans dread climbing overhead bridges with our lumbering bodies to cross busy roads, the animals which we share the island with don’t quite have the same luxury. Chancing upon roadkill is not uncommon when driving near green corridors like forest edges, and so NParks has decided to intervene.
Image credit: NParks
Many know about the massive Eco-Link@BKE bridge, but along Old Upper Thomson Road lies another one of NParks’ wildlife crossings, in the form of rope bridges . Strung across the road, several meters away from the zooming cars down below, these rope bridges help increase aerial connectivity for arboreal animals like the critically endangered Raffles banded langur .
The elusive primates have even been captured on video while crossing these bridges near Thomson Nature Park , showing tangible success for the project.
4. Jalan Ulu Seletar
Many of us take to the long, cross-island expressways such as the PIE, CTE, and TPE every day to get to and from work. On the flip side, we’re sure not many have travelled on Jalan Ulu Seletar .
Image credit: Reddit
It’s a road located near the outskirts of Nee Soon Camp, and its claim to fame is that it’s possibly Singapore’s shortest road , measuring in at around a mind-boggling 5 metres long . That makes it only a tad longer than an average-sized car, so we won’t blame you if you mistake it for a parking lot.
The road in the 1980s.
Image credit: National Archives of Singapore
According to a local historian, the road first appeared on maps dating back as early as 1923, and started off as an unnamed track, most likely serving nearby rubber plantations in Nee Soon Village. It was given its name in 1948, and by 1993, the last villagers residing in the area moved out, and most of the remaining road disappeared as private housing estates popped up in the area.
5. 3D road markings
Image credit: TestHub
At certain Silver Zones in Singapore, you might notice your peepers playing tricks on you, but it’s for your own good. Known as 3D traffic calming road markings , these eye-catching additions to our roads were implemented by the LTA in late 2018 to support their efforts in creating safer roads for all, drivers and pedestrians alike.
Image credit: LTA
…
summary: All eyes on the road please.
title: 8 Quirky Road Features In SG, From A “Shibuya Crossing” In Joo Chiat To A 5m-Long Road

4D3N Seoul i tinerary
Planning your next getaway to Seoul ? South Korea’s capital is packed with things to see and do, from centuries-old palaces and bustling shopping streets to trendy cafes and scenic parks. Plus, K-pop fans can visit filming locations featured in music videos by BTS, TWICE, and PSY.
For those visiting South Korea’s capital for the 1st time, this 4D3N Seoul itinerary covers popular attractions, cultural experiences, shopping districts, and even a few K-drama filming spots. We’ve also included flight options from Singapore, hotel recommendations, estimated prices, and useful travel apps to help you plan your trip.
The current exchange rate is S$1 = ~₩1037.30 as of 15th November 2026.
How to get to Seoul from Singapore?
Image credit: Trip.com
Travellers can fly directly from Singapore Changi Airport to Incheon International Airport , with flights taking approximately 6 hours and 20 minutes .
Several airlines operate direct affordable flights from Singapore to Seoul , including full-service and budget carriers.

Day 1
9.50am – Incheon Airport
Image credit: Incheon Airport
For this itinerary, we’re assuming a red-eye flight departing Singapore at 2.30am , with arrival at Incheon International Airport at 9.50am on the same day. Do factor in some time to clear immigration, collect your luggage, and travel to your accommodation in Myeongdong , where you can drop off your bags before heading out to explore the city.
1 pm – Myeongdong Kyoja
Michelin Bib Gourmand eatery that has been around since 1966
Image credit: 명동교자 본점 via Google Maps
Kick off your Seoul adventure with a hearty lunch at Myeongdong Kyoja , a family-run restaurant that’s been serving traditional Korean dishes since 1966. With just 4 dishes on the menu, the restaurant keeps things simple, focusing on its well-loved noodle and dumpling recipes.
Try the Kalguksu (₩8,000/~S$7.60) , a comforting bowl of hand-cut noodles served in a rich broth. Another crowd favourite is the Mandu (₩10,000/~S$9.60) , featuring generously filled Korean dumplings that pair well with the restaurant’s signature garlicky kimchi.
Image credit: Tripadvisor
If you’re visiting during summer, you can also try the seasonal Kongguksu , a refreshing Korean summer dish featuring chilled noodles served in a creamy, nutty soybean broth, for ₩13,000 (~S$12.40) .
Getting there: Take Subway Line 4 to Myeongdong Station , Exit 8 .

Anime conventions in Singapore 2026
Fans of anime, manga, and video games will be delighted to know that there’s no shortage of events which they can look forward to attending this year. To help you keep tabs on what’s on, we’ve compiled a list of upcoming anime conventions in Singapore in 2026 that will make your weeb heart sing.
1. Anime Festival Asia Singapore – 27th-29th Nov
One of the biggest anime conventions in Southeast Asia
Image credit: @animefestivalasia via Instagram
Anime Festival Asia is a core event for all anime fans, showcasing the latest anime, pop culture, manga, and novels. Every cranny of the convention hall will be crammed with things to do: live performances, meet-and-greets with celebrity cosplayers, and a Creators Hub where you can shop for fan-made or official merch.
This year’s concert lineup is one of AFA’s strongest yet. It kicks off on 27th November with composer Yuki Kajiura , the musical mind behind Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba and Puella Magi Madoka Magica . Next up, the AFASG26 Music Fest on 28th November brings Kyary Pamyu Pamyu and May’n to the stage.
The festival wraps up on 29th November with AFA VOCALOID NIGHT featuring Hatsune Miku . Concerts are ticketed separately from exhibition entry, so check the AFA ticketing page for details.
AFASG also has a food street if you’re feeling peckish at the event. If you’re not into shopping, you can bask in the festive atmosphere at their Day stage, which will have talk shows, live performances, and stage appearances from famous anime voice actors.
Image credit: Rhapsody Concept Pte Ltd
The big names in the industry are setting up shop here too; in particular, anime streaming site Crunchyroll is returning for yet another year. Cosplayers, you’ll want to swing by their booth for major photo ops. They’ve also got interactive sets recreating scenes from iconic series, such as the Crossroads Café from Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc and an Overgeared puzzle wall.
Admission: $25/pax
Date: 27th-29th November 2026
Venue: 1 Raffles Boulevard, Suntec Singapore Convention & Exhibition Centre, Singapore 039593
Find out more about Anime Festival Asia .
2. Singapore Comic Con – 5th-6th Dec
Curated booths with the best of comics, toys & gaming content
Image credit: @sgcomiccon via Instagram
Singapore Comic Con is where fans of comic culture gather. The convention celebrates comics, toys, and gaming – there will be something for everyone, even the normies. Come as a comic book character, or cosplay as your favourite show or game character. SGCC is known for their cosplay competitions, where you can win prizes worth up to $3,000.
BTW , you can use your SG Culture Pass credits to pay for your admission tickets to SGCC, so if you’ve got any left, now’s the time to put them to good use.
Admission: $38/pax
Date: 5th-6th December 2026
Time: 10.30am-8pm
Venue: 10 Bayfront Avenue, Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Singapore 018956
Find out more about Singapore Comic Con .
3. Doujin Market Mini – 12th-13th Dec
Indie artist haven with tons of fan-made merch
Image credit: Doujin Market
If you missed out on Doujin Market earlier this year, fret not, as Doujin Market Mini 2026 will be happening later this December. Even though it can’t quite match its predecessor in terms of scale, the vibe remains the same; expect to sieve through booths upon booths of fan-made merch , made by over 300 indie artists from all over the world.
Moreover, this one spotlights otome, josei, and gaming titles, so expect to fill your shopping bags with goodies from series like Love and Deepspace . There’ll also be stamp rallies to keep busy with during your visit – we’ve heard it’ll be Bungou Stray Dogs -themed. Finally, the event has a strict ban on AI art, so rest assured you’ll be supporting real, human creators.
Admission: $11.45/pax
Date: 12th-13th December 2026
Time: 12pm-7pm
Venue: 1 Raffles Boulevard, Suntec Singapore Convention & Exhibition Centre, Hall 405, Singapore 039593
Find out more about Doujin Market Mini 2026 .
4. EOY Music, Comics & Arts Festival – 25th-26th Dec
Live J-pop & Anime song performances with huge Creators’ Alley
For something to do over the Christmas break, look no further than the EOY Music, Comics & Arts Festival 2026 . As its name suggests, it’s a massive Japanese pop culture-fuelled event that’s taking place right before we tick over to 2027. But other than shopping at the popular Creators’ Alley that’s populated with over 100 booths, the main draw of the festival is its various live performances.
Image credit: Han Siong WONG via Flickr
Over at the event’s main stage is where you can tune in to captivating live J-pop & Anime song performances. Get your lightsticks ready for stunning shows put on by musical artists, cosplayers, and idol groups; a couple of them are even homegrown performers, so do pop by to #supportlocal.
Admission: From $19.90/pax
Date: 25th-26th December 2026
Time: 12.30pm-8pm
…

If you’re set on ending the year with a feast worthy of fireworks, check out our list to enjoy the best New Year’s Eve dinner in Singapore. Our favourite restaurants around the city are pulling out all the stops with all-you-can-eat feasts, luxe course menus, beachfront bashes, and non-stop bubbles. Wine, dine, and continue the festivities at the best New Year’s Eve countdown parties in Singapore after your meal.
Best New Year’s Eve dinner in Singapore
1. Writers Bar
Photography: Writers Bar
Fresh oysters, premium champagne and soulful live music – Writers Bar at Raffles Hotel Singapore is all set for an elegant pre-countdown celebration this New Year’s Eve. From 5pm to 8pm, this alluring bar offers an intimate and sophisticated atmosphere to wrap up 2026 and ring in new beginnings.
Come along with your beau or a loved one for an evening with fresh oysters and bubbly, alongside live music performances. Priced at $150, each set includes two glasses of Billecart-Salmon Brut NV Champagne and six Fin de Claire No. 3 French oysters. We can’t think of a better way to enjoy the last evening of the year!
Best for: An elegant celebration with fresh oysters and bubbly
Price: $150 per set
Date: 31 December 2026
Time: 5pm to 8pm
Address: Raffles Hotel Singapore, 1 Beach Road, Singapore 189673
Visit Writers Bar
2. Wu Yue Ting at Andaz Singapore
Photography: Andaz Singapore
Forget the usual New Year’s Eve menus and celebrations! Wu Yue Ting at Andaz Singapore puts a Cantonese spin on year-end celebrations at its first New Year’s Eve dinner cocktail party. Picture a convivial and sophisticated atmosphere, with refined Cantonese flavours and celebratory toasts throughout the evening. Taking centre stage is the restaurant’s signature Cherry Valley Roast duck. Gather around the live duck station to enjoy this succulent roast elevated with Oscietra caviar and traditional condiments.
More Cantonese specialties await, including Hong Kong-style thick seafood soup with black cod, sea cucumber and fish maw, as well as Cape Grim angus beef tenderloin with kampot black pepper. The desserts draw inspiration from both tradition and modern indulgence. Sweeten the celebrations with ginger milk curd with organic honeycomb, red bean soup with dried tangerine peel, and a Grand Cru chocolate ice cream bar with Wu Liang Ye Baijiu. Post-dinner, head to the Lobby Party to enjoy a late-night patisserie spread and await for the clock to strike midnight.
Perk alert: make a booking by 30 November 2026 to enjoy 20% off (T&Cs apply).
Best for: A convivial cocktail party with Cantonese specialties
Price: $168++ per adult (with access to the Lobby Party); $84++ per child aged 12 and below
Date: 31 December 2026
Time: 7pm to 11pm
Address: Level 25, Andaz Singapore, 5 Fraser Street, Singapore 189354
Visit Wu Yue Ting
3. Singapore Flyer
Photography: Singapore Flyer
Fancy living the high life (literally)? If you want your New Year’s Eve dinner to feel like a main-character moment, the festive menu at 165 Sky Dining by Singapore Flyer is hard to beat. This 90-minute experience takes you into the sky aboard Asia’s largest observation wheel, complete with priority boarding, welcome refreshments at the VIP Lounge, and a complimentary glass of champagne on festive dates.
On board, a five-course menu unfolds over three rotations. The meal opens with enticing appetisers like warm brie winter black truffle salad, and chilled pumpkin with honey pomelo. For mains, choose from Australian wagyu beef sirloin steak, Patagonian toothfish and Boston lobster, and vegetarian-friendly Chinese cabbage rolls. Sweeten the experience with raspberry chocolate pearl drizzled with vanilla sauce, petit fours by Janice Wong, and a selection of Nespresso coffee or Gryphon tea.
Perk alert: use the promo code ‘PEAK10’ from now till 30 Nov 2026 to enjoy 10% off 165 Sky Dining’s festive experience (T&Cs apply).
Best for: A cinematic, sky-high countdown dinner
Price: $560 for two pax
Date: 24, 25 & 31 Dec 2026 and 1 Jan 2027
Time: 90-minute experience with selected festive dinner slots (check booking page for exact times)
Address: 30 Raffles Avenue, Singapore 039803
Visit Singapore Flyer
4. Kinki Restaurant + Bar
Photography: Kinki Restaurant + Bar
On the hunt for free-flow bites, non-stop drinks, and a rooftop view of the fireworks? Make your way to Kinki Restaurant + Bar for your New Year’s Eve dinner bash in Singapore. The 2026 Grand Finale celebration is a free-flowing feast of Japanese fusion fare and tipples, including starters, mains, sushi, sashimi and desserts.
Expect plates like wagyu edamame, seaweed fries, rainbow maki, miso wagyu short ribs, and okonomiyaki mac and cheese. For more indulgence, pre-order the High Roller sashimi omakase for a chef’s selection of fresh cuts. And for those who want to party with a glass of bubbly, top up $128 per person to welcome 2026 with fizz, fireworks in the background, and Kinki’s DJ on the decks.

‘Tis the season for panettone in Singapore! Sure, Christmas log cakes may capture everyone’s attention, but a good ol’ panettone elevates the holiday celebration. Think of it as Italy’s golden, cloud-like Christmas bread: sweet, buttery, studded with fruit, and perfect for gifting or demolishing solo (or with a few friends). Here are the top places to find panettone in Singapore. But if you prefer something fruity, we know where to get the best Christmas fruit cakes in Singapore .
Why trust this guide
Consider this your festive panettone cheat sheet. We’ve rounded up Singapore’s noteworthy bakeries and shops, with options spanning traditional Italian recipes to indulgent modern twists. Our extensive research highlights flavour profiles, prices and ordering details to help you find the perfect loaf for gifting, hosting or keeping all to yourself.
Where to buy panettone in Singapore
1. Burnt Ends Bakery
Photography: Burnt Ends Bakery
Burnt Ends Bakery may be known for its wood-fired sourdough loaves and filled brioche doughnuts . But come Christmastime, the bakery goes above and beyond in delivering seasonal bakes that’ll be the talk of your group chats. Get your hands on the towering classic panettone round, and pair it with the lip-smacking doughnuts filled with chestnut pastry cream and topped with candied chestnuts.
Best for: Anyone who wants a luxe, bakery-style panettone that hits like a festive mic drop
How much: $88+
When to order: Pre-orders open now; available from 12 to 24 December 2026
Where to buy: Burnt Ends Bakery , order online
2. Fico
Photography: Fico
It’s beginning to look a lot like Christmas ‘cos Fico is going all out with its panettone festivo once again! This year’s bread, created in collaboration with Olivieri 1882, a family-run artisanal pastry house from Italy, pairs white chocolate with pistachio cream and a touch of sea salt. The offering comes in Fico’s signature chatreuse green box, complete with a fig-leaf-shaped card – it’ll make a lovely Christmas gift for family and friends, we reckon.
Best for: Lovers of rich, indulgent, ultra-premium panettone
How much: $89+
When to order: Available now
Where to buy: Fico , multiple locations in Singapore including East Coast Park and Tanjong Beach Club
3. Maiolika
Photography: Maiolika
Maiolika curates a small selection of Italian-style panettones, importing only the top three from Italy each week ensuring freshness. Expect classic and playful modern flavours like salted caramel. For this year’s celebration, the founder recommends getting the Tiri (“the premium choice”) or the Infermentum, the softest, tallest festive bread and one that kids love the most.
Best for: Those looking for fresh, imported artisan panettone with a twist
How much: From $79
When to order: Available now
Where to buy: Maiolika , order online
4. Prada Caffe
Photography: Prada Caffe
Want to spread a little festive cheer this year? Do it with a selection of panettone courtesy of Prada Caffe! Stick to the basics with the classic creation, or go a little ham with the chocolate, candied chestnut and pistachio variations. Chocolate lovers should get their hands on the decadent chocolate-covered mandorlato, chocolate-coated torroncini and chocolate mendiants. Oh, and be sure to save the (gorgeous) packaging!
Best for: Treating someone (or yourself) to the finer things
How much: $55
When to order: Daily, 12pm to 9pm
Where to buy: Prada Caffe , #01-01 and #02-15, Ion Orchard, 2 Orchard Turn, Singapore 238801
5. Baker & Cook
Photography: Baker & Cook
Celebrate the most wonderful time of the year with Baker & Cook’s selection of festive goodies, including the panettone. Each bread is made with lievito madre (traditional Italian sourdough starter) and slow-fermented for over 24 hours. The result: a soft, brioche-like creation filled with handmade almond marzipan and rum-soaked raisins, finished with a coating of melted hazelnut butter and a dusting of powdered sugar. We just know this will be a certified hit with your guests!
Best for: Shoppers who want something easy to grab at a neighbourhood bakery
How much: $32
When to order: Available from 1 to 27 December 2026
Where to buy: Baker & Cook , order online or at multiple locations in Singapore including Asian Civilisations Museum, Dairy Farm and Swan Lake
6. Da Paolo Gastronomia
Photography: Da Paolo Gastronomia
You can always trust the Da Paolo fam to bring out the Italian classics for Christmas. Go for the mini version if it’s your first time trying panettone. Otherwise, you’re welcome to sink your teeth into the tiramisu, rum and chocolate, or strawberries and white chocolate flavours. Packing Christmas hampers for your loved ones? Da Paolo’s festive breads will fit right in, snug as a bug in a rug.
Best for: Households that like to serve multiple flavours because everyone is a diva with preferences
How much: From $12.90
When to order: Available now (order three days in advance before 12pm)

body: The Hotel An old luxury name in Bangkok’s hotel scene, I finally stayed at Grand Hyatt Erawan Bangkok recently. My first impression after stepping into the hotel is the old-school grandeur. The Victorian-style atrium lobby is massive and is flanked by towering white pillars and dramatic high ceilings. It is classic luxury at its core, and you can tell the property has been standing its ground in the Ratchaprasong district for quite a while now. The biggest selling point for me is the unbeatable location. The hotel is located right next to the iconic Erawan Shrine, and it offers direct, covered access to the Bangkok Skywalk and Chit Lom BTS station, CentralWorld, and Siam Paragon. These are merits worth noting especially in Bangkok’s notorious traffic jam, where being able to get to spots by walking is a plus for me. In fact, I had to walk past this hotel previously when I stayed at the Waldorf Astoria Bangkok. As my room comes with club access, I was able to check in at the club lounge located on level 17. The Room I checked into the King Bed, Deluxe room with Club Access, and it is a decent 430 sq ft.

body:
Maan Maan Haang is a retro-themed cafe in JB Mount Austin
To me, the three most important things in a cafe are good food, good drinks, and good vibes. I especially love beautiful cafes where I can soak up the vibes and, more importantly, fill up my digicam. Recently, I visited Maan Maan Haang , a retro cafe in Austin Crest that delivered on all three.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~SS$0.31 as of 17 November 2026.
Maan Maan Haang is a pretty low-key cafe that looks unassuming from the entrance—we even got lost trying to find the cafe! However, step inside, and you’ll find the whole interior decked out in antique-looking decor. It’s almost like a time capsule that holds childhood memories of the ‘80s.
The area’s dimly lit, too, which makes it even more cosy and vibey. Every corner is chock-full of old-school furniture that makes for the perfect vintage digicam photo. I especially liked the display case showcasing digital cameras from different eras.
While the cafe maxed out on the aesthetics, they didn’t compromise on desserts and drinks either. Maan Maan Haang specialises in house-made tarts along with a lineup of refreshing beverages to wash it all down.
As a big fan of tangy desserts, I got the Lemon & Passionfruit Tart (RM17) , featuring lemon and passionfruit-flavoured curd sitting on a crumbly shortbread crust, topped with a swirl of meringue.
The lemon curd had a good balance of acidity and sweetness, and the tartness cut through the rich butteriness of the shortbread. The curd was also soft and jiggly, and it almost melted in my mouth. Overall, it wasn’t too sweet, which made it refreshing to eat.
We also ordered their signature Grape Yoghurt Cheese (RM19) , starring a yoghurt-cheese filling zhnged up with raspberry jam in the same shortbread crust, topped with Shine Muscat grapes and a gelatin coating.
If you love fruity desserts, this tart is for you. The jelly-like filling was sweet with a subtle tang from the yoghurt, amped up by the tangy raspberry jam. The grapes were fresh, big, and sweet, which helped to mellow everything out.
The weather was incredibly hot the day we visited, so my colleague and I had some drinks to cool ourselves down. Their Iced Matcha Latte (RM16) was among the best I’ve tried in Johor Bahru . It was strong, earthy, and umami. It wasn’t too sweet either, which was perfect for me. However, if you prefer your matcha milkier, you might want to give this a miss.
Instead, you can try the cafe’s speciality Train to Yuzu (RM15) : a blend of tea, soda water, and yuzu syrup for a sweet, refreshing drink.
Maan Maan Haang is located in Austin Crest, a 30-minute drive from CIQ Jalan Jim Quee .
If you’re cafe hopping in Johor Bahru, check out 365 Bakery , a TikTok-viral bakery with over 100 bakes, located just a five-minute walk away. Otherwise, read our guide to the best Mount Austin cafes for more solid spots in the area.
Address: 55, Jalan Jaya Putra 7/6, Bandar Jaya Putra, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia
Opening hours: Tue-Wed 12:30pm to 7:30pm, Thurs-Sat 12:30pm to 9:30pm
Website
Maan Maan Haang is not halal-certified.

summary: We visited Maan Maan Haang, a retro cafe in Austin Crest specialising in house-made tarts and refreshing drinks.

MODU, the samgyetang specialist from Mandarin Gallery and Amoy Street, opens its third Singapore outlet at Raffles City tomorrow, Thursday 19 November, and two of its soups will be sold nowhere else.
The new bowls are a Curry Laksa Samgyetang at S$40 and a Mugwort Samgyetang at S$37. The laksa one is MODU’s Singapore debut flavour, with the chicken in a rich coconut broth built on Southeast Asian spices. The same broth also comes as Curry Laksa Kalguksu, with handmade noodles, for S$34.
Curry Laksa Samgyetang, S$40, only at MODU Raffles City. Image: MODU
What is new at Raffles City
The Mugwort Samgyetang uses fresh Korean mugwort, or ssuk, in a light broth with a herbal edge. It is the gentler of the two Raffles City exclusives, and the one to pick if a laksa-flavoured ginseng chicken sounds like one idea too many.
Mugwort Samgyetang, S$37, another Raffles City exclusive. Image: MODU
Raffles City will serve 12 samgyetang. Classic Herbal is the cheapest at S$35. Perilla Seed is S$38, Black Garlic and Wild Mushroom are S$42, Truffle is S$46, and the Black Chicken and Premium Seafood bowl, with abalone and octopus, tops the menu at S$52. Every samgyetang there comes with unlimited herbal soup. If you order the Scorched Rice version at S$40, allow 20 to 30 minutes for it.
Classic Herbal Samgyetang, the cheapest bowl on the Raffles City menu at S$35. Image: MODU
Raffles City will serve organic chicken by the half, while Mandarin Gallery and Amoy Street use organic spring chicken. MODU says its chicken comes from halal-certified suppliers and every dish is pork-free and lard-free.
The grilled eel offer
Until 18 December, every two samgyetang ordered at Raffles City come with one Grilled Eel free. The eel is a S$34 sharing plate on the regular menu, served with two house sauces. The campaign is pitched at bringing your parents along, though that part is encouraged rather than required.
Order two samgyetang at Raffles City and the Grilled Eel is free until 18 December. Image: MODU
To claim it, show staff MODU’s campaign post on its @modu.singapore Instagram account when you order. The offer is dine-in only and valid at Raffles City only.
For two people, the 2-Gather Set at S$98 covers tea, an appetiser, two samgyetang, a sharing plate and dessert. Curry Laksa adds S$2 to the set and Truffle adds S$8.
Getting there
MODU Raffles City is at 252 North Bridge Road, #B1-06/07 Raffles City, Singapore 179103, in the basement of the mall at City Hall. From tomorrow it opens daily from 11am to 10pm. It is walk-in first, and groups can WhatsApp the outlet on 8087 0757. All prices are before the 10 per cent service charge and GST.
summary: MODU's third Singapore outlet opens at Raffles City tomorrow, 19 November, with two exclusive soups, Curry Laksa Samgyetang at S$40 and Mugwort at S$37, plus a free Grilled Eel for every two samgyetang until 18 December.
title: MODU opens at Raffles City on 19 November with a S$40 Curry Laksa Samgyetang sold only there

Ang Mo Kio residents can rejoice as neighbourhood coffeeshop S-11 AMK 530 Food House has finally reopened following renovations. The refreshed kopitiam welcomes back several beloved hawker stalls alongside a fresh look for diners.
Credit – Piow Piow via Google Maps
To celebrate the relaunch, 178 Fish Head Steamboat is offering an opening promotion that regulars will not want to miss. Diners can enjoy their XO Fish Head Steamboat at S$23 instead of its usual price of S$33 . This limited-time deal makes it an ideal spot for hearty family dinners without breaking the bank.
Credit – William Lai & Jia Her Yong via Google Reviews
For herbal soup enthusiasts, Ju Xiang Bak Kut Teh has also returned to serve warming claypot dishes. It’s helmed by a chef hailing from Klang, Malaysia, so you know you’re getting the real deal.
You can order their Klang Signature Claypot Bak Kut Teh (S$8.60/16.80/32.20) which is intensely herbal and nourishing. If you’re in the mood for more addictively tangy and savoury flavours, order their Claypot Vinegar Pork Trotter (S$7.50) instead.
Supper lovers will be glad to see Geylang Lor 9 Fresh Frog Porridge back in action at the coffee shop. The famous brand serves comforting bowls of its signature Frog Porridge (S$11/22/33) alongside smokey claypot goodies like Ginger Spring Onion Frog (S$11/22/33) .
Credit – Winston Ho & Soh Wee Kian via Google Reviews
Returning favourite Jin Long Wu Xiang Prawn Cracker is also back with crispy fried goodies starting from S$1.40 . Swing by for crunchy ngoh hiang and savoury sausages paired with a classic side of bee hoon .
Meanwhile, Auntie Jessie Rojak rounds up the line-up with plates of Traditional Rojak (S$5/7/9) and my personal favourite, Fruit Rojak ( S$5/7/9) , made with a generous heap of chopped cucumber, onions and pineapple dressed in a sticky-sweet sauce.

Singapore public holidays 2027
We all wish we could live the tai tai life, jetting off on holidays whenever we please without having to worry about work. Unfortunately, most of us still have bills to pay and a limited number of annual leave (AL) days to play with. But that doesn’t mean we can’t squeeze in a few extra getaways.
With a little strategic planning, you can turn Singapore’s public holidays in 2027 into 8 trips using just 12 days of AL. From quick weekend escapes to longer overseas adventures, here’s our guide to making the most of your leave without having to quit your day job.

*Saturday public holidays do not automatically mean the following Monday is a holiday. Eligible employees may receive a separate day off or extra pay instead. This affects Labour Day, Christmas 2027, and New Year’s Day 2028.
What happens if a public holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday?
Nothing hurts quite like seeing a public holiday fall on a weekend. But before you mourn the loss of an extra day off, here’s some good news: you might still be entitled to one, depending on which day the holiday falls.
According to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) , here’s how it works for those on a standard 5-day workweek:
• Saturday: Since it’s typically a non-working day, you’re entitled to either an extra day’s salary or a day off in lieu. But the following Monday isn’t automatically a public holiday, depending on your company’s policy.
• Sunday: Since it’s typically a rest day, the following Monday becomes a paid public holiday. Case in point: Monday, 8th February 2027, is a public holiday because the second day of Chinese New Year falls on Sunday.
These arrangements may differ depending on your work schedule, especially if you work shifts or have different designated rest days. We’d recommend checking with HR before you start plotting your next getaway.

Escape the CNY crowds and swap the usual trip to China or Taiwan for Siem Reap, Cambodia . February is one of the better months to visit Siem Reap, with relatively dry weather before Cambodia’s scorching hot season kicks in around March and April.
Channel your inner Lara Croft at Ta Prohm , the iconic temple featured in Tomb Raider , where massive tree roots have taken over centuries-old ruins. Then, explore the magnificent Angkor Wat and Bayon Temple , known for its giant stone faces. Once you’ve had your fill of temple-hopping, wind down with Khmer street food, local markets, and a traditional Apsara dance performance.

Image credit: Martijn Vonk on Unsplash
If you’ve been dreaming of seeing the Himalayas, March is a good time to plan a trip to Nepal . Spring is just kicking off, bringing relatively pleasant weather for exploring Kathmandu ‘s cultural landmarks and market stalls selling everything from singing bowls to handcrafted jewellery.
Start with the UNESCO-listed Boudhanath Stupa , one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world, before visiting Swayambhunath Temple , AKA the Monkey Temple, and the historic Bhaktapur Durbar Square . For a change of scenery, make a trip to Nagarkot , a hill station just outside Kathmandu, where you can catch sweeping views of the Himalayas at sunrise if the skies are clear.
You won’t be conquering Everest in 5 days, but at least you’ll get a taste of Nepal’s mountain scenery without having to lace up your trekking boots.

body:
Hey Yi Dessert has Chinese snow ice desserts in Johor Bahru
I have a confession: when I was younger, I was a die-hard hater of Chinese desserts (except for mango pudding—it’s still my kryptonite to this day). Perhaps one of the main reasons is that they’re usually not too sweet, and as someone with a fanatical sweet tooth back then, they didn’t satisfy my cravings enough. However, I’ve recently developed a newfound appreciation for Chinese desserts, and in my quest to catch up on the sweet treats I’ve missed over the years, I ended up at Hey Yi Dessert on my most recent Johor Bahru trip.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~SS$0.31 as of 18 November 2026.
15 Best Stalls For Traditional Desserts From $1.80
If you didn’t know: Hey Yi Dessert is a popular Chinese dessert chain in Johor Bahru, with over 25 outlets across Malaysia at the time of writing. During our trip, we visited the Mount Austin outlet, which opens till 2am—perfect for a late-night treat.
Food at Hey Yi Dessert
Hey Yi Dessert has over 90 items on their menu, ranging from savoury bowls to sweet treats. I low-key had choice paralysis because everything looked good, and I took some time to decide which desserts to order.
The standout is their White Peach Oolong Snow Ice (RM19.90) , comprising finely shaved white peach and oolong-flavoured ice, served alongside a spoonful of cheese foam, grass jelly, and white pearls.
The snow ice tasted strongly of CHAGEE Peach Oolong Milk Tea , which was good news for a CHAGEE addict like myself. Instead of dousing the snow ice in syrup, which leaves the lower layers bland, the snow ice itself was infused with white peach and oolong, giving the dessert a prominent, earthy oolong tea flavour. It wasn’t too sweet either, and didn’t leave behind an astringent aftertaste.
I highly recommend drenching the whole dish in cheese foam, which added some saltiness that balanced out the sweet, earthy flavours of the snow ice. However, I wished they had provided more cheese foam, as there wasn’t enough to cover the whole dish.
The grass jelly was a nice addition as well. It was jiggly with a nice bite for textural contrast, and lacked the herbal bitterness that usually turns people away. The white pearls also added some texture, with a satisfying pop and a crunch from the lotus root inside.
We also ordered their Mango, Glutinous Balls & Grapefruits Milky Mochi (RM14.90) , featuring grapefruit segments, mango popping pearls, sesame tang yuan, AKA glutinous rice balls, and fresh mango chunks sitting on a bed of their signature milk mochi.
The milk mochi had an addictively soft, stretchy texture and almost melted in my mouth. It also had an intense milky flavour that reminded me of White Rabbit Creamy Candy. It was served slightly warm, which complemented the chilled garnishes.
The toppings also enhanced the dish. The tartness of the grapefruit and mangoes cut through the richness of the milk mochi, while the mango popping pearls added sweetness. The sesame tang yuan was chewy, with a rich, nutty sesame filling that made the dish even more indulgent.
As a fan of matcha desserts , I had to get the Beancurd Pudding With Matcha Sauce (RM15.90) : soy beancurd slathered in an umami matcha sauce, then topped with a heap of black glutinous rice, slabs of matcha pudding, and chewy sweet potato and taro pearls.
The beancurd had a strong soy bean flavour and a velvety texture, though it wasn’t as jiggly or soft as I would have preferred. The matcha jelly and pearls were decent—I liked that they were QQ and not too sweet. Unfortunately, the glutinous rice was slightly undercooked, so it was hard to bite through.
For a change of palate, we tried their signature Traditional Chu Cheong Fan (RM9.90) , a medley of rice rolls, deep-fried fishballs, fishcakes and more, tossed in curry or sweet sauce. We opted for a mix, on the staff’s recommendation.
We definitely second their recommendation: the sweet sauce added a savoury depth with a subtle sweetness, while the curry added a slight spicy kick. The rice rolls were soft and provided the perfect base to soak up the flavours. The other toppings were average, though, and slightly too soggy.
Ambience at Hey Yi Dessert
Hey Yi Dessert’s interior reminds me of an old-school Hong Kong cafe, brightly lit with a retro Chinese aesthetic and distinctive red-and-white colour palette. Chinese elements and motifs are plastered around, while the red tiles and old-school metal seats and tables transport me back to an ‘80s Hong Kong film. The space was still well-ventilated, though, and felt breezy with ample aircon and fans.
The outlet we visited is in Mount Austin, but if you’re coming from JB customs, there’s also an outlet in Taman Melodies located just a 14-minute drive away.
Hey Yi Dessert—Eatbook Review
…
