body:
Sol & Manta is an aquarium-themed cafe in Joo Chiat
Image credit: Jay via Google Maps
I’ve always been fascinated by the sea, so dining at the aquarium restaurant in Sentosa has been on my wishlist for years. Unfortunately, it was always out of my budget, so I was happy to hear that Sol & Manta , Singapore’s first interactive aquarium-themed cafe, has just opened on Joo Chiat Road. Here, you can dine with marine animals for the price of a coffee.
Image credit: Lim Jaspar via Google Maps
Step into the cafe and you’ll notice large saltwater coral reef tanks that wrap around the dining area, along with floor projections that send “waves” rolling beneath your feet. The fun doesn’t stop there, because between bites, you can feed the goldfish or marine fish for $5 , or even pet a starfish.
Image credit: Mild Waranya via Google Maps
The food menu is more extensive than one might expect. For mains, highlights include the Charred Octopus ($37) , Duroc Porchetta ($33) , and Katsu Curry Don ($24) , while the pasta list features Uni Pasta ($32) , Cold Truffle Capellini ($27) , and Vongole ($25) , amongst others.
If you’re there for brunch, consider getting the Smashed Avocado Toast ($27) or Sol Garden Salad ($16) for something light. There’s also a kids’ menu with Spaghetti Bolognese ($14) and Fish & Chips ($16) , so it works for a family outing too.
The cafe offers a coffee menu too. We recommend the Ocean Dream ($10) , an espresso paired with coconut water, topped with a blue curacao cloud and coconut flakes to match the ocean theme. If you prefer the classics, get an Americano (from $6) or Latte (from $6.50) instead . Flavoured lattes are also available, including Hazelnut , Vanilla , Caramel and more.
Image credit: Mild Waranya via Google Maps
Matcha lovers will be spoilt for choice with Sol & Manta’s matcha-based signature drinks, which include the Violet Sea Cloud ($10) and Emerald Wave ($10) . The former comes with an ube cloud, while the latter features pistachio cloud foam and crushed pistachio
Image credit: Jay via Google Maps
Order some desserts to go with your drinks. A crowd favourite is the Chef Classic Tiramisu ($14) , along with the addictive Banana Fritters ($12) . Ice cream fans can go for a single scoop of Kapiti Ice Cream ($6) .
Sol & Manta is a 15-minute walk from Paya Lebar MRT Station .

body:
89 Carrot Cake sells handmade carrot cake in MacPherson
Image credit: MarilynC via Google Maps
Every time my friends and I discuss what to get for breakfast, the same few local dishes always pop up: kaya toast , economic bee hoon , and dim sum . However, I am a firm believer that fried carrot cake is the underrated GOAT of local breakfast dishes, and 89 Carrot Cake in Macpherson is one of the best. They even accept CDC vouchers , which is good news if you’re still looking for ways to spend them.
Which Is The Best Kaya Toast Franchise In SG? We Rank Ya Kun, Toast Box And More
Image credit: Hao Jun Chua via Google Maps
89 Carrot Cake was founded over 60 years ago by Uncle Zhang, who started off selling soon kueh and radish cake. Since his retirement in 2024, his daughter, a former childcare teacher, has taken up the mantle to continue his legacy with the same 60-year-old recipe.
Image credit: CP via Google Maps
What makes their dish stand out is that they make the radish cake fresh daily, lending a softer, smoother texture compared to store-bought variants, which tend to be denser and more starchy. It’s also said to have a subtle sweetness of radishes, with carrot chunks interlaced within the cake adding textural contrast.
Image credit: Chuan YEO via Google Maps
In the debate over whether black or white carrot cake is better, I’m on the latter team, and 89 Carrot Cake does their White Carrot Cake ($4) well. It’s said to be super garlicky and savoury, with a slight kick from the chilli paste. The scrambled eggs complement the soft, fluffy texture of the radish cakes, while the wok hei ties it all together.
Image credit: CP via Google Maps
For all Black Carrot Cake ($5) fans, theirs is equally good too. It features the same shebang of ingredients tossed in a sweet-savoury dark soy sauce that helps mellow out the chilli’s spice.
According to online reviews, wait times can stretch up to 20 minutes, so factor that in before you head down.
89 Carrot Cake is located at MacPherson Market & Food Centre , a nine-minute walk from Mattar MRT Station and a 14-minute walk from MacPherson MRT Station .
If you’re on a hunt for more hawker eats, check out our Three Bowls feature : a hawker stall run by an ex-Din Tai Fung chef selling kolo mee from only $4. Otherwise, read our Tampines hawker food guide for another hawker centre worth visiting on the Downtown Line.

Opening hours: Wed-Sun 6am to 11am
89 Carrot Cake is not halal-certified.

body:
Most of us grew up eating local fare. Over the years, we’ve grown so accustomed to the default ingredients that make up each dish that hanging one or two elements might seem like a mortal sin to purists. Take for example, nasi lemak , which is always paired with an open-faced omelette and chicken wings. So, when I found out through Google Reviews that Warmhouse Nasi Lemak at Chinatown Complex makes a couple of tweaks to this classic dish, curiosity got the better of me, and I had to swing by to try it for myself.
When we arrived, the inspiration behind the word ‘warmhouse’ became apparent. A quaint ceiling lamp cast a warm orange glow over the space, making it feel as though we had stepped into the kitchen of a welcoming household, awaiting for a humble home-cooked meal to be served.
We met Kenneth, a Singaporean ex-photographer, together with his ex-makeup artist wife, Cindy, a Taiwanese from Kaohsiung. Cindy shared that Kenneth enjoys cooking and loves to eat, while she’s obsessed over nasi lemak . Together, the couple decided to experience what it’s like to be a hawker and made the decision to combine the essences of both countries into their plates of nasi lemak . It also reminds them of their daughter, who is also a blend of 2 cultures.
What to order at Warmhouse Nasi Lemak
I fondly remember my first trip to Taiwan, where my ex-interns from my previous job had brought me to a pushcart stall near their university in Kaohsiung. An elderly uncle sold an assortment of deep-fried goodies, and that was where I first discovered my love for salt and pepper fried snacks. One bite, and I was hooked!
Thus, I was excited when we started off with the Set B Taiwanese Salt & Pepper Popcorn Chicken Nasi Lemak (S$5.50) — yes, I know, what a mouthful. I must say, for S$5.50 , to have at least 8 to 9 pieces of popcorn chicken was more than worth the price. They were accompanied by the usual peanut-anchovies combo, a fried onsen egg, sambal , and sliced Japanese cucumbers.
If you’re wondering whether this is the usual supermarket-bought frozen chicken nonsense, think again. Kenneth painstakingly marinates, breads, and deep-fries fresh chicken from scratch. As my molars sank into each crispy morsel, I was greeted by an almost-scalding gush of natural juices, accompanied by fragrant breading seasoned with salt, pepper, and five-spice powder, plus crispy fried basil leaves. Man, was it shiok !
Instead of the usual omelette or fried sunny-side up, the couple serves the dish with a lightly-fried whole ramen egg. I mean, who on earth would have thought that a flowy ramen egg would go so impeccably well with nasi lemak ? Soft, oozy, and melt-in-the-mouth — it was the perfect pairing. Cindy said the reason why they use ajitama eggs was because she dislikes how hard an omelette can get especially when it becomes cold.
The house-made sambal deserves a shout-out, too. Beyond its sweetness, it had a gritty texture and strong notes of sauteed onions and dried shrimp that gave it plenty of character. Mix copious amounts into the rice and thank me later!
Speaking of which, the rice wasn’t forgettable either, boasting a fluffy texture and rich coconut fragrance. I’m rarely blown away by every single component of a dish, but this was one of those rare occasions when everything just clicked with my palate.
We then moved on to the Set A Warmhouse Nasi Lemak (S$5) , which looked more like the default presentation that you see at almost every kopitiam or hawker centre stall. It came with a fried chicken wing, luncheon meat, and the same partners in crime as the previous dish.
The chicken wing was executed well, crispy and still maintained its juiciness. It also was seasoned properly — both skin and flesh — something that many other establishments fail to do. I’m rather icky whenever the skin and outer layer is flavourful, but the meat turns out bland and boring. It just goes to show that many of them didn’t marinate it long enough for the seasoning to penetrate thoroughly. As someone who drastically cut down on processed foods, that piece of luncheon meat felt like a little guilty pleasure. Simple, comforting, and thoroughly satisfying, it tasted like my childhood.
Who Warmhouse Nasi Lemak is best for
It’s perfect for nasi lemak traditionalists who love their default combinations. However, I’d recommend bringing a friend or two along so you can order one each to share, giving you the opportunity to savour both the traditional and more unique fusion versions.
How to get there?
You can take the MRT and alight at either Chinatown MRT Station (NE4/DT19) or Maxwell MRT Station (TE18) . Alternatively, there are bus services bringing you to the nearest bus stops: Maxwell Stn Exit 2 and New Bridge Ctr .
Do we recommend Warmhouse Nasi Lemak?
…

With fluffy coconut rice, generous portions and familiar sides such as chicken wings and luncheon meat, it is a reasonably priced option for nasi lemak enthusiasts curious about alternative ingredient combinations.

body:
I know it’s a cliché to say that time flies by, especially when it’s nearing the end of the year. But so much has happened in the last decade alone that I feel we all need a moment to relax and reminisce. Luckily for us, Vintage Market 2026 returns for its 4th edition at SAFRA Mount Faber from 27 to 29 Nov 2026. This year, the theme is ‘Growing Up with Singapore’, so I expect a lot of toys from when I was a kid. This might be the perfect spot to get a cheeky present right before Christmas as well.
Credit – Google
As the years fly by, we tend to forget all those electrifying childhood memories. That feeling of childlike wonder after seeing an old toy from when I was a kid genuinely heals my soul. I’m hoping that at Vintage Market 2026, we can all just take a step back and remember simpler times, a time when our biggest worry was getting our consoles to start after coming home from school.
Credit – Instagram
As for the venue, the Old Habit Cafe seems only fitting. The interior of the cafe is already decorated like a retro-style museum, filled with memorabilia from the 90s and before. For this event, SAFRA and their partners have curated over 50 booths that sell a variety of vintage items. From designer collectables to classic comics and retro arcade games, I would be surprised if there’s nothing there that ‘takes you back’.
Credit – Instagram
On top of that, visitors can explore around the market to collect stamps from booths and even try out different activities. Participation earns you souvenir patches, each representing a different hobby. You could also enter the lucky draw for a shot at winning a Nintendo Switch . For more details, check out their Instagram .
Credit – Google
While you’re there, why not partake in some of their delicious treats? Old Habits Cafe will still be open, serving signature dishes like their Simply Salmon (S$16.90) and sweet hits like the Old Habits Coconut Kueh Pouffle (S$9.90) .
Credit – Instagram
This event is also completely free! Step into your past and, who knows, you might find yourself recalling amazing memories long forgotten. Also, with events like these, you might find people cosplaying as their favourite childhood characters, so don’t forget your cameras.
On a personal note, it is so heartwarming that there are events and organisations like this that encourage us to embrace our inner child. While it’s only for 3 days, I can see myself being more excited to explore the games and toys from my childhood. I can only hope the same for all of you as well. So head down on Friday , 12pm to 9pm or on Saturday and Sunday from 11am to 8pm at SAFRA Mount Faber .
Best immersive VR experiences for a digital getaway
summary: Vintage Market 2026 is a free, 3-day event at the SAFRA Mount Faber Atrium from 27 - 29 Nov 2026, with no registration required. It has over 50 booths selling collectables, classic comics and retro arcade games, plus stamp-collecting activities and a Nintendo Switch lucky draw. It suits visitors who enjoy nostalgia and retro shopping.
title: Vintage Market 2026 – 50+ booths of retro toys, arcade games & classic merch

Christmas is around the corner. And that means it’s time for festive feasting! This Christmas, Rasel Catering welcomes the season of togetherness with ‘ Tinsel Gardenland ,’ a festive collection that unfolds across 6 themed menus, or ‘chapters,’ complemented by exclusive tea-infused appetisers and desserts specially curated with tea blends from The 1872 Clipper Tea Co.
Credit: Rasel Catering
Rasel Catering’s seasonal Christmas collection includes buffet , mini-buffet , and high tea options suitable for different group sizes and gatherings. As a halal-certified brand, Rasel Catering also lets customers plan inclusive Christmas parties with confidence.
Beyond delicious festive treats, the Tinsel Gardenland collection brings the vibes and aesthetics of a sparkling botanical garden to every table, turning every meal into a Christmas story.
High Tea Buffet
Credit: Rasel Catering
One set that stands out is The Secret Teahouse , which includes 9 items and 1 beverage . Customers can look forward to a range of festive pastries perfect for an afternoon tea party, from savoury treats to sweet desserts.

Buffet

Hello, Jellicle Cats , Theater lovers, or fans of Cats . With only a few days left to catch CATS the Musical , here’s our honest review ! Whiskers, wonder, and a whole lot of immaculate dancing (but not for long).
Photo by Adoncia Ho (Confirm Good)
CATS is one of the longest-running shows in West End and Broadway history , and seeing it live, it’s easy to understand why. Unlike most musicals, it doesn’t lean on a heavy, traditional storyline. It introduces a tribe of cats , a show about characters and spectacle more than plot, which is a big part of its charm. The enjoyment comes from feeling the rhythm and letting the live performance pull you in .
Credit: SISTIC
Up close, the cast is mesmerising and truly cat-like . From their facial expressions to their footwork and posture, every actor moves, prowls, and behaves like a cat, right down to the smallest flick of the head – talk about flawless chemistry and synchronisation . The mischievous costumes and detailed appearances brought each character to life, while the stage settings make you feel as though you’ve shrunk down and wandered into a world built for cats.
Credit: SISTIC
We were particularly amused by how each cast member had a distinctive costume that’s unique to them. It was easy to differentiate each character through their recognisable features, especially with so many cats on stage at once. Don’t be surprised if a cat wanders into your space! The cast steps off the stage to interact with the audience, making for an immersive show unlike any typical night at the theatre.
Who Should Watch
The interactive moments and playful costumes make it a fun group outing with friends and family. With no complicated plot to follow, it’s an easy, welcoming way to experience a musical. For dance and music lovers, the choreography and magnificent score are the real stars. Most importantly, this is a great chance to witness the classic live .
Credit: SISTIC
CATS isn’t your typical musical, and that’s exactly the point. It’s a dazzling song-and-dance spectacular that definitely gets your attention. Take this as your sign to catch the performance, soak up the music, appreciate the costumes, and simply enjoy the musical, with ticket prices starting at S$68 ! Grab yours here before the curtains come down on 22 November.
Do note that sales are final . No refunds or exchanges will be permitted. Go in with an open mind, enjoy the music, appreciate the costumes and let the cats draw you into the performance.

An Avengers: Doomsday Christmas at Orchard
If you’re a Marvel fan who’s been counting down to Avengers: Doomsday , here’s something to keep you occupied while waiting for the movie to release.
Orchard Road is getting a superhero makeover this Christmas, with an Avengers: Doomsday interactive trail featuring larger-than-life displays inspired by your favourite Marvel superheroes, a stamp rally, and exclusive merchandise up for grabs.
And the best part is you won’t have to spend a single cent to join the fun. Here’s what to expect there.
Explore Marvel-themed installations around Orchard Road
Image credit: @stanley_chee via Instagram
For those who have always dreamt of stepping into the Marvel Cinematic Universe, this might just be the closest you’ll get.
As part of this year’s Christmas on A Great Street celebrations, Orchard Road has been transformed with Marvel-themed displays featuring familiar superhero teams, including the Avengers.
Rather than having everything confined to one location, the installations are spread across the shopping district, turning your usual Orchard Road stroll into a mini superhero adventure. Fans can also look out for themed displays along the way, snap photos with their favourite superheroes, and collect stamps to complete a special Marvel mission.
Snap photos with Doctor Doom & a 13m-tall Avengers Christmas tree
Image adapted from: @bringyourkidout via Instagram
An Avengers: Doomsday experience wouldn’t be complete without an appearance from the movie’s iconic villain.
Head over to Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza , where you’ll find a life-sized figure of Doctor Doom, one of Marvel’s most formidable villains. It’s also one of the photo spots you’ll need to visit to complete the stamp rally.
And if you thought Orchard Road’s Christmas trees couldn’t get any more impressive, think again, because standing at a whopping 13m tall is an Avengers: Doomsday -themed Christmas tree , combining the festive spirit with the excitement surrounding the upcoming movie.
Complete a free Marvel stamp rally & redeem exclusive merch
Image adapted from: @ eternalieswme_ via Instagram
If you’re someone who can’t resist collecting limited-edition memorabilia, here’s another reason to head down.
You can embark on a free stamp rally around Orchard Road, tracking down designated stations to collect stamps and unlock a special reward. All you’ll need is your stamp card, a pair of comfortable walking shoes, and your phone for the final photo challenge.
Stamp rally hours run from 3pm to 10pm daily . Come December, the stamp rally hours on Saturdays and Sundays run from 3pm to 10.30pm . And on 24th December, Christmas Eve, the stamp rally runs from 3pm to 1am . However, the stamp rally is not available on eves of public holidays and on public holidays.
How to complete the Avengers: Doomsday stamp rally
Step 1: Collect your stamp card
Make your way to the Avengers: Doomsday Experience at Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza to pick up your free stamp rally card.
Step 2: Hunt for 4 stamps
Look out for the first 4 designated stamp stations outside Louis Vuitton, Prada, Coach, and at Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza. Follow the map on your card to avoid missing any stations.
Step 3: Complete your final mission
Image credit: @fishx7 via Instagram
Once you’ve collected the first 4 stamps, return to Ngee Ann City and snap a photo with Doctor Doom. Upload it to social media, tagging @MarvelSingapore and include #AvengersDoomsdaySG. This gets you the 5th and final stamp to complete the stamp card.
Step 4: Redeem your free Marvel gift
Present your completed stamp card and social media post at the redemption counter near Doctor Doom’s Throne Room to collect your final stamp and redeem a free gift, while stocks last.
Is the Avengers: Doomsday trail at Orchard Road free?
Yes, there is no purchase needed to participate in the Avengers: Doomsday trail and stamp rally.
When does the Avengers: Doomsday trail end?
The event’s last day is on 3rd January 2027 .
Where can I collect the stamp card?
You can collect the stamp card for the Avengers: Doomsday stamp rally at the Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza.
What time can I collect the stamp rally and the gift?
The stamp rally can be done from 3pm to 10pm daily . During weekends in December, the hours are extended to 10.30pm, and up till 1am on Christmas Eve. However, the stamp rally will not be available on the eve of public holidays and on public holidays.
When does Avengers: Doomsday release in Singapore?
Avengers: Doomsday comes out in cinemas on 17th December 2026 in Singapore.
Assemble your squad for the free Avengers: Doomsday trail
If you’re looking for something different from the usual Christmas shopping trip, the Avengers: Doomsday interactive trail is a fun way to soak up some festive vibe while getting your fill of superhero action.
Just remember to bring your phone, gather your squad, and complete your mission before the event wraps up on 3rd January 2027.
Avengers: Doomsday trail
Admission: Free

summary: There's a free Avengers: Doomsday interactive trail in Orchard Road.

Singapore’s new traffic rules
Whether you’re a seasoned driver or have just gotten your licence, there are a few changes to Singapore’s traffic rules worth taking note of.
With road fatalities reaching a 10-year high in 2025, the Traffic Police are tightening regulations to discourage reckless driving and improve road safety. From stricter demerit point thresholds to lower drink-driving limits, these changes could mean heftier penalties for motorists who flout the rules.
Here’s a rundown of the new and upcoming traffic rules in Singapore, what they mean for drivers, and when they kick in. Changes to the demerit points system start on 1st January 2027 , while the amended Road Traffic Act, passed in Parliament in August 2026, will take effect on a date yet to be announced.
1. Drivers can face suspensions with fewer demerit points from 2027
Image credit: Sky Media
If you’ve been driving for a while, chances are you’re familiar with Singapore’s Driver Improvement Points System (DIPS) . There’s a change to it coming that you’ll want to pay attention to, especially if you’ve accumulated a few demerit points.
From 1st January 2027 , non-probationary drivers, or those who have held their licences for more than a year, will face suspension after accumulating 18 demerit points within 24 months , down from the current 24-point threshold.
To put that into perspective, getting caught speeding and beating a red light within 24 months will get you 6 and 12 points respectively for a total of 18 points, and that’s enough to get you suspended.
Certain serious offences, such as dangerous driving and exceeding the speed limit by more than 50km/h, will also have their demerit point penalties adjusted from 24 to 18 points to align with the revised suspension threshold.
However, the good news is that motorists won’t be immediately disadvantaged by the revised thresholds. On 1st January 2027, there’ll be a one-time deduction of up to 6 demerit points for non-probationary drivers and 1 point for probationary drivers, based on their existing records.
2. New drivers face stricter licence revocation rules
Image credit: Sime Motors Singapore
Drivers who have held their licences for less than a year are considered probationary drivers , and they’re subject to a stricter set of rules. Currently, accumulating 13 demerit points during the probationary period will result in licence revocation. From 1st January 2027 , this threshold will be lowered to 12 points .
If you’re wondering what the difference between a licence suspension and revocation is, a suspension means you’re temporarily prohibited from driving for a specified period, while a revocation means your licence is cancelled.
This means probationary drivers who have their licences revoked will have to go through the process of obtaining a driving licence again, including passing the necessary tests.
3. Merely holding your phone while driving could land you in trouble
Image credit: Skylink Holdings
We’ve all been tempted to check our phones when a notification pops up. Under the amended traffic laws, simply holding a mobile communication device while your vehicle is moving will constitute an offence, even if you’re not actively using it. Currently, authorities have to prove that drivers are operating their phones, such as texting while holding them and driving.
It’s not just mobile phones. Other mobile communication devices, including tablets and smartwatches, fall under the amended rule too.
That said, drivers can still use properly mounted devices , such as a phone secured to a dashboard holder, for navigation. Holding a device while the vehicle is stationary is also not an offence.
The change will also allow the Traffic Police to enforce the rule using cameras and photographic or video evidence submitted by members of the public. However, this rule has not come into effect yet, and the date has also not been announced.
As for the penalties, first-time offenders can face a fine of up to $1,000 , imprisonment of up to 6 months , or both. Repeat offenders may face a fine of up to $2,000, imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.
4. Lower drink-driving limits in Singapore
Image credit: Adobe Stock
If you usually have a drink or two before driving home, it’s time to rethink that habit. Singapore is lowering its legal drink-driving limits by more than half , meaning even a single beer could put you over.
Under the revised limits, the drink-driving limit in Singapore for breath tests will drop from 35 micrograms to 15 micrograms per 100ml of breath .
Similarly, the blood alcohol limit will be reduced from 80mg to 30mg per 100ml of blood. The revised limits will bring Singapore more closely in line with countries such as Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan, which have stricter drink-driving regulations.
…
summary: Singapore is tightening its traffic rules, with changes to demerit points, drink-driving limits and mobile phone use. Here's what motorists need to know.
title: 7 New & Upcoming Traffic Rules For SG Drivers To Know, Including Changes To Demerit Points

Finding the best Christmas desserts in Singapore is a must for sweet tooths. From rich chocolate log cakes and sugary cookies to traditional bakes like panettone and stollen, the glorious assortment makes our hearts flutter. We scoured the city for top bakeries, restaurants and cafes to bring you the most decadent desserts worth indulging in – or, to share the love with someone. Ah, Christmas in Singapore is starting to look oh-so-magical!
Why trust this guide
When it comes to Christmas desserts in Singapore, we take them just as seriously as our festive dinners. When your calorie bank is at stake, you should make room for only the best sweets. To make it worth your waistline (and your wallet), we meticulously taste, try, and hunt down desserts that sound delicious and are often tried and tested by our team. You’re welcome.
Christmas desserts in Singapore
1. Cloudmills
Photography: Cloudmills
Cloudmills has been one of our favourite bakeries to visit lately, and it has just added six new festive creations to get into the holiday spirit. The black forest Christmas shokupan takes Cloudmills’ signature double chocolate shokupan up another level with rum-soaked cherries. A whimsical touch is the Little Merry Man, a gingerbread man-shaped doughnut that’s almost too cute to eat. And we can’t say no to a shio pan, especially when it’s stuffed with black forest ham, cranberry, brie, and truffle mayonnaise. Everything is baked fresh daily, so all bakes are on a pre-order basis and only available in limited quantities. Get your orders in ASAP!
Price: Bakes start from $2.20
Availability: Until 31 December 2026
Delivery: Pick-up only
Where to purchase: Cloudmills , order online
2. Cafe Mary Grace
Photography: Cafe Mary Grace
Cafe Mary Grace is celebrating its first Christmas in Singapore and is bringing full-on Filipino vibes with it! The cafe has transformed for Christmas, with a new festive menu to go along with it. You can expect the same soulful fare, inspired by home-cooked family favourites like chorizo tapas, longganisa meatball linguine, and the Mary Grace beef stew. But we’ve got our eyes on the desserts! There’s a classic fruit cake (of course), but we’re going for the banana caramel log cake and the fabulous hazelnut praline mousse decorated with a chocolate Christmas tree.
Price: Cookies from $21; brownies from $22; cakes from $48.50
Availability: Available until 31 December 2026
Delivery: Delivery starts from $20
Where to purchase: Cafe Mary Grace , order online
3. Janice Wong
Photography: Janice Wong
What better way to add festive magic to your celebrations than with edible works of art from Janice Wong? This beloved chocolatier returns this holiday season with the Art of Christmas Collection, a whimsical line-up of cakes, hand-painted chocolates and other edible works of art. For a striking statement piece, bring out the winter globe yule log, featuring chestnut mousse, redcurrant compote and a rich brownie base. Slice through the cake to reveal a charming, hidden snow globe design.
Another showstopper is the emerald-hued Christmas wreath, with layers of blueberry lavender cheese mousse, mascarpone mousse, apricot crumble, blueberry madeleine cake and ruby chocolate feuilletine. Other charming picks include hand-painted bon bons in unique renditions like Earl Grey lavender and salted caramel popcorn, and paper baubles filled with chocolate dragees that’ll look pretty on your tree.
Price: Cookies from $20; chocolates from $22; cakes from $88
Availability: Online orders open from now till 31 December 2026
Delivery: Delivery starts from $18; express delivery from $23
Where to purchase: Janice Wong , order online
4. Old Seng Choong
Photography: Old Seng Choong
We can always count on Old Seng Choong to put out nostalgic festive-themed treats every Christmas season. This year, the brand launches two new desserts that both the young and young at heart will adore. Peep the watermelon lychee swiss roll with raspberry bits, a refreshing alternative to the usual indulgent festive desserts. Bite into the light and fluffy Swiss roll lined with luscious cream and tangy raspberry bits.
Meanwhile, the new giant festive cookies are sure hits with the kiddos. These whimsical creations come in three irresistible varieties: an Oreo-flavoured reindeer, a red velvet variation topped with a Christmas tree, and sea salt dark chocolate with snowflake frosting. Need gifting ideas? We reckon the classic brandy fruit cake and baked mini palmier make timeless options.
Price: A la carte items from $35.80; bundles from $41.80
When to order: Online orders open now; available for delivery and pick-up from now till 31 December 2026
Delivery: Delivery starts from $15; free for orders above $120
Where to purchase: Old Seng Choong , order online and at multiple locations including Paragon and Weave at Resorts World Sentosa
5. Alice Boulangerie & Restaurant
Photography: Alice Boulangerie

From rich chocolate log cakes and sugary cookies to traditional bakes like panettone and stollen, the glorious assortment makes our hearts flutter. We scoured the city for top bakeries, restaurants and cafes to bring you the most decadent desserts worth indulging in

Ever been told not to play with your food? This dinner says go for it. 7 Paintings – The Art of Dining is Conrad Singapore Marina Bay ’s newest dining experience, a 7-course dinner show where you paint, play and puzzle your way through the works of Michelangelo, Banksy, Picasso, Pollock, Warhol, Dalí and Van Gogh. It’s held at Lounge by the Pool on Level 4, runs Wednesday to Sunday.
It’s a natural fit for a hotel with over 3,400 artworks. Each course honours one artist and hands you a little task over about two and a half hours, whether that’s painting, listening to a short story or cracking a riddle. Banksy’s Girl with Balloon is even stencilled on a plate, waiting for you to finish it with spray cans.
I went for the Premium Menu (S$230++), created by Executive Chef Thomas Jakobi and his team and found only at the hotel. It kicked off with Brown Crab , a dainty tartlet with curry emulsion, nashi pear and caviar, brightened by organic lemon dashi . The Veal Carpaccio followed, with silky slices lifted by truffle mayonnaise, sakura cress, olives and rucola. Then came the Flamed Murray River Cod , a tender fillet in lemon beurre blanc with chargrilled broccolini, potato pavé and tomato chutney . Hands down, this was the highlight of the entire spread.
The Vegetable Painting was my favourite course to play with. This is Pollock’s turn, so you get a palette of spinach coconut, beetroot and pumpkin purée to paint with, alongside goma dressing, leaf lettuce, chicory, primal carrot and young celery.
Next was the Wagyu Beef Tenderloin , rich and indulgent with creamy smoked morels, asparagus-hazelnut, fermented garlic and rutabaga-cress.
Dessert came in two acts. The Crema Catalana arrived with mint and berries and a scoop of salted caramel ice cream, and the grand finale was the Chocolate Painting on Citrus Cake . Inspired by Van Gogh, it comes with chocolate-chilli, white chocolate raspberry and tart strawberry sauces, so you get to add the finishing touches yourself.
There are 4 menus to choose from, all following the same seven acts: Classic and Vegetarian (S$190++ each) , Premium (S$230++) and a Children’s Menu for ages 6 to 12 (S$99+) . Free Flow Drinks Packages are available as add-ons from S$20++ .
Dining starts at 7pm on Wed, Thu, Fri and Sun, with two Sat sessions at 5pm and 8.30pm.

body:
The Ralph Lauren Holiday Experience at Marina Bay Sands
Singapore might not be getting a white Christmas, but that doesn’t mean we can’t enjoy a little festive magic. While Mariah Carey is busy defrosting for the season, Ralph Lauren is bringing its signature The Ralph Lauren Holiday Experience to Marina Bay Sands (MBS) for the first time.
The Adirondack spirit runs through the whole thing, giving the free Christmas pop-up a cosy countryside charm that feels worlds away from the city with its own outdoor ice rink. We were able to get a sneak peek, so here are some of the highlights to look out for.
What is The Ralph Lauren Holiday Experience all about?
Now in its 2nd year, the Ralph Lauren Holiday Experience is making its Singapore debut , with the global festive campaign expanding from 4 cities last year to 7 this year, including London, Tokyo, and Seoul.
The Lion City is among the first to welcome the holiday activation, with it running from 20th November to 26th December 2026 at Marina Bay Sands Event Plaza , right beside the Rain Oculus. This year, the pop-up takes its design cues from the traditional lakeside retreats of the Adirondack Mountains, with a Boathouse-inspired setting that brings a touch of Americana to the waterfront.
Open from 10am to 10pm daily , you’ll be able to explore the whimsical installations, take part in decorative workshops, or indulge in festive treats. Admission is free , but you’ll have to reserve a slot beforehand to enter the pop-up.
What to expect from The Ralph Lauren Holiday Experience
Customise your own Christmas wreath & postcards
Step inside and the first thing you’ll clock is the massive wooden cabin, the kind you’d expect to see in a holiday flick like The Christmas Chronicles . The fully air-conditioned interior is decked out with classic Yuletide decorations and pieces from Ralph Lauren’s latest seasonal collection.
In the cabin, you’ll find the Wreath Making Bar where you can design your own Christmas wreath to hang on your front door. Each session runs 30 minutes , and while there are no instructors leading you through it, staff are on hand if you need a little nudge in the right direction.
The wreath base is prepared, so all you have to do is dress it up. Pick from a selection of foliage and ornaments, including ribbons , acorns , and magnolia leaves . You can also add holly berry branches and trim them to your preferred length with the scissors provided.
Once you’ve settled on your design, use the hot glue gun to secure everything in place.
Fun fact: The foliage and berries are all natural, adding an extra touch of authenticity to your handmade wreaths.
To finish things off, choose a charm to complete your wreath. There are 3 designs to pick from, including a Christmas stocking and 2 variations of Polo Bear , Ralph Lauren’s iconic mascot. If you’re happy with your creation, let the staff know, and they’ll pack it up for you to bring home.
There are also complimentary postcards for all visitors. Write a heartfelt message and mail it to your loved ones, or hold onto it as a memento of your visit.
For Ralph Lauren fans, there’s another little perk here to look out for. Hit a minimum spend of $800 on selected products at Ralph Lauren’s MBS outlet to redeem a custom embroidery on your purchases. Simply show your receipt to the staff at the embroidery station to get yours personalised.
Wreath Making Bar:
Date: 20th-22th & 27th-30th Nov, 5th-6th, 12th-13th & 19th-20th Dec 2026
Time: Sessions at various timings
Postcard Atelier:
Date: 20th Nov to 26th Dec 2026
Time: 10am to 10pm
Embroidery Station:
Date: 20th-22th & 26th-29th Nov 2026
Time: 12pm to 8pm
Lace up your skates at the ice rink
For the kiddos, the Ralph Lauren Ice Skating Rink is probably the main highlight of the whole experience. Live out your own little winter wonderland without having to get on a plane away from Singapore. Just like Ice Penguin Singapore , it uses synthetic ice , but that doesn’t take away from the fun; it still gives you a similar feeling to skating on the real thing.
Before hitting the ice, make sure you’re geared up with the necessary safety equipment. Knee , elbow , and wrist guards are provided, along with helmets to protect you from any accidental falls. You can also pick out a free pair of ice skates that fit you comfortably before heading out to the rink.
There are also lockers available, so you can keep your belongings safely stored away while you skate.
If skating isn’t your forte, there are skating aids to help you find your footing while you wobble about. Little ones can also pretend to be Santa by hopping on one of the mini sleighs and taking a ride around the rink.
Each session accommodates up to 20 people and lasts 45 minutes ; that’s plenty of time to practise your moves and live out your Disney On Ice fantasies. The rink is recommended for those aged 7 and above , while skaters aged 18 and below must be accompanied by an adult.

Christmas fruit cakes are a nice alternative for your holiday table in Singapore. They may not be as eye-catching as Christmas log cakes or as symbolic as panettone in Singapore , but the festive treats still pull their fair share of fans. If you’ve been waiting for the one list to find Christmas fruit cakes in Singapore, look no further – we’ve got you covered. Diet who? Exactly.
Why trust this guide
Our team has rounded up Christmas fruit cakes from bakeries and patisseries across Singapore, looking at everything from traditional rum-soaked recipes to contemporary twists. We’ve considered flavour profiles, ingredients, price points and ordering details to help you find the right festive centrepiece, whether you’re shopping for a family gathering, a thoughtful gift or simply a slice to enjoy with your afternoon cuppa. So you can spend less time searching and more time savouring the festive season.
Where to buy the best Christmas fruit cakes in Singapore
1. Burnt Ends Bakery
Photography: Burnt Ends Bakery
Burnt Ends Bakery doesn’t just stock panettone in Singapore – you can get a Christmas fruit cake here too. Yes, the team’s going all out to make sure you have a holly jolly Yuletide this year. Its version is studded with black raisins and candied citrus soaked in Drambuie for a lush kick. But why stop there? The bakery stocks other Christmas desserts in Singapore that’ll satisfy all sweet-tooth cravings.
Best for: Boozy fruit cake fans who like their bakes luxe
How much: $48+
When to order: Pre-order is open now; Available from 12 to 24 December 2026
Where to buy: Burnt Ends Bakery , order online
2. Old Seng Choong
Photography: Old Seng Choong
Nothing screams Christmas more than the aroma of the classic fruit cake, and Old Seng Choong has one that’ll drive you absolutely nuts. The homegrown brand’s offering is densely packed with candied fruits and nuts, complemented by a splash of brandy for a festive touch. We say it’s a stellar addition to your holiday spread.
Best for: Fans of dense, nostalgic, nut-packed festive bakes

Where to buy: Old Seng Choong , order online
3. Baker & Cook
Photography: Baker & Cook
Baking a festive fruit cake ain’t easy, but we know a quick solution: by hitting up Baker & Cook. This homegrown brand’s aged rum fruit cake features mixed fruits slowly macerated in dark rum for almost a year. The patience! The dedication! This results in plump, tender fruits that have fully absorbed the liquor, enhancing the flavours and textures.
Best for: Traditionalists who want a rum-soaked classic done right
How much: $55+
When to order: Available now
Where to buy: Baker & Cook , order online
4. Swissbake
Photography: Swissbake
Chocolate and orange go well together – and that’s one hill we’re willing to die on! If you’re on our side, you’ll love Swissbake’s chocolate orange fruit cake. It’s a delightful twist on a Yuletide tradition, brimming with zesty orange and rich, indulgent chocolate.
If you prefer a more classic flavour, the cranberry lemon fruit cake is your jam. Picture tangy cranberries, refreshing lemon and festive fruits, all melting decadently in your mouth as you chew into the confectionery. Delicious!
Best for: Chocolate-orange lovers and newbies who need converting
How much: $28
When to order: Pre-order is open now; available from 7 to 27 December 2026
Where to buy: Swissbake , order online
5. Keong Saik Bakery
Photography: Keong Saik Bakery
Who says Christmas fruit cakes in Singapore gotta cost an arm and a leg? Keong Saik Bakery comes through with this number: a buttery creation bursting with flavour, thanks to the mixed fruits, toasted almonds, honey and molasses. There’s a touch of spices too for a lovely balance. The large cake can be shared among nine people, while you can consider the mini or sliced versions for your Christmas hampers .
Best for: Budget-friendly gifting without skimping on flavour
How much: From $4.90
When to order: Pre-order is open now; no deliveries from 24 to 28 December 2025 and 31 December 2025 & 1 January 2026 (only self pick-up at its outlets)
Where to buy: Keong Saik Bakery , order online
6. Nesuto
Photography: Nesuto
It ain’t Christmas without a traditional brandy fruit cake – and this homegrown brand is serving just that this holiday season. Nesuto’s rendition is infused with the finest brandy, sweet fruits, nuts and spices. The first bite will immediately transport you to a winter wonderland! The fruit cake is best enjoyed at room temperature. Or, keep it in the fridge if you want to store it for longer. Nesuto also offers an alcohol-free option that can be shared by all.
Best for: Anyone craving a proper old-school brandy fruit cake
How much: $66
When to order: Available now (order must be placed by 2pm the day before for next-day delivery)
Where to buy: Nesuto , order online

body:
SanSara, the North Indian restaurant at Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel on Havelock Road, has a refreshed à la carte menu, and its most unusual new dish is octopus cooked in the tandoor.
The Tandoori Octopus is S$36: 130g of tentacles charred in the clay oven that usually turns out naan and tikka, served with a smoky yoghurt chutney. At that weight it is a starter to share, ordered next to a curry, rather than a main.
Tandoori Octopus (top left) and Duck Leg Biryani (left) lead SanSara’s refreshed menu. Image: Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel Singapore
What is on the refreshed menu
The menu is the work of Master Chef Pannalal Nath, who comes from West Bengal and made Awadhi cooking, the cuisine of the old royal kitchens of Lucknow, his speciality. The newer plates lean modern without leaving the tandoor behind.
• Duck Leg Biryani, S$42: duck leg confit over basmati rice, with yoghurt raita on the side. It sits next to the Shahi Gosht Dum Biryani with Australian lamb shank at S$39 and the Lucknowi Murgh Dum Biryani at S$30.
• Kurkure Kekda, S$32: a 300g deep-fried soft-shell blue swimmer crab with an Indian romesco sauce and pickled vegetables.
• Barrah Chops, S$56: a 250g grass-fed New Zealand lamb rack from the tandoor, marinated in ginger and garlic, with smoky yoghurt chutney, Indian mashed aubergine and an olive goat cheese naan. It is a reworked dish: the August 2025 menu listed a 380g Australian rack at S$59.
• Ratna-E-Samundar Curry, S$54: Hokkaido scallops, prawns, mussels and squid in a sauce of turmeric, fenugreek and coconut cream.
Barrah Chops, S$56. Image: Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel Singapore
For vegetarians
Two of the newer small plates are meat-free. Avocado Ki Tikki, S$28, is a pan-seared spinach and avocado cake topped with avocado mousse and finger lime caviar. Lotus Papdi Chaat, S$22, is the chef’s own chaat finished with crisp lotus chips.
To try both at once, the vegetarian Combo Platter at S$42 puts them together with the Aloo Bukhara Tschaman Tikka, a Kashmiri cottage cheese starter with spiced prunes.
Avocado Ki Tikki (right) and Lotus Papdi Chaat (back) on the vegetarian side of the menu. Image: Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel Singapore
The vegetarian regulars stay, among them Sarson Ka Saag Makki Di Roti at S$26 and the black lentil Dal-E-SanSara at S$27.
The signatures that stay
Most of the old menu stays. Gosht Ki Galouti, the soft minced lamb cake that the restaurant traces to the kitchen of Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula of Lucknow, is S$38. Nasila Dungar Lal Maas, a smoky Rajasthani lamb shank curry with Mathania chilli and rum, is now S$45, up from S$40 on the August 2025 menu.
For dessert, the new Exotic Fruit Chutney is S$21, a plate of tropical fruit with coconut ice cream, passion fruit coulis and meringue. Gajar Ka Halwa and Rasmalai are also S$21, and the Salted Caramel Malai Kulfi is S$23.
Exotic Fruit Chutney, S$21. Image: Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel Singapore
À la carte or the festival set
If you already know SanSara for its galouti and dal, the octopus and the duck biryani are the two new reasons to go back. If you would rather not order à la carte, the restaurant’s North Indian Food Festival set menus, one vegetarian and one non-vegetarian, run until 31 December at S$98 each.
Getting there
SanSara is inside Grand Copthorne Waterfront Hotel at 392 Havelock Road. It is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. From Wednesday to Sunday it serves lunch from 12pm to 2.30pm and dinner from 6.30pm to 10.30pm. Reservations are on +65 6233 1338. All prices are in Singapore dollars and before service charge and GST.
summary: SanSara at Grand Copthorne Waterfront has refreshed its North Indian menu: Tandoori Octopus at S$36, Duck Leg Biryani at S$42, Kurkure Kekda soft-shell crab at S$32 and two new vegetarian small plates.
title: SanSara refreshes its North Indian menu with S$36 Tandoori Octopus and a S$42 Duck Leg Biryani

If your idea of a good bakery haul involves squeezing your purchases rather than eating them, Squishery’s latest pop-up might be right up your alley. Making its debut at KLGCC Mall , the brand has set up a bakery-themed space filled with slow-rising squishies inspired by bread, pastries and other sweet treats.
Credit – Squishery
Running until 22 Nov 2026 , the pop-up offers a playful shopping experience where you can grab a basket and fill it with squishy versions of bagels, cookies, chocolate bars and giant waffles.
There’s even a special interactive bakery experience for those who pick between 8 and 12 squishies , where the staff take on the role of little chefs to prepare your purchases before you bring them home.
Credit – Squishery
Among the collections to look out for is the Squishy Squad , featuring a lineup of charming characters such as Capy Red Bean Cake, Butter Cat, Mini Butter Cat, Cream Hug Roll, Capy Bread, Moozy Cheese, Little Piggy, Bear Swiss Roll and Pink Bean Squishy.
Bread lovers, meanwhile, will want to browse the Moozy Bakery Series . Expect plenty of familiar bakery-inspired designs, including Grandpa Toast, Butter Croissant, Butter Pineapple Bun, Pupu Milk Butter Crisp, Giant Waffle, Moozy Lava Pineapple Bun, Toasted Marshmallow Toast and Twist Bread, alongside other designs.
Credit – Squishery
Beyond their cute appearances, these squishies are fun to play with, thanks to their soft textures and slow-rising quality. The bakery-style gift boxes also make them a charming pick for anyone who enjoys collecting novelty toys or is looking for a quirky little gift.
There’s another reason to stop by KLGCC Mall while the pop-up is around. Shoppers who spend RM100 at any mall outlet in a single receipt can redeem a Polo Bun Squishy , while stocks last.
The Squishery pop-up is located at G-02-01 , in front of Jaya Grocer Signature at KLGCC Mall. You can drop by daily from 10am to 10pm until 22 Nov 2026 , so there’s still time to pick out a few squishy treats before the bakery closes.

summary: Squishery’s bakery-themed pop-up at KLGCC Mall features slow-rising squishies modelled after breads, pastries and sweet treats, including the Squishy Squad and Moozy Bakery Series. Running daily from 10am to 10pm until 22 November 2026, it is suited to novelty toy collectors and shoppers seeking quirky gifts, with an interactive shopping experience for purchases of 8 to 12 squishies and a free Polo Bun Squishy with RM100 mall spending.

Christmas plans don’t always have to revolve around a meal (although we’re not saying no to one). Sometimes, a couple of hours spent making something with friends is just as good a way to get into the festive mood.
This December, A Very Palais Christmas brings together an evening of festive creativity featuring hands-on Christmas craft workshops and a premium gift-wrapping experience paired with a festive meal.
Taking place on Thursday, 10 December, each workshop is limited to just 20 spots a. Bring a friend, make it a date night or drop by for some creative time after work.
A Very Palais Christmas: Details at a glance
Best for: A festive evening out with friends, a partner or yourself
Date: Thursday, 10 December 2026
Time: 6.30pm to 8pm; registration from 6.15pm
Price: $50 for a Single ticket; $95 for a Duo ticket, excluding Eventbrite fees
Address: Palais Renaissance, 390 Orchard Road, Singapore 238871
Get your tickets here!
Pick your Christmas craft
Photography: Cottonbro Studio via Pexels
First things first: what would you like to make? There are three 45-minute workshops to choose from (all crafting materials included!) – personalise a festive faux wreath, decorate four Christmas cookies, or style two transparent baubles for your tree. Everything you make is yours to take home, and all workshops are beginner-friendly.
Add a festive touch to your home with a personalised faux Christmas wreath. Get creative with the decorative elements and put together a seasonal piece to hang on your door or give to someone special.
Photography: Miguel González via Pexels
Prefer something edible? At the Christmas cookie decorating workshop, you’ll decorate four pre-baked cookies with icing and festive details, with no baking required.
Or, give your Christmas tree a personal touch at the Christmas bauble decorating session, where you’ll fill and style two transparent, shatterproof baubles. All three workshops are beginner-friendly, so no prior crafting experience is needed. Just pick your favourite and come ready to get creative!
Give your presents a finishing touch
Photography: Laura James via Pexels
Whichever workshop you choose, your ticket also includes a 20-minute premium festive gift wrapping session. You’ll practise styling a small gift box with wrapping materials and ribbons Pick up a few creative techniques to give your Christmas presents an extra-special finish. After all, a beautifully wrapped gift makes the festive season feel that little bit more special.
A little something to enjoy while you craft
Photography: Binary
No festive evening is complete without something good to eat. What’s on the menu depends on the workshop you choose, with each experience taking place at a different venue within Palais Renaissance.
At Cakebar’s Christmas cookie decorating workshop, you can choose a single cake and a drink from the available selection to enjoy during the activity. There’s more to take home, too: each participant will receive a box of four assorted Fatty Macarons, alongside their decorated cookies.
Joining the Christmas wreath workshop at Binary? You’ll get to choose one main: slow-braised Angus beef cheek with celeriac purée, beef jus and edamame; pan-seared Norwegian salmon with pomme purée, mixed greens and brown butter; or Iberico secreto with basil chimichurri and roasted greens. Your meal also comes with a choice of selected coffee, tea or another beverage.
Additional food and drinks ordered beyond the event inclusions will be charged separately.
Choose your workshop when you book
The three workshops take place at the same time in separate venues within Palais Renaissance, so you’ll need to select your preferred experience when purchasing your ticket. Guests will stay at their chosen venue throughout the event.
A Single ticket admits one person, while a Duo ticket admits two people to the same workshop. Each session is limited to 20 participants, with places available on a first-come, first-served basis.
Pick your craft, bring your Christmas spirit and leave with something you’ve made for the season!

Sometimes, a couple of hours spent making something with friends is just as good a way to get into the festive mood. This December, A Very Palais Christmas brings together an evening of festive creativity featuring hands-on Christmas

We’ve sussed out the best bakeries that provide everything you need to put together your own edible masterpiece. The Christmas festivities aren’t complete without an activity to bond over. And what better way to bond than to get messy with icing? Except maybe playing Overcooked… If you’re on the lookout for other Christmas desserts in Singapore , we’ve also got a list of where to get the best Christmas panettone in Singapore and Christmas fruit cakes in Singapore .
Why trust this guide
Christmas is a big deal with our team, especially the little rituals that come with it. Family bonding is sacred personal time that we always try to make extra special, and what better way to get everyone involved than making something together? And when you don’t have the time to create the building blocks yourself, trust in these gingerbread house kits that are as fuss-free as it gets.
Where to buy gingerbread house kits in Singapore
1. Lego
Photography: Lego
Things can get messy when icing sugar is involved, and we get it. After giving your house its much-needed holiday sprucing, you don’t need sticky fingerprints everywhere. Which is why Lego’s solved all your problems! This festive gingerbread house will keep the kids (and even adults) occupied without worrying about any clean-up afterwards. The best part? You can keep it on display or dismantle the whole thing and restart the process for next year!
Price: $59.90
Where to buy: Lego , available online
2. All Things Delicious
Photography: All Things Delicious
All Things Delicious is best known for its halal treats, so its gingerbread house kit is ideal if you’re sharing it with a big group with dietary restrictions. This set comes with gloves, which means no need to actually get your hands all dirty and sticky! Pipe the house together with the naturally coloured royal icing and dust it with the snow powder for that frosted look. Psst: for every kit sold, All Things Delicious donates $1 to its It Takes A Village fund for kids at Sun Beam Place!
Price: $39.80
Where to buy: All Things Delicious , available online
3. Bud of Joy
Photography: Bud of Joy via Facebook
If you know someone with strict dietary restrictions, but you still want to include them in the fun, turn to Bud of Joy. It might have the only gingerbread house kit in Singapore that’s gluten-free, vegan, and made without eggs, dairy, or nuts! It also includes all-natural icing free from additives and preservatives, coloured with natural pigments from beetroot juice, carrot powder, and barley grass powder.
Price: $49
Where to buy: Bud of Joy , available online
4. The Frosted Chick
Photography: The Frosted Chick
The Frosted Chick’s kid-friendly gingerbread house kit comes with everything your kiddos need to put their own festive display together. You’ve got the usual suspects like the gingerbread biscuits, icing sugar, decorations, and cake board. There are also written and video instructions that are easy to follow! Leave them to handle the assembling while you focus on your Christmas dinner prep.
Price: $69
Where to buy: The Frosted Chick , available online
5. Anna’s Gourmet
Photography: Anna’s Gourmet
Anna’s Gourmet brings food and specialities from Central and Eastern Europe, so it doesn’t get any more authentic than this. Its gingerbread house kits come straight from Germany, the veritable home of gingerbread. You’ll get a full kit plus decorative candies to bring the house to life. You can also find gingerbread men cookie cutters if you plan on baking for Christmas.
Price: $55.90
Where to buy: Anna’s Gourmet , available online
6. Redman by Phoon Huat
Photography: Redman by Phoon Huat via Facebook
Singapore-based company Phoon Huat has always been our best friend when it comes to stocking up on baking necessities, and it’ll be yours with its pre-made gingerbread house. The kit comes with powdered sugar, a piping bag, and some ornaments for decoration. If you want to get out of the house for some family bonding time, consider signing up for Redman’s Christmas log cake or butter cookie-making workshops.
Price: $59.70
Where to buy: Redman by Phoon Huat , available online and at NTUC Fairprice outlets
7. Ikea
Photography: Ikea
Building gingerbread houses is a Swedish tradition, so it’s only natural Ikea stocks plenty of them for the holidays. This budget-friendly option is a great pick if you’ve got multiple guests to entertain. And don’t worry – in true Ikea fashion, the kit comes with a pictorial instruction manual. It’s even easier to build than the furniture! P.S. This kit doesn’t come with icing sugar, so you’ll have to get some to put it together.
Price: $10.50
Where to buy: Ikea , available online and at multiple locations including Tampines, Alexandra, and Jurong
8. Marks & Spencer
Photography: Marks & Spencer
…
summary: Gingerbread house kits in Singapore may seem difficult to find, but that’s where we come in! We’ve sussed out the best bakeries that provide everything you need to put together your own edible masterpiece. The Christmas festivities aren’t complete without an activity to bond over. And what better way to bond than to get messy
title: Where to buy gingerbread house kits in Singapore

Check into the best staycation hotels in Singapore for a well-deserved break. After being tired out from endless deadlines and to-do lists, there’s nothing like a rejuvenating weekend lounging by an infinity pool or enjoying royal treatment at a world-class spa . Having stayed at diverse abodes throughout the years, we’ve sussed out the best staycation in Singapore spots for your next escape. Need options for a longer stay? We’ve got your back with the best serviced apartments in Singapore .
Best hotels in Singapore for staycations
Our recommendations if you’re pressed for time:
• For unparalleled luxury: Capella Singapore
• A taste of local heritage: Hotel Indigo Singapore Katong
• For a sustainable stay: Parkroyal Collection Pickering, Singapore
• Best for exploring the city centre: JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach
1. Four Seasons Hotel Singapore
Photography: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore
Stroll along the tree-lined Orchard Boulevard, and a tranquil urban sanctuary will come into full view: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore. This luxurious stay puts you at the heart of Singapore’s vibrant shopping district, with curated dining, wellness and other leisure experiences that make it hard to leave. Check into one of the 259 rooms and suites, and you’ll know what we mean. Bright, airy and spacious, the abodes come outfitted with all the essentials and boast spectacular views of the city or verdant greenery.
You don’t have to venture far to satisfy your hunger pangs. The hotel’s distinct dining experiences span across Japanese-Peruvian cuisine at Nobu, a Michelin-selected experience at Jiang-Nan Chun, as well as local and Western fare at One-Ninety Restaurant. For well-deserved R&R, make your way to the award-winning spa for holistic wellness therapies, massages and treatments, or Chi Longevity Clinic for medical expertise on optimising your health. Other noteworthy amenities include two swimming pools and three outdoor courts for tennis, padel and pickleball – we hear it’s the only hotel pickleball court in Singapore to offer a Krystal Pro surface that enhances shock absorption!
Perk alert: as part of the Experience More offer, receive spending credits (eligible for dining, wellness and other curated experiences) with a minimum three-night stay at Four Seasons Hotel Singapore; valid for stays from now till 31 Dec 2027 (T&Cs apply).
Best for: A luxurious urban sanctuary with curated dining and wellness experiences

Address: Four Seasons Hotel Singapore , 190 Orchard Boulevard, Singapore 248646
2. The Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore
Photography: The Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore
With its sleek and modern facade, you can’t miss this waterfront jewel that sits along the vibrant Fullerton Heritage precinct. The Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore is a tribute to the Lion City’s bygone era, occupying the space of old Clifford Pier where Singapore’s forefathers landed. We’re big fans of the luxurious rooms and suites that come equipped with elegant interiors, floor-to-ceiling windows and spectacular views. Psst: some top-tier rooms even have an outdoor sundeck!
The hotel’s not short of exquisite dining experiences, too. Indulge in classic French bistro favourites at La Brasserie, or head to The Landing Point for a fancy afternoon tea and bespoke cocktails. If you’re looking to impress, swanky rooftop bar Lantern is the place to be. Savour gourmet snacks, bubbly and cocktails while grooving to live DJ sets.
Best for: A historical waterfront destination
Key facilities: Rooftop pool and jacuzzi; gym; spa
Address: The Fullerton Bay Hotel Singapore , 80 Collyer Quay, Singapore 049326
3. Paradox Singapore
Photography: Paradox Singapore
Check into a stylish stay with authentic local charm at Paradox Singapore. Situated in the vibrant Clarke Quay area, this urban resort offers picturesque views, comfy abodes and an unbeatable location. From vibrant dining and nightlife to family-friendly attractions and iconic cultural landmarks, its location sets you up for easy-breezy city exploration. Plus, enjoy handpicked local-inspired experiences at the hotel’s dining destinations. Savour gourmet local delicacies and sip botanical cocktails infused with fresh herbs from the edible garden, or go on a curated neighbourhood tour.
We have to talk about the 476 chic rooms and suites. Each spacious abode features thoughtful amenities like a water filter tap, a modern bathroom, and an ergonomic chair and desk set-up. For a family retreat or friends’ getaway, opt for the Premier Two Queen room that comfortably accommodates up to four guests. To complete your rejuvenating stay, unwind at the free-form swimming pool with a water slide and a jacuzzi. Or, chase endorphins with a sweaty workout at the double-storey fitness centre that’s open 24 hours.
Best for: An urban stay in Clarke Quay with authentic local charm

body:
McDonald’s Maple BBQ burgers launch on 26 November 2026
Image credit: McDonald’s Singapore
PSA: From 26 November 2026 , 11am, McDonald’s is rolling out a limited-time menu built around flavours from its outlets in Canada, Japan, and Australia. Headlining it are the new Maple BBQ Burgers , which come in beef and chicken versions.
McDonald’s x G-DRAGON Collab: Spicy Bulgogi Burger, Exclusive Merch And More
Hamburglar, the masked, stripe-shirted troublemaker from McDonaldland, is the face of this campaign. He’s getting his own merch drop and a run of in-store appearances too. It’s been a busy year for McDonald’s burgers in Singapore, from the Honey Mustard McCrispy Burger launch in April to the McDonald’s x G-DRAGON Spicy Bulgogi Chicken Burger in October, and this is its big festive-season drop.
Image credit: McDonald’s Singapore
The beef version is the Maple BBQ Quarter Pounder with Cheese , inspired by a McDonald’s Canada item. The double has two beef patties stacked with crispy chicken bacon and fried onions, then slathered in a maple BBQ sauce that’s meant to be both smoky and sweet. Meals start from $10.50 for the single and $12.90 for the double.
Image credit: McDonald’s Singapore
For chicken fans, the Maple BBQ Chicken Burger swaps the beef for a crispy chicken fillet. It keeps the chicken bacon and maple BBQ sauce, so you get plenty of crunch. Meals go from $10.50 for the single and $12.80 for the double.
You can get both burgers after breakfast hours at all outlets and Drive-Thrus, plus on McDelivery, GrabFood, foodpanda and Deliveroo.
Image credit: McDonald’s Singapore
That’s not all: the new Szechuan Sauce is a mildly spicy dip with peppercorn notes, made for your fries and Chicken McNuggets. You can choose it as your dip when you buy Chicken McNuggets, or add a tub for $0.70 .
To wash it all down, the Sakura McFizz comes from McDonald’s Japan and is a nod to the country’s cherry blossom season. It’s an icy pink drink with a light floral note, from $3.65 .
Image credit: McDonald’s Singapore
McPops, AKA McDonald’s rendition of mini doughnuts, are back in Singapore with two new flavours. The Pistachio McPops are fluffy chocolate pastries with a creamy pistachio filling. The Biscoff McPops come from McDonald’s Australia and are making their debut here, with Biscoff cream piped into the centre of a soft pastry. Each flavour comes in a set of two, from $2.95 .
Image credit: McDonald’s Singapore
There’s also a new Popcorn Caramel soft serve that mixes caramel with a toasted popcorn flavour. You can get it as a Twist Cone, ChocoCone, Sundae with hot fudge or strawberry sauce, or a McFlurry with Oreo bits. Look for it after breakfast hours at Dessert Kiosks and participating outlets.
The Maple BBQ Burgers and the rest of the menu are only around for a limited time while stocks last, so go soon if you want to try everything.
For more burger options around the island, check out our best burgers in Singapore guide . You can also read our guide to the best 1-for-1 buffet deals in 2026 for more affordable eats!

McDonald’s is halal-certified.

body:
Shuu Cafe is a cottagecore cafe in Johor Bahru
I’ve always joked with my friends that my dream life is to live in the countryside, surrounded by lush greenery and mountains, fully embracing my cottagecore dreams. While that ideal stays firmly in the realm of fantasy, the recently relocated Shuu Cafe in Johor Bahru gets me pretty close, especially when cafe hopping is already on the agenda.
15 New JB Cafes To Visit In 2026: Sausage Dog Cafe, Free Boardgames And More
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~SS$0.31 as of 18 November 2026.
Shuu Cafe is a quaint Korean-inspired cafe with a cottagecore vibe, specialising in choux pastries, caneles, and other artisanal bakes. They first opened in Dato Onn before relocating to their newer, bigger space in Taman Abad late last year.
The cafe is set in a rustic brick-and-wood cottage structure, the kind you’d stumble across in Seoul or rural Europe. There’s even a private garden decked out with aesthetic white garden furniture and picturesque views, making every corner perfect for the ‘gram.
Step inside and it genuinely feels like you’ve wandered into someone’s home. The space is furnished with wooden tables and personal knick-knacks, which adds to the homely feeling.
Natural light streams through the windows, making it a lovely space for a slow brunch or afternoon tea with friends.
The ambience alone could carry the visit, but the food and drinks hold their own just as well.
Their signature is their choux pastries, available in a plethora of flavours, from familiar picks such as Chocolate (RM15++) and Madagascar Vanilla (RM17++) , to more unexpected ones including Calamansi Guava (RM15++) .
We, however, settled on their Pistachio Choux (RM18++) . It featured choux pastry with a crunchy craquelin coating, generously packed with pistachio cream, then finished with roasted pistachio bits.
Honestly, it was one of the best choux pastries we’ve had in a while. The choux pastry was light and airy on the outside, while the pistachio cream inside was rich and nutty, making the whole experience feel very indulgent. The pistachio flavour was further enhanced by chunks of pistachio for additional crunch and sweetness.
We also got their Matcha Canele (RM12++) , a matcha-flavoured variant of the French patisserie that’s filled with an oozy matcha lava centre.
Though their choux pastries get all the hype, we feel the caneles are just as delicious. It had a hard, caramelised outer crust and a slightly chewy, almost custard-like interior. The matcha lava centre was bittersweet, which helped balance the sweetness of the pastry.
Before our sugar high fully set in, we pivoted to their Rosti Benny (RM36++) : pan-fried rosti topped with poached egg and garden salad, finished with hollandaise sauce.
This provided a savoury contrast to the sweet pastries we had. The rosti base was golden-brown and crispy with a soft, fluffy interior, while the eggs were perfectly poached and runny. The hollandaise sauce was rich and creamy, elevating the whole dish.
We tried some of their drinks to wash it all down. Their Flat White (RM15++) was smooth and well-balanced, and wasn’t overly milky either. It even managed to receive a stamp of approval from my coffee-obsessed colleague.
The Creamy Matcha Peach (RM20++) was a decent option; the matcha was rich, umami, and wasn’t too sweet. Surprisingly, the flavour of the peach complemented the earthiness of the matcha for a cohesive, refreshing drink.
Shuu Cafe is located an eight-minute drive from JB customs.
If you’re hunting down more aesthetic cafes in Johor Bahru to snap more aesthetic pictures for your feed, check out Maan Maan Haang , a retro ‘80s-themed cafe with handmade tarts. Alternatively, read our guide to the best food in KSL City , located a 14-minute walk away.
Address: 203, Jln Wijaya, Taman Abad, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia
Opening hours: Thurs-Tue 10am to 6pm
Website
Shuu Cafe is not halal-certified.

Photos taken by Chan Zi Xuan.
This was an independent visit by Eatbook.sg.
summary: Shuu Cafe is a cottagecore cafe in Johor Bahru serving pistachio choux, rosti, and picturesque views.

IKEA’s Christmas Vinterland is starting this December
Image credit: IKEA Singapore
Ho ho ho! December is ‘round the corner, which means Christmas is on its way. What better way to celebrate the season than to head to IKEA Singapore for their first-ever Christmas market , Christmas Vinterland .
Image credit: IKEA Singapore
From 4 December 2026, IKEA Singapore’s Joyful Bites brings together over 20 traditional Swedish brands and beloved homegrown ones, including Old Chang Kee , Le Matin Patisserie and more. IKEA Family members also get special deals from selected participating vendors from 4 December to 6 December 2026 .
Curry Puff, Empanada Or Pasty? Londoners Try To Guess Singapore’s Favourite Snack
It’ll be running at IKEA Tampines over three weekends: 4 December to 6 December , 11 December to 13 December , and 18 December to 20 December , from 2pm to 4pm. If you’re not near the East, fret not; you can enjoy the same festivities at their Alexandra outlet from 2pm to 4pm on 6 December , 13 December , and 20 December, and at their Jurong outlet from 2pm to 4pm on 5 December , 12 December , and 19 December .
Image credit: IKEA Singapore
There are also workshops your kids can enjoy while you do your Christmas shopping. The Joyful Cookie Party is happening on 12 December , 13 December , and 20 December at their Tampines, Alexandra, and Jurong outlets , respectively, and allows participants to decorate their own Vintersaga gingerbread cookies with a variety of toppings, from icing to candies to jellies. Do note that there are only three time slots per day: 1pm, 3pm, and 5pm, with limited availability for each.
Alternatively, you can join their myriad of Christmas Craft Workshops , where you’ll get the chance to make your very own Christmas craft using IKEA products, including the Snow Globe Making , Candy Jar , and Snowflake Decoration workshops. Each outlet is hosting its workshops on different days, so check IKEA Singapore’s website before heading down.
Image credit: IKEA Singapore
For a taste of a more traditional Swedish Christmas, IKEA Singapore is hosting a Luciatag performance at their Tampines outlet. For the uninitiated, Luciatag is a Swedish procession in December that celebrates Lucia Day, a holiday commemorating the martyr Lucia of Syracuse, who brought food to Christians hiding in Roman catacombs, using only a candlelit wreath to light her way. On 6 December 2026 at 2pm, catch this tradition of light, hope, and togetherness live, through a series of Lucia songs that may include the centrepiece, Sankta Lucia .
There are more events happening at IKEA outlets islandwide, so check their website to see what’s on the schedule before heading down.
As part of the Christmas celebrations, IKEA has a Christmas buffet for just $29.90. Read our IKEA Christmas buffet feature for a sneak peek at what’s in the lineup. Alternatively, if you’re hosting your Christmas celebrations at home, check out our guide to the best catering companies to tick food off your checklist.

IKEA Singapore is not halal-certified.

Apartment Coffee ranks 6th on World’s Best Coffee Shops list
Image credit: @apartmentcoffee
You may have heard the news by now: Apartment Coffee has officially become the 6th best coffee shop in the world and the best in Asia-Pacific for the second consecutive year.
The Singaporean roastery secured its spot on the World’s Top 100 Coffee Shops 2026 list through a combination of international panel evaluations and public votes, further cementing its reputation as one of the finest cafes on our shores.
If you haven’t visited Apartment Coffee before, it’s time to fix that. They’re located along 139 Selegie Road , a short six-minute walk from Rochor MRT Station .
Image credit: @apartmentcoffee
The cafe is helmed by Yeo Qing He, an award-winning barista who placed in numerous coffee brewing competitions before this latest accolade, including sixth place at the World Brewers Cup in 2018.
40 Best Coffee Cafes In Singapore, Including Local Roasters That Sell Coffee Beans
Regulars love their seasonal menu as there’s always something new to explore each time. Filter coffee is the focus here, but you can also get your favourite espresso-based White (from $6) or Black (from $5.50) if you prefer. Look forward to trying beans from around the world, including less common options.
Image credit: @a p artmentcoffee
Coffee enthusiasts can also recreate the cafe experience at home with Apartment Coffee’s monthly subscription plan . Enjoy freshly roasted whole coffee beans delivered to your doorstep, and choose between filter roast or espresso roast. Additionally, subscribers get first dips on small-batch, seasonal coffee drops from time to time.
Image credit: @apartmentcoffee
Apartment Coffee’s space is bright and airy, with an industrial, minimalist aesthetic. Expect concrete floors, clean walls adorned with quirky artwork, and modular seating areas designed for different group sizes.
You can keep your eyes peeled on Apartment Coffee’s Instagram page for the latest updates.
For other places to sort your caffeine fix, check out our guide to some of the best local kopi stalls in Singapore ! The list includes YY Kafei Dian along Beach Road for traditional Hainanese kopi, fluffy kaya buns, and chicken rice. Otherwise, check out our guide to the best food places in Dhoby Ghaut for more options in the area.

How’s Catering introduces its Festive Platter Boxes for intimate gatherings of 5 to 12 pax . Savour the Meat Up Platter or Sea La Vie that’s teeming with ocean treasures. Can’t make up your mind? The All In Platter features the best of both worlds. Hosting family gatherings or corporate events is easy with its various Buffet Packages (S$28 to S$88 per pax) . A complimentary Christmas-themed setup is provided to set the ideal vibe. There’s also a Grazing Table featuring artisan cheese, cold cuts, dried fruits, nuts, housecrafted dips, among others, that make for a neat centrepiece.

Dreading the annual task of organising your company’s Christmas catering? Lavish Dine Catering has your back with its range of premium Halal Christmas menus that will satisfy a wide range of occasions and party sizes.
Whether it’s a grand festive buffet, party platter, potluck-ready sets, or mini buffets, you’ll find something that suits you. Self-heating tray options are also included to make hosting seamless.
The 12-course Rouge (S$45 each , min. 30 pax) is a glorious spread featuring yummy dishes like Roasted Beef with Truffle Ju s , Blackened Salmon with Creamy Dill Butter Sauce , Christmas Basil & Bocconcini Fusilli , and Winter Fennel & Smoked Salmon Salad .
