My fellow Eastsiders, I bring you glad tidings! After months of waiting, Tampines MRT Pasar Malam is returning from 21 Nov to 20 Dec 2026 . That means 30 days of non-stop food, drinks and even souvenirs if you’re into that. As the name suggests, this pasar malam is located right next to the Tampines MRT Station . Can’t wait to go down for the 100th time myself.
Credit – Facebook
The ‘ pasar malam’ is a beloved and sacred event for all Singaporeans, letting us enjoy street food amongst our community. Regardless of your opinions about the food, there is no doubt everyone looks forward to these night markets all year round across Singapore. I think it gives us the excuse to just hang out with our loved ones under the stars.
Credit – Facebook
All my Eastsiders know that the Tampines pasar malam occurs several times a year. Some of us, me included, wonder why they don’t just have it up all year round. I don’t know about y’all, but I have a very strict list of food I get at any pasar malam. This list includes keropok lekor (both soft and crunchy versions), Thai milk tea, Ramly burger and mixed takoyaki. I’m one of those people who aren’t a huge fan of the more trendy items, but I totally understand the appeal.
Credit – Facebook
For this next opening, TLK Events and Lighting have added a dedicated beer area in its own separate zone. Live performances will be playing throughout the night, really giving a more ‘party’ vibe. On top of that, there will be a retail booth and a large squishy shop selling squishies and other toys. What’s another reason to spend even more cash?
Credit – Facebook
While I’m sure everyone is excited about this return, the Tampines MRT Pasar Malam is infamous for its huge, roaring crowds. Because of that, it might get very stuffy and humid. I hope everyone stays safe and healthy, which is why I suggest bringing along the following items to keep yourself in tiptop shape: N95 masks, a portable fan, loads of water, hand sanitiser, and antibacterial wipes.
Other than that, have a good time! Also, here’s a tip: If you want to try those trendy spots but aren’t willing to dish out some of the exorbitant prices, bring along a group of friends. I normally roll with a crew of 4 guys. We made it a rule not to buy the same items so we can really try as much as possible. I’m the traditional eater, and yes, this is that serious.
summary: Tampines MRT Pasar Malam runs for 30 days from 21 Nov to 20 Dec 2026 beside Tampines MRT Station. It has food and drink stalls, live performances, a retail booth, a large squishy shop and a newly added, dedicated beer area. Crowds can get stuffy and humid, so it suits groups prepared for a busy night out.
title: Tampines MRT Pasar Malam – 30 days of street food, live music & squishies

Looking for something different to do this weekend? You’re in luck: Xventure , a brand-new indoor adventure destination, is opening its doors on 20 Nov 2026 . Located in Tiong Bahru Plaza , it hosts a plethora of activities within its massive 20,000 sq ft space. It will open daily, 10.30am – 8.30pm from Mon to Thu and 10am – 9pm from Fri to Sun .
You can look forward to physical challenges, immersive multiplayer games and aerial adventures. Tickets start from US$13.99 , and you can choose between 2-hour and 3-hour Single Admission passes. If you’re heading there in a group, get the X4 (US$22.89 each) and X10 (US$20.79 each) Shareable Passes ; you’ll be able to use them for repeat visits or share with eligible friends and family.
Designed with teens, young adults and families in mind, this indoor adventure park will feature 10 activity zones and more than 30 challenges. From multiplayer virtual reality (VR) games to high ropes courses and thrilling slides, here is what you can look forward to when Xventure opens.
To mark its grand opening, Xventure will host a series of interactive experiences, including challenges and games from 20 to 22 Nov 2026 . For the opening weekend, Xventure will be open from 4pm – 9pm on Fri and 10am – 9pm on Sat and Sun .
These experiences include Surf’s Up, The High Route, Beat The Clock, Beat The Crew and Xventure Rave. You can look forward to putting your agility to the test, with opportunities to win merchandise and compete for the top spot.
Besides the grand opening specials, here are some other Xventure highlights. First, you won’t want to miss MIRRA Arena . It’s a social multiplayer VR experience where players use their body movements to control their actions in the virtual world in real time. The live gameplay is displayed on a large screen so everyone can follow along with the action.
If you’re a thrillseeker, try out the High Ropes Course , where you’ll need to rely on your balance, coordination and confidence to navigate obstacles. If that’s not enough for you, the 30m-long Air Glide will offer you an exhilarating aerial adventure.
Don’t miss out on the attractions available in their Slide Park . Whoever said slides are just for the little ones will definitely have their minds changed after experiencing this. The 3 slides available are Roller Ski Slide, Rocket Slide, and Swing Slide. Enjoy the slide by yourself or race with your friends for even more fun.
Xventure combines physical obstacles, agility-based activities, digital games and more, all under one roof. There will be more than 30 challenges spread across 10 activity zones , so there’s plenty to keep you occupied. Head down and try out their thrilling activities!
Get your tickets from US$13.99 here
Making waves: 11 must-try water activities in Singapore [Nov 2026]
summary: Xventure is a 20,000 sq ft indoor adventure park opening at Tiong Bahru Plaza on 20 Nov 2026, featuring over 30 challenges across 10 activity zones. Designed for teens, young adults and families, its attractions include multiplayer VR games, a high ropes course, a 30m Air Glide and three slides. With admission from US$13.99 and 2-hour or 3-hour passes, it offers a range of indoor activities for groups and families.

Holiday greetings are due! But this year, I’m saying “Merry Christmas” and “Avengers, Assemble!” The annual Great Christmas Village returns to Orchard Road from 13 November 2026 to 3 January 2027 , spanning Ngee Ann City and Shaw House .
We had the opportunity to check out Great Christmas Village early, and were pleasantly surprised by how this year’s edition expanded in fun, grandeur, and scale. From an Avengers: Doomsday-themed installation and Christmas tree to a bigger Kiztopia carnival to a fun-filled LEGO Santa’s Toy Factory , here are our highlights.
Avengers: Doomsday experience
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
One of the main attractions of Great Christmas Village 2026 is this 13-metre-tall, stained-glass-style Christmas tree located right outside Ngee Ann City. But what’s truly exciting here is not the tree itself, but what lies beneath – an immersive , Avengers: Doomsday- themed installation .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Enter, and you will step into the world of the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU). You will find numerous themed rooms that are essentially recreations of scenes from Avengers: Doomsday . This includes Professor X’s office, a corner of Fantastic Four’s Baxter Building, Doom’s throne room, and more.
Snap many photos and let your hype for the movie reach fever pitch!
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Talking about Doom – a realistic statue of the film’s main antagonist will greet you the moment you step into the installation. Think you can aura-farm better than him? Take a selfie with the man or get a friend’s help to take a photo as you do your own superhero pose.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The Doomsday experience does not end when you finish exploring the installation. For all the biggest fans, you can go on a trail around Orchard Road to collect stamps at 4 other themed installations .
Afterwards, return to this main installation at Ngee Ann City, snap a photo with the Doctor Doom statue, share it on social media , and tag @MarvelSingapore and #AvengersDoomsdaySG to redeem a limited Marvel premium .
If you’re visiting the experience after watching the movie, you can also skip the trail and redeem the premium by presenting a movie ticket stub .
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Confirm Good (@confirmgoodsg)
Kiztopia Christmas Carnival
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
For those who want a little Christmas fun, head over to the Kiztopia Christmas Carnival ! This year’s edition feels upgraded and expanded in comparison to last year, with about 50 game booths , children’s rides , and game stations in total.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
One part of the carnival has already opened at Ngee Ann City Civic Plaza and is fully air-conditioned . More games and rides will open at Shaw House Urban Plaza from 20 November 2026 onwards . The Kiztopia Christmas Carnival at both locations will run till 3 January 2027 , so there’s plenty of time to head down for a fun time .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
To play any of the games, you will need to purchase a card , which is usable at both locations. New cards are priced at S$35 for 35 credits , S$50 for 60 credits , and S$100 for 130 credits . If you have a Mastercard , use it to purchase or top up your card for extra credits !
LEGO Santa’s Toy Factory
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Whether you’re young or just young at heart, you probably have some fond memories with LEGO growing up. This festive season, it’s time to revive the child on the inside of you!
LEGO brings its own twist of Christmas magic to Orchard Road at this year’s Christmas Village, with the debut of its first-ever LEGO Santa’s Toy Factory in Singapore .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Children aged 4 to 12 years old can step inside and complete hands-on workshop missions to receive a free LEGO Make & Take mini-build and voucher .
Whether it’s decorating festive treats at Gingerbread’s Bakery, sorting bricks at Santa’s Sorting Station, or fulfilling orders at Yeti’s Order Station, kids will get to experience being LEGO Santa’s assistant.
They can also meet LEGO Santa himself at 5pm , 6pm , 7pm and 8pm daily , when he will make special 30-minute appearances.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Finished a day’s work at LEGO Santa’s Toy Factory? Head on over to a pop-up store just opposite and grab a holiday gift for yourself or for loved ones! Also, keep a lookout for Santa’s Holiday Gift Drop , where one participant stands to win LEGO sets worth up to S$200 !
Great Christmas Village
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Beyond the highlights we’ve listed, there’s much more to discover at Orchard Road’s Great Christmas Village this year. From numerous photo spots to festive food & drinks , including a CHAGEE Pop-up tea truck and exclusive merchandise display , there are plenty of reasons to visit the shopping district this end of year.
Merry Christmas and Avengers, Assemble!
The Great Christmas Village 2026
…
summary: The Great Christmas Village is back with Avengers: Doomsday installations, more carnival games, and a LEGO Santa’s Toy Factory.

Zhenghua Nature Park
Think you’ve explored all of Singapore’s hidden parks ? Think again. Tucked away in Bukit Panjang is Zhenghua Nature Park , a lesser-known green escape where forest trails, chirping birds, and unexpected wildlife encounters await. And the best part is that you won’t have to conquer any steep hills to enjoy the scenery.
Spanning 17.3 hectares, this is more than just another spot to clock your daily 10,000 steps at. From spotting colourful birds and wandering along lush trails to letting the kiddos run wild at playgrounds, here’s why Zhenghua Nature Park deserves a spot on your list of walking and hiking trails in Singapore .
What are some things to know about Zhenghua Nature Park?
Stretching approximately 2.5km along Bukit Timah Expressway (BKE), Zhenghua Nature Park is a linear park that connects the Bukit Panjang Park Connector to the surrounding nature network.
Central Catchment Nature Reserve
Image credit: NParks
Beyond being a recreational space, the park also serves as an important ecological corridor and green buffer for the Central Catchment Nature Reserve . It helps support biodiversity by providing a link between green spaces, including Chestnut Nature Park and Dairy Farm Nature Park .
Chestnut Nature Park (left) and Dairy Farm Nature Park (right).
Image adapted from: Yongsuk Hur & pearl black via Google Maps
Despite its proximity to the expressway, the park is surrounded by dense vegetation, making it a convenient spot for residents to enjoy a dose of nature without travelling too far.
How to get to Zhenghua Nature Park?
There are 3 main entrances to Zhenghua Nature Park, located along Segar Road , Bangkit Road , and Chestnut Avenue .
Image credit: SAA Architects
If you’re going by MRT and LRT, take the Downtown Line to Bukit Panjang MRT Station , then transfer to the Bukit Panjang LRT . You can alight at Segar , Fajar , or Bangkit LRT Station , depending on which entrance you plan to use.
Alternatively, you can walk from Bukit Panjang MRT Station (Exit D) , which is approximately 1.4km away, or approximately 23 minutes on foot.
Bus services serving the surrounding area include 171 , 187 , 960 , 966 , and 972 . Check the nearest bus stop to your preferred entrance before heading down.
Drivers can access the park via local roads in Bukit Panjang , with connections from BKE and Kranji Expressway (KJE) . The entrances along Segar Road , Bangkit Road , and Chestnut Avenue offer different starting points for your walk.
What can I do at Zhenghua Nature Park?
Take a walk along the scenic 2.5km nature trail
If you’re looking to get your steps in without tackling steep slopes, Zhenghua Nature Park has a relatively flat walking trail that’s suitable for a casual stroll. The 2.5km-long route runs parallel to the BKE, with plenty of greenery lining the pathway.
For those who prefer a long-distance hike , an out-and-back route of the entire park can cover approximately 4.3km , taking around 1 to 1.5 hours to complete. The gentle terrain makes it a manageable option for beginners and families looking to spend some time outdoors.
The trail also connects to the wider park network, so avid walkers can extend their adventure towards Chestnut Nature Park and other nearby green spaces.
Keep an eye out for birds & other wildlife
Image credit: Alson Teo via Facebook
Nature lovers, you’ll want to keep your eyes peeled while exploring the park. Zhenghua Nature Park is home to more than 30 species of birds , making it a great spot for casual birdwatching.
Image credit: NSS Public Forum via Facebook
Some feathered residents you might encounter include the Olive-backed Sunbird , Flameback Woodpecker , and Greater Racket-tailed Drongo . You might even hear their calls before spotting them among the trees.
Birds aren’t the only animals roaming the park. Keep a lookout for squirrels, free-roaming chickens, monitor lizards, and the occasional wild boar.
Image credit: VT Loh via Google Maps
Just remember to admire wildlife from a safe distance and avoid feeding or approaching the animals.
Discover the park’s diverse greenery
Image adapted from: Tom Goh, Alvin Yap & Ng Teong Soon via Google Maps
There’s more to Zhenghua Nature Park than its walking trails. The park features a variety of native and introduced tree species, including Tembusu and Jejawi , which contribute to its lush landscape.
As you wander along the pathways, take some time to appreciate the surrounding vegetation. The greenery also provides shelter and food sources for wildlife, making the park an important habitat for the area’s biodiversity.
Bring the kids to the playgrounds
Families with young children can make a pit stop at the park’s 2 playgrounds , which offer a change of pace from the walking trails.
Image credit: Sing Eu via Google Maps
…
summary: A peaceful nature escape in Bukit Panjang with lush greenery, wildlife, and family-friendly trails.
title: Zhenghua Nature Park Guide: Hidden Forest Trails, Wildlife Spotting & Scenic Walks In Bukit Panjang

Adventure Cove Waterpark guide
Ask any Singaporean kid who grew up post-2012 about their best Sentosa memories, and chances are Adventure Cove Waterpark makes the list – from screaming down the Riptide Rocket to drifting along Adventure River pretending you’re on holiday.
So here’s your heads up: Adventure Cove Waterpark will be closed from 1st January to 31st December 2027 for a major refurbishment and transformation. Resorts World Sentosa says the year-long works will pave the way for an exciting new concept, with more details to come.
That means you’ve got until the end of 2026 to make your last splash at the waterpark as we know it. Whether you’re planning a December school holiday outing with the kids or one final slide marathon with your friends, here’s everything you need to know before you go.
What you should know before visiting Adventure Cove Waterpark
Adventure Cove Waterpark is a family-friendly water park located on the island of Sentosa. Since you’ll be splashing around in water, you’ll want to make sure you’re properly dressed for the occasion. We’ve covered that under the section “ What to wear at Adventure Cove Waterpark? ”
As with any outdoor activity in Singapore , remember to apply and reapply sunscreen regularly. Wear hats and caps to protect your scalp as well. It’s also a good idea to stay hydrated. There are plenty of drinking fountains around the water park. Just be sure to bring your own bottle so you can fill up when necessary.
But alas, Adventure Cove Waterpark is temporarily closing on 31st December 2026 for a year-long renovation, and should reopen by 31st December 2027. So if you were planning to make a splash in Sentosa in the new year, you better bring forth those plans to get wet ASAP.
Where can I keep my belongings at Adventure Cove Waterpark?
Alongside your valuables, that nagging, kiasu voice in your head is responsible for the cap, sun visor , and copious amounts of snacks that have miraculously managed to fit into your backpack.
Upon entry, changing rooms and lockers are located on your left.
Lockers are located strategically at the entrance and come in 2 sizes. It costs $10 to rent the smaller one and $20 for the larger one. You can access your locker anytime you want during the day.
The smaller locker should be able to comfortably fit 2 regular sized backpacks.
If the lockers by the entrance are full during peak periods, take a stroll to Bluwater Bay to deposit your belongings at the lockers there. Bluwater Bay happens to be closer to the attractions, so this might come in handy.
Cabanas near Bluwater Bay.
If you are coming to the waterpark in a group, a more value-for-money option is to rent a cabana at Bluwater Bay or Seahorse Hideaway & Adventure River Gardens. Prices range from $88-$186 , varying with duration of booking, location, and peak/non-peak season.
Renting a cabana comes with perks like F&B vouchers worth up to $35, 2 towels, and a locker to stow all your belongings. Cabana bookings come on a first-come, first-served basis – you can book one at the Guest Services Counter inside the park, located near the entrance when you arrive. Else, make a booking in advance on RWS’ website to play safe.
Note: Cabana bookings are not inclusive of entry tickets.
What rides are there at Adventure Cove Waterpark?
All rides are clustered at the west side of Adventure Cove Waterpark, so you can get from one ride to another quickly. We recommend starting with the rides first before moving on to the other attractions as the queues tend to get longer here over the course of the day.
Grab a float and hop on the Adventure River for a fast-track journey to your first stop after depositing your stuff in the lockers. The Adventure River circles the entire waterpark, and you can get off anywhere you want.
Float through dark caves and watch out for surprise splashes from tipping water buckets.
There’s no need to worry about returning your float – you can either leave them in the pool or deposit them at the many float return stations dotting the river’s course.

There are a couple of regulations imposed by the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) when bringing your groceries from JB back into Singapore.
For starters, you are only allowed to bring in food strictly for your own consumption and not for sale. Next, you have to check whether the food item is allowed to be brought back into Singapore or not by consulting SFA’s website .

BB.Q Chicken Singapore opens at VivoCity’s Food Republic
Image credit: Hiro Nonoda via Google Maps
Calling all K-drama and Stray Kids fans: the chicken Felix keeps talking about is opening near you. BB.Q Chicken , which says it’s the world’s biggest Korean fried chicken chain, is set to open a food court stall at Food Republic , VivoCity on 27 November 2026 . Two more outlets will follow over the next couple of months.
17 Korean Fried Chicken In Singapore, Including Hawker And Halal Options
The VivoCity stall is a BB.Q Chicken Express, a smaller grab-and-go version of the brand. Next, another stall will open at Food Opera, ION Orchard in December 2026 . Then a second BB.Q Chicken Express opens at Food Junction, Junction 8 in January 2027 , which is good news for Bishan folks who’d rather not trek to HarbourFront for a chicken fix.
Image credit: BB.Q Chicken
If the name sounds familiar, you may have spotted it on screen. The chain has turned up in K-dramas such as Crash Landing on You and Guardian: The Lonely and Great God , better known as Goblin , and in variety shows Running Man and Knowing Bros .
Image credit: @felix.lee.00
It started in Korea in 1995, and the name stands for “Best of the Best Quality.” Today it has about 4,500 stores across 57 countries. It even has its own training school for franchisees, Chicken University, which has been running since 1999. Stray Kids member Felix was also a fan long before he became the brand’s global ambassador.
Image credit: Raymond Fu via Google Maps
The full Singapore menu and prices haven’t been released, but two signatures are confirmed for the VivoCity launch. Soy Garlic Chicken (price TBD) comes coated in a sweet-savoury soy glaze with plenty of garlic, the go-to pick if you don’t do spice. Heat-seekers should get the Red Chak Chak Seasoning Chicken (price TBD) , coated in a spicy red pepper seasoning instead of a sauce. From the opening promos, expect combos, boneless chicken, bone-in chicken, and burgers on the menu too.
Image credit: Ivonne Rivera via Google Maps
Now for the freebies. From 3 December to 17 December 2026 , every order comes with a free two-piece boneless chicken; orders of sides alone don’t qualify. The outlet picks the flavour, so there’s no choosing.
Felix fans get their own perk from 3 December 2026 . Buy any two items from the combo, boneless chicken, or bone-in chicken categories, or the burger category, and you’ll get a sealed surprise pack with two Felix photocards and one photo strip. There are four photocard designs and two photo strip designs, so collecting the full set could take a few visits.
Can’t wait till the 27th? Read our Lotteria review for another popular Korean fast food chain that’s recently set up shop in Singapore! Otherwise, read our guide to the best 1-for-1 buffet deals for 2026 for more affordable eats.
Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, #03-01, Food Republic, VivoCity, Singapore 098585
Opening hours: TBD
Website
BB.Q Chicken is not halal-certified.

body:
The local hawker scene is notoriously unforgiving, and has claimed another notable stall in its wake. Kiang Kiang Taiwan Teppanyaki is officially shuttering its flagship stall in Woodlands . It’s a hawker venture that was launched in 2024 by former Singapore Airlines (SIA) stewardess Cherry Tan and her husband Duncan Hsu, a Taiwanese native who has 20 years’ experience cooking in Taipei hotel kitchens.
Credit – Melvin J via Google Reviews
However, mounting financial pressure has forced the couple to make the painful decision to wind down operations. As Cherry Tan revealed on TikTok, the Woodlands stall has been consistently losing money and pulling in low daily revenue, sometimes averaging only S$300-400 a day.
The couple hasn’t been able to draw a salary for the past 3 months following the birth of their baby in Sep 2026. Their second branch in Bedok is also barely breaking even amid rising operational costs and no longer able to offset losses sustained by the Woodlands outlet. The founders plan to keep the shutters up until Jan 2027, when their lease ends.
As the name suggests, Kiang Kiang Taiwan Teppanyaki brings authentic Taiwanese night market flavours to heartland neighbourhoods. They specialise in Western-style sizzling hotplate steaks, and some highlight dishes include Pork Collar Chop (S$9.50) . It’s served on a hotplate alongside a bed of spaghetti and teppanyaki beansprouts topped with a sunny-side-up egg and an eye-catching basil garnish.
You can choose between either mushroom or black pepper sauce, with both being house-made and famously chunky and flavourful, a style you’d be hard-pressed to find anywhere other than a Taiwanese night market. Other proteins include Chicken Chop (S$8.50) , Australian Ribeye Steak (S$13.50) and Halibut (S$13.50) .
Cherry Tan appealed to followers to drop by and enjoy their sizzling plates before the stall closes for good in Jan next year.
Kiang Kiang Taiwan Teppanyaki: Ex-hotel chef from Taipei serves sizzling hotplate pasta with ribeye steak, basil pork & halibut
summary: Kiang Kiang Taiwan Teppanyaki in Woodlands is closing by January 2027 due to mounting financial losses and low daily revenue. Founded by former Singapore Airlines stewardess Cherry Tan and Taiwanese hotel chef Duncan Hsu, the hawker stall serves Western-style sizzling hotplates priced between S$8.50 and S$13.50. The outlet remains open until its lease ends, making it relevant for diners seeking Taiwanese night market-style steaks in northern Singapore before the closure.
title: Ex-SIA stewardess & 5-star chef closing Kiang Kiang Taiwan Teppanyaki in Woodlands

PSLE 2026
The wait is almost over for Primary 6 students, with PSLE results 2026 set to be released on 24th November 2026 . But once the results are in, there’s another important decision to be made: choosing the right secondary school for the next chapter of their education.
From navigating the Secondary 1 (S1) Posting Exercise to shortlisting schools and attending open houses, there’s plenty for parents to keep track of. Here’s a guide to the important dates, application process, and things to consider before submitting your child’s secondary school choices.
Important dates to take note of
Image credit: Ministry Of Education
Before diving into school choices, it’s worth marking these important dates on your calendar. The S1 Posting Exercise begins on the same day PSLE results are released, so you will have a relatively short window to finalise yours and your child’s selections.
Event
Date & time
PSLE results released
24th November 2026, 11am
S1 school choice submission opens
24th November 2026, 11.30am
S1 school choice submission closes
30th November 2026, 4.30pm
S1 posting results release (tentative)
18th December 2026
How to submit your secondary school choices through the S1 Portal
Image credit: Ministry of Education
Once your child’s PSLE results are out, the next step is to submit their preferred secondary schools through the S1 Portal . This official online platform, managed by the Ministry of Education (MOE) , allows parents and legal guardians to complete the school selection process using Singpass .
The portal will be accessible from 24th to 30th November 2026 , and will operate 24 hours a day throughout the submission period. However, do note that it closes at 4.30pm on the final day, so it’s best not to leave everything until the last minute.
Steps to submit school choices
Image credit: Bendemeer Secondary School
• Select a Posting Group: If your child qualifies for 2 Posting Groups, choose their preferred group before proceeding. This selection will apply to all their school choices.
• Choose up to 6 secondary schools: List your child’s preferred schools in order of preference, starting with the one they most want to attend.
• Provide your contact details: Enter the necessary contact information so you can receive relevant updates regarding the posting exercise.
• Review your selections: Double-check your school choices, their ranking, and any applicable Third Language options before confirming your submission.
• Submit your choices: Complete the process by 4.30pm on 30th November 2026 . Any changes to your selections must also be made before this deadline.
Parents who need additional guidance can refer to the official MOE S1 Portal User Guide for detailed instructions on navigating the platform.
What happens if you miss the S1 submission deadline?
Missing the submission window doesn’t mean your child won’t receive a secondary school placement. However, students whose parents do not submit their choices on time will be allocated to schools with remaining vacancies.
This allocation happens only after students who submitted their school preferences have been posted, so your child could end up in a school that wasn’t originally on your shortlist. To avoid undue stress, it’s worth submitting your choices well before the deadline.
Common S1 posting terms parents should know
Image credit: AEIS Exam Paper
If you’ve been researching secondary schools, you’ve probably come across terms like COP , Posting Groups , and affiliation priority . Understanding what these mean can help you make more informed decisions when narrowing down your options.
What is affiliation priority?
Nanyang Primary School (left) is affiliated to Nanyang Girls’ High School (right).
Image adapted from: U O via Google Maps, Nanyang Girls’ High School
Some primary schools are affiliated with secondary schools, allowing eligible students to receive priority during the posting process. However, this doesn’t automatically guarantee admission, as placements still depend on PSLE scores, available vacancies, and other admission requirements.
To qualify for affiliation priority, students must indicate their affiliated secondary school as their 1st choice . Parents should also check the school’s specific eligibility criteria before relying on this admission pathway.
What are posting groups?
Image credit: Lee Hsien Loong via Facebook
Under Singapore’s secondary school posting system, students are placed into Posting Groups 1, 2, or 3 based on their PSLE scores. These groups determine the posting process and guide the initial subject levels students can take in Secondary 1.
With Full Subject-Based Banding (Full SBB) , students may also be able to take certain subjects at different levels according to their strengths and learning needs, rather than following a single fixed academic stream.

Halal Food Friday goes to a name that has fed Kampong Gelam since 1992. Hjh Maimunah is a Malay and Indonesian restaurant serving halal nasi padang, where a beef rendang set costs S$10.70 on its delivery menu, and a Premium Ambeng platter for 2 to 3 people is S$47.
It is a Muslim-owned family business, founded by Mdm Mahiran Abdul Rahman with her late mother’s recipes, and now run by the second generation. The restaurant describes all of its food as halal-certified. We will come back to how to check that yourself.
Halal status: what we could verify
Hjh Maimunah states on its official website that its Malay and Indonesian cuisine is halal-certified, and that its kitchens are halal-certified. The business is also Muslim-owned, as the founding family’s own story on the site makes clear.
Halal certification is issued outlet by outlet, so do not assume that every stall carrying the name has the same certificate. Search the MUIS HalalSG directory for the specific address before you go, especially for the smaller outlets inside food courts.
Source: Hjh Maimunah
Where to find Hjh Maimunah and when it is open
The flagship is a pair of shophouses at Jalan Pisang, a short walk from Bugis MRT (roughly 8 minutes, going by the usual estimates). Joo Chiat is the second full restaurant, and there are smaller Mini outlets across the island.
• Jalan Pisang: 11 Jalan Pisang, Singapore 199078. Open 7.30am to 7pm, Monday to Saturday, closed on Sundays. Nearest MRT: Bugis (DT14/EW12).
• Joo Chiat: 20 Joo Chiat Road, Singapore 427357. Open 8am to 7pm, Tuesday to Sunday, closed on Mondays.
• Tampines Mall: Kopitiam, #04-27-29, 4 Tampines Central 5. Open daily, 10am to 9pm.
• City Square Mall: Food Republic, #B3-04, 180 Kitchener Road. Open daily, 10am to 9pm.
• Westgate: Food Junction, #B1-29, 3 Gateway Drive. Open daily, 10am to 9pm.
• Hong Leong Building: #B1-45, 16 Raffles Quay. Open 10am to 3pm, Monday to Friday, handy for the CBD lunch crowd.
The restaurant lists more Mini outlets, including Clementi Mall, Compass One, Yishun and Parkway Parade, on its locations page. Hours can change, so check the page before a long trip.
What to order at this halal nasi padang
You pick your own dishes from the counter and pile them over rice, so the order is yours to build. The restaurant says its menu runs past 100 items at the main restaurants, and the Minis serve at least 40.
• Beef Rendang, the slow-cooked dry curry the restaurant counts as its signature.
• Tahu Telur, a thick fried tofu omelette topped with vegetables, crushed peanuts and prawn paste sauce.
• Lemak Siput Sedut, sea snails in a spicy coconut gravy, for the adventurous.
• Ikan Bakar, grilled fish with a traditional rempah marinade.
• Sotong Hitam, squid in a spicy ink stew.
• Sayur Lodeh, a coconut vegetable stew that cools down the sambal.
• Kueh such as ondeh-ondeh, kueh lapis and kueh dadar to finish.
Source: Hjh Maimunah
Hjh Maimunah prices
The restaurant does not publish a dine-in price list online, but its delivery menu on Oddle gives a clear idea. Dine-in prices at the counter will depend on which dishes you pick, so treat the figures below as a guide only.
• Beef Rendang Set: S$10.70
• Ayam Lemak Cili Padi Set: S$10.20
• Asam Pedas Fish Set: S$10.70
• Beef, Chicken or Fish Deluxe Set: S$12.20
• Nasi Rawon Set: S$12
• Vegetable Set: S$8
• Original Ambeng Platter (2 to 3 people): S$44
• Premium Ambeng Platter: S$47
• Family Bundle (4 pax): S$58
Bring a group if you can. The Ambeng platters are made for sharing, and splitting a S$47 platter among three people works out to about S$16 each.
Planning your visit
Jalan Pisang is small and gets busy at lunch, particularly on weekends, so go early or aim for mid-afternoon. The restaurant also takes reservations through its website, which helps if you are a bigger group.
If you are making a day of it around Kampong Gelam, the Malay Heritage Centre has free admission and is close by. For this weekend’s other plans, see our things to do guide . Meal planning for the festive season? Here is the Holiday Inn Atrium 1-for-1 buffet .
Source: Hjh Maimunah
summary: Hjh Maimunah, a Muslim-owned halal nasi padang name since 1992, serves rendang sets from S$10.70 and Ambeng platters from S$44. Here are the addresses, hours and best dishes.

body:
1-day Orchard itinerary on a budget
Orchard has always read as somewhere bougie to me, notorious for sky-high prices and luxury-brand outlets, which is probably why my friends and I tend to steer clear. After all, we don’t really have the money to splurge on a $50 meal at ION Orchard or a lavish hotel buffet .
However, after FOMO drove me down Orchard Road to admire the extravagant festive lights, I ended up putting together a full-day Orchard budget itinerary for under $30 that proves you can actually enjoy the heart of Singapore without burning a hole in your wallet.
BTW, if you’re willing to spend a little more, check out our 12-hour Orchard food itinerary instead!
How To Spend 12 Hours In Orchard: $22.80++ Porridge Buffet, $2 Thrift Stores And More
Breakfast: THE CITY BAKERY
As someone who can’t stomach a full meal during breakfast, THE CITY BAKERY is a good place to start the day with a small bite. It’s located at Mandarin Gallery , a 10-minute walk from Orchard MRT Station , offering a wide variety of pastries, bakes, and sandwiches.
ICYMI: This cafe-bakery started as a small neighbourhood bakery in New York City, founded by an ex-television producer with two Emmy Awards to his name. They’ve since expanded to Japan, with over 40 outlets at the time of writing, and recently opened their first Southeast Asian outpost in Singapore.
The bakery’s signature, and what put them on the map, is the Pretzel Croissant ($5) : a fluffy croissant with a savoury, pretzel-like crust. Inside, it’s just what you’d expect from a regular croissant—flaky with well-defined layers.
When we visited, we particularly enjoyed the Coffee Cinnamon Roll ($5) . It’s a spin on the classic breakfast pastry, zhnged up with a hit of coffee. The fragrance of the coffee brought out the earthiness and warmth of cinnamon, tying everything together.
Read our THE CITY BAKERY coverage .
Expect to spend : $5 for bakes
Address: 333A Orchard Road, #02-05 Mandarin Gallery, Singapore 238897
Opening hours: Daily 9am to 9:30pm
Website
THE CITY BAKERY is not halal-certified.
Japan-Famous Bakery Chain From NYC Opens At Mandarin Gallery—Here’s What To Try
Lunch: Maddie’s Kitchen
Image credit: Xin Hao via Google Maps
After breakfast, take some time to window-shop and soak up the atmosphere of Orchard Road before heading over to lunch at Maddie’s Kitchen in Far East Plaza . The walk from Mandarin Gallery to Far East Plaza takes about 17 minutes, which is plenty of time to jalan jalan.
Image credit: Ah Kay via Google Maps
Maddie’s Kitchen is a no-frills eatery selling affordable zi char. While most dishes are in large portions meant to be shared ‘round the table, their Hainanese Curry Rice is an item well loved by solo diners. The Pork Chop Hainanese Curry Rice ($6.80) features crispy pork cutlets served on a bed of rice, paired with a sweet-spicy Hainanese-style curry, said to be made with their house-made rempah. The set also comes with a pile of braised cabbage and a sunny-side-up fried egg, dressed with dark soya sauce.
Image credit: Glen Y via Google Maps
If deep-fried foods aren’t really your thing, their Curry Chicken Hainanese Curry Rice ($6.80) is a decent alternative, featuring the same rice and veggies, served with curried potatoes and tender chicken instead. You can also get their Braised Pork Belly Hainanese Curry Rice ($6.80) , topped with melt-in-your-mouth slices of braised pork belly.
Image credit: Snoop Ee via Google Maps
Alternatively, for something lighter, try their Batang Fish Soup or Fried Fish Soup , both priced at $7.80 . Both feature a clear, clean-tasting fish broth packed generously with a medley of ingredients: your preferred fish, tomatoes, cabbage, and silken tofu. It’s a comforting, protein-packed meal for your day’s activities.
Expect to spend : $6.80-$7.80 for mains
Address: 14 Scotts Road, #02-10/11/12/13, Far East Plaza, Singapore 228213
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 9pm
Website
Maddie’s Kitchen is not halal-certified.
20 Far East Plaza Food Gems Including Popular Salted Egg Pork Rice And Fresh Shio Pan
Activity: Check out the events at *SCAPE
Image credit: Evelyn Yong via Google Maps
*SCAPE is one of my favourite activity spaces, and is usually chock-full of things to do. It’s a non-profit community space that supports youths’ interests in the creative arts, meaning there’s usually a wide variety of events, from arts festivals to workshops. While some require paid tickets, there are plenty of upcoming free events.
Image credit: *SCAPE
A current event running from now till 22 November 2026 is *SCAPE’s Singapore Youth Photography Awards 2026 Exhibition , which showcases the competition’s winning works, selected from over 500 submissions by a panel of distinguished judges. The collection is displayed at *SCAPE Whitespace Level 3 , free of charge. If you have an eye for photography and all things creative, take this opportunity to support Singapore’s photography talents.
Image credit: *SCAPE

body:
HanBroth is a new Korean hawker stall in Beauty World
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
The weather’s been quite chilly recently, with seemingly never-ending rain. To me, that only means it’s time to snuggle up under a blanket, sip a cup of hot chocolate, and slurp on a comforting bowl of hot soup. If you’re anything like me, you’re in luck: MasterChef Singapore Season 2 winner Derek Cheong recently opened HanBroth , specialising in Busan-style pork bone soup, following the resounding success of sister stall Berempah Bros .
MasterChef Finalist Opens Ayam Berempah Stall At Beauty World—Here’s Our Honest Review
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
Dwaeji-gukbap, AKA Busan-style pork bone soup, is one of Busan’s iconic dishes, its name literally translating to “pork, soup, rice”. It originated during the Korean War in the 1950s, and is made by simmering pork bones for hours, resulting in a milky white broth best served with banchan, or Korean side dishes.
To replicate the flavours you’ll get in Busan, founder Derek Cheong scoured Korea’s best dwaeji-gukbap restaurants to learn more about the dish and bring the techniques back to Singapore. You can see that effort in how the dish is prepared: the broth is boiled for four to eight hours with pork femur bones, pork shank, trotters, pork belly, and pork collar, giving the soup a deep, porky flavour and a creamy, almost gelatinous finish.
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
Their best-seller is the Original Busan-Style Pork Soup ($9.90) , featuring their signature pork bone soup, served piping hot and packed with tender pork belly and pork collar. Each set also comes with a bowl of steamed rice, kimchi, ssamjang—a spicy Korean chilli sauce—a blend of salt and pepper, and dadaegi, which is a spicy house-made chilli paste.
The recommended way to eat it is to dump the whole bowl of rice into the soup, pao fan style. If you want to zhng up your broth, add a spoonful of the spicy-salty dadaegi paste and the salt-and-pepper blend. Season the pork by dipping it into ssamjang or pairing it with kimchi.
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
If you’re feeling under the weather, order their Herbal Busan-Style Pork Soup ($11.90) instead, spiked with ginseng, dates, and other Korean herbs for a samgyetang-like experience .
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
Their Seaweed Busan-style Pork Soup ($11.90) is another variant that’s made by boiling seaweed in the broth, which lends it a deep, umami, and briny taste.
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
That’s not all: they also have sides to share ‘round the table, including the Potato Pancake ($9.90) : a rosti-like potato pancake drizzled with smoked gochujang-flavoured and bonito-flavoured mayo, then finished with seaweed for additional crunch. The pancake is said to be crispy on the outside, while soft and fluffy on the inside.
Image credit: HANBROTH via Google Maps
Otherwise, their Pork Bossam ($9.90) is also highly popular. It comprises pork shoulder that’s simmered in an aromatic blend of garlic, Korean soybean paste, ginger, and more, served with wasabi, the same salt-and-pepper mix, and ssamjang. Online reviews have raved about it being tender yet not too fatty.
HanBroth is located in Bukit Timah Wet Market & Food Centre , a three-minute walk away from Beauty World MRT Station .
If you’re already in the area, 133 Penang Authentic is worth a visit too, a stall by another award-winning chef in the same hawker centre serving up affordable Penang food. You can also browse our guide to the best foods in Beauty World for more ideas.
Address: 2A Jalan Seh Chuan, #01-41, Bukit Timah Wet Market & Food Centre, Singapore 599213
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 2:30pm, 5:30pm to 8:30pm
Website
HanBroth is not halal-certified.
30 Beauty World Food Gems Including DIY Okonomiyaki, Famous Eng Kee Wings And More
Feature image adapted from HANBROTH via Google Maps.
summary: HanBroth is a new hawker stall opened by MasterChef Singapore Season 2 winner Derek Cheong, specialising in dwaeji-gukbap, AKA Busan-style pork soup.
title: MasterChef Singapore Season 2 Winner Opens Stall With $9.90 Busan-Style Pork Soup

body:
Best shio pan in Singapore
Carb lovers, this one’s for you. We recently visited and ranked the 11 best bakeries for fresh shio pan in Singapore ! In case you don’t know, shio pan is a type of Japanese bread featuring a lightly salted crust with a buttery, fluffy, and slightly chewy middle. Also known as salt bread, this trendy bun is known for its simple yet delicious flavour. It’s been on the rise lately, with local bakeries coming up with their own renditions of the bake.
A disclaimer before I get started: as with most snacks, the components of a good shio pan can be subjective. Some like theirs light and fluffy, while others prefer a dense and chewy crumb.
Regardless, I’ve finalised three criteria: taste, texture, and price. A good shio pan should have a pleasant flavour. It should be buttery and savoury, without being overly rich or greasy. Next, the texture: we want a slight crunch on the top and bottom of the bread, giving way to a light and chewy middle. Bonus points if the base of the bun is visibly crunchy and buttery. Lastly, we’ll compare the price of one plain shio pan across the board.
For a fair test, we ordered two shio pan from each bakery: one plain, one flavoured. Some places only offered the plain version, so for those, we got two plain shio pan instead.
Do also note that prices are subject to change.
Update: Bakery 1946, Bae.gal, and Shio & Sato are permanently closed.
11. The Lunar Rabbit Boulangerie
The Lunar Rabbit Boulangerie is a cosy bakery and cafe located in Katong and Bendemeer —we visited the latter. They specialise in French-style pastries and croissants, but also offer whole sourdough loaves, baguettes, cakes and more.
Interestingly, the bakery’s shio pan comes in an unconventional, square-like shape.
Unfortunately, I was let down by the Sea Salt Shio Pan ($4.60) . There wasn’t a discernible butter base, and the bun was rather dry on the outside. For $4.60, I was expecting something more.
The Kinako Mochi Shio Pan ($5.10) fared better. The roasted soybean powder added a lovely fragrance to the otherwise plain bun. I wish there was more mochi in the middle, though.
Perhaps we caught the bakery on the wrong day, as online reviews of their other pastries seem to be largely positive.
Taste: 2.5/5
Texture: 2/5
Price: 2.5/5
Total: 46%
Website | Full list of outlets
The Lunar Rabbit Boulangerie is not halal-certified.
10. Bakery 1946
Bakery 1946 , a popular Korean bakery at Suntec City and Bugis Junction , is most known for their cute fruit-and-veggie-shaped buns. I held high hopes for their shio pan as Bakery 1946 is a big name in Korea.
While these buns were the largest ones we’ve tried, they were also the priciest. A Plain Salted Bread cost $4 , which I felt was too steep for any type of plain bun. The crumb was light and airy, but without much of a bite, and the crust of the bun was weak without much structure. The salted bread was very buttery, but I felt that the flavour was rather one-dimensional.
The Garlic Butter Salted Bread costs a whopping $5.90 —NGL, I gawked when I saw the price. Unlike the plain version, this garlic butter-filled bun was much heavier and denser. The garlic middle was too sweet for my liking, too.
Taste: 2.75/5
Texture: 2.75/5
Price: 2/5
Total: 50%
Read our Bakery 1946 review .

Bakery 1946 is not halal-certified.
Bakery 1946: Popular Korean Bakery Opens In SG With Viral Fruit-Shaped Buns
9. Bae.gal
Bae.gal by homegrown chain Swee Heng is known for their wide range of bagels and breads, all at wallet-friendly prices. The Century Square bakery also offers a small selection of shio pan.
Their Sea Salt Butter ($2.50) was surprisingly buttery, though it lacked that crunchy bottom I was looking for. This bake tasted just like any other neighbourhood bakery bun, just more buttery.
I preferred their Taiwan Taro ($2.50) flavour. This shio pan came with a dab of sweet orh nee paste in the middle that paired well with rich, buttery notes.
For what these buns lacked, they made up for with their affordable prices. At just $2.50 a pop, I’m not complaining.
Taste: 2.25/5

Price: 4/5

8. SL Bakehouse
For affordable breads, pastries, and cakes in Jalan Besar , visit SL Bakehouse . The no-frills bakery also offers Shio Pan , priced at $2.80 a pop.
This shio pan was shaped like a puffy crescent. The exterior of both buns looked rather uneven, adding a rustic charm to the handmade treat. I particularly enjoyed the generous specks of sea salt chunks dotted on top of the bread, so you get a burst of flavour in each bite.

Xiao Jiao Tian, the Sichuan-inspired chain that came to Singapore by way of Fujian, is now open at Wisma Atria. It is the brand’s second outlet here, after City Square Mall in Farrer Park, and it brings the same wok-fired menu to the third floor of an Orchard Road mall.
The headline dish at both is the Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, one of four signatures and the hottest of them, marked with two chilli symbols on the menu.
Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, one of Xiao Jiao Tian’s four signatures. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
Who is behind it
Xiao Jiao Tian started in Fujian Province in 2013 and grew across more than 80 kitchens in China before it crossed over. The cooking is Sichuan in spirit but softened for a wider range of palates. Several dishes come with a spice-to-taste option, which helps if one person at the table wants it hot and another does not.
The kitchen’s own rule is that every dish is cooked once it is ordered, with nothing reheated and nothing made the night before. Rice is Wuchang rice from north-east China. The brand also promises that a dish which falls short of its standard is free.
What to order
The four signatures are a good first round for two or three people:
• Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli, the spiciest of the four
• Chinese Sauerkraut Fish, sliced fish in a pickled mustard green broth, one chilli on the menu
• Honey Spicy Chicken Bites, also one chilli
• Crispy Roast Chicken, for anyone avoiding heat altogether
Chinese Sauerkraut Fish. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
Beyond those, the best-seller section leans towards dishes that go with rice: Sizzling Beef, Golden Claypot Tofu, Steamed Pork Ribs with Rice Flour, Salted Egg Yolk Prawn and a Secret Recipe Grilled Frog. The Sweet and Sour Pork carries the Chinese name for lychee pork, the Fuzhou classic where the meat is scored so it curls up like the fruit, which is a quiet nod to where the brand began.
The full menu runs to 11 sections and more than 50 dishes, plus drinks, including a farmhouse section with Mapo Tofu and Country-Style Stir-Fried Pork, a cordyceps flower chicken soup, and shaved ices such as Golden Osmanthus Longan Ice and Fresh Fig Milk Ice. There is a separate kids’ section with crispy pork, chicken drumettes and fries, and the Steamed Egg with Minced Pork is labelled as a kids’ favourite.
Sizzling Beef, from the best-seller section. Image: Xiao Jiao Tian
The menu includes pork and pork intestines, so it is not one for halal diners.
Getting there and booking
Xiao Jiao Tian Wisma Atria is at 435 Orchard Road, #03-32/33/34, Singapore 238877. From Orchard MRT, Exit 3 leads underground into Wisma Atria at Basement 1, and the lifts go up to level three.
It opens from 11.30am to 10pm on weekdays and from 11am to 10pm on weekends, with last orders at 9pm on weekdays and 9.30pm on weekends. The hours are the same at City Square Mall, 180 Kitchener Road, #04-37.
Wisma Atria is walk-in only. Reservations are taken at City Square Mall alone, and only for groups of eight or more, on WhatsApp at +65 8099 7139 or by phone on +65 6312 4698. Delivery is through GrabFood, Foodpanda and Chinatown Delivery.
summary: Xiao Jiao Tian, the Sichuan-inspired chain from Fujian, is now open at Wisma Atria, its second Singapore outlet after City Square Mall. Signatures, hours and how to get there.
title: Xiao Jiao Tian opens its second Singapore outlet at Wisma Atria, with Bullfrog with Pickled Chilli as the signature

Been meaning to enjoy a day of water-based fun at Adventure Cove Waterpark ? Now’s your time to do so. Sadly, the popular waterpark at Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) will be closed for the entirety of 2027 , from 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2027.
Credit – Adventure Cove Waterpark, Resorts World Sentosa
Announced by RWS on 15 Nov 2026, the year-long closure is part of wider plans to refresh the attraction and “pave the way for an exciting new concept”. RWS has yet to reveal details of the revamped waterpark. More information about the transformation and reopening date will be unveiled at a later time .
Credit – Adventure Cove Waterpark, Resorts World Sentosa
The waterpark was first opened in 2012 and is home to several water rides. Its array of water slides includes the adrenaline-pumping Riptide Rocket and Dueling Racer , where visitors can race against one another down parallel slides. Besides exhilarating rides, the park features more relaxing experiences. One such ride is Adventure River , which is essentially a lazy river that’ll take you through 14 themed zones.
Other popular features of the park include Rainbow Reef , a snorkelling experience alongside around 20,000 colourful reef inhabitants and Big Bucket Treehouse , where visitors can experience a large water bucket tipping. If you are a season passholder and this closure affects your pass, the RWS team will reach out to you, so fret not. Alternatively, you can contact Guest Services at membershop@rwsentosa.com.
Credit – Universal Studio Singapore, Resorts World Sentosa (left) & Singapore Oceanarium, Resorts World Sentosa (right)
Other attractions at Sentosa include the iconic Universal Studios Singapore , where you can experience thrilling rides as well. For a more water-based attraction, you can consider Singapore Oceanarium. It also recently underwent a revamp and reopened on 24 Jul 2025.
If you’ll miss the Rainbow Reef in Adventure Cove Waterpark, try out PADI Discover Snorkelling (S$109) in Singapore Oceanarium . The experience includes a 1-day ticket to the oceanarium. You can expect to see manta rays, sharks and thousands of other animals from the Open Ocean habitat’s surface.
Head down before the year ends and the temporary closure begins!
Making waves: 11 must-try water activities in Singapore [Nov 2026]
summary: Adventure Cove Waterpark at Resorts World Sentosa will close from 1 Jan to 31 Dec 2027 for a major transformation, with details of its new concept and reopening date yet to be announced. Visitors can enjoy its water slides, lazy river and snorkelling experience before the closure, while those seeking alternatives can consider Universal Studios Singapore or PADI Discover Snorkelling at Singapore Oceanarium, priced at S$109 with a 1-day admission ticket.
title: Adventure Cove Waterpark closes for major upgrading

Since a trip to Spain, tapas has been my favourite kind of lunch and dinner. The idea is simple and sociable: order a spread of bite-size dishes, share them around the table, and try a bit of everything. So I’m always on the hunt for a taste of Spain in Singapore, and Casa Lola keeps calling my name, especially with a set lunch offer. How could I say no?
The location is another big draw. Casa Lola sits right in the heart of Singapore’s CBD , which makes it an easy lunch break for office workers nearby. The set lunch starts from S$34++ , and runs from Monday to Friday , 12 pm to 3pm .
Not sure what to order? Fret not, Casa Lola has an assortment of tapas to choose from, ranging from Toasted Bread with Butter , Seasonal Vegetables , Soup of the Day , and Spanish Side of the Day ! With 9 options , you’re spoilt for choice for their main courses .
Credit: Casa Lola
Want to feast like a king ? The Crispy Deboned Suckling Pig with Roasted Apple and Pumpkin (S$50) is slow-cooked until tender, then crisped for a golden, crunchy exterior. Prefer beef over duck? The Black Angus Striploin (S$58) or Wagyu Schnitzel (S$40) sounds good, both with a side of Arugula, Almond, and Sun-Dried Tomato Salad.
For a healthier option , try the Pan-Seared Barramundi with “Bilbaina” Sauce (S$38 ) or hit your protein count with the BBQ Achiote Spiced Chicken Skewer (S$28) . Or if comfort meals are your kind of lunch, definitely get Grandma Lola’s Baked Macaroni Ragu (S$26) , each bite warm and delightful, topped with melted cheese for that extra savouriness.
Credit: Casa Lola
We know there’s always room for dessert and coffee. Indulge in Casa Lola’s Chocolate Cake with Manjari 66% Dark Chocolate Ganache (S$14) , finished with a glossy chocolate glaze. If chocolate isn’t your thing, the Classic Santiago Almond Tart (S$10) or Spanish Creamy Flan Caramel with Chantilly (S$10) might entice you.
Make lunch less ordinary, bring a colleague, and reserve a table here to beat the lunch peak hours!

When it comes to planning a shopping spree as an East-sider, the stalwart trio of malls in Tampines should immediately spring to mind. While Tampines 1 and Century Square have their own charms, it is Tampines Mall that seems to attract the largest hoards; just swing by after 6pm and you’ll bear witness to its unending stream of shoppers.
Well, the crowds aren’t going to get any better, as the largest of the 3 malls just got a mini revamp that sees it becoming the largest beauty cluster in all of the East. Strategically introduced on the cusp of the holiday season, here’s everything new you can expect, from massive names in the beauty industry to yummy eats for all.

Fair warning to the guys: a decent amount of them land in the beauty category, so you’ll be following the missus around quite a bit as she makes her rounds in the mall. On the other hand, something that’s more universally enjoyed is their range of new eateries too, so be sure to come on an empty stomach.
1. Kiehl’s
For those looking to beef up their skincare routine, consider making a pit stop at Kiehl’s . You’ll be able to wave hello to Mr Bones – that’s his official name – at #01-10 and shop for their highly-raved skincare products. The faithful shoppers of Tampines Mall will notice that they’ve moved to a new unit within the mall, but the same familiar favourites still line their shelves.
In particular, they’ve got festive sets that come beautifully packaged, making for great gifts to leave under the Christmas tree . Their All Is Calm & Soothed set ($69) bundles the Calendula Deep Cleansing Foaming Face Wash with the Calendula Herbal-Extract Toner, perfect for folks with oily or combination skin.
The Winter Skin Soothers set ($107) is another option to bring home and provides a more comprehensive combo, as it’s packed with the brand’s Ultra Facial Barrier-Hydrating Cleanser and Ultra Facial Cream that’s better suited for dehydrated skin.
This outlet also offers free skin analysis for all customers, regardless of whether you’ve bought anything or not. The 10-minute session entails a reading with their Derma-Reader Pro tool, and based on your results, a Kiehl’s skincare expert will provide insights on which products to get.

Where are the top Chinese restaurants in Singapore?
From affordable options to Michelin – recommended eateries, these best Chinese restaurant options in Singapore will have something for everyone. We’ve also included Chinese restaurants with private rooms on this list!
1. PUTIEN
In 2000, a Chinese immigrant named Uncle Fong moved to Singapore from his Fujian hometown, Putian. Here, he was surprised to find that, despite the rich diversity of Chinese restaurants in Singapore, none served authentic Putian or Fujian cuisine. Determined to fill this gap, he founded PUTIEN ’s flagship restaurant along Kitchener Road. The restaurant quickly gained acclaim, earning a Michelin Star for six consecutive years and expanding to over 15 outlets across Singapore, with many more in the region.
PUTIEN stands out as one of the rare Chinese restaurant franchises in Singapore that truly honours its culinary roots. Specialising in Fujian cooking, the brand focuses on seasonal ingredients, with an emphasis on fresh seafood, particularly shellfish and fish, and mushrooms that build deep, complex flavours.
The Fujian Red Mushroom Seafood Lor Mee (from $18.80 ++ ) is a signature dish for good reason. 13 ingredients, including rare red mushrooms harvested from China’s Wuyi Mountains, are prepared in a pork bone broth that has been boiled for up to eight hours. If you’re dining with a group, don’t skip the ‘ 100-Secon d’ Stewed Yellow Croaker ($ 16.80 ++ per person) , expertly boiled for precisely 100 seconds to preserve the natural freshness and delicate texture of the fish.
Diners can enjoy up to 10% off when dining in at all PUTIEN outlets, including their celebrated Michelin-approved Kitchener Road outlet! To enjoy this deal while it lasts, open your Grab app when it’s time to pay for your meal. Select Dine Out, search for PUTIEN, then tap on “Pay Bill”. Enter the amount of your total bill, and the 10% offer will be applied automatically.
Plus, first-time Dine Out users get an additional $5 off their total using the code ‘ DINEOUTNEW ’, with a minimum spend of $10.
Browse more deals on Grab Dine Out .

PUTIEN is not halal-certified.
Putien Has $25 Breakfast Buffet With Free-Flow Porridge, Pan-Fried Buns And More
2. Wu Yue Ting
Image credit: Andaz Singapore
For refined Cantonese cuisine with a stunning view, head up to Wu Yue Ting , formerly known as 5 ON 25, on Level 25 of Andaz Singapore . It’s just a short walk from Bugis MRT Station , and the modern, upscale dining room looks out over the city skyline. The menu can be customised to suit your table, and seasonal specialties and guest chef collaborations mean there’s usually something new to try on repeat visits.
Start with the Cantonese Style Roasted Cage-Free Cherry Valley Duck ($50++ for half, $98++ for full) , then warm up with the Hong Kong Style Braised Fish Soup ( $28 ) , packed with black cod, sea cucumber, fish maw, yellow chives, and vermicelli. Seafood lovers can go for the Stir-Fried Maine Lobster & Jade Tiger Abalone ($72++) with Chinese yam, golden fungus mushrooms, and asparagus. There’s also a hearty Stir-Fried Tasmanian Cape Grim Angus Tenderloin ($52++) , tossed with leek, two kinds of garlic, and single-estate Kampot black pepper. Round it off with the comforting Signature Handmade Tofu in Stone Pot ($35++) , served in a superior yellow chicken broth, and a glass or two from the restaurant’s range of Chinese wines.
Wu Yue Ting’s wine selection comes from key wine-producing regions in China—think Ningxia, Xinjiang, Shanxi, Hebei, Shandong, Yunnan, and Huanren County in Liaoning. As a result, diners are able to savour an impressive showcase of exceptional wines shaped by China’s diverse terroirs.
Swing by on weekends for their rotational Weekend Yum Cha menu. It features delicate dim sum creations, nourishing soups, and special chef-recommended dishes . And if you’re planning a celebration, Wu Yue Ting has two private dining suites, each with stunning views. The Ruby suite seats eight pax, and the Emerald suite seats 12. For large-scale events, the restaurant is able to host anywhere from 20 to 90 guests, something to keep in mind when you’re planning birthdays, full-month celebrations, solemnisations, company gatherings, and so on.

Bandar Utama ‘s newest neighbourhood destination, One Square , brings together dining, lifestyle, wellness and everyday essentials in one convenient spot. Just a short walk from Bandar Utama MRT and LRT stations , this community hub is home to everything from artisanal bakeries and specialty cafes to Malaysian comfort food .
More tenants are on the way, but here are 5 food spots at One Square that are already open and worth checking out .

1. Yellow Brick Road (SQ3)
A familiar name among KL’s cafe crowd, Yellow Brick Road (YBR) is known for its quality coffee, brunch favourites and Western fare. It is also home to 4-time Malaysian Barista Champion Jason Loo, with community and a welcoming, home-away-from-home atmosphere at the heart of its identity.
Now with 3 outlets across The Five in Bukit Damansara, Chinatown KL and its newest and largest branch at One Square, YBR offers an extensive menu spanning brunch plates, fusion mains, specialty coffee, creative beverages and desserts. Its pancakes and tiramisu are among the must-tries.
For brunch, Big Breakfast Bash (RM48) is a hearty option featuring eggs prepared your way, chicken sausage, beef bacon or chicken ham, hash brown, grilled portobello mushroom, roast tomato and wholemeal sourdough. Those after something lighter can opt for the Berry Smoothie Bowl (RM29) , topped with homemade coconut granola, fresh seasonal fruits and mixed seeds.
The menu also ventures into more substantial territory, including Seafood Aglio Olio (RM40) with tiger prawns and kepah clams, and Salted Egg Squid Pasta (RM38) for those who enjoy a little heat. Sweet tooths, meanwhile, will find plenty to love in its pancake selection, particularly the local-inspired Peter Pandan (RM29) with jackfruit, gula Melaka sauce and salted caramel ice cream.
Round off your meal with one of its signature drinks, such as the Malaysian Pride (RM21) , combining Liberica espresso from Johor with Chemor chocolate and gula Melaka.
+603 2011 7690
Daily: 8.30am – 10pm
Facebook | Instagram | Website
2. Wolfgang’s by Wolf & Turtle (SQ8)
If you’re craving a proper American-style diner food, Wolfgang’s by Wolf & Turtle is one to check out at One Square. A retro-inspired spin-off of Wolf & Turtle Coffee Roasters , this casual eatery brings together comforting diner classics, hearty breakfast plates, quality coffee and what the brand describes as some of PJ’s best smashed burgers.
The menu covers plenty of options, starting with the Björn Big Breakfast (RM35) , a generous plate of sausages, sauteed mushrooms, eggs, hash browns, baked beans and toast. For something more filling, the Steak And Eggs (RM39) pairs Australian sirloin with potatoes, sunny-side-up kampung eggs and chimichurri , while the Swedish Meatballs (RM30) come served with brown gravy, mashed potatoes and berry jam.
There are also fuss-free diner staples such as Fish & Chips (RM29) , featuring golden battered fish with crispy fries and tartar sauce, and Chicken Tenders (RM20) with ranch dressing. Sausage lovers can customise their Classic Dawg (RM22) or House Dawg (RM24) with a choice of lamb, beef or chicken sausage, with the latter topped with caramelised onions and melted Parmesan.
Leave room for dessert, too. The pancake selection includes Blueberry Pancakes (RM24) and Banana & Walnuts Pancakes (RM25) , while Grandma’s Key Lime Pie (RM16) offers a refreshing finish to all that savoury goodness.

3. Bengbeng Sourdough (SQ3A)
Bread lovers may want to make a pit stop at Bengbeng Sourdough , a neighbourhood bakery specialising in freshly baked sourdough made with quality ingredients. Beyond its selection of artisan loaves and pastries, the cafe also serves a range of coffee and light bites.
Credit – Bengbeng Sourdough
Its bakery selection includes Sourdough Country Loaf (RM21) and Plain Bagels (RM15 for 2 pieces) , alongside flaky pastries such as Almond Croissant (RM21) , Lemon Croissant (RM21) and Honey Sea Salt Croissant (RM21) .
For a quick bite, the sourdough toasties are worth browsing. Options include Grilled Tuna & Cheese (RM19) , Minced Beef In Tomato Sauce & Melted Cheese (RM21) and Green Salsa Chicken & Cheese (RM21) , while vegetarians can opt for Shrooms & Veggie Saute (RM19) . There are also breakfast sandwiches, including the local-inspired Kahwin Toast (RM10) , made with sourdough white bread, locally made kaya and premium salted butter.
…
summary: One Square in Bandar Utama offers a mix of cafes, bakeries, casual diners and Malaysian eateries, just a short walk from the MRT and LRT stations. These food spots cover brunch, American-style diner fare, artisan sourdough, halal-certified local dishes and speciality matcha, with prices starting from RM8.90, making them useful options for nearby residents, commuters and visitors.
title: Best food at One Square, Bandar Utama PJ for brunch, coffee & local favourites

If you asked me the age-old question, “What’s your favourite cuisine?”, I’d have one straight answer for you and it’s Korean . However, I’ve become a bit of a ‘snob’ where the cuisine is concerned.
Don’t get me wrong, I couldn’t be more grateful for the sheer number of Korean eateries and stalls that fuel my penchant. But you see, it’s one thing to serve the cuisine and another to do it well. So, when I caught wind of GAHE Traditional Korean Cuisine and its promises of the latter, I was already halfway out the door and on my way to Sengkang .
Credit – Shawn Tye via Google Reviews
I’m not quite sure if I can call this stall a hidden gem. On one hand, it’s nestled in an unassuming kopitiam under a HDB block in the ulu , almost-pin drop quiet neighbourhood of Fernvale . On the other hand, it has steadily gained recognition since it opened in Feb 2024 . I’m talking about how hordes of people have flocked there and how the food sells out in less than an hour after opening.
As an unfortunately regular victim of Murphy’s law, I couldn’t help but worry about the crowd situation and how I might end up not securing what I set out to try. Thankfully, these worries were unfounded as the queue had only just begun to form when I arrived. Oh, and in case you were wondering, the waves of patrons remained rather small and sporadic during my visit on a Friday evening.
What I tried at GAHE Traditional Korean Cuisine
GAHE has a pretty well-rounded menu with wallet-friendly price tags. You’ll find the usual suspects — hotplate meat sets like Beef Bulgogi (S$8.90) , soothing stew sets like Kimchi Soup (S$6.90) and Toufu Soup (S$6.90) , and light bites like Tteokbokki (S$6.90) .
That aside, there are a handful of Korean staples you don’t usually find in coffeeshop settings — Naengmyeon (S$7.90) and Samgyetang (S$9.90/S$15.90) , for instance.
First things first, I gunned for none other than my favourite Korean dish of all time: Jjajangmyeon (S$7.90) . Although this delicious dish of black bean noodles is a dime a dozen in Korea, it stands among the coffeeshop rarities I was just talking about. Of course, I couldn’t have been more thrilled to see it right there.
Part of me just loves delighting in the little things, like the sleek steel bowl the dish was served in — instant plus points for presentation, if you ask me. At its base lay a bed of thick wheat noodles topped with a generous portion of rich black bean sauce and julienned cucumber strips. Crowning it was a perfectly cooked sunny-side-up egg and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.
Giving the noodles a good mix took quite a fair bit of effort; the sauce was just so thick! After that vigorous arm workout, I was rewarded with the sight of each strand slathered generously in that silky sauce and sporting an enticing glossy sheen.
As a huge sucker for great mouthfeel and all things chewy, I had my expectations set pretty high. Sadly, the noodles missed the mark by a smidge as they weren’t as chewy or as springy as I’d have liked. Nonetheless, I’d say that they did possess a sufficient bite that paired well with the thick, hearty sauce.
On the flip side, the luscious black bean sauce was hands down the star of the show. It was thick and clumpy in the most indulgent way, studded with soft black beans and tender chunks of meat that rendered depth to each mouthful. Its flavour profile was complex and deeply umami , with a prominent shallot-y undertone that enhanced its richness.
Not to worry if you’re not huge on strong flavours; the fresh cucumber slivers on the side effectively cut through the heaviness of the sauce with a refreshing crunch.
Utterly addictive and packed with flavour, the sauce more than made up for the shortcomings of the noodles. And honestly, it could very well go head to head with those that I’ve tried from the motherland.
We tried Singapore’s worst-rated Korean food stall
Enter my next conquest, the reliable Hot Bibimbap with Chicken (S$7.90) . Yes, *hot* bibimbap . I was rather amused by the need for ‘clarification’ — there’s a Warm Bibimbap option priced at a dollar less, except it’s served in a regular bowl instead of a sizzlin’ stone pot.
This visually striking dish featured a plethora of fresh ingredients arranged meticulously atop the bed of white rice. One of the things I adore most about bibimbap has got to be its colours, and GAHE definitely delivered in that arena.
Accompanying the bibimbap was a little heart-shaped dish filled with vibrant red gochujang . As an avid lover of spice and that ‘magical’ sweet-spicy condiment, I was sure to leave no drop untouched. Or you could say I poured my heart out (ha ha).
I gave the bowl a good toss, ensuring that the ingredients melded together so I’d get hefty spoonfuls of everything. Despite my efforts, there was barely enough gochujang to go around. I couldn’t help but gripe about the portions of rice that were left bare.
…
summary: GAHE Traditional Korean Cuisine is a coffeeshop stall in Fernvale, Sengkang, serving Korean staples at wallet-friendly prices, with dishes ranging from S$6.90 soups to S$9.90 samgyetang. Its jjajangmyeon stands out for its rich, umami black bean sauce, while the bibimbap and army soup have some shortcomings. The stall suits diners seeking affordable Korean food and less common dishes, though its location may require extra travelling time.
title: GAHE Traditional Korean Cuisine: Popular gem with quality affordable Korean faves like jjajangmyeon & army stew

body:
Tucked away in the bustling basement of Golden Mile Food Centre is Charr’d The Hawker , a vibrant Muslim-owned hawker stall run by 2 friendly young chefs. Don’t expect to find wagyu tomahawks at these hawker tables — despite the similar name, this modest Western stall is completely unrelated to Changi’s famous halal steakhouse.
Helmed by 2 young chefs who previously worked in fine-dining kitchens, their dream of running their own F&B business dates all the way back to their university days at The Culinary Institute of America under the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT). Prior to establishing Charr’d The Hawker, they ran a home-based venture called The Layered Brothers, where they served up lapis rempah , traditional spiced cakes.
Today, they bring expertise picked up from both university and professional kitchens to Golden Mile Food Centre, churning out comfort Western fare.
What to order at Charr’d The Hawker
For my main, I went straight for their bestselling Charr’d Chicken Chop (S$8.50) . It features a crisp chicken chop, a scoop of coleslaw, baked beans, a cup of BBQ sauce, a lightly toasted buttered bun and a choice between garlic butter rice, fries and mashed potato. I opted for the garlic butter rice. Visually, it’s a pretty plate as the colours of the garlic rice and purple cabbage in the coleslaw pop and make it look that much more appetising.
As the stall’s name suggests, I expected nothing less than a perfectly charred protein, and I’m glad to report it delivered. The chicken had a crisp, golden-brown crust that was absolutely delicious and well-seasoned.
The meat didn’t lean as salty as I would have preferred but when dipped in the provided BBQ sauce, it hit all the spots of tangy, spicy and salty. While the sauce was a little watery, I loved how tart it was and how the spice blend lent it a nice warmth.
The chicken fillet was a little thinner than other chicken chops I’ve had in the past, but the crispy skin and seasoning do make up for it.
Although the menu bills it as garlic butter rice, I didn’t pick up much of a garlicky aroma. To me, it tasted a lot more like traditional chicken rice. While it was still tasty, it wasn’t really what I had expected from garlic butter rice.
I appreciated that the rice was cooked nicely — the grains kept a pleasant bite without turning mushy or clumping together.
One of the best elements on the plate for me was the coleslaw. Sporting vibrant orange and purple hues from the shredded carrot and purple cabbage, it was visually appealing. It tasted fresh, helping to cut through the richness of the other components, while its crisp texture added a delightful crunch to every bite. The owner was even kind enough to top up extra coleslaw when I packed up my food to-go after the tasting.
The serving of baked beans was reminiscent of old-school Western hawkers and offered an elevated take on a familiar, old-school staple.
ATECOOKIES.SG: Are these $5.50 NY-style cookies on Beach Road actually worth it?
Next, I moved on to the 2-pc Chicken Wing (S$4) . These absolutely stole the spotlight for me, hitting every mark of what a great fried chicken wing should be. Marinated in yoghurt, the meat stayed wonderfully tender and juicy on the inside.
Outside, the crust boasted a super crispy finish packed with savoury seasoning. Honestly, it was a masterclass in fried chicken wings — flavourful enough that you don’t even need the accompanying chilli sauce.
Who is Charr’d The Hawker best for?
If you’re looking for a comforting, old-school Western-style meal with generous and thoughtfully executed sides, Charr’d The Hawker is well worth a visit. The chefs’ fine-dining background shines through in the little details, elevating familiar hawker staples like the vibrant, crunchy coleslaw. It’s an easy go-to for Muslim diners and groups hunting for hearty and affordable Western fare in the Beach Road area.
How to get to Charr’d The Hawker
Charr’d The Hawker is located on the basement level of Golden Mile Food Centre, which is a quick 7-minute walk from Nicoll Highway MRT Station . The station connects to the MRT Circle Line. Take Exit A and walk along Java Road before turning left onto Beach Road.
If you prefer to travel by bus, alight at Opp St. John HQ (01411) or St. John HQ (01419) along Beach Road. Do note that bus service 961M operates exclusively on Sundays and public holidays, while all other bus services operate daily.
Do we recommend Charr’d The Hawker?
Yes! I thoroughly enjoyed every element of the plate as each felt intentional and was done well. That said, on my next visit, I would opt for the chicken wing set instead of the chicken chop. While the chicken chop had a great crust, the fillet was slightly on the thinner side, whereas the wings were easily the star of the meal.
People also read:
What are the best Western hawkers in Singapore?
What’s there to eat in Lavender?
summary: Charr’d The Hawker is a Muslim-owned Western food stall in the basement of Golden Mile Food Centre along Beach Road, run by 2 Culinary Institute of America graduates with fine-dining backgrounds. Located a 7-minute walk from Nicoll Highway MRT Station, the stall serves comfort dishes like the S$8.50 chicken chop and S$4 yoghurt-marinated fried chicken wings alongside house-made coleslaw and baked beans. It is well suited for Muslim diners and groups seeking affordable, hearty hawker meals with thoughtfully executed sides.
title: Charr’d The Hawker: Ex-fine-dining chefs dish out $4 hearty Western comfort food
