The last time I visited Lotteria was at the start of the year, when it first arrived on our shores with its Jewel Changi Airport outlet. Since then, Lotteria has opened another outlet at Jurong Point and has also recently received its official Halal certification .
At the same time, they just introduced a Teriyaki series featuring a couple of new burgers . I enjoyed my meal on my last visit, so of course, when we had the chance to visit Lotteria again to check out the new menu, I said yes. But do the new items compare to the classics I liked? Keep reading to find out!
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The new Teriyaki burgers in question are the Teri Egg Crispy Chicken Burger (S$7.20) and Teri Egg Beef Burger (S$7.20) . Both are available at S$10.50 for a combo with regular fries and a soft drink.
For those who want more meaty goodness, you can also opt for the Double Teri Egg Beef Burger ( S$7.90 a la carte, S$11.20 combo), available at just S$0.70 more than its single counterpart.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
As you can probably tell, the menu combines sweet , savoury , and egg-cellent flavours for satisfying bites each time. Out of the two burgers we had, I preferred the crunch of the Teri Egg Crispy Chicken Burger.
The sweet teriyaki sauce paired surprisingly well with the deep-fried, lightly salted chicken, which came tucked into a bun with an egg.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Still, the chicken classics are what I’d go back to Lotteria for. Both the Original Chicken and Gangjung Chicken packed a flavourful punch. For someone with a low spice tolerance, the Gangjung Chicken wasn’t too spicy and was a perfect balance of heat and flavour.
I especially loved the sweet-savoury glaze at the top, combined with the crispy texture underneath. It’s no surprise that Gangjung Chicken is one of Lotteria’s signature items.
Both the Original Chicken and Gangjung Chicken are now also available in K-Bap Chicken Combos , which come with 2 pieces of chicken , K-Bap (rice) , Iced Lemon Tea , and 4 pieces of Onion Rings .
These sets are priced at S$11.50 for Original Chicken , S$12.50 for Gangjung Chicken , and S$12.80 for a mix of both .
Photos by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
And of course, we can’t leave Lotteria without having a dessert! I remember being pleasantly surprised by the sweet treats last time, so I looked forward to trying the Mango Peach Bingsu (S$5.90) this time.
Honestly, the texture of the ice was not what I pictured for bingsu , but the taste did not disappoint. The generous servings of diced mango and sliced peach, red bean at the bottom, and ice cream on top are a combination worth gaining a few calories for.
If you’ve yet to visit the Korean burger chain and are looking for a place to satisfy your fast food cravings, take this as your sign to visit Lotteria!

Starbucks Bearista Glass Cold Cup in Singapore
Starbucks merch has a way of making you question your life choices, like whether you really need another cup. But once it’s cute enough, logic flies straight out the window, and honestly, we’re just as guilty. And so the glass bear that turned grown adults into dawn-queue warriors is back, and this time Starbucks has decided the hunt wasn’t stressful enough.
The new Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box lands in Singapore on 23rd November 2026 , and you won’t know which bear you’ve got until the box is open.
There are 5 festive designs to collect, including a rare golden bear that’s already sending collectors overseas into a frenzy. Here’s everything you need to know: what’s inside, when and where to buy, and how to give yourself a fighting chance.
What is the Starbucks Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box?
Starbucks says it sold out in less than a day.
Image credit: @一颗西柚 via RED
First released in the US, the Starbucks Bearista Glass Cold Cup quickly went viral for obvious reasons. Its bear-shaped glass body features the iconic Bearista rocking a beanie in the brand’s signature green, and it’s even clutching a tiny Starbucks cup in its hands. Excuse us while we squeal – we’re trying to keep it together, but it’s not easy.
Image credit: @小红薯 via RED
And because it’s glass, it’s reusable, so you can have your morning cuppa every day with a side of cuteness. The look of it also adapts according to your drink choice because the cup is transparent.
Singapore got its own restock in March 2026 at $35.90 a pop, and it vanished about as quickly as you’d expect.
View this post on Instagram
The holiday version keeps the same 20 fl oz (591ml) hand-blown glass body , but each bear is dressed for winter and sealed inside a red mystery box. Every box also comes with a little personality card that tells you your bear’s vibe, its favourite holiday tradition and its go-to Starbucks order. Yes, your cup has a drink order now.
Meet the 5 Bearista designs, from a skiing bear to a rare golden one
Image adapted from: Starbucks
Starbucks has named 4 of the bears, with the 5th kept under wraps as the chase piece:
• Reiny: A reindeer bear in a brown antler hood, complete with a North Pole sign topper. Starbucks pegs this one as the high-energy type who winds down with classic Christmas movies.
• Aspen: A frosty white skier in purple goggles, made for people whose idea of winter is a ski trip they haven’t booked yet.
• Joy: An ice-skating dreamer wearing a snow globe on her head, because apparently she collects them.
• Bunny: A snow bunny in green earmuffs, and the only one in the set that changes colour when you pour in a cold drink. Fill her with your iced latte and watch her go from clear to a blue-purple ombré.
• Goldie: The rare golden bear, and the one everyone secretly wants. Starbucks hasn’t said how rare, only that you’ll need luck to pull one.
To put Goldie’s rarity in perspective, resellers in the US were reportedly asking around 6 times the retail price for one within days of launch. Keep that in mind before you pay a scalper’s markup here.
How much is the Starbucks Bearista blind box in Singapore?
Image adapted from: Ebay
Starbucks Singapore hasn’t revealed local pricing yet. For reference, each box retails for US$39.95 (~S$52) in the US, which is about US$10 more than the original bear, a bump Starbucks put down to the extra design details & accessories.
Previous drops were limited to 2 pieces per transaction , perfect for keeping 1 for yourself and gifting the other to friends or family. As for scalpers hoping to make a quick buck… don’t. We see you.
We’ll update this article once Starbucks Singapore confirms the local price and purchase cap.
Where can you buy the Bearista Glass Cold Cup?
Watch how your Bearista cup transforms depending on your choice of beverage.
Image adapted from: Starbucks
The collection goes on sale on 23rd November 2026 across 3 channels:
• In stores: From store opening, or from 6.30am at 24-hour Starbucks outlets
• Starbucks Online Store: From 10am
• Starbucks Flagship Store on LazMall: From 12pm
Stocks are limited, so treat this like a concert ticket drop rather than a casual coffee run. The 24-hour outlets give you the earliest shot, while the online store is your best bet if you’d rather refresh a page in pyjamas than queue in the dark.

It’s time to unleash the Armys as the excitement of the BTS World Tour Arirang builds ahead of the band’s four-night show at the National Stadium happening in December. This is one of the biggest city-wide activations we’ve seen for a concert in Singapore ! And it comes as no surprise. Now that the band has completed their mandatory military service, we’re set to welcome them back to the stage with a humongous bang. Ready to clock your steps in as you hit up every activity happening in Singapore? Let’s get started…
BTS The City Arirang Singapore activations & attractions: National Gallery Singapore
1. BTS The City Arirang Gallery Rave
Photography: National Gallery Singapore
A BTS-inspired activation isn’t complete without some kind of rave – our favourite type of event in the city nowadays! As the sun sets and daytime visitors stream out, the gallery opens its doors to a special after-hours crowd. Fans will be treated to BTS-inspired remix sets, immersive lighting, and projection visuals at the Singapore Courtyard. Your ticket also gets you after-hours access to the Pop after Pop: Art around Us exhibition, photobooths, and a complimentary Gallery Insider membership. Super fans can also treat yourselves to ticket-exclusive BTS The City Arirang water bottles, available in limited quantities.
When: 18 to 19 December 2026; after-hours exhibition, 7pm to 8pm; rave starts at 8pm
Price: $78 for rave tickets; $113 for the rave and a water bottle
Where: BTS The City Arirang Gallery Rave , various locations around National Gallery Singapore, 1 St Andrew’s Road, Singapore 178957
2. Pop After Pop: BTS The City Arirang Art Trail
Photography: National Gallery Singapore
This unique art trail is being given a much-needed BTS treatment as the National Gallery Singapore weaves Pop Art and Arirang together in this tour. As you explore selected artwork through the building, each piece will be tied to a song from the Arirang album, complemented by access to the Gallery Photobooth. Tickets to the guided tour are sold out, but you can enjoy a self-guided tour and take your time to browse.
When: Various dates between 12 and20 December 2026
Price: Tickets start from $35
Where: Pop After Pop BTS The City Arirang Art Trail , various locations around National Gallery Singapore, 1 St Andrew’s Road, Singapore 178957

Photography: National Gallery Singapore
It wouldn’t be a city-wide takeover without some delectable food and drinks! Select restaurants within National Gallery Singapore will be dishing out a curated menu of BTS The City Arirang-inspired dishes. Think signature cocktails and pastries, to big plates and special dining offers for fans.
When: 11 to 31 December 2026
Price: Varies with each location
Where: BTS The City Arirang-inspired menus , available at Bakery Brera, Rempapa, Milli Sky Dining & Bar, and Milli Lounge
4. BTS The City Arirang photo spots
Photography: National Gallery Singapore
National Gallery Singapore is taking the BTS vibe very seriously because it’s gonna dress to impress for the occasion! As you tour the gallery, enjoy the special menus, and vibe to the Arirang album playing through the gallery tours, remember to snap some photos at various photo spots around the building. That way, you’ll show everyone who the true super fan is!
When: 11 to 31 December 2026
Price : Free
Where: BTS The City Arirang photo spots , various locations around the National Gallery Singapore
BTS The City Arirang Singapore activations & attractions: Orchard Central & Clarke Quay Central
5. BTS The City Holiday Escape: Themed photo spots
The Pool House at Orchard Central. Photography: Far East Malls
A BTS-inspired pop-up may be a lot closer than you think! Throughout December, Orchard Central and Clarke Quay Central will host a series of themed photo zones, from an industrial-chic urban lounge to a pool-inspired backdrop. You can also drop a message on the holiday message wall and participate in a mini stamp rally at stations across both malls. There’s also an excuse to shop because you can redeem limited-edition collectibles with qualifying spends.
When: 1 to 31 December 2026; daily, 11am to 9pm
Price: Free
Where: BTS The City Holiday Escape: Themed photo spots , multiple locations including Orchard Central and Clarke Quay Central
BTS The City Arirang Singapore activations & attractions: Sentosa
6. BTS The City Arirang Rave & Drone Party
Photography: Sentosa
If you didn’t get tickets to the BTS concert, fear not! You can still get the vibe at Sentosa’s rave and drone party happening over three days. This fan experience features live DJing by local K-pop DJ and Waterbomb Singapore performer DJ Raw, spinning tunes as the sun sets and bathes you in the golden hour glow. McDonald’s Singapore is giving diners a taste of its international outposts starting from 26 Nov 2026 at 11am . The limited-time rollout is part of McDonald’s ‘Robble Air’ campaign, which aims to import fan-favourite specials from around the world, including exclusive burgers , sides and desserts.
Joining in on the fun, a merchandise collection starring the striped McDonaldland bandit, Hamburglar, will also be available with the purchase of any McDonald’s meal.
Credit – McDonald’s Singapore
Headlining the international lineup are 2 burgers inspired by the Canadian McDonald’s menu. Dressed in smoky, sweet maple BBQ sauce and topped with crispy chicken bacon and fried onions, the Maple BBQ Quarter Pounder with Cheese ( from S$10.50 for a Single Meal; from S$12.90 for a Double Meal) and Maple BBQ Chicken Burger (from S$10.50 for a Single Meal; from S$12.80 for a Double Meal) are available after breakfast hours across restaurants islandwide.
Credit – McDonald’s Singapore
Accompanying the mains are a peppery Szechuan Sauce dip ( S$0.70 per tub, or complimentary with Chicken McNuggets meals) and the floral, cherry-blossom-inspired Sakura McFizz ( from S$3.65 ) from McDonald’s Japan.
Credit – McDonald’s Singapore
To end your meal on a sweet note, don’t forget to try the soft mini-doughnut McPops , which are returning in 2 flavours — chocolate pastry McPops filled with Pistachio and McDonald’s Australia’s viral Biscoff filling ( S$2.95 for 2 pieces). At the dessert kiosk, look out for the Popcorn Caramel soft-serve range spanning Sundaes, McFlurries, Twist Cones, and ChocoCones.
Credit – McDonald’s Singapore
Besides the all-new menu, McDonaldland fans can snag limited-edition Hamburglar Mischief Tees starting from 26 Nov at 11am for S$14.90 each (available in Master or Mini sizes) with any meal purchase. A Hamburglar Reusable Bag follows on 3 Dec at 11am for S$8.90 with any meal, complemented by over 60 in-store Hamburglar meet-and-greet appearances islandwide starting 28 Nov .
11 best old-school Western food spots in Singapore
summary: McDonald’s Singapore launches its limited-time Robble Air menu on 26 Nov 2026 at 11am, introducing international specials such as Maple BBQ burgers from S$10.50, Szechuan Sauce, Sakura McFizz, Pistachio and Biscoff McPops, and Popcorn Caramel soft-serve across restaurants islandwide. Useful for diners seeking overseas fast-food flavours locally and McDonaldland collectors, the rollout also pairs meal purchases with Hamburglar T-shirts (S$14.90) and reusable bags (S$8.90 from 3 Dec).
title: New Hamburglar merch drops as McDonald’s launches Maple BBQ burgers

body:
Do you enjoy hanging out at New Bahru ? A new pop-up has appeared in the form of a Taiwanese convenience store with a hot kitchen serving freshly cooked fried chicken .
The vibes here are immaculate as expected, but how is the food? Keep reading to find out more from our experience.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
BAO Fast Foods (BFF) is open from 11 November 2026 to 28 December 2026 . Located at Level 1 of New Bahru near CS Fresh with a brightly lit sign, it’s hard to miss. Half the unit is a convenience store and kitchen , while the other half is a diner with seating.
If you prefer the outdoors, there is also a seating area outside the store.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Stepping through the entrance, we were immediately greeted by the aroma of fried chicken. It’s almost like BFF is saying, “Here’s our main character, and it deserves the spotlight.” And it would be fair because BFF’s Chicken Chopper is the highlight of everything we tried here.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Before we explore the rest of the pop-up, let’s jump straight into the food! The Chicken Choppers are available à la carte for S$6.50 each , or with a meal from S$7.90 to S$15.50 . There are 3 flavours available: Original Crispy , Master Scalded , and Flame Glazed .
We opted for Meal B – Original Crispy Chicken Chopper with Chicken Bao Soupie & Cabbage (S$9.50) , and Meal D – Master Scalded Chicken Chopper with Beef Spit Noodle Soup (S$15.50) .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Both flavours of Chicken Choppers we had were delightful. The Master Scalded Chicken Chopper is dipped into a boiling master sauce during cooking, which is something you can watch the kitchen crew do from over the counter.
The result is a sweet glaze with hints of soy sauce, star anise, and cinnamon, combined with the savoury flavours of fried chicken underneath. Somehow, even after being dipped fully into the sauce, the chicken maintains its satisfying, crunchy texture.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
But for me personally, my top choice would have to be the Original Crispy Chicken Chopper. From the outside, you might expect it to be dry, but it’s not at all.
It is crispier than the Master Scalded Chicken Chopper and is seasoned to perfection with salt and Taiwanese white pepper. Every bite packs a delicious punch, a result of both the crispy, flavourful skin outside and the juicy meat inside.
And the best part? You can enjoy any of the Chicken Choppers with your hands without getting them dirty, because of how they are prepared and packaged. Making the chicken bone a handle is such a simple but genius idea.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Another item worth mentioning is the Chicken Bao Soupie ( S$3.50 à la carte), which is essentially a larger version of a sheng jian bao . If you’re a fan of those or xiao long bao , you will enjoy this one. Just imagine the soft top, pan-fried bottom, and rich soup filling and meat on the inside – simply heavenly.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
If you prefer having something with hot soup, the Beef Spit Noodle Soup ( S$12.50 à la carte) is another tasty option. The beef steak slices were tender and well-seasoned, while the noodles were springy.
The soup was served on the side and was rich and savoury with a gentle tang. Whether you have it separately or use it to dip the noodles, you can enjoy the meal the way you want.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Want to grab a dessert before heading off? Those of you with a really sweet tooth would probably enjoy the Banoffee Soy Pudding (S$5) from the grab-and-go section. There is also a soft-serve station for those of you who prefer ice cream.
Photos by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
For drinks, there are two signature items to look out for: The Fluffy Orange Guava Beauty Tea (S$6.80) and the Peanut Oatside M*lk (S$6.20) . The first is a refreshing drink with cheese foam on top, while the second is a nutty sweet treat with Oat Boba and Tea Jelly.
If you opt for the Fluffy Orange Guava Beauty Tea, you can try out the Drinks Printer machine and customise your foam top with the BFF logo. My drink of choice, however, would be the Peanut Oatside M*lk, with its indulgent combination of flavours I love.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Even if you’re not planning to dine at BFF, drop by the convenience store section where you will discover a selection of snacks rarely found in local supermarkets.
You will also find exclusive BAO merchandise , from tote bags (S$30) and umbrellas (S$13) to socks (S$13) and even Pocket Tissue packs (S$0.50 each) .
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
If convenience store dates are your vibe, or if you’re looking for a new hangout spot at New Bahru, check out the BFF pop-up while it is still open this month .
You might find Taiwanese-inspired flavours you like while you’re at it.

The Centrepoint – Snoopy’s Christmas Recipe for Joy
Orchard Road’s Christmas light-up usually steals the show every year-end period, but this year, there’s a beagle worth making a detour for while you’re already in town. From 13th November to 31st December 2026 , The Centrepoint is throwing a Snoopy-themed Christmas event, complete with a bakehouse where you can design your own cupcake plushie, a 3.5m-tall Snoopy, and a meet-and-greet with Snoopy and Charlie Brown themselves.
With the EOY school holidays in full swing, it’s an easy way to keep the kids entertained while you knock out your Christmas shopping. To top it all off, The Centrepoint is even offering a free postcard mailing service for you to spread festive well wishes at no charge, and Christmas carolling to immerse you in holiday vibes.
Customise a Snoopy Cupcake Plushie at the Snoopy Bakehouse
The star of the show is the Snoopy Bakehouse at the Level 1 Atrium , a pop-up where you and your kiddo get to play pastry chefs minus the flour all over your kitchen counter.
Here, you’ll personalise your very own Snoopy Cupcake Plushie with festive touches and pick out a cosy holiday outfit for your pup.
Once you’re done, watch as your creation gets “baked” to life before you take it home.
These plushies aren’t for sale, so you’ll have to earn them. Spend $200 at participating FRx stores at The Centrepoint to redeem 1 Snoopy Cupcake Plushie, or spend $300 to redeem 2. Once you’ve made your qualifying purchase, head to the Level 3 Concierge to collect your Redemption Ticket before making your way to the Snoopy Bakehouse at Level 1 Atrium.
They’re available while stocks last, and the Bakehouse is only around over 2 weekends, so don’t leave it till the last day.
Venue: Level 1 Atrium
Date: 20th-22nd & 27th-29th Nov
Time: 12pm-8pm
Snap photos with a 3.5m-tall Snoopy centrepiece
You don’t need to spend a cent for this one. Standing in the Level 1 Atrium is a 3.5m-tall Snoopy , roughly twice the height of the average adult, so you’ll need to take a few steps back to fit him in frame.
He makes for a solid family photo backdrop, and an equally good excuse to finally update your profile pic just in time for the festive season.
Also at the Level 1 Atrium is a retail zone for all manner of PEANUTS-themed merch, perfect for gifting, or for PEANUTS fans to pick up new pieces for their collection.
From plushies of various sizes to stationery and even pet gear, you’ll have a ball of a time sifting through all the goodies.
Venue: Level 1 Atrium
Date: 16th-29th Nov
Time: 11am to 10pm
Meet Snoopy & Charlie Brown in person
While the kids may have first met Snoopy through plushies and merch collabs, parents and grandparents will remember him from the PEANUTS comic strips and cartoons they grew up with. It makes this meet and greet with Snoopy and his best friend Charlie Brown one of the rare Christmas activities that 3 generations can get equally excited about.
Their mascots will be making appearances on 28th and 29th November , with 3 sessions a day.
Do note that meet and greet slots are limited to the first 50 groups per session, on a first-come, first-served basis.
Venue: Level 1 Atrium
Date: 28th & 29th Nov
Time: 1pm, 4pm & 7pm
Send Snoopy postcards to your loved ones for free
With most of us firing off Christmas greetings over WhatsApp these days, a handwritten card is a nice old-school touch, especially for relatives and friends overseas. Over at The Centrepoint, you can mail out a complimentary Snoopy-themed postcard , available in 2 designs.
Pen your Christmas wishes and The Centrepoint will take care of the postage. Head to the Level 3 Concierge where the staff will affix the stamps for free. Yes, all you have to do is provide the handwritten well wishes, the mall will pay for postage!
Then, simply drop the postcard into the festival mailbox located at the Level 1 Walkway, and it’ll be on its way. Do note that the postcards are available while stocks last, so hurry down to ensure you can get one.
While you’re at the Level 1 Walkway, check out the stunning festive setups and snap a couple of memorable pics with your date, family, or pals.
There’s even a snowglobe setup that you can actually walk into, and pose with Lucy and a jolly snowman.
Venue: Level 3 Concierge to receive, Level 1 Walkway to drop off
Date: 13th Nov-31st Dec
Time: 10am-9.30pm
Catch live Christmas carolling performances
Close out your shopping trip with some live Christmas carolling along the Level 1 Walkway , with 6 evening performances throughout December. It’s a surefire way to immerse yourself in peak Christmas vibes, and feel all warm and fuzzy inside.
Venue: Level 1 Walkway
Date: 5th, 6th, 12th, 13th, 19th & 20th Dec
Time: 7.30pm
Celebrate a Snoopy Christmas at The Centrepoint

HealthHub app
Keeping track of doctor’s appointments is enough of a chore without having to remember which healthcare app to use for which hospital. Thankfully, that’s one less thing to worry about soon. You won’t have to switch between Health Buddy , NHG Health , and NUHS every time you visit a different public hospital or polyclinic.
That’s because all 3 apps are being merged into HealthHub , bringing Singapore’s public healthcare services under one roof, or rather, one app. You can already start using HealthHub, although the other existing apps will gradually shut down by February 2027. Here’s what you need to know about the switch and what to do before the old apps call it quits.
Which healthcare apps are shutting down & when?
Singapore’s public healthcare system is divided into 3 clusters, each with its own app. Depending on which hospital or polyclinic you visit, you might have had to download a different app just to manage your appointments or check your medical records.
Here’s a quick breakdown of the apps that will be discontinued:
• Health Buddy: Used by SingHealth patients visiting institutions like Singapore General Hospital, Changi General Hospital, and KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital.
• NHG Health: Used by patients of Tan Tock Seng Hospital, Khoo Teck Puat Hospital, and other NHG Health institutions.
• NUHS: Used by patients of National University Hospital, Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, and other NUHS institutions.
All 3 apps have now been consolidated into the enhanced HealthHub app. But don’t delete your existing apps just yet; they’ll continue running alongside HealthHub during the transition period before being phased out by February 2027. Once discontinued, the old apps will no longer work.
What should you do before the apps shut down?
If you’ve been using the apps separately, you don’t need to rush to transfer your medical records. Your existing appointments, medical records, and ongoing healthcare services won’t be affected by the switch to HealthHub.
But we’ve put together a step-by-step guide on how to make the transition a smooth one:
• Download HealthHub: Get the app from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store if you haven’t already.
• Log in to your account: Open HealthHub and sign in securely to access your healthcare services.
• Check your medical information: Familiarise yourself with the app by looking up your upcoming appointments, medical records, and other available services.
• Start using HealthHub: Make the switch before the old apps are discontinued, so you have time to figure things out.
And no, you don’t have to manually transfer your medical records from the old apps. HealthHub retrieves your information from the relevant public healthcare systems, so there’s no need to download and re-upload your medical history.
You can also continue using your existing cluster app alongside HealthHub during the transition period, until the old apps are phased out by February 2027. This is super useful, especially if you’re helping your parents to transition to HealthHub.
What can you do on the unified HealthHub app?
Think of HealthHub as your one-stop app for managing your healthcare needs. Developed and operated by national healthtech agency Synapxe under an initiative by the Ministry of Health (MOH), the platform brings together services from NHG Health, NUHS, and SingHealth.
You can book, reschedule, or cancel medical appointments at participating public hospitals and polyclinics, register for appointments, and check your queue number. The app also lets you pay medical bills, keep track of past payments, and access health records such as lab test results, health screenings, and immunisation records.
Image credit: HealthHub
And if you need to top up your regular medication, you can request medication refills or renew repeat prescriptions digitally too. There’s also the option to add your loved ones’ health profiles, making it easier to manage your parents’ medical appointments or your kids’ check-ups.
Plus, there’s also the option to browse healthcare events and activities across the different public healthcare clusters.
Manage your healthcare needs with just one app
With everything moving to HealthHub, keeping track of your medical appointments and records should be a lot less troublesome. If you’re still using Health Buddy, NHG Health, or NUHS, now’s a good time to familiarise yourself with the new app before the old ones shut down in February 2027. That’s more storage space on your phone that you get to save.
We love convenience in our lives, but prevention is often better than cure.

Guide To Health Screenings In SG: Subsidy Eligibility, Recommended Tests & Best Clinics In 2026

body:
New Ang Mo Kio Library at AMK HUB
Bookworms in the North, there’s a new hangout spot in town. Ang Mo Kio Library has officially reopened in its new home on Level 4 of AMK Hub , where Cathay Cineplex once stood.
But this isn’t your typical library. Think towering bookshelves, AR-powered experiences, a 360° immersive screen, and cosy study spots open till 10pm. We went down to check out the revamped space and see what’s in store for visitors.
What are the key features in the new Ang Mo Kio Library?
360 ° immersive screen that brings Ang Mo Kio’s history to life
One of the biggest highlights of the new library is its Immersive Hub , a 6 m -tall structure located near the entrance. Its curved structure is decorated with hundreds of books, with the curvature inspired by Ang Mo Kio’s hilly landscape before the neighbourhood was developed.
Step inside, and you’ll find NLB’s 1st 360 ° curved screen , which showcases interactive digital experiences celebrating Singapore’s history.
Catch The Heart of Ang Mo Kio , a short cinematic film that takes visitors through the neighbourhood’s transformation from a humble kampong to the bustling residential town we know today.
There are also 2 interactive kiosks for Ang Mo Kio Memories Alive , where visitors can select archival photographs of the neighbourhood and watch them come to life using AI technology.
These archival photos include images of Ang Mo Kio’s iconic landmarks, its communities, tokens from the past, as well as Ang Mo Kio town itself. It’s a chance for older residents to revisit familiar sights, and for younger visitors to discover what the area used to look like.
Simply swipe up on the kiosk to display an archival photo on the large 360° screen, where you can explore the nostalgic views.
18 m -long mural with augmented reality features
Just outside the Immersive Hub, you’ll spot an 18 m -long Singapore Collection Mural featuring familiar landmarks from Ang Mo Kio’s past and present.
Keep an eye out for the former Broadway Cinema building and the iconic Clover Block at Block 259 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 2 , both of which are featured in the artwork.
But there’s more to the mural than meets the eye. Using the NLB Mobile app ( App Store | Google Play ), visitors can scan the embedded augmented reality (AR) codes to access curated reading lists and discover books from the library’s Singapore Collection .
It’s a fun way to learn more about Singapore’s heritage while picking up a new read along the way.
Nostalgic decor inspired by Ang Mo Kio’s iconic landmarks
The library’s design is a love letter to Ang Mo Kio, incorporating familiar landmarks and green spaces into its interiors.
For starters, the curved entrance takes inspiration from the neighbourhood’s famous Clover Block , Singapore’s only circular HDB block. The design creates a sweeping view of the library, giving visitors a peek inside before they even enter.
Take a closer look at the books and empty shelves on the floor-to-ceiling shelves – they’ve been deliberately arranged to mimic the hilly landscape of AMK.
The nature-inspired furnishings create a calming atmosphere, making these spaces ideal for visitors looking to catch up on some reading or studying.
Children’s zone inspired by a retro traffic garden
Little ones aren’t left out of the fun either. The library’s Children Zone takes inspiration from the mini Traffic Garden that once stood at Ang Mo Kio Town Centre in the 1980s.
Instead of ordinary bookshelves, children will find vehicle-shaped shelving, road markings on the floor, and playful traffic signs that give the space a miniature road-themed makeover.
It’s a playful setting for young readers to explore books and get acquainted with a little piece of Ang Mo Kio’s history.
Check out 16 retro library artefacts from the past
Before self-checkout machines and digital library cards became the norm, borrowing a book involved quite a bit more paperwork.
At the library’s Collaboration Bridge , visitors can discover 16 historical library artefacts showcasing how Singapore’s libraries have evolved over the years.
These include old borrowing card slots, which were once used to manually record book loans, and date stamps that librarians used to indicate when books were due for return.
You’ll also find vintage spine label stickers, which previously used colour-coding to help librarians organise books. These were eventually phased out in 2012, making way for the modern labels used today. It’s a little throwback for those who remember borrowing books before everything went digital.
7 bookable study nooks & study zones open till 10pm
Students, this one’s for you. The revamped Ang Mo Kio Library has more reading and study spaces than before, including 7 cosy study nooks suitable for group discussions, collaborative projects, and co-working sessions.

summary: Ang Mo Kio Library gets a glow-up with a 360° immersive screen, AR mural, and study spots open till 10pm.

body:
NoMad Singapore, the Orchard Road hotel from the New York brand, has opened reservations for all four of its restaurants and bars, and the first menus are out. The hotel itself is due to open in late 2026, with Hilton yet to name a date.
The four are NoMad Grill and Tropicana Club on level 19, Lù Bar by the pool on level five and Sticky Fingers on the ground floor. The menus mix locally inspired flavours with NoMad classics, from bak kut teh dumplings to a soft-serve take on mango sticky rice. LBRD first looked at NoMad Grill in August , before any menus were out.
Dry-aged rib eye at NoMad Grill. Photo: Hilton
NoMad Grill, the steakhouse on level 19
The flagship is a New York chophouse with in-house dry-ageing and live-fire cooking. The main room seats 65, and a private room takes up to 18 people around one table.
Steaks and chops lead the menu, with a raw bar and a seafood plateau that changes with the season. The local touches are grilled snail toast and fried frog legs with black bean, white pepper and curry leaf. On the seafood side there is wasabi yellowtail crudo, razor clams with escabeche and finger lime, and golden snapper in coconut leche de tigre.
The two big-table dishes are a suckling pig and the return of the NoMad Black Truffle Chicken, both served for two to four people. Dessert is a Baked Alaska, finished at the table.
NoMad Grill runs from breakfast to dinner daily: 6.30am to 10.30am, noon to 3pm and 5.30pm to 10.30pm.
Tropicana Club, cocktails and late nights
The name nods to two clubs: Havana’s Tropicana of 1939 and Singapore’s own Tropicana Club of 1968. This one is a cocktail bar with entertainment, also on level 19.
Cuban classics such as the daiquiri and El Presidente sit next to a long martini list, a pandan vesper and a passion fruit and tomato martini, with no- and low-alcohol versions too. The bar food is where Havana meets Singapore: chilli brown crab empanadas with bottarga aioli, bak kut teh dumplings with shiitake, pork belly and white pepper, and seabream ceviche with calamansi.
It opens 5pm to 1am on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, and 5pm to 2am on Friday and Saturday. It is closed on Monday and Tuesday.
Seabream ceviche at Tropicana Club. Photo: Hilton
Sticky Fingers, the soft-serve counter
The 20-seat ground-floor spot changes three times a day. Mornings are coffee from Singapore roaster PPP, house-made viennoiserie and New York-style breakfast sandwiches. Afternoons are soft-serve sundaes, including a Cacio e Pepe Sundae with pecorino, black pepper and olive oil, and the Sticky Mango, which pairs coconut ice cream with vanilla sticky rice and candied peanut. Evenings bring cocktails such as a pandan and coconut Negroni and a banoffee martini. Hours are 8am to 8pm daily.
The Sticky Mango at Sticky Fingers. Photo: Hilton
Lù Bar, by the pool
Lù Bar seats 35 beside the level-five pool, with drinks and small plates including black pepper crab pockets, prawn fresh rolls and a crispy pork belly bánh mì. It opens 9am to 10pm daily.
Prawn fresh rolls at Lù Bar. Photo: Hilton
Booking
Tables at all four go through the NoMad Singapore dining reservations on Hilton’s site. No prices have been published yet for any of the menus. The cocktail list is the work of Leo Robitschek of Sydell Group, a James Beard Award winner for bar programmes, while the food is led by Josh Harnden, a former Eleven Madison Park partner, with Lorenz Hoja, who spent more than ten years with Joël Robuchon, running the Singapore kitchens.
summary: NoMad Singapore has opened reservations for NoMad Grill, Tropicana Club, Sticky Fingers and Lù Bar ahead of its late-2026 opening on Orchard Road. What is on each menu, and the hours.
title: NoMad Singapore opens bookings for its four Orchard Road venues, from a level-19 steakhouse to a soft-serve bar

body:
Bugis is a food mecca that draws all types of food and people. But sometimes, nothing beats a simple juicy burger. That’s why I can’t wait to sink my teeth into a smashed burger from LOBANG , a hole-in-the-wall joint that serves scintillating burgers at 17 Mohamed Sultan Road .
Their opening came as a surprise, much like their way of serving their burgers .
Credit – Instagram
Notice the shutters? Yeah, even when they’re open, the shutters remain closed. The spot is located in an alley with a tent and some seating for customers to eat. But bear in mind, this is a grab-and-go type of food, so there aren’t many seats.
The entire storefront has a minimalist, yet busy style that a lot of millennials and Gen Z would love. I hate to say this, but this spot is as Instagram-worthy as it gets.
You order by scanning the QR code next to their door. When your order is ready, the shutter will open ever so slightly. A mysterious hand will place your order on the metal table for you to grab. It feels like you’re doing some shady stuff.
Credit – Instagram
The colour palette reminds me heavily of Spider-Punk, one of the many variants of Spider-Man. The music posters are pasted haphazardly, creating a dense layer similar to wallpaper. The neon light buzzes and settles across the pavement. A part of me wishes I had just stumbled onto this place. The mystery and punkish ambience would make for a sick story to tell my friends.
Credit – Instagram
Now, enough about the decor and the vibes. Let’s talk burgers. They offer their normal Smash Burger (S$15) and an upgraded Double Smash Burger (S$18) . Simple and easy but wait till you read what’s in these bad boys.
The burger is made with a blend of beef short rib, brisket and wagyu. The blend of flavour, fat and texture is key to making the ultimate burger.
Credit – Instagram
On top of that, the burger contains caramelised onions and pickles. Those who need some heat (like me) can add their house-made lacto-fermented hot sauce.
A popular pairing with these burgers is a side of their French Fries (S$6) and their Calamansi Soda (S$6) . Personally, if I had to choose between their 4 drink options, I’d definitely go for the Calamansi Soda ; all that rich fat needs some acid to cut through it.
Do note that they only sell 88 burgers daily . While they’re open from 4pm to 12 am , they stop service for the day once they hit that 88-burger quota. I suggest coming earlier so you don’t miss this classic and succulent meal.
You can check if they’re sold out for the day on their Instagram . Also, for my fellow Muslims, all meat used in the burger is Halal-certified.
One Fattened Calf: What makes this burger extraordinary is the homemade potato bun
summary: LOBANG is a takeaway-only smash burger spot in an alley next to 17 Mohamed Sultan Road in Singapore. It sells a Smash Burger at S$15 and a Double Smash Burger at S$18, capped at 88 burgers a day, ordered by QR code and collected from a window hatch. It suits those after a quick burger from Tuesday to Sunday, 4pm to 12am, with limited seating.
title: LOBANG – New hole-in-the-wall spot serves only 88 smash burgers a day

S$4 for 6 pieces; handmade Beef Ramen
Flourful Delight
Made-to-order steaming and meaty filling
Golden Mile Food Centre
S$6 per basket; translucent, sturdy skin
Shan Dong Dong Ji La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Convenient islandwide neighbourhood access
Multiple locations (Syed Alwi, Old Airport Rd, West Coast)
S$6 for 6 pieces; sturdy skins and la mian
Zhang Ji Shanghai La Mian Xiao Long Bao
Clear, savoury broth with balanced skin
Alexandra Village Food Centre
S$6 for 6 pieces; Steamed Mini Buns
1. Taste of Jiang Nan
Tucked away in the ever-popular Maxwell Food Centre , Taste of Jiang Nan often flies under the radar. Helmed by an ex-Din Tai Fung Chef who now serves eastern Chinese cuisine, including his take on Xiao Long Bao , starting from S$5 for 6 pieces.
Each dumpling arrives with meticulous, uniform pleating that signals true technical skill. XLB purists will tell you to poke a hole in the skin to sip the soup first, but I personally prefer popping the entire dumpling into my mouth, so it bursts in a piping hot umami explosion of broth.
The near-translucent skin yields effortlessly, releasing a rush of deeply savoury pork broth that coats your tongue without feeling greasy. The flavour of the broth is so clean that I almost prefer these morsels without the classic julienned ginger and black vinegar, but I’d encourage you to try it with at least one dumpling, as it lends a completely new flavour profile to the dish.
The ginger strands served here are exceptionally fine, immediately reminding me of high-end dim sum restaurants. Most hawkers opt for thicker matchstick cuts since julienning them so finely is much more labour-intensive.
They also make a great Pork Dumpling in Chilli Oil (S$5.50 for 8 pieces) , which has an addictive numbing chilli oil that complements the fatty pork filling well.
Key Highlights: Xiao Long Bao , Pork Dumpling in Chilli Oil
Price Range: S$5 – S$13.50 per pax
1 Kadayanallur Street, Maxwell Food Centre, #01-62, Singapore 069184
+65 8342 9898
Sun to Fri: 11.30am – 8.30pm
Closed on Sat
Facebook
2. XI YING KE 喜迎客 Dumplings & Noodles
Interestingly, this rival stall is also located within Maxwell Food Centre and boasts an array of Chinese comfort food. XI YING KE 喜迎客 Dumplings & Noodles dishes out expertly handcrafted dumplings that are not to be underestimated. At S$5.50 for 7 Xiao Long Bao , it offers an incredible price point for central Singapore.
Despite sharing a roof with the previous entry, the XLB served here differ quite drastically. The filling was flavourful but on the heavier side compared to the previous entry and there was slightly less broth within. The skin was paper-thin and fell apart easily when picked up, with its overall structure remarkably similar to the XLB served at chain restaurants, albeit slightly less polished. The broth leaned quite sweet and burst out when bitten.
…
summary: 10 hawker stalls across Singapore serve handcrafted xiao long bao offering an affordable, GST-free alternative to restaurant chains. Situated in neighbourhoods from Maxwell and Chinatown to Whampoa and Old Airport Road, these spots vary by wrapper thickness, broth richness, and morning-to-night operating hours. The selection is ideal for diners seeking quality soup dumplings for everyday lunches or casual meals.
title: Best hidden hawker xiao long bao stalls in Singapore that rival big restaurant chains

Bandar Utama has a new place to eat, unwind and run everyday errands — The Capitol , a newly opened lifestyle and commercial hub by 1 Utama City Group . It brings together a growing lineup of restaurants, cafes, wellness facilities and essential services under one roof.
Credit – The Capitol
Officially soft-launched on 16 Nov 2026 , the 215m-tall development features two Grade A office towers sitting above a 6-level retail and lifestyle podium. Located next to the BU11 station on the Shah Alam LRT3 line , it is designed to make getting around the neighbourhood convenient.
Credit – The Capitol
Foodies will find plenty to look forward to, with a mix of local favourites and international concepts already joining the tenant lineup. Kiwami Ramen & Japanese Bistro serves Japanese comfort food, while Bakar Thai Bowl offers Thai-inspired bowls.
Those craving Korean fare can check out Dodo Korea , while Se’Indonesia is making its Malaysian debut with Indonesian quick-service dishes.
Credit – The Capitol
There are also familiar names for your coffee and dessert fix, including Bean Brothers , ZUS Signature Coffee , Maru Coffee , Inside Scoop and Kobo Bakery . Other dining options include Fowlboys Diner , Galito’s , India Gate , Old Nanyang Coffee , Pulau Ketam Yong Tau Foo and The Pantry by Bricks & Butter .
For lighter bites and refreshments, Anytime Acai , All About Chew , Ningji , hétam GO and Ikat Tepi B289 add even more variety. With new tenants expected to open in stages, the dining selection should continue to grow.
Credit – The Capitol
Beyond its F&B offerings, The Capitol is also designed around everyday convenience. Visitors can look forward to neighbourhood grocer Qra , Guardian , Common Ground coworking spaces, Cutie Cottage childcare services and PUMP Fitness .
Another major addition is Health Capitol , a dedicated medical hub planned to house more than 120 practitioners across over 20 specialties, bringing healthcare services closer to the surrounding community.
Those who enjoy staying active can also look forward to a recreational floor on Level 16, featuring pickleball and badminton courts. Meanwhile, SkyHall , a 10K sq ft event space, is slated to open in the second quarter of 2027.
While a pedestrian link connecting the BU11 station to the development is part of its transit-oriented design, visitors should check the latest access arrangements before heading over.
For drivers, the development has approximately 3.2K parking bays. Complimentary parking with no minimum spending requirement is also available until 31 Dec 2026 .
Will you be dropping by The Capitol at Bandar Utama soon?
Best food at One Square, Bandar Utama PJ for brunch, coffee & local favourites
summary: Bandar Utama’s newly opened The Capitol brings together a growing mix of restaurants, cafes, wellness facilities and everyday services, from local dining options to international food concepts. Soft-launched on 16 November 2026 beside the BU11 LRT3 station, the hub is useful for nearby residents and office workers, with complimentary parking available until 31 December 2026 and more tenants opening in stages.
title: The Capitol is Bandar Utama’s newest LRT-connected lifestyle destination for restaurants & cafes

Ho ho ho, Merry Christmas! Besides celebrating with good food and great company, don’t forget about the desserts. For some, dessert is non-negotiable, while for others it’s just an afterthought to the main course. To each their own, but I must say, yule regret it if you don’t get these best desserts on this list to add to your festive table.
How I chose these best Christmas desserts
These are the 3 main criteria I used to decide which desserts to recommend:
• Variety : The desserts on this list include more than just the typical yule log cakes.
• Taste & flavour : How delicious the desserts were, and not overly cloying.
• Presentation : I took into account the visual appeal of these treats, because let’s be real, it has to look as good as it tastes, right?
Based on my spiking blood sugar, here are the the most decadent Christmas desserts for 2026 in Singapore .

1. Bob The Baker Boy
Bob the Baker Boy has been baking celebration cakes for over 10 years, with lower-sugar treats that don’t skimp on flavour. This Christmas, its lineup is made for sharing and gifting. Our top pick for the season, we’re sure you’ll love it as much as we do.
The star of the lineup (and what caught my eye first) is the Christmas Brownie Tree (Large from S$69.95, Mini from S$34.95), billed as Singapore’s original, with thousands sold every year. Layers of rich, fudgy brownies are finished with green piping, snowy details and gold decorations. Trust me, it’ll be the first thing guests spot!
Chocolate lovers, meet the Midnight Belgian Chocolate Log Cake (S$69.95). Soft chocolate sponge wraps around a rich 55% Belgian chocolate filling, finished with glossy piping, golden baubles and a pair of little gold reindeer. Yes, it tastes as good as it looks.
Want more variety? Assorted Festive Party Pack (Box of 24 for S$44.95) offers festive bite-sized treats in cheerful Christmas designs. With islandwide delivery from multiple locations, it’s ideal for office parties and bulk or corporate gifting.
On the hunt for a generous gift? The Premium Christmas Cookie Tins Set of 3 (S$66.95) packs in festive flavours like Apple Cinnamon Vanilla, Double Chocolate Chip and Sea Salt 55% Dark Chocolate — your loved ones will certainly appreciate this.

Some cakes are made to be eaten, and others to be remembered. Established in 2000, The Patissier brings together French pâtisserie craftsmanship and Asian-inspired flavours, creating handcrafted cakes that balance tradition with creativity. This Christmas, its festive centrepieces and thoughtful gifts are made for sharing and celebrating.
The showstopper is the Choc Much Christmas (Chocolate Croquembouche, S$194.02 for 40 puffs) , a playful take on the French classic. These delicate choux puffs are dipped in dark or white chocolate and stuffed with the same chocolate mousse. They’re then topped with miniature brownie gifts and festive trinkets — get your cameras out!

It is useful for anyone planning a festive dessert spread, looking for alternative Christmas sweets or choosing gifts for the season.

Starbucks Singapore is adding to its festive line-up with the Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box, a first for the chain here. The blind box goes on sale from 23 November, alongside plush keychains, a free reusable cup with a minimum spend and the final run of the Pompompurin collection, as the brand celebrates 30 Years of Shared Moments.
Starbucks Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box designs. Image: Starbucks Singapore
Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box
Each Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box comes with an authentication card and holds one of five festive designs: Snow Globe, Reindeer, Retro Ski, Snow Bunny, and an elusive Ultra Rare Mystery edition. It is available from 23 November at selected Starbucks stores, on the Starbucks Online Store at 10am, and on LazMall at 12pm, while stocks last.
Holiday Bearista Cold Cup Surprise Blind Box banner. Image: Starbucks Singapore
More festive finds to unwrap
For Secret Santa swaps and stocking stuffers, two Mini Holiday Cup Plush Keychain designs are on offer. They can hang off a bag or double as Christmas tree ornaments, and cost S$9.90 each, exclusively in-store while stocks last.
Holiday Bearista blind box available from 23 November. Image: Starbucks Singapore
Mini Holiday Cup Plush Keychains. Image: Starbucks Singapore
Christmas drinks, treats and a free cup
The Christmas menu continues with the Toffee Nut Crunch Latte and Peppermint Mocha, plus seasonal bakes including the S’mores Cookie, Peppermint Chocolate Cake and Caramel Apple Cheesecake. Customers can also redeem a complimentary Christmas Reusable Cup with a minimum S$15 nett spend in-store, while stocks last.
Starbucks Rewards members earn Stars with every purchase, with exclusive treats and seasonal rewards through the year. Sign-up is free.
Free Christmas Special Edition Reusable Cup with S$15 nett spend. Image: Starbucks Singapore
Pompompurin + Starbucks: still available
The limited-edition, Singapore-exclusive Pompompurin + Starbucks collection is now in stores, on the Starbucks Online Store at 10am and on LazMall at 12pm. Purchase is limited to six pieces per item per customer. The Pompompurin + Starbucks Phone Lanyard with Charms Blind Bag costs S$11.90 with any purchase, in-store and online.
Our take
Blind boxes are hard to resist for collectors, so expect the Ultra Rare Mystery edition to get plenty of attention on 23 November. If you are still planning your Starbucks Christmas runs, read our guide to the Starbucks Bearista Christmas offers at CapitaLand malls , and see how to stack savings with the Plaza Singapura eCapitaVoucher . For more festive plans, check out Christmas Wonderland 2026 at Gardens by the Bay .
Information is based on a media alert from Starbucks Singapore. Availability is while stocks last and may vary by store.

body:
Carousel at Royal Plaza on Scotts started its Christmas buffet on Saturday, and it runs every day until New Year’s Day. Lunch starts at S$92++ a head and dinner at S$118++. Every kitchen in the hotel, Carousel’s open stations included, is halal-certified by MUIS, so the turkey, the roasts and the log cakes are all halal.
This year’s theme is Once Upon A Feast, a storybook Christmas. The festive additions sit on top of the usual Carousel spread: turkey, a log cake, Christmas pudding and stollen, plus a heavier hand with lobster after dark.
Once Upon A Feast, Carousel’s festive buffet, 21 November 2026 to 1 January 2027. Image: Royal Plaza on Scotts
Lunch or dinner: where the money goes
Both sessions share the same base. There is a seafood station with whole Atlantic salmon, blue swimmer crab, mussels, clams, half-shell scallops, tiger prawns and lobster claws. There is a live carving station with a slow-baked Christmas turkey in giblet sauce and BBQ beef striploin, plus teppanyaki, sushi and sashimi, a pasta station and a run of Indian dishes.
Dinner adds the expensive items. Hyogo Bay oysters, boiled Maine lobster and Snow Queen crab legs go on ice, and on weekends the crab legs also come hot and steamed. The dinner specials are a chilli crab chawanmushi, Japanese garlic butter baby lobster, and yuzu miso barramundi with a curry leaf furikake, and the dinner crab section includes tom yum chilli crab with golden mantou.
If the point of the evening is seafood, dinner is the session to book. If the group is mostly there for turkey, roast beef and dessert, lunch covers the same ground for less.
Seafood on ice at the Carousel buffet. Photo: Royal Plaza on Scotts
The festive rates
Prices are per adult and before service charge and GST.
• Monday to Thursday: lunch S$92++, dinner S$118++
• Friday: lunch S$92++, dinner S$128++
• Saturday: lunch S$102++, dinner S$128++
• Sunday: lunch S$102++, dinner S$118++
Carousel counts Sunday dinner as a weekday dinner, so Sunday night is priced like Monday.
The four special dates have their own rates, which replace the usual ones:
• Christmas Eve, Thursday 24 December: lunch S$92++, dinner S$168++
• Christmas Day, Friday 25 December: lunch and dinner both S$138++
• New Year’s Eve, Thursday 31 December: lunch S$92++, dinner S$168++
• New Year’s Day, Friday 1 January: lunch S$98++, dinner S$128++
Children aged 6 to 11 pay half the adult rate, and children under 6 eat free. Tables of 21 or more get 15 per cent off the buffet, except on public holidays or with other offers.
What changes on the big nights
The special dates bring extra dishes on top of the regular spread. On Christmas Eve dinner there is aburi Maine lobster with mentaiko, slipper lobster in a heritage curry with butter croutons, and Carousel’s signature laksa-spiced turkey, stuffed with otah and chestnut. Slow-baked prime ribs come with a truffle lobster risotto.
On New Year’s Eve dinner the headline is Maine lobster braised in Singapore chilli crab sauce, with golden mantou to mop it up. Christmas Day lunch has a golden tempura live station.
The special-date logs are a Chocolat Mochi Log with Valrhona dark chocolate and gula melaka mochi, a Nonya Emerald Yule Log with calamansi confit and caramel miso, and a burnt cheese log.
Taking it home instead
Royal Plaza on Scotts also does a festive takeaway range: whole roast turkey, beef sirloin, lamb, seafood, Nonya roast chicken, hampers and log cakes. Orders go through the hotel’s online shop, with delivery or self-collection from 21 November. Delivery is free on orders of S$120 or more after discounts, and orders of S$1,000 or more before discount take 15 per cent off with the code FESTIVE until 25 December. There is no delivery on 24 and 25 December, only self-collection.
Roasts from the Grand Carvery Hamper in the hotel’s festive takeaway range. Photo: Royal Plaza on Scotts
Getting there
Carousel is at Royal Plaza on Scotts, 25 Scotts Road, Singapore 228220. Bookings go through the hotel’s website, and the hotel’s number is 6589 7799. The hotel says its halal certification is under MUIS’s Eating Establishment Scheme (Food Station), under which alcoholic drinks can still be served with strict controls in place.
summary: Carousel at Royal Plaza on Scotts serves its Once Upon A Feast halal Christmas buffet daily from 21 November to 1 January. Rates by day, what dinner adds, and the special-date menus.
title: Carousel’s halal Christmas buffet runs to 1 January, from S$92++ at lunch and S$118++ at dinner

Love all things Japanese ? Japanese culture, food and entertainment are coming together at SJ60 MUSUBI Singapore-Japan Festival 2026 . This 2-day festival celebrates 60 years of diplomatic relations between our red dot and Japan. It’ll take place on 28 and 29 Nov 2026 at Marina Bay Sands , Hall D & E , 10am – 8pm daily .
Credit – SJ60 MUSUBI Singapore-Japan Festival
1-Day passes for the festival cost S$4 for children aged 4 to 12 years and S$8 for visitors aged 13 and above . If you’d like to attend both days, get the 2-Day pass at S$6 for children aged 4 to 12 years and S$12 for visitors aged 13 and above .
Credit – SJ60 MUSUBI Singapore-Japan Festival
You can expect plenty of booths, meet-and-greets, performances, cultural activities, technology showcases, and so much more. This festival is bustling and action-packed, so I’ll mention my personal highlights and can’t-miss events. To learn more about their lively performance schedule, you can refer here .
More information about the various booths across themes such as sightseeing, technology, culture, food & beverage (F&B), and the connect hub is available here .
Credit – Toho Co., Ltd.
In my opinion, one of the biggest draws of this festival is the entertainment line-up. Fans of Godzilla should make a beeline for the stage, as there’ll be special appearances from Godzilla on 28 Nov 2026 , and its cuter counterpart, Chibi Godzilla , on 29 Nov 2026 . Be sure to snap a photo with them for memories!
Besides the meet-and-greet, there’ll also be a Godzilla booth with original TOHO Entertainment Asia merchandise related to the latest film, Godzilla Minus Zero, and Chibi Godzilla and more photo opportunities.
Credit – Tsuburaya Productions
Singapore and Japan aren’t the only ones celebrating 60 years; Ultraman is also marking its 60-year milestone. To celebrate this occasion, the ULTRA HEROES will be having a special stage on 29 Nov 2026 . As with Godzilla, there’ll be a dedicated booth featuring all things ULTRAMAN.
If you’ve been to Kumamoto Prefecture in Japan, chances are that you’ll recognise a familiar face on day 2 — Kumamon . Don’t miss out on his captivating dance moves; you can even join in.
Beyond the adorable mascots and characters you can catch, there’s plenty more available at the festival. Jet-setters should head to the sightseeing booths to explore travel destinations such as Hokkaido and Okinawa. Those who love technology can check out the showcases by companies such as Kikkoman and Fujitsu Limited.
There will also be plenty of food options to explore; participating names include Yoshinoya, Ginkakuji Onishi and TACORUSH. Don’t miss the entertaining live Maguro (tuna) cutting show on 29 Nov 2026 at the Sakura Stage.
Book your tickets HERE
17 affordable Japanese food in Singapore that will make you go Oishii!
summary: SJ60 MUSUBI Singapore-Japan Festival 2026 takes place on 28 and 29 Nov at Marina Bay Sands, featuring Japanese food, cultural activities, technology showcases and character meet-and-greets. With 1-day passes from S$4 and 2-day passes from S$6, it is useful for families and Japanese culture enthusiasts looking to explore performances by GODZILLA, ULTRAMAN and Kumamon, alongside food booths and live demonstrations.
title: Meet Godzilla, Ultraman, Kumamon & more at SJ60 MUSUBI festival

NEX is the largest mall in Singapore’s North-East as well as one of the largest in the country. ‘NEX’ is the acronym for North-East Exchange, as it is the nex-us (haha) between Serangoon Bus Interchange and the Serangoon MRT Station, which links the North-East Line to the Circle Line.
Credit – Google
Over its 7 floors, there are 2 food courts and no less than 66 restaurants, cafes and fast-food outlets. How does one navigate the sea of choices? With this list at the helm, of course!

1. Gokoku Japanese Bakery (#B1-K1)
Gokoku Japanese Bakery is one of Singapore’s most popular Japanese bakeries. Their NEX outlet offers shoppers a wide variety of delicious bakes, ranging from buns to scones to cream horns.
The Kokutou x Kokutou Pan (S$2.30) is a crowd favourite, while the Komeko Pan (S$2.40) is a super hearty and fragrant bun to munch on if you’re health-conscious.
If you have a sweet tooth, go for buns like Apple Earl Grey (S$3) , the Kouign-Amann (S$2.60) or the Crispy Choco Pafu (S$2.60) . My personal favourite is the Kouign-Amann (S$2.40) , a super fragrant scone made with Earl Grey tea.
Of course, don’t miss out on the delicious salt buns— grab a regular Shio Butter Pan (S$2) to curb your buttery cravings, or opt for the An Shio Butter Pan (S$2.40) or Rennyu Shio Butter Pan (S$2.30) for a little something extra.
Signature highlights: Kokutou x Kokutou Pan , Koucha Scone , Shio Butter Pan
Price range: S$2 – S$3 per pax
+65 6634 0049
Daily: 10 am -10 pmm
Website
2. Tim Hortons (#01-10)
Canadian brand Tim Hortons made waves when it opened its first outlet in Singapore within VivoCity back in late 2023. Today, you can find this coffee shop within NEX, sans the crowd, allowing you to enjoy its drinks and bakes without crazy waiting times.
Grab a Signature Latte to go, with options such as Maple Cinnamon (from S$7) and Belgian Chocolate Mocha (from S$7) . Alternatively, indulge in non-coffee classics like the Iced Salted Caramel (from S$7) .
Credit – Tim Hortons
Why not spoil yourself with a sweet treat? At Tim Hortons, you’ll get to try various doughnut flavours like Maple Salted Caramel (S$3.50) , Caramel Biscoff (S$3.50) and Yuzu Lemon Cream (S$4.50) . Perhaps doughnuts aren’t your thing— not to worry, for you can easily find other desserts such as Apple Chestnut Mont Blanc Cake(S$8.50) and Mango Passionfruit Tart (S$6) .
Signature highlights: Maple Cinnamon latte, Maple Salted Caramel doughnut, Apple Chestnut Mont Blanc Cake
Price range: S$3.50 – S$8.50 per pax
Daily: 10 am – 10pm
Facebook | Instagram | Website
3. Monster Curry (#B1-08)
Credit – Google
Monster Curry is an iconic brand that has been operating for over 10 years. Their delicious Japanese demi-glace curry is made from no less than 14 different vegetables and spices and prepared over 2 days. The result is a delectably fragrant curry, rich in taste and bursting with flavour. They earn their ‘monster’ name by presenting meals in 2 huge plate sizes: 35cm and 41cm .
If you are in a group of up to 3, it’s hard to pass on the Monster Combo Curry (S$31.90) , which comes with pork cutlet, fried fish, sliced pork belly, fried battered shrimp and flame-torched cheese. Prefer seafood? The Sea Monster Curry (S$31.90) with fried fish, fried oyster, fried battered shrimp and fried breaded shrimp will definitely be up your alley.
Dishes are available in 5 different levels of spiciness. Only go for the ‘ Monster Spicy ’ one if you have a fire extinguisher handy.
Signature highlights: Monster Combo Curry , Sea Monster Curry
Price range: S$20 – S$31.90 per pax
+65 6634 2168
Daily: 11am – 10pm
Facebook | Instagram | Website
4. Idaten Udon (#B1-02)
Credit Google
Idaten Udon bills itself as the udon speciality concept restaurant where diners become the head chef. It’s an allusion to their approach of letting you choose each element of your dish as you create your meal at the self-serve stations.
…
summary: NEX, the mall linking Serangoon Bus Interchange and Serangoon MRT Station, has a food line-up spanning Japanese bakeries, ramen, udon and hotpot, alongside Thai chicken rice, Chinese burgers and Canadian coffee. Prices run from about S$2 for a bakery bun to over S$60 for a hotpot platter, across basement and upper-floor outlets. Best suited for shoppers choosing between quick snacks and sit-down meals.
title: 11 best places to eat at NEX mall from ramen to hotpot (Nov 2026 update)

In the beating heart of Chinatown stands REXKL , a living, breathing time capsule where Kuala Lumpur ’s past and present mingle over coffee, burgers, noodles, and the occasional waft of ink and printed pages.
Credit
Once a grand cinema, this cultural icon has traded its silver screens for espresso machines, indie bookshops , and vintage treasures that feel plucked straight out of a dream. REXKL has a way of pulling you in; before you know it, hours have passed between bites, sips, and spontaneous discoveries.
So if you ever find yourself wandering through the old streets of Chinatown, here are 9 spots at REXKL worth getting lost in — from cult-favourite eats to other gems you’ll want to gatekeep (but probably won’t).
Name
Key highlight
Decker’s
Angus beef burgers and creative soft-serve flavours
Phil’s Pizza
New York-style pizza by the slice, including truffle mushroom and pepperoni
Summation Cafe
Alcohol-free canelés and matcha drinks
Berrygood
Organically grown strawberries, frozen yoghurt and daifuku
KANTIN
Sarawak laksa, bamboo-cooked meat and Borneo-inspired dishes (temporarily closed)
Stellar Coffee
Single-origin espresso and pour-over brews
Raijin Ramen
Hakata-style tonkotsu broth and black garlic ramen
BookXCess
6,000-square-foot bookshop with a maze-like layout
KANOE
Limited-run clothing featuring regional batik and local artisan craftsmanship
Food & beverage
1. Decker’s
Formerly known as Triple Decker , Decker’s at REXKL has earned its stripes as one of the city’s top spots for smash burgers . The rebrand came with a refreshed space and a tight, confident menu focused on what they do best — juicy, flavour-packed burgers priced between RM20 and RM60 .
The Decker’s Original Burger is a solid starting point. Stacked with Angus beef patties, melted cheddar, caramelised onions, and the signature House sauce, it hits all the right notes of savoury comfort.
If you’re after something with more personality, the Sichuan Chilli Crisp Burger brings subtle heat and crunch with crispy shallots and that addictive chilli oil fragrance. It’s not overly spicy, just enough to cut through the beef’s richness.
For non-beef lovers, the Crispy Chicken Tenders come in Original and Spicy versions — both are crisp on the outside, tender inside, and made for dipping. Add RM5 for fries and a drink , and make it count with the KL Ginger Ale , a refreshing house brew that perfectly balances out the meal.
To end on a sweet note, Decker’s has teamed up with Sōfte for soft-serve ice cream in creative flavours like Butter Pecan , Calamansi Asam Boi , and even French Fries .
+6012 893 6392
Tue to Sun: 12pm – 9pm
Closed on Mon
Instagram
2. Phil’s Pizza
If your love language is pizza by the slice and wings on the side, Phil’s Pizza at REXKL might just be your next go-to. What started as a humble pizza counter has become one of the city’s most beloved spots for that perfectly foldable New York–style slice.
Their Truffle Mushroom (RM75 for 12’’) is the crowd favourite, and rightfully so. Each slice oozes with earthy truffle aroma and gooey cheese, perfectly balanced on a thin, crisp crust. If you prefer something classic, the Pepperoni (RM69 for 12’’) never fails — salty, chewy, and loaded with just enough pepperoni to make every bite satisfying.
For smaller appetites, their single slices are a smart move. The Slice Truffle (RM15.50) remains the bestseller, while the Slice Hot Wings (RM13.50) adds a kick with local Linggam hot sauce, spicy and sweet in equal measure. The Slice Meat La Pinyo (RM14) features minced beef and in-house pickled chilli, a bolder take on bolognese-on-pizza.
Pair it with a Soda (RM12.50) or one of their Cookies (RM10) , baked with 60% milk chocolate, and you’ve got yourself a meal!
+6010 909 3208
Daily: 11am – 10pm
Instagram
3. Summation Cafe
One of my favourite discoveries this year has to be Summation Cafe in Serdang — but if you’re not keen on long drives or traffic jams, their kiosk at REXKL brings the same charm.
Summation may be small, but its menu feels thoughtfully curated. Expect a comforting lineup of hot dishes, pastries, and crafted beverages that lean on quality rather than quantity. Still, the real showstoppers here are their alcohol-free canelés and matcha creations .
The Orange Nutmeg Canelé (RM8) is pure elegance in pastry form. Infused with the zest of fresh oranges and a strong whisper of nutmeg, it’s caramelised on the outside yet custardy inside.
If you prefer something cosier, the Apple Cinnamon Canelé (RM9.50) is a warm hug in dessert form. Filled to the brim with soft apple chunks slow-cooked in cinnamon and sugar, it’s the kind of treat that pairs beautifully with an afternoon chat or a slow Sunday read.
To drink, the Matcha Strawberry Latte (Iced) (RM16) is as pretty as it is refreshing. The combination of earthy Japanese matcha and housemade strawberry puree creates that perfect sweet-tart balance. For something simpler, the Matcha Latte (RM15) keeps it classic.
+6016 291 9917
…
summary: REXKL in Chinatown, Kuala Lumpur, brings together food, coffee, shopping and cultural experiences within a restored former cinema. The nine featured spots range from smash burgers, New York-style pizza and Hakata ramen to speciality coffee, independent bookshops and local batik fashion, with food and drinks at various price points. It is a useful stop for visitors seeking a mix of dining and independent retail under one roof.
title: 9 spots to check out at REXKL — Chinatown’s lepak hub for food, books & vintage finds

body:
I’m new to cafe hopping. I honestly never understood the appeal and felt that all cafes look the same, smell the same, and taste the same. To a certain extent, I was right — many cafes are guilty of sporting macabre brown tables reeking of burnt coffee. That is, until I went to Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant at Marina Square . This cafe is a breath of fresh air, literally (you’ll see why shortly).
Look at how vibrant this place is. The randomly coloured chair cushions, intricate chandeliers, turquoise tiles framing the kitchen window and, of course, the lovely carpet and its light pastel tones. It felt like I’d walked into a Turkish home. This decor feels like it was designed with both intention and whimsy. Also, the room had a subtle fragrance of bright herbs and flowers. The light gave off warmth without feeling overly intense. All in all, this place has a charming personality, and the view definitely adds to it.
I mean, do I really need to say anything? Playful clouds danced across the sky over an unobstructed view of Singapore’s most beautiful building, Marina Bay Sands . In the same breath, you could also mention the construction surrounding the area and even the docks further in the background. Maybe I’m looking too deeply into this, but I feel like this view encapsulated both the beauty and the constant busyness of Singapore. Also, the air was so crisp that day that I felt like I was floating.
What to order at Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant
The cafe was so comfy that I was starting to doze off, and decided to rectify that with a Sweet Turkish Coffee (S$6) and a Turkish Tea (S$2) . Don’t worry, I didn’t have both of these drinks myself and had brought along 2 friends to share the experience.
Firstly, the Turkish Coffee . It was not at all what I expected. I figured it would have that classic roast flavour with a slight sweetness. It did not. It was intense in its fruitiness. Each sip was surprisingly easy. I normally flinch at the first bitter note, but it came and passed. A delightful experience overall.
The Turkish Tea is also similar. It had a floral medley that cleansed the palate. The flavour was intense but didn’t overstay its welcome. Overall, both drinks were unique and like nothing I’d ever tried before.
Now, onto the mains. I figured the Chicken Shish Kebab (S$22.50) was a good choice, seeing as it had a lot of different components on one plate. To be honest, this dish was a mixed bag for me. There were a few items on this dish that were disappointing. I will start with the parts I enjoyed the least.
Summer Folk Cafe & Steakhouse: Halal spot with Da Ji Pai-style calamari & platters galore
My biggest problem with this dish is the bulgur pilaf , which acts as a whole-grain replacement for rice. It has a base of tomato paste, red pepper paste, mint and other aromatics. When I first took a bite, I was shocked by the texture of the pilaf . The grain was so soft and mushy that I found it quite off-putting.
The flavour didn’t help much either. It tasted like unripe, out-of-season tomatoes, and that was the most prominent flavour. My suggestion is that they cook the pilaf for a shorter amount of time and be more generous with the seasoning.
The salad, while definitely an improvement, still lacked seasoning. I could taste a slight char over the vegetal sweetness of the salad. However, it was still quite bland. I feel a little more salt and pepper would make this salad perfect.
Now onto what I loved on this plate. The red cabbage and onion salad paired perfectly with the chicken kebabs. The onion had a tartness, bitterness and crispness that I enjoyed a lot. The red cabbage brought a sweet crunch, creating a balance of sweet, salty, sour and savoury when paired with the chicken. I found myself repeatedly going back to them.
And to the best part of the dish, the chicken shish kebab. Traditionally, shish kebab is marinated heavily in olive oil and lemon juice, then coated in herbs and spices. With this specific kebab , the spices gave the chicken an earthy, rich flavour throughout every bite.
The flames give the chicken a lovely char that caramelises some of the sugars in the spice mix. Despite the char, however, the chicken remains juicy, which is a feat unto itself as white meat famously dries out very easily. The chicken was so good, it almost redeemed the whole dish.
To end the meal, we had the Baklava (S$9.80) . I’m not going to beat around the bush; it was a perfect bite of Baklava. The filo pastry was thin and stacked on top of each other, nice and uniform. This makes each bite very satisfying as your teeth sink in and split each layer. The syrup was soaked into the pistachio filling and pastry, giving the treat its sweet floral notes. A perfect treat to end the day.
Who is Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant best for?
…
summary: Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant at Marina Square offers Turkish decor, a Marina Bay Sands view and dishes such as Turkish coffee, chicken shish kebab and baklava, priced from S$2 to S$22.50. The kebab’s chicken was juicy, though the bulgur pilaf and salad lacked seasoning. It suits friends looking for a comfortable cafe stop with a skyline view.
title: Sofra Turkish Cafe & Restaurant: Stunning MBS views with juicy kebabs & fruity Turkish coffee

Sweet Stuff is a chiffon cake bakery in Toa Payoh
Image credit: Don Leow via Facebook
Most of us grew up eating chiffon cake, and its soft, fluffy texture is hard to resist. Chances are, though, you’ve probably only tried the pandan flavour . Sweet Stuff , an old-school bakery in Toa Payoh, is here to change that.
27 Traditional Bakeries In Singapore For Old-School Apple Crumble, $0.70 Muffins And More
Image credit: @sweetstuff.toapayoh
Founded in 2007 by two sisters, Sweet Stuff specialises in chiffon cakes. At the time of writing, they offer 37 unique flavours, from familiar classics such as Pandan ($5.50) and Gula Melaka ($5.50) to more experimental ones including Oreo Cheese (from $6.50) and Mint Chocolate (from $6.50) .
Do note that only the Pandan flavour and two to three other rotating flavours are available for walk-in purchase every day. If you would like a specific flavour, you can reserve it in advance via WhatsApp.
Image credit: ZY Ng via Google Maps
Their most unique, and potentially most polarising flavour is the Coriander Chiffon Cake (from $6.50) , made from fresh coriander stalks. If you’re a coriander lover like me, you’ll be pleased to find specks of the herb throughout the cake, along with a strong, aromatic coriander fragrance. The cake itself is said to be soft, fluffy, and savoury, best enjoyed toasted with a slab of butter or dipped into a hearty bowl of soup.
Image credit: @sweetstuff.toapayoh
If you have a sweet tooth, their newest flavour is worth a try: the Pistachio Chocolate Chiffon Cake ($10) features the same spongy chiffon cake, spotted with chunks of chocolate and pistachio paste for that iconic Dubai chocolate experience. Pair it with a cup of hot chocolate or Milo for a comforting treat.
Image credit: @sweetstuff.toapayoh
Chiffon cake isn’t all they do, though. They also offer traditional bakes that are just as loved by regulars. Their handmade Ang Ku Kueh (price TBD) is highly popular, generously stuffed with peanut or sweet bean filling and wrapped in a stretchy, QQ kueh layer. The Kueh Ubi Kayu (price TBD) , AKA tapioca kueh, is also a fan favourite, said to be made fresh daily for a soft texture that almost melts in your mouth.
Sweet Stuff is located in Toa Payoh Block 212 , a 14-minute walk away from Braddell MRT Station .
If you’re looking to support more local businesses, check out Herng Hao Chi Hokkien Mee , a Hokkien mee hawker stall next door run by a 28-year-old NUS graduate. Otherwise, our guide to the best bakeries in Singapore can help you uncover more old-school bakeries alongside new, contemporary ones.
Address: 212 Lorong 8 Toa Payoh, Singapore 310212
Opening hours: Daily 8:30am to 7pm
Website
Sweet Stuff is not halal-certified.
