World Christmas Market returns from 10 December 2026
Image credit: World Christmas Market
PSA: The Christmas market that drew more than 218,000 people to Marina Bay last year is moving house. World Christmas Market is back for a third edition, now called A Christmas Story by World Christmas Market . It runs from 10 December 2026 to 3 January 2027 on the grounds of METT Hotel Singapore and Fort Canning Park . Even better, entry is free for everyone.
We Visited World Christmas Market 2025, A Festive Fair At Bayfront With Over 40 Stalls
The fair started in 2024 at The Promontory at Marina Bay. In 2025, it moved to the much bigger Bayfront Event Space as Togetherland by World Christmas Market .
We went last year and counted over 40 food and drink stalls, from Rollney’s ice cream-stuffed chimney cakes to chilled and grilled oysters at Slurp Your Oysters.
Image credit: World Christmas Market
This year the organisers, DareDreamer, are swapping the waterfront for something greener and more old-school, with the fair spread across the hilltop park and the grounds of the colonial-era hotel.
The fair is split into three zones. The first, The Story Terrace, has festive shopping, gifts, and hands-on workshops. It’s also home to The Long Table, a communal dining setup where you can share a meal with friends or end up chatting with strangers.
Image credit: World Christmas Market
Next is The Piazza, the main square. A 38-foot real Christmas tree stands in the middle, with smaller decorated trees all around it. The third zone, The Merry Grounds, is where the food is. Expect seasonal bites, festive drinks, and plenty of reasons to stick around. If you’re mainly going to eat, start here. The full vendor lineup is still TBD, since the festival is still taking applications from F&B, retail, and craft vendors. We’ll update this article once the stalls are confirmed.
Across the grounds, look out for giant nutcrackers and glowing reindeer, which make good photo backdrops. There’s plenty of music too. A 42-piece orchestra plays on opening weekend. Brass sextets, saxophone quartets, and choirs perform on other dates throughout the season.
Image credit: World Christmas Market
On opening night, 10 December 2026, the gates open at 5pm. The tree-lighting and opening ceremony starts at 7.30pm, so arrive early for a good spot. The fair also stays open until 1am on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve, so it works for a late-night date or a countdown with friends.
In other exciting food news, McDonald’s is launching new Maple BBQ Burgers for a limited time! If you’re watching your spending this month, check out our 12-hour Orchard budget itinerary .
Address: 11 Canning Walk, METT Hotel Singapore, Singapore 178881
Opening hours: Mon-Thurs 5pm to 11pm, Fri-Sun 4pm to 11pm (10 December 2026 to 3 January 2027); 24 and 31 December 4pm to 1am
Website
Orchard On A Budget: How To Spend A Day In Town For Under $30
Feature image adapted from World Christmas Market.
summary: World Christmas Market is back from 10 December 2026 to 3 January 2027 on the grounds of METT Hotel Singapore and Fort Canning Park!

Sushiro says on its Instagram that its Great World outlet opens on Tuesday 24 November, with a rotating 1-for-1 sushi plate and S$6++ alcoholic drinks from then until 7 December. Great World lists the promotion as available while stocks last.
An artist’s impression of Sushiro Great World. Image: Sushiro Singapore
The new restaurant sits on the first floor of Great World at 1 Kim Seng Promenade, units #01-112/113/114. It is a Digiro concept store, the second in Singapore after Mandai, so the conveyor belt here is a screen rather than a moving track of plates.
The 1-for-1 plate, date by date
Each 1-for-1 runs for two or three days before the next plate takes over. Sushiro lists this run on its Instagram, with the opening price and the usual price for each plate:
• 24 to 26 November: Bluefin Fatty Tuna, S$5.20++ (usually S$10.40++)
• 27 to 28 November: Big Cut Fresh Tasmanian Salmon, S$3.20++ (usually S$6.40++)
• 29 to 30 November: Salmon Roe Wrap, S$4.20++ (usually S$8.40++)
• 1 to 3 December: Shio Koji Big Red Shrimp, S$3.20++ (usually S$6.40++)
• 4 to 5 December: Medium Fatty Tuna, S$4.20++ (usually S$8.40++)
• 6 to 7 December: Jumbo Scallop, S$5.20++ (usually S$10.40++)
The bluefin fatty tuna in the first three days and the jumbo scallop at the very end are the two dearest plates in the run, so those are the dates to aim for if you are choosing one visit. If salmon is what you order every time anyway, 27 or 28 November is the cheaper trip.
Sushiro says alcoholic drinks are S$6++ each for the full two weeks.
Fatty tuna nigiri. Image: Sushiro Singapore
Opening day only
On 24 November itself, Sushiro says a bill of S$50 or more earns one spin of a sure-win prize wheel, with prizes ranging from S$10 return vouchers to limited-edition merchandise. Terms and conditions apply.
How Digiro works
Instead of plates going round on a belt, a touchscreen panel at the table shows animated sushi plates moving across a digital conveyor. You tap a plate to order it, and the same screen doubles as the menu. Ordering also fills up a progress bar that unlocks mini games featuring Sushiro’s Dakkosushi characters, with a chance to win Dakkosushi merchandise.
If you have been to the Mandai outlet at Mandai Wildlife East, it is the same idea. If you like watching real plates go past before you commit, the screens are the trade-off.
Tuna, ikura, unagi and salmon from Sushiro’s regular menu. Photo: Sushiro Singapore
Getting a seat
Reservations go through the Sushiro Singapore app. With a 1-for-1 on from the first day, booking ahead for a weekend dinner is the sensible move.
Great World is also not the last new Sushiro this year. Funan, also a Digiro concept store, is slated for early December at #02-16.
Sushiro Great World details
Address: 1 Kim Seng Promenade, #01-112/113/114, Great World, Singapore 237994
Hours: 11am to 10pm daily, last order 9.30pm
Opening deals: 24 November to 7 December 2026, while stocks last
Prices: before service charge and GST
Reservations: Sushiro Singapore app
summary: Sushiro says its Great World Digiro outlet opens on 24 November, with a 1-for-1 plate that changes every two or three days to 7 December and S$6++ alcoholic drinks.

Wok-kissed, sweet and sinfully good — these are some non-negotiables for a solid plate of char kway teow in my books.
While it isn’t exactly difficult to find a rendition in Singapore that ticks off all these boxes, I (almost desperately) needed to know if Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow would. Why? Well, when a stall finds itself perched at the apex of *multiple* best-of lists, it’s bound to run circles in my mind.
The highly raved stall in question resides in the otherwise nondescript Havelock Road Cooked Food Centre , and very prominently so. An incredible smoky aroma wafted from the stall, so heavenly I practically turned into a heart-eyed cartoon character levitating my way towards it. Consider that one box checked?
Now, for a little history: Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow has been frying up plates of the delicious noodle dish for over 4 decades. At its helm today is the daughter of the original hawker who, according to some, might even have better gong fu than her father.
You bet my expectations were sky-high. I’d recently had a plate of char kway teow that left me so awed I went speechless (hint: it’s from an eponymous stall in the Central North). I was hoping to be floored like that .
What I tried at Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow
Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow serves its glorious titular dish in S$4 and S$5 portions, with the option to add Extra Egg (S$1) , Sausage (S$1) and Cockles (S$2) .
Frankly, I couldn’t help but raise an eyebrow when I received my S$5 order. So… this is the larger portion? But I wasn’t about to complain at that price point — especially since the glistening plate of grub smelled nothing short of incredible.
The plate contained a good mix of noodles and kway teow , so well-fried I swear I could see subtle char marks on their glossy surfaces. And oh, yum. One bite in and I was greeted by that divine wok hei fragrance, layered over the sweetness I so love in char kway teow .
However, as I worked my way through the plate, the dish’s richness began to taper off. While undeniably tasty, it lacked that sticky, sinful decadence that usually makes me weak at the knees. Great news for those who prefer their indulgence a little more understated, though!
Char Kway Teow Showdown: Outram Park Fried Kway Teow Mee vs Hill Street Fried Kway Teow
Dotted throughout the plate were the usual suspects, each adding its own distinct touch. The lup cheong slices lent pleasant pops of winey sweetness, while slivers of taugeh threaded through and offered the supple noodle strands a fresh, crunchy contrast.
Of all, the egg bits were my favourite component. Fluffy and embellished with a rich, smoky char, they deepened the dish’s aroma in the best way. Coming in second were the golden nuggets of pork lard, which rendered a nutty, unctuous richness.
And wow, were there many cockles. I didn’t bother to count each blood-red morsel, but there were enough to pile onto a heaped spoonful, as you can see. They were chubbier than average too, bursting with a brininess that, for me, leaned a tad too metallic.
Final thoughts
Wok-kissed? Check. Sinfully good? Not quite.
Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow presented a solid plate of char kway teow for sure, with the star of the show undoubtedly being that powerful wok hei perfuming each bite. Its flavours, though enjoyable and moreish, however leaned a little restrained for my heavy palate.
Of course, to each their own. While my personal preferences lie elsewhere, I can certainly get behind this stall’s acclaim, and am all for returning for another plate if I’m in the area while the craving hits.

summary: Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow at Havelock Road Cooked Food Centre has been serving char kway teow for over 40 years, with S$4 and S$5 portions and optional add-ons. Its noodles deliver pronounced wok hei, sweet flavours, smoky egg and generous cockles, though the richness is relatively restrained. It is well suited to diners who prefer a lighter rendition of this classic hawker dish.
title: Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow: Smoky plates of moreish CKT from highly raved Havelock hawker

Dreaming of hosting your own podcast or interview in front of a live audience? You’re in luck – Poddster has opened Poddster Live, a new 2,000 sq ft event space in Singapore for live podcast recordings, interviews and talks.
The venue can accommodate up to 80 guests and comes with an in-house production team, so events can be recorded professionally at the same time. It also sits right next to Poddster’s existing podcast studio, with an in-house production team handling the recording side of things.
In other words, the live event and the content that comes out of it can happen under one roof.
More than just another event venue
The appeal here isn’t really about adding another event space to Singapore’s already lengthy list. This space is geared towards formats built around conversation, whether that’s a podcast recording, founder interview, panel or community event.
For creators, it’s a way to take a show that usually lives online and bring listeners into the room. For brands, it can work as a more engaging alternative to the standard launch or presentation format, with live interviews, discussions or panels that audiences can actually sit in on.
And because the event can be professionally recorded, the content doesn’t necessarily end when everyone heads home. A live conversation can go on to become a podcast episode, longer-form video, social clips or other digital content afterwards.
Why live conversations are having a moment
Photography: Poddster
As more of life shifts online, in-person experiences are starting to feel a little more valuable again.
A live podcast or interview gives audiences access to the parts that don’t always make the final edit: the tangents, audience questions, unexpected moments and conversations that unfold in real time.
There’s also the community side of it: Online audiences may follow the same creator, topic or brand for years without ever being in the same room. A live event changes that, giving people the chance to meet the person behind the content – and, just as importantly, each other. That sense of community is a big part of what Poddster Live is designed to tap into.
A different way to think about branded events
Photography: Poddster
If you’re a brand, you could also tap into Poddster Live’s space, especially for hosting something between a traditional media event and a full-scale public activation.
A founder might host an interview around a new launch. A beauty or wellness brand could bring together experts for a live discussion. A creator could record an episode in front of their community, with the post-show mingle becoming part of the experience itself.
The advantage is that the event can keep working after the audience leaves. Rather than putting everything into a one-night-only activation, the same conversation can potentially be repurposed into longer-form content and social assets afterwards.

It’s official: we’ve compiled the best Christmas dinners, brunches and other festive menus in Singapore so you don’t have to. We love the holiday season, but between sussing out the best Christmas gifts in Singapore to making space in our cals for all the festive parties we can’t wait to attend, choosing the right restaurant for Christmas in Singapore can feel like just another item on a lengthy to-do list.
That’s why we’ve done the searching for you – from grand hotel buffets to intimate festive dinners, keep scrolling for the best Christmas feasts to book, complete with some of the best Christmas cocktails in Singapore for your yuletide toast. Staying in for the holidays instead? Peep our list of the best Christmas food delivery and takeaway spots in Singapore .
Why trust this guide
Every year, during Christmas, our team combs through the festive menus, gift sets, hampers, and turkey and log cake offerings. We compare notes, taste menus where we can, and research everything else, so you don’t have to spend time figuring out what’s worth spending your money on. We prioritise stand-outs over exhaustive lists, we fact-check prices and availability before publishing, and we update guides as new launches come in. When in doubt, we ask around – our community is generous with its seasonal picks.
Where to go for Christmas dinner in Singapore
1. Butcher’s Block
Photography: Butcher’s Block
Revel in the splendour of the Christmas season with an avant-garde wood-fire dining experience at Butcher’s Block at Raffles Hotel Singapore. Hawaiian Chef de cuisine Jordan Keao curates a Festive IMUA Wood-fire set menu that adds holiday cheer, while encapsulating the restaurant’s focus on wood-fire cooking, whole animal butchery and zero waste. Take a look at the multi-course menu, and you’ll spot premium ingredients including Japanese uni, bluefin tuna, wagyu and premium Oscietra caviar.
Every dish on the menu sounds enticing, but we’ve got our eyes on the huli-huli dry-aged duck that pays homage to a popular Hawaiian dish, and the stone-axe full blood wagyu beef wellington elevated with truffle beef jus. To complete the experience, top up from $188++ for a tailored beverage pairing or a Dom Perignon wine pairing – all specially handpicked by the resident sommelier. Psst: Raffles Hotel Singapore also offers festive menus and seasonal dining experiences at its other restaurants and bars, so round up your loved ones for more gourmet experiences this Christmas!
Best for: An elegant wood-fire experience with a festive twist

2. Andaz
Photography: Andaz Singapore
You can count on Andaz Singapore to deliver a sumptuous feast this festive season. The hotel’s sophisticated steakhouse, 665°F, welcomes you to an intimate setting that overlooks the stunning Marina Bay. The feast begins from 1 December with the 665°F festive table set menu with the likes of Applewood-smoked sustainable Atlantic salmon, Black North Onyx tenderloin and more.
Alternatively, come by on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day for specially curated set menus available for both lunch and dinner. The multi-course menu is a treat for both the eyes and the palate, featuring premium ingredients across every course. Think pine-smoked Puglian burrata, Jerusalem artichoke cappuccino, Australian pure black crossbred F1 wagyu striploin and kombu-aged Mediterranean sea bream. Vegetarian options are available, too. For a decadent finale to the experience, indulge in a festive dessert and petit fours, featuring roasted Japanese persimmon, mascarpone mousse, Fewster’s honeycomb and vanilla bean ice cream.

Base Gelato is a new gelato bar in Joo Chiat
If you’ve recently gone cafe-hopping in Joo Chiat , you’ve probably visited the usual hotspots such as Common Man Coffee Roasters and Elijah Pies . You might, however, miss an unassuming hole-in-the-wall shop that has recently opened right under everyone’s noses. Base Gelato is a new cafe in Joo Chiat by Creamier, selling specialty gelato flavours at nett prices.
How To Spend 12 Hours In Katong: Viral Matcha Cafe, Vintage Shopping And More
The space itself is very cosy and slightly dim. It boasts an industrial look, with natural light seeping in through the glass door.
Their menu is relatively straightforward: there are only six items to choose from. Each flavour of ice cream is specially curated, paired with its own unique accompaniments.
Their signature flavour is the Joo Chiat Heritage ($10) , which pays homage to the locale’s Peranakan history. It features a scoop of refreshing young coconut gelato topped with smoked gula melaka caramel and grated coconut, served alongside a skewer of QQ, house-made ondeh ondeh dango.
For those who prefer stronger flavours, order the Rum Raisin Vanilla Panna Cotta ($12) . The base is a layer of jiggly, silky vanilla panna cotta, made from locally grown Madagascar vanilla pods. It is topped with Jamaican rum-infused gelato and chewy sun-dried Xinjiang raisins for a nice textural contrast.
As a matcha addict, my personal favourite has got to be their Matchagato ($12) .
You can expect kinako, AKA roasted soybean powder, gelato encased in a chewy mochi wrapper and topped with azuki bean paste. Matcha is then hand-whisked right in front of you and poured over the whole shebang. I was pleased to know that their matcha is sourced from Wazakura, a prominent tea-producing region from Uji known for producing matcha that tastes rich with a smooth finish.
For something on the lighter end, the Yoghurt & Honey ($10) features triple-strained Greek yoghurt gelato similar to frozen yoghurt . It is topped with toasted honey fluff and garnished with wildflower honey and locally grown edible flowers.
This was my colleague’s favourite. The gelato was creamy with a slight tang from the yoghurt, while the honey fluff was similar to meringue, adding a nice airiness and sweetness to the dessert.
Image credit: Cindy Tan via Google Maps
We didn’t get to try all of their flavours, but the Black Forest ($12) will probably be a hit among chocolate lovers . This dessert consists of a bittersweet Valrhona Coeur De Guanaja 80% chocolate gelato topped with a dollop of cream and a wild Morello cherry, served alongside a dark chocolate sponge that’s soaked in cherry-infused kirsch.
Image credit: Cindy Tan via Google Maps
Alternatively, their Kaya Butter Toast ($9) is one flavour that nods to the classic Singaporean breakfast. It comprises butter-flavoured gelato and pandan coconut kaya jam sandwiched between two crispy brown toasts.
Overall, the price tag is a little steep for ice cream, but every item at Base Gelato earns its keep. Every flavour we tried was bold yet balanced, and exactly what you want in this sweltering heat.
Base Gelato is a 19-minute walk away from Marine Parade MRT Station . Do take note that it’s takeaway only.
For a full-fledged meal before your gelato treat, read our guide to the best food in Joo Chiat . If you’re not in the area but still craving a sweet treat, check out CHAGEE’s new gelato series .
Address: 198 Joo Chiat Road, #01-01, Singapore 427469
Opening Hours: Fri-Sun 12pm to 7pm
Website
Base Gelato is not halal-certified.

Images taken by Chan Zi Xuan.
This was a media tasting at Base Gelato.
summary: We visited Base Gelato, Creamier's new gelato bar in Joo Chiat selling specialty gelato flavours at nett prices.
title: We Tried Creamier’s New Gelato Bar In Joo Chiat: Is It Worth The $10 Price Tag?

Korean fashion fans, here’s another brand to add to your shopping radar. Musinsa Standard , the South Korean label known for its minimalist wardrobe staples and effortlessly put-together looks, is making its way to Malaysia with plans to open its first physical stores in the country .
Credit – Musinsa
If you’ve ever found yourself gravitating towards clean-cut basics that go with practically everything, Musinsa Standard might be right up your alley.
Credit – Musinsa
The brand focuses on contemporary everyday wear, spanning relaxed-fit T-shirts, crisp shirts, tailored trousers, outerwear and accessories. Its signature aesthetic leans towards understated colours, fuss-free silhouettes and versatile designs.
Think of it as South Korea’s answer to UNIQLO, with an emphasis on timeless essentials that don’t require an entire wardrobe overhaul to look good. Rather than relying on loud prints or fleeting trends, Musinsa Standard makes a case for investing in everyday pieces that you can wear on repeat.
Credit – Musinsa
Malaysia will mark the brand’s fourth Southeast Asian market , following its expansion into the Philippines, Indonesia and Vietnam.
Its local debut comes through an exclusive distribution partnership with Indonesian retail giant PT Mitra Adiperkasa (MAP), which is also working with Musinsa on its Indonesian expansion.
Credit – Musinsa
The two companies plan to establish outlets in major commercial districts across Malaysia , including Kuala Lumpur .
While the exact locations and opening dates have yet to be revealed , the expansion should be welcome news for shoppers who have previously had to rely on online purchases to get their Musinsa Standard fix.
There’s already plenty of interest from Malaysian shoppers. According to Musinsa, purchases made by local customers through its global online store grew by an average of 63% annually between 2023 and 2025.
Soon, you’ll be able to browse the collections , feel the fabrics and try on different fits without having to guess your sizing online. Keep an eye out for more updates as Musinsa Standard gets ready for its debut in Malaysia.
The Capitol is Bandar Utama’s newest LRT-connected lifestyle destination for restaurants & cafes
summary: Musinsa Standard, the South Korean fashion label known for minimalist everyday wear, is preparing to open its first physical stores in Malaysia through a partnership with Indonesian retail group MAP. Planned outlets in major commercial districts, including Kuala Lumpur, will give shoppers easier access to its wardrobe basics, shirts and tailored pieces. Opening dates and exact locations have yet to be announced.
title: Musinsa Standard is opening 1st store in Malaysia, bringing Korean minimalist fashion to KL

Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee is a nearly 4-decade-old Michelin-recognised institution which has been serving handmade fishballs and Teochew-style noodles in Pasar 16 @ Bedok . For any foodies hunting down old-school hawker fare in the East, this stall is a must-visit for the decades of heritage it brings to the table.
As rare as handmade fishballs are, handmade fishballs made from ikan parang are even harder to come across. I kan parang is bony and difficult to process into fishballs and most stalls use yellowtail instead. Stepping up to a stall that goes the extra mile immediately had me excited to try their fare.
What to order at Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee
I opted for Dry Fishball Noodles with Mee Pok (S$4) to enjoy at the hawker centre, and got the Fishball Noodle Soup with Kway Teow (S$4) along with an extra side of Fishball Soup (S$7) to-go.
One serving of Dry Fishball Noodles gets you a generous portion of your noodles of choice, a bowl of clear soup containing 5 precious fishballs and 1 her giao , a traditional Teochew fish dumpling.
The fishballs are definitely the highlight for me. They possess a satisfying bounce and irregular shaping, all telltale signs of a handmade fishball. They possess a naturally sweet flavour from the flesh of ikan parang , and you can tell that not much filler is used as the fishballs don’t have that flour-heavy, starchy bite that commercial surimi fishballs are often guilty of.
When bitten, it breaks apart in tender layers of flesh. It’s quite minimally seasoned so the flavour of the fresh fish meat really shines through. The her giao differs texturally with a firmer, chewier texture and is distinctly less sweet than the fishballs.
The soup was similarly lightly seasoned and contained bits of preserved vegetables which gave it a slight salty finish, which complemented the subtle sweetness of the fishballs well.
Mei Ling Fishball Noodle Showdown: Xin Lu Teochew Fishball Noodles vs Hup Kee Teochew Fishball Noodles
Unfortunately, the mee pok noodles were a little disappointing. I opted for the spicy version, which had the perfect kick and a good balance of sweet and savoury. Sadly, the noodles were quite alkaline-tasting and the sauce didn’t cling but had a clumpy, gummy texture. On the bright side, it was an extremely generous portion and quite filling.
If I came back, I’d recommend either skipping or getting a small portion of noodles and filling up on more fishballs.
As for the Fishball Noodle Soup with Kway Teow , it features the same amount of handmade fishballs and her giao as the dry version, but with flat, white rice noodles in the soup instead.
Disclaimer: If the fishballs look extra plentiful in this photo, that’s because I combined the noodles with the S $7 Fishball Soup, which comes with more fishballs and her giao than the standard S$ 4 bowl!
As I had them to-go, the noodles had soaked up the soup by the time I got home and became quite soft, easily breaking apart when I held them up with chopsticks. Texturally, it wasn’t too bad and was able to retain some chew despite the long journey home.
Who is Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee best for?
I can imagine Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee being best for handmade fishball purists who appreciate labour-intensive ikan parang fishballs. With how rare such fishballs are, I’d highly recommend this stall to anyone looking to try the real deal before it disappears from the hawker scene entirely. The stall is also ideal for those with larger appetites who prefer generous portions of filling noodles.
How to get to Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee
Hock Seng Choon Fish Ball Kway Teow Mee is located within Pasar 16 @ Bedok, which is a 15-minute walk from Bedok MRT Station (EW5) . The station connects to the MRT East-West (Green) Line.
Alternatively, take bus service 31 or 137 from Bedok Stn Exit A (84039) and alight at Fujitech S’pore Ltd (84129) and walk 7 min down Bedok South Road towards Pasar 16 @ Bedok. You can also alight at Blk 18 (84119) or Opp Blk 17 (84111) and walk 3 min towards Pasar 16 @ Bedok.
Do we recommend Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee?
Overall, I’d recommend Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee purely for the handmade ikan parang fishballs — after almost 40 years, they remain the undeniable star of the stall. While the noodles may have been slightly below expectations, you can easily work around this by skipping the noodles altogether or ordering a small portion and loading up on extra fishballs instead.

Where can I find the best fishball noodles in Singapore?
Where are the best places to eat in Bedok?
summary: Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee is a Michelin-recognised hawker stall in Pasar 16 @ Bedok serving Teochew-style noodles and rare handmade ikan parang fishballs from S$4. Operating for nearly 4 decades in East Singapore, the stall offers generous portions with sweet, layered fishballs that stand out over its gummy mee pok. It is best suited for handmade fishball purists and diners with larger appetites seeking traditional hawker fare.
title: Hock Seng Choon Fishball Kway Teow Mee: 40 y.o Michelin-recognised stall has $4 rare ikan parang fishballs

Residents living around Hougang Avenue 8 , near McDonald’s and FairPrice, now have more supper options to look forward to with the grand opening of the revamped BK Eating House . Night owls, brace yourselves! A quartet of 24-hour stalls has joined the 10-stall kopitiam .
Credit – BK Eating House
Those who love crustaceans can head to Lao San Prawn Noodles to enjoy a bowl of dry or soup Traditional Prawn Noodles (S$5.20/S$6.20/S$7.20) , Pig Stomach Noodles (S$5.70) , or Pork Rib Noodles (S$6) at any time of the day. There’s also 24-hour Heng Heng Noodle House for noodle fans craving for Signature Laksa (S$5) and Signature Mee Pok Dry (S$5.50) . There’s even Black Soy Sauce Noodles that allows you to choose an accompaniment of your choice — Minced Meat (S$4.50) , Fishball (S$4.30) , or Fuzhou Fishball (S$4.80) .
For Western food fans wondering why The Pasta & Tortizza at block 631 closed despite its popularity, don’t panic! The stall has simply relocated to a new home right here. Owners Li Xuan and Steven serve up delightful Western offerings like Classic Fish & Chips with Tartar Sauce (S$8.50) and Chicken & Mushroom Rose Pasta (S$10) . They also serve light and crisp Tortizzas ( tortilla skin-based pizzas) in flavours like Satay Chicken (S$10.50) , and my personal favourites — Garlic Shrimp (S$11) and Truffle Mushroom (S$11.50) .
Credit – BK Eating House
Joining the 24-hour gang is Wang Li Xiang 旺栗香 , serving economical bee hoon and nasi lemak . Indulge in Nasi Lemak Set A (S$4.80) that comes with chicken wing, hot dog, and fried egg. You can also build your own plate of White Bee Hoon (S$1.40) with added ingredients like Otah (S$1) , Beancurd (S$1.20) , Taiwan Sausage (S$1.50) , and Hashbrown (S$1) .
Other stalls include Hua Dee Hong Kong Style Roasted Delight (open 24 hours), Kin Fish , Sinar Sumang , Xie Ji Beef Noodle , and Lao Jie Fang Kitchen ( zi char ).

When we stepped into JING , tucked away in a cosy corner of KINEX , I was pleasantly surprised. This buffet restaurant might look unassuming from the outside, but once you step in, you’re greeted by a welcoming atmosphere, friendly staff, and a space decorated with traditional touches.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The vibes here are luxurious yet casual. And the menu? Distinctively local and halal-sourced . I don’t visit Muslim-friendly hotpot restaurants that often, so I wasn’t exactly sure what to expect. But let’s just say that after having lunch here, I’m definitely coming back if I get the chance!
The Kopitiam Classics
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
The concept at JING Halal Hotpot & Grill Buffet is simple: each diner gets their own individual hotpot , while every table has a shared grill . Buffet lunch prices for adults start at S$41.90++ on weekdays and from S$47.90++ on weekends . All-you-can-eat dinner prices start at S$47.9++ .
During our weekday lunch at JING, we tried signature menu items themed around ‘ Kopitiam Classics ’ On The Grill , such as Housemade Otah , Hainanese Chicken , and Salted Egg Prawns . My personal recommendation would be the Salted Egg Prawns, which had freshness and flavour that kept me going back for seconds.
Hotpot Broths
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
We also opted for hotpot broths with strong local inspiration – Laksa and Prawn Mee . These flavours might be too rich and savoury for some, but I never felt it was too much for me. I especially loved the Prawn Mee broth, which worked really well with the hotpot ingredients, adding umami goodness to every bite and sip.
Range of Ingredients
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Speaking of hotpot ingredients, there is quite a wide range to choose from here, especially for meat lovers. Marinated House Specialities include Goji Berry Chicken , Sarawak Black Pepper Beef , Beef Mala , Tom Yum Chicken , and more.
Seafood such as Tiger Prawns , Freshwater Patin Fish , and Black Mussels are also available. Cook your ingredients in your soup of choice or throw them on the grill – it’s up to you how you want to enjoy your meal.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
There are also ready-to-eat items at one of the counters. Do yourself a favour and get some of these fried mantou with chilli crab sauce . There’s nothing better to have while waiting for your other ingredients to finish cooking.
Desserts
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Another honourable mention under The Kopitiam Classics menu is the Bubur Pulut Hitam . Yes, desserts are available! And we devoured a bowl of these so quickly. The warm black glutinous rice and coconut cream combination has just the right sweetness and texture that leaves you wanting more.
The Lucky Roll
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
If the food at JING hasn’t convinced you to visit yet, this probably will. From now to 30 December 2026 , groups of 3–6 pax can participate in The Lucky Roll and stand a chance to win an entire meal on the restaurant’s tab.
A S$10 return voucher for 2 is a guaranteed Consolation Prize for eligible groups that participate. The Lucky Roll is only available from Monday to Thursday , 12pm–5pm , so make your reservations with this in mind!
For more information on JING’s menu and bookings, visit their website .

Share it with some friends. Or don’t. We won’t judge. The Grand Croissant is made for moments worth sharing. It’s the kind of pastry that gets everyone reaching in, and everyone talking. Click here to pre-order yours today!

body:
Xventure Singapore , Tiong Bahru Plaza
If your usual weekend plans involve cafe-hopping or catching a movie, here’s something that might get your adrenaline pumping instead. A new indoor playground has opened at Tiong Bahru Plaza, complete with high ropes, obstacle courses, thrilling slides, and even virtual reality games.
Meet Xventure Singapore , a 1,900sqm adventure park featuring 10 play zones and more than 30 challenges from the same folks behind Kiztopia, and just opened on 20th November 2026.
We went down for a peek on its opening day to find out what you can expect.
What can I expect at Xventure SG?
A 1,900sqm adventure park at the former GV cinema
Those who frequent Tiong Bahru Plaza might remember catching movies at its former Golden Village cinema. Well, the space has undergone quite the transformation, swapping movie screens and cinema seats for climbing walls, high ropes, and giant slides.
Xventure is split into 10 adventure zones catered to different interests and thrill levels. Whether you’re the sort who enjoys scaling heights or someone who prefers competing against friends on solid ground, there are plenty of activities to keep you entertained.
Chill-out area.
What’s particularly interesting is how parts of the former cinema have been incorporated into the new space. Some of its original tiered seating structures have been retained and repurposed into a chill-out area, where visitors can take a break between activities.
And unlike a typical indoor playground geared towards younger children, Xventure is designed with older kids, teenagers, and adults in mind, making it a good spot for group outings.
Take on high ropes & soar across a 30m air glide
If you’re not afraid of heights, the High Ropes Course is probably the zone to hit.
Suspended above the ground, the course features a series of elevated obstacles, including swinging bridges and challenging crossings that’ll test your balance, coordination, and nerves.
And it’s not just a matter of getting from one end to the other. You’ll have to carefully navigate the obstacles while suspended in the air, which might be easier said than done. We tried it out with confidence at the beginning, and couldn’t even make it through the first obstacle with the tyres.
The reward for making it through is a 30m air glide , where you’ll get to soar across the adventure park and take in the action from above.
There’s also a separate Zip Line attraction for visitors who want another opportunity to experience the thrill of gliding through the air.
Zoom down 6m-tall slides
For those who love the adrenaline rush of roller coasters, Xventure’s Slide Park might be right up your alley. The attraction features 3 different slides, each offering a different experience.
The first one we tried was the Swing Slide , a U-shaped slide which stands 6m tall and stretches 13.4m long. Instead of simply sliding straight down, you’ll be sent sweeping down and back up a curved slope, almost like you’re riding a wave. This experience was pretty reminiscent of a ride on a Viking.
The Swing Slide makes its Xventure debut in Singapore, so it isn’t like anything you can try at another place.
We also tried the Launch Slide , another 6m-tall attraction where you’ll be pushed off the platform sitting on a donut-shaped seat. It’s a pretty steep slide over an interestingly-manufactured, bumpy terrain that reminds us vaguely of Lego, and rather than stopping at the bottom, riders are propelled off the slide before landing on a giant airbag.
If that sounds a little too intense, there’s also the Roller Ski Slide , giving you a third option to try.
Compete in Singapore’s first MIRRA Arena
Image credit: Xventure Singapore
Not everything at Xventure involves climbing, jumping, or testing your fear of heights. The park also houses Singapore’s first MIRRA Arena , bringing an immersive multiplayer virtual reality experience to visitors.
Unlike conventional VR experiences where players might be exploring virtual worlds on their own, MIRRA Arena allows participants to navigate and compete in shared virtual environments. It’s a fun alternative for those who enjoy gaming and friendly competition, while giving players a chance to experience something different from the usual physical challenges around the park.
Test your agility at obstacle courses & climbing walls
Obstacle course zone.
If the high ropes haven’t tired you out, there are more physical challenges waiting at the Obstacle Course and Challenger Arena .
Channel your inner ninja as you make your way through obstacles that require you to climb, crawl, and jump to reach the finish line. We took on the Obstacle Course which involves climbing across a wall with moving elements in the way, and we must say that it looks much easier than it really is.
…
summary: Replaces the GV cinema.
title: Xventure Singapore Opens At Tiong Bahru Plaza With High Ropes, Obstacle Courses & 10 Play Zones

Nothing beats having a stunning tree in your home to usher in Christmas in Singapore . An evergreen centrepiece is a key to fab festive decor, whether you choose to put presents under it, or string it with lights and ornaments. From lush live Christmas trees to hyper-realistic fake alternatives, we’ve put together a list of the best spots to get your hands on gorgeous trees. While you’re getting in the holly jolly mood, check out where to snag Christmas decorations in Singapore and delicious Christmas food delivery in Singapore .
Why trust this guide
In order to achieve the ultimate Christmas vibe, we fully believe that a good Christmas tree is going to tie it all together. We’re partial to the fresh ones, in order to get that beautiful pine smell throughout the festive season. However, the reusable trees are also fuss-free and perfect to break out when you’re ready and at your convenience. No matter which type of tree you’re looking for, we’ve got you covered by making sure the brands are reliable, trustworthy, and worth your money.
Where to buy fake but festive Christmas trees in Singapore: 2026 guide
1. Masons Home Decor
Photography: Masons Home Decor
Think your house is too small for a Christmas tree? Overwhelmed by the sheer effort needed to decorate a festive tree? Leave these woes behind, and count on Masons Home Decor to find the perfect tree for your home. Since 2016, this homegrown Christmas specialist has been brightening homes with its vast selection of hyper-realistic trees, ornaments, lights, tree bundles and decorating services. This year, it returns with its biggest collection yet. From compact and pre-lit trees to first-timer starter kits and premium bundles, there’s an option that caters to every home size.

The best part? You don’t have to wait till November for the fresh trees to arrive in Singapore – you can simply start decorating your tree early!

body:
Foca Kumpir has Turkish baked potatoes in Siglap
Image credit: Foca Kumpir
Singapore’s food scene just got a little more diverse with the opening of Foca Kumpir , the country’s first dedicated Turkish kumpir kiosk. If you’ve never heard of kumpir, it is a popular Turkish street food that’s basically a giant stuffed baked potato.
Image credit: E P via Google Maps
FYI: The new kiosk is helmed by Turkish owner-chef Caner, who named the eatery after Foça, a coastal town near İzmir in his home country.
Unlike the usual baked potatoes we’re familiar with, kumpir is made by mashing the potato with shredded cheese and butter until it turns smooth and fluffy. It’s then loaded with toppings such as olives, gherkins, beef sausages and more.
Image credit: Amon Ho via Google Maps
They have three set options: Plain ($6) , which features just the plain potato base; Classic ($9) ; and Ultimate ($12) , both of which offer three toppings.
Alternatively, you can build your own kumpir, with prices depending on the toppings you pick.
Image credit: EA via Google Maps
Classic toppings ($2 each) include sauteed mushrooms, corn, black olives, and pickled jalapenos. For something more traditional, try the ezme, a Turkish relish made with chopped tomatoes, or atom, a spicy yoghurt dip topped with fried chilli.
Ultimate toppings ($3) include bolognese sauce, shredded chicken, cocktail sausage, and tuna.
Image credit: Sss via Google Maps
Beyond the giant spuds, Foca Kumpir also offers pasta such as Spicy Mushroom Pasta ($11.90) , Tomato Spaghetti ($11.90) , Alfredo Penne ($11.90) and more. If you need a protein boost, you can even add a grilled chicken breast for $5.
Image credit: Foca Kumpir
The dessert offerings are also worth looking at, with unique items such as Olive Oil Chocolate Cake ($6) and Yoghurt Cheesecake ($7) .
Of course, a meal is not complete without a refreshing beverage, and Foca Kumpir offers a range of lemonades, including Classic, Mixed Berry, Peach, Pink Rose , and Tropical ($5 each).
If you’re feeling adventurous, the Ayran ($4) is a savoury yoghurt-based beverage that’s not commonly found in Singapore and is worth a try.
If you’re on the hunt for more Middle Eastern fare and other unique cuisines, check out our Nomad Kitchen review , featuring lesser-seen dishes from seven countries. And while you’re in the area, check out this 12-hour Katong and Joo Chiat itinerary for viral cafes, vintage shopping and more.
Address: 55 Siglap Road, #01-12 Siglap Centre, Singapore 455871
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 9pm
Tel: 8711 2301
Website
Foca Kumpir is not halal-certified but uses no pork or lard.

Feature image adapted from E P and Amon Ho
summary: Foca Kumpir is a Turkish-owned kiosk serving kumpir, a giant cheesy potato with topping such as olives, mushrooms, sausages and more.
title: Get Giant Cheesy Loaded Potatoes At This New Turkish-Owned Kiosk In Siglap

body:
OGOG: GO is a new Korean cai fan stall at Bugis Junction
Image credit: OGOG: GO Bugis Junction via Google Maps
Believe it or not, I could eat cai fan every day. It’s my go-to option for a fuss-free, affordable, and yummy meal, with countless combinations to choose from. Recently, however, there’s been a surge in Korean-inspired cai png, with eateries putting a modern twist on one of the nation’s most beloved foods. OGOG: GO , a new takeaway kiosk at Bugis Junction , is one of them.
ICYMI: OGOG first debuted last year as a sit-down store at Marina One , serving homestyle Korean food with a cai fan-inspired concept, alongside gimbap and other Korean dishes. They’ve since opened four other outlets in the CBD, catering to busy lunch crowds. Enter OGOG: GO, the brand’s most recent express version of the OG dine-in concept.
Build Your Own Korean Cai Png From $9.90 At This Raffles Place Kiosk
Image credit: OGOG: GO Bugis Junction via Google Maps
The new grab-and-go outlet is located at Basement 1 of Bugis Junction, giving office-goers around the area yet another spot to dabao lunch from. There are 13 dishes to choose from, with prices starting from $8.90 , making it slightly more affordable than their sister brand.
Image credit: Veronica Lumy via Google Maps
Building a bowl here is simple, with a bowl typically comprising one base, one main, and two sides, much like a standard plate of cai fan. Start by picking your desired base. Popular picks include 18-Grain Rice , though there’s also Tofu Noodle or White Rice for something simpler.
Image credit: OGOG: GO Bugis Junction via Google Maps
Moving on to the proteins or mains. Four flavours of chicken are up for grabs, including Signature Soy , as well as Gochujang Dakgalbi and Buldak Cream for a spicy kick. The must-try here would be the Beef Bulgogi for an additional $1 . They also have Soybean Tofu for a vegetarian option.
Image credit: OGOG: GO Bugis Junction via Google Maps
Last but not least, complete your bowl with their selection of sides, featuring classic banchan such as Honey-Glazed Sweet Potatoes , Silky Steamed Egg , and Japchae . For something more unique, they also have Gochujang Broccoli and Perilla Long Beans .
That’s not all—each bowl also comes with your pick of Napa Cabbage Kimchi or Omija Pickled Radish . You also get to top your bowl off with either Gochujang Salsa or Creamy Sesame sauce.
Image credit: OGOG: GO Bugis Junction via Google Maps
If all that food isn’t enough, you can top up $3 to make your bowl a meal, which comes with a soup and a drink. For protein maxxers, add on the Oven-Baked Chicken Bites (from $4.90) , available a la carte in three sizes and two flavours: Classic Gochujang and Soy Garlic .
For more good Korean food, check out our Hanbroth coverage for Busan-style pork soup by a MasterChef Singapore Season 2 winner, or our BB.Q Chicken feature for more deets on the famous Korean fried chicken chain’s opening in Singapore.
Address: 200 Victoria Street, #B1-K06, Bugis Junction, Singapore 188201
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 9pm
Tel: 8227 8068

body:
Best Orchard Central food to enjoy in town
Orchard Central is one of the prime shopping and dining hubs in town, along with other contenders such as Paragon, Takashimaya , and 313 Somerset right next door. The sprawling vertical mall, which is the tallest mall in Singapore, has tons of different cuisines from Western to the bustling Japanese food court down in the basement. Here’s our guide to dining at Orchard Central for any occasion!
1. Shi Li Fang Hot Pot
Image credit: Eunice Loo via Google Maps
Shi Li Fang is a casual Taiwanese hotpot chain originally from Beijing, China, known for its affordable fare and laid-back setup. You might recognise it from its unique storefront that’s usually decorated with a mountain of stuffed toys.
Unlike many hotpot restaurants that cater mostly to groups, you can find two-person set meals here starting from $33.90++ , which come with beef, meatballs, and a variety of vegetables. If you want to order a la carte, you’ll also be able to find staple hotpot ingredients here, such as cheese tofu, imitation crab leg, mushrooms, vegetables and more.
Unit number: #08-13
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 10pm
Website
Shi Li Fang is not halal-certified.
2. HEYTEA
If you need a pick-me-up from all the shopping, you can drop by HEYTEA for a bubble tea break. The Chinese chain is well known for its innovative menu, with its most viral creation being the salty-sweet cheese foam topping.
If you want something classic, you won’t go wrong with the Bobo Milk Tea ($4.50) . For more refreshing, fruity options, get the Grape Boom ($6.50) , Cloud Grape ($6.90) , or Coconut Mango Boom ($5.90) . They also have matcha drinks such as the Supreme Matcha Latte ($6.90) for matcha lovers.
Read our HEYTEA feature .
Unit: #01-26
Opening hours: Mon-Thu, Sun 10am to 10pm, Fri-Sat 10am to 10:30pm
Website
HeyTea is not halal-certified.
HEYTEA Orchard Central Reopens With 1-For-1 Drinks From 15 To 21 May
3. Nantsuttei
Nantsuttei is known for their Negi Ramen (from $15++), which comes with a creamy, thick, and fragrant tonkotsu broth that’s flavoured with copious amounts of black ma-yu garlic oil. It’s then topped with several pieces of soft chashu that melts in the mouth. The overwhelmingly spicy Dragon Ramen ($15++) hits you with a burst of heat right from the very first sip. It uses a house-made spicy paste that comprises minced pork, chilli paste, chillies, sake, and cayenne pepper.

Singapore’s Holland Village is a lively neighbourhood that attracts both residents and foreign visitors due to its unique blend of cafes, restaurants, and bars. The neighbourhood combines technology and charm, and the recently-opened One Holland Village Mall brings excitement to the mix.
The mall provides a modern dining and shopping experience, with a wide selection of fashionable restaurants, artisanal cafes, and retail stores. It’s also pet-friendly, with numerous pet-friendly shops and even a dog parking sign outside. Let’s jump in to see the top 11 best restaurants in One Holland Village Mall .

1. Matsukiya
A sister company to Sushi Tei, Matsukiya is a Japanese Kushiyaki restaurant that serves yakitori over binchotan , or Japanese charcoal. As it burns hotter and cleaner than regular charcoal, each skewer can be grilled meticulously while still encapsulating the smoky char of the binchotan .
Skewers like the Bacon Ebi (S$8) and Tsukune (S$7) were must-orders and even the Asparagus (S$3) was delicious. All of them have encapsulated the smoky char of the charcoal grill with a deep woody note.
My recommendation would be to go for the Wagyu Ikura Don (S$58) , an A4 ribeye beef on top of burdock rice. I love the contrast in flavour profiles from the savoury, melt-in-your-mouth beef to the bursting brininess of the Ikura to the earthy, almost woody, burdock rice.
7 Holland Village Way, #03-21, Singapore 275748
+65 6322 7868
Daily: 11.30am – 3pm & 6pm – 10pm
Facebook | Instagram | Website
2. Sushi Tei
Singaporeans are huge suckers for Japanese food and Sushi Tei seems to be one of those restaurants that never disappoint. Starting off with the Dragon Roll (S$17.80) , which is a king prawn sushi roll topped with avocado. I loved the play in texture with the crispy yet juicy king prawn tempura wrapped on the inside contrasting the creamy avocado on the outside.
For those looking for a heavier meal, I would recommend the Una Bara Chirashi Don (S$22.80) . An all-in-one mixed sashimi bowl together with premium unagi . I enjoyed the variety of sashimi, especially because each was thickly chopped so you get a good chew of every piece of fish.
They also serve sides like Tempura Moriawase ($11.80) , a platter of different kinds of tempura coated in a light, crisp batter that makes for an irresistible treat.
Order delivery: foodpanda
7 Holland Village Way, #03-19/20 One, Singapore 275748
+ 65 6694 0731

Facebook | Instagram | Website
3. Tsujiri
Staying on the same Japanese theme, we have Tsujiri . A matcha -centric cafe that also serves mains like Scallop Pasta (S$18.80) . What I was expecting was another mediocre pasta with a watery sauce and an average flavour profile. However, it turns out that the sauce was just enough for the pasta to cling on to. The cream was garlicky and rich and complemented the sweetness of the scallops. That said, I felt that the scallops were perhaps just a minute overcooked, but it was nonetheless a great bowl of pasta.
…
summary: One Holland Village Mall at 7 Holland Village Way features 12 dining options spanning Japanese kushiyaki, gyukatsu, Chinese claypot and Hunan dishes, Australian brunch, Vietnamese pho, British fish and chips, and fast-casual Mexican fare, with dishes ranging from S$3 skewers to S$58 wagyu bowls. Ideal for residents, visitors, and pet owners seeking pet-friendly venues like Surrey Hills Grocer, the selection covers sit-down meals, matcha desserts, and quick takeaways.

3 months ago, it was announced that D23 Asia: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event will be coming to Singapore on 25–27 June 2027 . And we’re here to remind you that ticket sales for the much-anticipated event go live this week!
Credit: D23 Asia
From 10am on 24 November 2026 to 5am on 25 November 2026 , UOB Visa Cardholders in Singapore , Malaysia , Thailand , Indonesia , and Vietnam will gain access to the first wave of ticket presales .
Visa Infinite , Visa Infinite Privilege , and Visa Infinite Private Cardholders in select countries will then gain access to a second wave of presales from 10am on 25 November 2026 to 5am on 26 November 2026 .
General sales to the rest of the public will then begin starting 10am on 26 November . All listed dates and timings are in Singapore time (SGT) .
Credit: D23 Asia
Hardcore Disney fanatics probably need no further introduction to D23 Asia. But for the rest of you who are curious, here is a more detailed breakdown of tickets and experiences to expect.
There are 3 tiers of passes: Convention Pass , Convention + Premiere Stage Pass , and Platinum Pass . Convention Passes give you access to the Convention Floor , which houses over 15 immersive experiences inspired by the worlds of Disney , Pixar, Marvel , Star Wars, and more.
Credit: D23 Asia
There are also opportunities to meet your favourite Disney characters at Talent Central and go behind the scenes at The Storytellers Stage . Here is where creators and talents behind some of Disney’s biggest films, series, and experiences will explore the artistic process of shaping the stories we know and love.
The Convention Floor is also where the D23 Marketplace will be, featuring exclusive merchandise and collectables only available at D23 Asia. I can already imagine all the fans shopping and bringing home a piece of Disney with them.
1-Day Convention Passes are priced at S$69 , while 2-Day and 3-Day Convention Passes are priced at S$138 and $207 , respectively.
Credit: D23 Asia
Beyond just access to the Convention Floor, Convention + Premiere Stage Passes also give fans access to nightly Star-Studded Showcases at the Premiere Stage . I’d personally keep an eye out for the Studio Showcase on 25 June , where fans will be among the first to look at upcoming projects from Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and more.
There will also be surprise celebrity appearances and live performances across the 3 nights. Convention + Premiere Stage Passes are priced from S$129 to S$747 , depending on Category and Days.
Credit: D23 Asia
The biggest fans can also choose the Platinum Pass , which is limited to just 200 purchases . For S$989 , these fans will have access to the Convention Floor on all 3 days of the event and preferred Category 1 seating at all 3 nights of the Premiere Stage .
They will also bring home an exclusive D23 Asia gift pack .
Credit: D23 Asia
D23 Asia 2027 in Singapore is shaping up to be a magical, three-day celebration of all the worlds and stories of the Disney multiverse. If you think you’re the ultimate Disney fan, mark your calendars and secure your spot at D23 Asia!
For detailed ticketing information, visit D23 Asia’s official website and Klook .

body:
Stillness Under The Christmas Tree at Great World
If your feed was full of people dozing off on mattresses at New Bahru last week, that was The Resting Room. Over 500 people signed up to lie down in a school hall while live gongs played around them, and plenty of you didn’t manage to get a spot.
Well, here’s another chance. Heveya and Future Resonance, the duo behind it, are bringing Stillness Under The Christmas Tree – a version of the pop-up to Great World this December. You’ll get guided meditation under the mall’s Christmas tree before it opens. There are only 2 dates: Saturdays, 12th and 19th December .
What to expect at Stillness Under The Christmas Tree
Lie down under the Christmas tree with an eye mask & headphones
Image adapted from: Haveya, Future Resonance
Each session lasts 45 minutes . You lie on a Heveya organic latex meditation mat under a soft bamboo blanket, with an eye mask on and wireless headphones that carry your guide’s voice. Think of it as a nap you’re socially permitted to take in a mall atrium.
You don’t need any meditation experience either. The guides are hypnotherapist Pudding Ibrahim, who pairs guided self-reflection with sound, and Maryam M, who mixes breathwork, yoga and meditation with healing soundscapes.
2 themed sessions to close out the year
The Resting Room at New Bahru.
Image credit: Haveya, Future Resonance
Each date has its own theme, so you can pick the one that fits your mood or jio a friend to both:
• A Year of Thank-Yous (12th Dec): A slow look back at the year, stopping on the people and moments you want to thank
• Let Go, Begin Again (19th Dec): Let go of whatever you’ve been carrying this year and pick one intention for 2027
Both run from 8.30am to 9.15am , so you’ll be done before the mall even opens. You could stay for brunch or get some Christmas shopping done before the crowds show up.
How much do tickets to Stillness Under The Christmas Tree cost?
Here’s the lobang. For $30 , on top of your spot in the session, every participant gets a Heveya goodie bag worth over $50 , handed out at the end while stocks last.
Every registration also goes into a lucky draw for that session, which has 2 prizes: an I AM WELL Journal (worth $49) and a Future Resonance LSV Signature 60 Session (worth $60).
You have to book ahead through the Stillness Under The Christmas Tree booking page , and you book each date separately. Spots at sessions like these tend to go fast, so book early.
How is it different from The Resting Room?
Image credit: Haveya, Future Resonance
The New Bahru event on 14th November filled the School Hall with Heveya mattresses for 1 day only. Sessions there ran 60 or 120 minutes with live gongs and acoustic instruments.
The Great World sessions are shorter at 45 minutes, with smaller groups and a guide’s voice in your headphones instead of live instruments. The 2 brands say they plan to bring The Resting Room to more spots around Singapore. Until then, this is the closest thing you can still book this year.
If you’d rather try the mattresses yourself, Heveya’s Tiong Bahru flagship showroom is at 32 Eng Hoon Street. We’ve also covered how its customisable mattresses work for couples .

body:
Christmas at Lendlease Malls
It’s November – which means Christmas is just around the corner! Lendlease malls are getting a festive makeover as homegrown character brand Mochiak & AhWoo makes its first-ever mall collaboration debut. Joining Mochiak the cheerful bunny and AhWoo the laid-back wolf is their mischievous feline friend, Nana, bringing festive cheer to shoppers.
From now till 3rd January 2027 , 313@somerset , Jem , Parkway Parade , and Paya Lebar Quarter will be decked out in their own Christmas themes, each with its own unique Christmas experience. Shoppers can look forward to colourful photo spots, exclusive Mochiak & AhWoo merchandise, and shopping rewards.
Celebrating homegrown creativity & local talent
Beyond bringing festive cheer to shoppers, this collaboration also shines a spotlight on Singapore’s homegrown creative talent. Mochiak & AhWoo are original characters created by local artist Charmaine Teo, providing the beloved IP with a larger platform to connect with new audiences.
The partnership also reflects a shared commitment to supporting local creatives and celebrating homegrown artistry, encouraging Singaporeans to discover and appreciate talent from within the community.
4 malls are getting a Mochiak & AhWoo Christmas makeover
Those planning to get some Christmas shopping done might want to keep your camera handy too. Each of the 4 Lendlease malls is getting its own Mochiak & AhWoo look, inspired by the neighbourhood around it.
313@somerset (left), Jem (right).
At 313@somerset , the trio are throwing a dessert-themed Christmas party, complete with an indoor Christmas tree set up for a festive baking showdown and candy arches lining the Discovery Walk outside. Over in the west, Jem is going for something calmer, with a peaceful garden on Level 2 where you can snap a pic on a park bench with Mochiak, AhWoo, and Nana dressed in Santa suits.
Parkway Parade (left), Paya Lebar Quarter (right).
Easties can look forward to a Peranakan twist at Parkway Parade , where the trio are bundled up in a snowy scene in front of a row of festive shophouses. Meanwhile at Paya Lebar Quarter , a 7m Christmas tree stands tall at PLQ Plaza, and the lawn at PLQ Parkside has been turned into a Christmas market scene, with the trio manning carts of festive treats.
Shop exclusive goodies at the Mochiak & AhWoo Christmas Pop-Up
If the Christmas decorations have you wanting to bring Mochiak & AhWoo home, you’re in luck. The Mochiak & AhWoo Christmas Pop-Up will make its rounds across all 4 Lendlease malls from now till 3rd January , with merch like squishies, T-shirts, pouches, passport covers, luggage tags, keycap keychains, foldable reusable bags, thermal flasks, and more. That’s your Christmas gifting sorted!
Here’s where and when you can catch the pop-up:

Make it a mall-hopping adventure with the festive sticker rally too. Collect an exclusive Mochiak & AhWoo sticker at each pop-up, and complete the set to redeem a bonus sticker at the final stop at Jem, while stocks last.
Play Mochiak & AhWoo’s Treasure Run to score Plus$
Image adapted from: iStock
And while you’re at it, why not test your gaming skills? Head over to the Lendlease Plus mobile app to play Mochiak & AhWoo’s Treasure Run , an exclusive mobile game just for Lendlease Plus Members where players can collect rewards while dodging obstacles to earn Lendlease Plus$. You’ll be playing for a share of 350,000,000 Plus$, which amounts to a whopping S$175,000 worth of Lendlease E-Vouchers!
Image adapted from: iStock
Simply spend $25 in a single receipt at Lendlease malls to earn a game chance, with Basic members getting up to 5 chances per day and Premium members getting up to 10 chances per day . The game runs from now till 21st February 2027 , so there’s plenty of time to give it a go, even after Christmas is over.
Redeem exclusive Mochiak & AhWoo merchandise when you shop
That’s not all. Lendlease Plus Members can score exclusive Mochiak & AhWoo merchandise when you hit the minimum spend at participating malls. Membership is free, all you have to do is register on the Lendlease Plus website or on the Lendlease Plus mobile app .
Here’s what you can redeem at each mall:
• 313@somerset: Spend $180 to redeem a Mochiak & AhWoo Magnetic Cardholder Phone Stand and 10,000 Plus$. Limited to the first 1,500 redemptions.
• Jem: Spend $280 to redeem a Mochiak & AhWoo foldable umbrella (Red) and 10,000 Plus$. Limited to the first 3,400 redemptions.
• Parkway Parade: Spend $280 to redeem a Mochiak & AhWoo foldable umbrella (Navy) and 10,000 Plus$. Limited to the first 7,000 redemptions.
• Paya Lebar Quarter: Spend $280 to redeem a Mochiak & AhWoo foldable umbrella (Cream) and 10,000 Plus$. Limited to the first 1,400 redemptions.

A Christmas shopping trip that comes with carnival rides, festive snacks, and the chance to send a letter to your future self? If that sounds right up your alley, mark your cals for Christmas Together 2026 at Marina Bay Sands from 27 to 29 November 2026. Expect around 150 brands, workshops, live performances and family-friendly activities packed into an indoor Christmas Village. And because the season of jolly is also a time for giving, contributions or proceeds from selected experiences will be going to charity as well. Keep reading for what to shop, eat and experience while you’re there.
Christmas Together 2026: Details at a glance
Best for: Christmas shopping, festive food and family-friendly activities
Date: 27 to 29 November 2026
Opening hours: 10am to 9pm daily
Prices: Free entry with registration; activities, workshops and products may be charged separately
Address: Christmas Together 2026 , Hall F, Sands Expo & Convention Centre, Marina Bay Sands, 10 Bayfront Avenue, Singapore 018956
Make a list and check it twice…
Photography: The Tiny Trooper (left), Scent Journer (right)
Let this be your sign to tackle your festive gift list. Step inside the Christmas market for around 150 brands to shop, with fashion, beauty, homeware, food and artisan pieces across the line-up. From Singapore makers and independent businesses to international labels, you’ll be spoilt for choice.
Photography: East Inspirations x Timber Actually
Among the finds to keep an eye out for: The Tiny Trooper is debuting two new colourways of its Williams sandals, while Scent Journer’s Clouds In Heaven takes inspiration from pandan chiffon cake. For someone who appreciates a good tea setup, East Inspirations and Timber Actually have created a tea tray set that pairs Peranakan porcelain with Singapore timber.
There’s also a selection of gifts made or contributed for the festival. These include paintings by 84-year-old Madam Chong Kwee Cheen, hanging anthurium charms by World of Ying, and Christmas Together room-mist sets by Engel’s Sense. Sales proceeds from the Made to Give collection go in full to charity.
Beauty bits from That Letter M
Photography: That Letter M
Beautyholics, heads up: Mong (@mongabong on Instagram) will be bringing products from her brand, That Letter M to Christmas Together. As the brand’s first pop-up, you can look forward to bagging its 100% cotton sheets, makeup brushes and more. Mong shares, “I think they make such lovely Christmas gifts because they’re practical, thoughtful and something you can actually use every day. Sometimes the best gifts are the little everyday essentials you never knew you needed!”
Personalised pieces from Good Addition
Photography: The Good Addition
Looking for a personalised gift? Andrea (@dreachong on Instagram) will be showcasing apparel from Good Addition, with the option to add embroidery to your selected pieces for a thoughtful touch. “Whether it’s an everyday essential or a wardrobe staple, the embroidered detail makes each piece feel thoughtful and unique – a gift that can be enjoyed well beyond the festive season,” Andrea says.
Come for the gifts, sleigh for the snacks
Feeling peckish after all the shopping? Luckily, there’s plenty of nosh to be had at Christmas Together 2026. Come hungry ‘cos Burnt Ends Bakery, Meatsmith and People People Brewing Co. are among the names joining the F&B lineup, along with Orchard Hotel Singapore, serving up chicken rice and its signature kaya toast from The Orchard Cafe.
Photography: Mdm Ling Bakery (left); Berrybar (right)
Need an excuse to indulge in desserts? Of course you do. Berrybar is bringing chocolate-covered strawberries, Mdm Ling Bakery has a build-your-own cookie travel tin, and Mr Bucket will serve a limited run of 600 cups of hot chocolate.
Keep an eye out for The Christmas Cookie Kombi, too. The vintage Volkswagen will be home to cookies made by inmates through Yellow Ribbon Bakery’s skills-training programme. Sales proceeds from the cookies will be donated in full and shared equally between Yellow Ribbon and Singapore Red Cross Young Hearts.
Little hands, big festive plans
There’s lots to do if you’re visiting Christmas Together 2026 with little ones who aren’t quite as invested in gift shopping. Let the kiddos have fun at ParkLab’s multi-level playground and seven-metre-tall play structure and slide, or keep them entertained with the rides and games from Uncle Ringo.
Image: Christmas Together 2026
You can’t miss the Kindness Bear House, an adorable photo op and a place for giving back, too. Pop by to personalise a Christmas bear with ribbons and a charm for a $20 donation to Singapore Red Cross Young Hearts. Each bear comes with a Kindness Passport, which the kiddos can take along to seven Kindness Stations as part of the Kindness Quest.

The Kiri x Monchhichi collaboration is landing in Singapore, pairing bite-sized Kiri Cheesecake Cubes with collectible Monchhichi stickers. It runs from 4 November to 31 December 2026, so there is still time to collect both sets.
Image: Kiri / Bel Group
How to get the Kiri x Monchhichi stickers
The mechanic is simple. Buy any two Kiri Cheesecake Cubes or The Laughing Cow Cheez Dipper Solo at participating 7-Eleven stores, and you can redeem one free Kiri x Monchhichi sticker set. There are two sets to collect, handed out at random, so each redemption is a small surprise. Stocks are limited.
Image: Kiri / Bel Group
Stickers made for phones, laptops and water bottles
The sticker designs take their cues from the three cheesecake flavours, blending Kiri’s colourful look with Monchhichi’s nostalgic charm. They are meant to be stuck on everyday items such as laptops, notebooks, phone cases and water bottles.
Image: Kiri / Bel Group
What are Kiri Cheesecake Cubes?
Kiri Cheesecake Cubes are soft, individually wrapped cheesecake bites inspired by well-loved desserts. The flavours are Strawberry Fraisier, Raspberry Tart and Lemon Tart, and they can be eaten straight from the pack.
Image: Kiri / Bel Group
For a little more effort, the brand suggests topping a cube on a biscuit for a quick “1 Second Cheesecake”, or freezing it for a DIY ice cream pop.
Image: Kiri / Bel Group
Our take
It is an easy snack-plus-collectible offer, and the 7-Eleven redemption keeps it convenient. If you like cheese-themed Monchhichi goodies, see our earlier piece on the Laughing Cow x Monchhichi keychains , and for more convenience-store treats, check our 7-Eleven ice cream deals roundup .

Baskin-Robbins Singapore launches new Pokémon collection
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
Pokémon fans are in for a treat: Baskin-Robbins Singapore has just launched a new Pokémon ice cream collection!
First Look At McDonald’s Maple BBQ Burgers, Pistachio McPops And More
The collection leads with the Pokémon Ver. Cone ($7.50) and Pokémon Ver. Cup ($7.50) . You pick whichever ice cream flavour you like, and it comes in a Pokémon-printed cup or a cone with a printed sleeve, which makes for good photos.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
There’s also the Pokémon Ver. Cake ($80) , an ice cream cake made for celebrations. It features a round cake with a fun Pokémon design.
Image credit: Baskin-Robbins Singapore
If you’d like to grab some merch, consider the Pokémon Ver. Pint Bundle ($22.90) , which comes with a pint of ice cream and a cream-coloured, Pokémon-themed cooler bag printed with Pikachu, Eevee, Squirtle, Charmander, Bulbasaur, and other Pokémon.
You can fill the pint with a flavour of your choice, including Beach Day , a sea salt vanilla ice cream with caramel-filled milk chocolate pieces, and a salty graham cracker ribbon. Do note that the bundle is only sold as a set, so you can’t buy the cooler bag on its own.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
That’s not all—fans can also snag a Pokémon Ver. Surprise Keychain ($4.90) with any Pokémon Ver. purchase. There are three round designs: Pikachu , Eevee , and Squirtle , each against a seaside backdrop, and you get one at random.
Image credit: Baskin-Robbins Singapore
Plus, spend at least $10 on Pokémon Ver. products in a single receipt, and you’ll get a free Pokémon TCG Fun Pack with three cards. The packs come from the Scarlet & Violet: Destined Rivals and Mega Evolution sets and will be given out at random.
Image credit: @baskinrobbinssg
If you’re ordering through Grab, any Pokémon Ver. product comes with a free Pokémon Ver. Ice Pack , a pink, round ice pack with Pikachu, Squirtle, Bulbasaur, and Charmander around a Poké Ball design.
Everything is available while stocks last, so if you’re hoping to catch ’em all, from the ice cream to the card packs, it’s best to head down early.

Sagye Lite, the casual sister of Orchard Korean pot rice restaurant Sagye, holds its grand opening at VivoCity on Wednesday 25 November with 1-for-1 sotbap for six days, to 30 November. The outlet is already in soft opening, so the doors are open now; the deal is what starts on Wednesday.
Spicy chicken with cheese sotbap at Sagye, Wheelock Place. Photo: Sagye
Sotbap is Korean rice cooked and served in its own pot, with the topping laid over the rice. At Sagye on Wheelock Place it is the centre of the menu, alongside stews and dishes to share. Sagye Lite keeps the pots and brings the prices down for everyday dining.
How the 1-for-1 works
Buy any eligible sotbap and a second eligible pot of equal or lower value is free. It is dine-in only and walk-in only, with no advance reservations for the promotion. A redemption is secured only when the order is placed in the restaurant, first come, first served.
• Lunch: 11am to 3pm, 150 redemptions
• Dinner: 5pm to 10pm, 150 redemptions
• Excluded: Signature Beef Short Rib and the F1 Japanese Wagyu Striploin sotbap
• Dates: 25 to 30 November 2026, while redemptions last
Because the free pot has to cost the same or less, two people ordering pots at the same price get the full value. Pair a cheaper pot with a dearer one and the free half of the deal is the cheaper one.
What the pots cost
Two pot prices have been shared ahead of the opening:
• Grilled Chicken Pot Rice: S$12.90
• Grilled Pork Belly Pot Rice: S$13.90
Under the 1-for-1, a grilled chicken pot paired with a grilled pork belly pot comes to S$13.90 for two. Rose yupdduk, rice cakes in a creamy rose sauce, is on the VivoCity menu too.
Inside Sagye Lite at VivoCity. Image: Sagye Lite / Instagram
Sagye at Wheelock Place
Sagye at Wheelock Place, 501 Orchard Road #02-19, serves beef short rib, scallop and dongpo rou sotbap, alongside Japanese Wagyu ribeye and army stew. It also takes walk-ins only and opens for lunch from 11am to 3pm and dinner from 5pm to 10pm daily. If the VivoCity queue is long on the first weekend, Orchard is another way to get sotbap from the same brand, at full menu prices and with no promotion. Sagye Lite also runs an outlet at Westgate.
Dongpo rou sotbap from the Wheelock Place menu. Photo: Sagye
Sagye Lite details
Address: 1 HarbourFront Walk, #01-167/168, VivoCity, Singapore 098585
Nearest MRT: HarbourFront (NE1/CC29)
Grand opening deal: 1-for-1 sotbap, 25 to 30 November 2026, dine-in only
Promotion sessions: 11am to 3pm and 5pm to 10pm
Reservations: walk-in only for the promotion
Instagram: @sagyelite_sg
summary: Sagye Lite, the casual offshoot of Orchard pot rice restaurant Sagye, marks its VivoCity opening with 1-for-1 sotbap from 25 to 30 November, 150 pots a session, dine-in only.
title: Sagye Lite opens at VivoCity with 1-for-1 sotbap from 25 to 30 November

A brand new live music dining spot has just landed in Bras Basah. Helmed by Tin Box Group, Simply Gemilang had its soft launch just this week on Nov 20 at Lazada One .
Anchored by the simple motto “ Muzik. Makan. Memori .”, the venue aims to deliver a welcoming, alcohol-free night out focusing on good food, music and community. The venue is currently in the process of obtaining halal certification, in hopes to broaden their dining and entertainment offerings.
Credit – Tin Box Group
Local radio station host and comedian Suhaimi Yusof is a partner and brand spokesperson, bringing his television background to round out the entertainment. Additionally, Simply Gemilang’s resident band performs 2 sets on Wed and Thu, and 3 sets on Fri and Sat, playing both English and Malay hits. You can catch monthly visiting local and international acts too!
Credit – Tin Box Group
Save some space if you’re planning to visit and indulge in Thai fusion plates that blend familiar flavours with modern touches. Look forward to well-loved options such as Red Tom Yum Soup ( Tom Yum Nam Khon ) and Pad Thai .
Credit – Tin Box Group
If that’s not your thing, try out the Thai-Style Wonton Noodles ( Ba Mee Kiew ) and Vegan Gado-Gado . Save room for dessert too and end the meal with a classic Thai Red Ruby , consisting of chewy tapioca-coated water chestnut cubes served in sweet coconut milk over ice.
Wash down your meal with an innovative mocktail lineup, so you can sip refreshing drinks throughout the night with no need for alcohol.
Do note that no prices are available at the time of writing.
