body:
I don’t often travel beyond central Singapore, mainly because I feel everything I could ever need is in the east. There are a few kebab options there, but I am always on the hunt for a good wrap. That’s how I came across Gaziantep Delight at Holland Drive Market & Food Centre .
On Google, this spot has 4.9 stars , which is very impressive. The question then becomes: is Gaziantep Delight really that good?
Holland Drive Market & Food Centre was packed and there was an unending number of people ordering from the stall. While it may be hard to tell from the picture, it’s a solo operation. I sleuthed out the most ordered items and chose 3 dishes to talk about today.
What to order at Gaziantep Delight
Let’s dive right into one of their most popular items. The Lamb Tombik (S$9) is just a premium pocket of meat; that is genuinely the perfect description. It is packed with crumbly, tender lamb. I could clock the presence of cumin from smell alone.
Due to how gamey lamb tends to be, you really want to heavily season the meat, lest you suffer the strong taste of earth and iron. Tombik , better known as pita bread, is also an ideal choice when dealing with this type of meat, allowing the fluffy bread to absorb the juices.
After taking a bite, I was immediately floored by the taste of savoury spiced lamb. The cumin didn’t mask the gamey flavour, but merely balanced it out, giving the overall flavour of the meat a surprising depth. Earthy, spicy, fatty and succulent in one hefty pita.
My only complaint is that when the wrapper ripped, the entire thing just fell apart. I feel that that’s more user error than anything, so I won’t hold it against them.
Now, you’d think after a few bites this dish would be too rich. Worry not, because the salad was unbelievably refreshing and is coated with a slightly sweet garlic mayo sauce. Just when I felt like it was a little much, the salad reset my taste buds, allowing me to enjoy more.
Sultan Kebab: Authentic Turkish stall in Maxwell Food Centre with crazy generous portions, unforgettable chicken kebab
Onto the next, the Chicken Doner (S$7) , more commonly known as the chicken kebab. If you can’t tell from the picture alone, this kebab is filled to the brim with chicken. For the amount of meat you get, it’s great value for money. The salad from the Lamb Tombik makes an appearance in the Chicken Doner as well. Both the chicken and salad are wrapped in a thin, yet surprisingly firm flour tortilla .
This wrap is loaded with juicy, peppery chicken and a refreshing salad. Parts of the sliced chicken were charred, giving every other bite a lovely crunch. It was nicely seasoned, but I do wish the spices were more prominent. Here’s why: the salad started to overpower the chicken, especially towards the end of the wrap, where the chicken was not as prominent. Other than that, this is still very satisfying.
We ended the day with a sweet treat. I’ll be honest, the Baklava (S$5 for 2 pieces ) looked pretty basic. It featured the classic baklava components: thin, golden filo pastry, sweet syrup drenched on the bottom layer and pistachio filling. I’ve had a lot of exceptional Baklava recently, so it was going to be quite hard to blow my mind.
Yeah, so I was very wrong. The Baklava had a secret weapon: kadayif. This is a pastry known for its soft, hair-like texture, commonly found in another dessert, kunefe (which they also serve). When packed tightly, the kadayif takes on a delicate and brittle texture, making every bite very satisfying.
Who would’ve thought that this one ingredient could make such a huge difference? When I took a bite, the Baklava gave way very easily. The syrup had settled between the cracks made by the kadayif , so every bite was equally sweet and buttery. The syrup itself had notes of rose as well, giving the treat a floral fragrance. Absolutely lovely.
Who is Gaziantep Delight best for?
If you’re looking for something delicious you can easily pick up and go about your day, Gaziantep Delight is a spot you should consider. Their meats, seasonings and other accoutrements are consistently good — they’ve gotten it down to a science.
Something that gets taken for granted these days is reliability. And to have such reliability with this level of quality is even rarer. My only tip is to be careful with the wrapper. If you tear too much of it, everything may come spilling out. I suppose that is a small sacrifice for having such a generous amount of filling.
How to get to Gaziantep Delight
I took the Green Line and alighted at Buona Vista MRT Station (Green Line and Yellow Line) . From there, it’s a 9-minute walk along North Buona Vista Road and Holland Drive . You could also alight at Holland Village MRT Station (Yellow Line) , which is also a 9-minute walk along Holland Avenue and Holland Drive .
…
summary: Gaziantep Delight, a solo-run Turkish stall at Holland Drive Market & Food Centre, sells a Lamb Tombik (S$9), Chicken Doner (S$7) and Baklava (S$5 for 2 pieces). The lamb pita and the baklava, which has kadayif strands inside, stand out more than the chicken wrap. It suits anyone after a quick, consistent takeaway meal near Buona Vista or Holland Village.
title: Gaziantep Delight: Is Holland Drive hiding one of Singapore’s best kebabs?

body:
If there’s any Malay dish that can rival nasi lemak for its devoted following, it’s the pride of Kelantan — nasi kerabu . Some say nasi lemak reigns supreme, but those who’ve seen the early morning queues at nasi kerabu stalls across KL and Selangor would beg to differ. The allure of blue-tinted rice, fragrant herbs, and smoky grilled meats seems to hold its own magnetic pull.
Continuing my little showdown series, I decided to do what any self-respecting food enthusiast would — feast like royalty while pitting two famed nasi kerabu spots against each other (all in good fun, of course).
Choosing Nasi Kerabu Moknab at Pantai Dalam was a no-brainer. It’s been a viral sensation for years, and the never-ending queues say it all. My second contender, Kak Su Nasi Kerabu Narak in Kajang , was admittedly a personal pick — conveniently close to home and, as I later learned, my family’s old favourite. The real surprise, however, is the fact that it actually outranked Moknab on Google reviews . A showdown worth having, indeed.
Nasi Kerabu Moknab
Credit
Nasi Kerabu Moknab sits unassumingly by the roadside in Pantai Dalam, reminiscent of Kampung Baru. I braced myself for the legendary queue that usually snakes toward the main road, but luck (and a heavy downpour) was on my side. The crowd thinned, though my shoes paid the price.
Do note that the outlet has since moved to Maluri , Cheras .
Ordering at both of these spots feel like a nasi campur or cai fan experience — you line up, point, and choose your sides before grabbing a seat. The main star is, of course, the nasi kerabu itself. The array of side dishes was simply irresistible — everything from grilled morsels to rich curries , glistening with spices and oil that whisper danger to your arteries but comfort to your soul.
My plate ended up with Ayam Gulai and their famous Lemak Bakar , costing RM16 in total — quite fair for the generous portion.
The rice, once mixed with ulam and fish coconut sambal , released a beautiful aroma and layered flavours, though I did wish the grains were a touch fluffier. The keropok on the side was a tad stale, likely due to storage mishaps, but that was easily forgiven once the Lemak Bakar entered the picture.
Hock Kee Kopitiam Bukit Bintang: Latest outlet with 8 must-try signature dishes & local favourites
Now this was the highlight of the day. Soft, fatty, and gloriously smoky, every bite melted on the tongue, perfectly balanced with just the right sweetness from the marinade. The Ayam Gulai didn’t lag behind either — tender, rich, and thoroughly seasoned.
Overall, Moknab impressed us the most with its side dishes, each plate brimming with bold yet balanced flavours that spoke of years of experience.
Kak Su Nasi Kerabu Narak
Credit
Over in Kajang, Kak Su Nasi Kerabu Narak — or “Su Narak,” as my parents fondly call it — carries a more neighbourhood vibe.
The stall offers an enticing breakfast lineup featuring nasi kerabu , nasi dagang , nasi lemak , and more. If nasi kerabu isn’t calling your name that morning, their nasi dagang is a solid backup. The queue usually builds early, but by 9.30am, we managed to avoid the crowd.
Compared to Moknab, their nasi kerabu side dish selection felt more modest, though the option to mix in nasi dagang accompaniments was a definite plus.
I went for Daging Bakar , Daging Goreng , and Gulai Ikan Tongkol — a hearty trio that cost RM12 .
The rice was fluffier and moister than Moknab’s, a lovely texture that made every bite comforting. That said, I personally found Moknab’s ulam and coconut sambal a touch more flavourful.
The beef options were tasty and tender, but I couldn’t help missing Moknab’s charred, fatty indulgence. The Gulai Ikan Tongkol , borrowed from the nasi dagang menu, added a pleasant note that tied the plate together beautifully.
Verdict
Both Nasi Kerabu Moknab and Kak Su Nasi Kerabu Narak hold their own in Malaysia’s beloved breakfast scene . Kak Su wins for rice texture and overall balance, while Moknab steals the show with unforgettable flavours and irresistible side dishes. My final pick ended up being Nasi Kerabu Moknab !
If you ever find yourself in Pantai Dalam or Kajang, don’t pick favourites just yet — try both and let your taste buds decide. When it comes to nasi kerabu , there are no losers, only very, very happy diners.

What to eat at Solaris, Mont Kiara?
Which Korean food spot in KL is worth the drive?
summary: Nasi Kerabu Moknab and Kak Su Nasi Kerabu Narak go head-to-head in a comparison of two popular breakfast spots in Klang Valley, located in Maluri, Cheras, and Kajang respectively. With plates ranging from RM12 to RM16, the review compares their rice, grilled meats, curries and side dishes, making it useful for diners deciding between generous accompaniments and better rice texture.
title: Nasi Kerabu Showdown: Nasi Kerabu Moknab vs Kak Su Nasi Kerabu Narak

Looking for a spot for lunch but you don’t wanna break the bank? Well, $5 Western & Japanese Food recently opened at Sim Lim Square , and the prices almost made me shed tears. Tears of joy, of course.
With the prices of everything skyrocketing, places like these are becoming few and far between. But for a restaurant to open with every main at just S$5 is both admirable and daring. This spot opened on 22 Nov 2026 , and I do hope they stay open a long time.
Credit – Facebook
The restaurant itself looks simple, with only posters of their dishes decorating the wall. Each poster proudly brandishes the S$5 pricing, which will likely draw crowds looking for a cheap but satisfying bite.
Credit – Facebook
For the pricing, I expected a more compact menu. I can happily say I was wrong. From the menu, you can get a variety of Western and Japanese dishes for S$5 each. Western food tends to be affordable, so the prices for those aren’t surprising. But Japanese food is definitely more expensive, especially in Singapore.
In fact, these prices beat some Japanese fast food restaurants, which is a huge feat. You can even choose 2 sides for — you guessed it — S$5 . I have a feeling this restaurant will be a hit with office workers and students alike.
Credit – Facebook
The serving size looks generous as well. The classic fish and chips, or in this case, mashed potatoes, look pretty decent. While you can’t expect the flavours to be mind-blowing or out-of-this-world good, you can certainly leave satisfied.
At the end of the day, we just need something to keep us fueled up for a long day’s work. If that sounds like something you need, head down to Sim Lim Square today and have your fill.
Charr’d The Hawker: Ex-fine-dining chefs dish out $4 hearty Western comfort food
summary: $5 Western & Japanese Food opened at Sim Lim Square on 22 Nov 2026, serving Western and Japanese dishes at S$5 each. Diners can also pick 2 sides for S$5, and the portions look generous, though the flavours are described as satisfying rather than standout. It suits office workers and students after a cheap lunch.
title: This new Sim Lim Square restaurant sells every main for $5

Looking for fresh ideas for your next date and want something beyond your usual dinner plans? Singapore has plenty of unique date options to explore.
If you have no time to look them up yourself, we’ve got you covered with 7 recommendations ! Keep reading to find your next itinerary for two.

Credit: Scentopia
For couples who are into fragrances, consider visiting Scentopia at Siloso Beach , Sentosa , for their Couple Experience . Not only will you have fun creating your own signature fragrances together, but you’ll also get to bring home a sealed bottle each to remember the day.
Through this experience, couples can also discover each other’s Scent Personality and explore a wide range of aromas before creating a customised perfume with expert guidance. It’ll not just be a unique date idea, but a way to learn another aspect of your partner.

Haochen Zhang & Hannu Lintu – Prokofiev Piano Concerto 2
Credit: Singapore Symphony Orchestra
Here’s another idea for those of you looking for something different from the usual dinner-and-movie date! Spend an evening with the Singapore Symphony Orchestra (SSO) on 15 January 2027 , as acclaimed pianist Haochen Zhang joins Music Director Hannu Lintu for a programme featuring Prokofiev’s virtuosic Piano Concerto No. 2, alongside colourful orchestral works by Donghoon Shin, Igor Stravinsky and John Adams.
One highlight that concertgoers can look forward to is Zhang’s performance of Prokofiev’s Second Piano Concerto, one of the most technically challenging piano pieces out there. But that’s not all you will experience during the night.
Beyond Prokofiev’s Piano Concerto, the programme also features a contrasting selection of orchestral works. These include South Korean composer Donghoon Shin’s Upon His Ghostly Solitude . Written in 2023, the piece explores the devastation and turbulence of war through a rich orchestral soundscape. The performance marks the work’s Singapore premiere.
Another piece worth noting is Stravinsky’s Song of the Nightingale , which has its origins in the composer’s opera The Nightingale and offers another orchestral perspective. It also provides an interesting connection to the final piece of the night, John Adams’s Slonimsky’s Earbox , which takes inspiration from Stravinsky’s work. Both compositions are presented in celebration of Adams’s 80th birthday year.
If you and your partner want to explore something beyond your usual musical tastes, this concert offers an opportunity to discover a variety of orchestral music together, making it an interesting date night!
Tickets are priced from S$15 and are redeemable under the SG Culture Pass. There is also a 30% discount on Cat 4–6 tickets for Seniors Citizens (55 years old and above), Full-time National Servicemen (NSFs), and Person with Disabilities (PWDs).

Kid-friendly holiday destinations for the school holidays
With the school holidays just around the corner, it’s time to start planning ways to keep the kids entertained. Rather than letting them loaf around at home, eyes glued to their screens, use the long break as an excuse to pack your bags and bring the whole family out for a proper vacation to a kid-friendly holiday destination .
But you don’t have to travel halfway across the world to keep the kids occupied. If you’re looking to skip the hassle of layovers and complicated travel plans, we’ve got you covered. Here are 16 kid-friendly holiday destinations near Singapore , packed with enough fun activities that’ll cure the kids of all that brainrot .

1. Johor Bahru, Malaysia
Image credit: Legoland Malaysia
Just across the Causeway, it’s good ol’ Johor Bahru ; every Singaporean’s go-to weekend getaway. Beyond the shopping malls , cafes , and countless other things to do in JB , there’s more than enough to turn the usual JB day trip into a few days of family fun.
LEGOLAND Malaysia can easily take up an entire day on its own. With 8 themed zones, hop on rides like LEGO NINJAGO The Ride and Dino Island, while younger kids can earn their LEGO driving license at the Driving School. And just right beside it is SEA LIFE , where you can get up close with marine creatures like sharks, stingrays, and seahorses.
For older kids craving an adrenaline rush, Austin Heights Water & Adventure Park has got it all. Zoom down thrilling water slides, tackle high-rope obstacle courses, or bounce around on trampolines in this 3-in-1 park. End your getaway with a trip to Johor Zoo , where you can spot exotic animals like tapirs, camels, and gorillas in what is Malaysia’s oldest zoo.
Suggested trip duration: 3 days
Getting there: For the fastest way to get to JB, take a 5-minute KTM Shuttle from Woodlands Train Checkpoint to JB Sentral. But there are other ways to get to JB, so make sure to check our transport guide to JB .
2. Desaru, Malaysia
While JB might steal the spotlight for Singaporeans looking for a quick escape, Desaru is an underrated alternative further into Johor, away from the hustle and bustle of the city centre. The coastal town is a solid pick for a few days of sun, sand, and sea, with no shortage of attractions to add to your itinerary.
Of course, you can’t plan a holiday to Desaru without including Adventure Waterpark Desaru Coast . With over 20 water-based rides and slides, there’s plenty to dive into, from windy flumes to relaxing river rides. Just note that some experiences like Tidal Wave Beach and Kids Ahoy! are currently unavailable until further notice.
For a change of pace, spend an afternoon at Desaru Ostrich Farm and Desaru Mini Zoo , which are just 10 minutes apart. Little ones get the chance to ride on an ostrich at the former, before dropping by the Mini Zoo to feed rabbits, alpacas, and even camels.
Keep an eye out for the upcoming KF Karting Circuit at The Sports Arina as well, scheduled to open by the end of 2026. It’ll feature both a competitive circuit and a dedicated indoor track, specially designed for kids aged 4 to 12 to try their hand at karting.
Suggested trip duration: 3 days

body:
Kindergartens with cool facilities & activities
As a Singaporean born right as the world ticked into the new millennium, my time as a wee tot in preschool on the Little Red Dot was as unremarkable as it could get. Learning how to tell the time, writing my Chinese name for the first time, and those afternoon naps that I sorely miss now in adulthood were all part and parcel of the carefree curriculum.
So you can imagine how flabbergasted I was when a colleague pitched an article outlining all the wonders the kids of today have at their fingertips in their kindergartens. From unique classes to overseas excursions, here are a couple of kindergartens in Singapore with cool facilities and activities that blow my formative years out of the water.
1. Kidz Meadow
Sportybots programme that introduces kids to 12 different sports
Image credit: Sportybots
Parents will know all too well how rowdy and restless kids can get, so Kidz Meadow has a solution to put their seemingly boundless energy to good use. They’ve partnered with Sportybots , an organisation that specialises in fun, non-competitive multi-sports programmes, to better their curriculum with some fun in the sun.
Image adapted from: Sportybots International Pte Ltd
Rather than letting them run aimlessly amok at the playground, children from N2 to K2 will get to have a go at 12 different sports . They’ll be introduced to a new one every 3 months, and the list features popular sports such as basketball, soccer, and tennis, as well as more niche ones like rugby, dance/cheerleading, hockey, and even golf.
Think of it as a precursor to the various CCAs your little one can pick from when they enrol in Primary School. Letting them have a shot at different sports beforehand helps them choose what they truly enjoy, rather than being shoehorned into something they don’t particularly like.
Learn more about Kidz Meadow’s Sportybots programme .
2. Overseas Family School
Building robots & cars & learning foreign languages like Dutch & French
Image credit: Overseas Family School
If you didn’t know, the Overseas Family School in Pasir Ris is a school that’s been serving expat families living in Singapore since 1991. Being an international institution, their range of enrichment activities is huge; even those still in Kindergarten have quite a few to spruce up their time in school with.
Image credit: Overseas Family School
For instance, they can sign up for a bunch of engineering-related programmes, and don’t go for a second thinking that these are as boring as they sound. The LEGO Engineers and LEGO Robotics programmes introduce concepts such as friction, gravity, and how gears and sensors work using intuitive and fun LEGO blocks to keep young minds engaged.
Naturally, the school also has a number of foreign language classes . Ones that they offer include Dutch, French, German, Italian, Russian, and Japanese to name a few. Interestingly, the school also has programmes for parents too, from useful Mandarin lessons to high-energy Zumba sessions.
Learn more about Overseas Family School’s enrichment programs .
3. Posso Preschool
Hydrotherapy pool for infants
Bathhouses and wellness recovery studios aren’t exactly commonplace in Singapore to begin with, so Posso Preschool ’s hydrotherapy pools for infants really caught our attention. Although we grown ups use such pools for muscle recovery after gruelling workouts, toddlers aren’t exactly working up a sweat at the gym.
Image credit: Posso Preschool
Instead, the preschool uses these pools to build confidence in the water , as well as to provide a multi-sensory experience through water play. The pools are also heated , so you won’t have to worry about junior catching a cold as they splash about. However, not all Posso Preschool locations have them; currently, only their Rivervale CC and Jurong East schools are equipped with the pools.
Learn more about Posso Preschool’s hydrotherapy pools .
4. EtonHouse Pre-School by the Beach
Lessons & activities held at Sentosa’s beaches
When you’ve got Sentosa’s beaches just a stone’s throw away from your classrooms, you can most definitely look forward to fun lil’ excursions that are equal parts fun and educational. That’s a luxury that students at EtonHouse Pre-School by the Beach have, as the school is the country’s first-ever beachfront preschool, located at Palawan Kidz City on Sentosa .
Image credit: EtonHouse
While tourists and locals alike visit the island from time to time to catch some sun, these kindergarteners are given the go-ahead to swing by the surrounding beaches and nature trails as part of their curriculum. Accompanied by their teachers, lessons here include painting by the beach , exploring tide lines , and learning about environmental sustainability through hands-on activities.
Image credit: EtonHouse
…
summary: How we wished these were around back in the day.
title: 8 Kindergartens In SG With Cool Facilities & Activities We Wish We Had As Kids

Free running tracks in Singapore
There are many ways to get into the groove of the #fitspo life in SG – think cycling , hiking , and an outdoor excursion to our many nature parks like Bukit Timah Nature Reserve . But if you thrive on lacing up your track shoes, these free running tracks in Singapore may be what you need to iron out your stamina with zero distractions.
What are the benefits of running?
While you might already know how useful running is when it comes to losing weight, there are many other benefits you may not know about, from improving mental health to reducing risks of certain health issues.
In general, every 1km run is equivalent to an average of 60 calories burned, though this varies on many factors like age and intensity of the run. For those focusing on weight loss, aim to get your heart rate into the fat-burning zone, which is about 70%-80% of your maximum heart rate.
To get your approximate maximum heart rate, subtract your age from 220. You can also use this heart rate calculator to find your target heart rate.
Other pros of running include positive impacts on your mental health. When we run or exercise, endorphins and other chemicals like serotonin and dopamine – AKA happy hormones – are released, which reduces the feeling of stress and anxiety. Running also helps to regulate sleep patterns and increases sleep quality by keeping the circadian rhythm in check.
In the long run, running can significantly reduce your risk of illnesses and diseases like osteoporosis, diabetes, stroke, and even cancer.
How to increase your running stamina?
When it comes to building up stamina, take it slow and easy by following a progressive training plan. This means gradually increasing the distance you run weekly by about 10% each week. You can also try incorporating longer runs at a slower pace to get your body used to the distance. The important thing is to stay consistent.
Is running on a running track better than in a park?
Yes, running on a synthetic running track is better compared to concrete paths in parks. The rubber surface helps to absorb more impact on your feet, knees, and back. Running tracks also provide more consistency compared to the sometimes uneven surface of paths in parks.
How to prepare for a run?
Being in the proper attire can improve performance and reduce the chances of injury, so make sure you’ve got appropriate running gear. Here are some essentials you’ll need:

Nature hideouts like Bedok Reservoir , Tampines Eco Green , and Pasir Ris Park form some of the places that Easties go to for their daily jog. But if the weather takes a downer, have Our Tampines Hub as your plan B.
Our Tampines Hub has both outdoor and indoor running tracks, both of which are on the 5th floor and come with shower and locker facilities. 1 lap around the outdoor track is 705m, while a lap around the indoor track is 455m. body:
Royal Caribbean’s Navigator of the Seas in Singapore
Annual leave is precious. So is the fantasy of a holiday where your toughest decision is tacos or lobster roll. Here’s some good news for the chronically overworked: Royal Caribbean’s Navigator of the Seas has docked at Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore, and it’s not going anywhere till October 2027 .
That’s a whole year of sailings that start and end right here at home, from a 2-night cruise to nowhere for quick getaways to a 13-night voyage to Tokyo for those hoarding leave like it’s limited-edition merch.
Below, we break down where the ship sails and how much it costs, the record-breaking waterslide worth queueing for, and what you can eat without paying extra. Plus, how Navigator compares to Quantum of the Seas, which takes over the Singapore berth after it leaves.
All you need to know about Navigator of the Seas being homeported in SG
Navigator sailed into Singapore on 29th October 2026, and this is the first time the ship has called our little red dot home. The plan was originally a 6-month season, but Royal Caribbean extended it to a full year-round, so you can now hop on any month till October 2027 .
Before this, the ship spent about 5 years sailing out of Los Angeles, where it ran year-round from November 2021. Translation: it knows short party getaways well, which is exactly the format Singaporeans love.
A quick spec sheet for the curious. Navigator is a Voyager Class ship that first set sail in 2002, and it carries around 3,368 guests. In 2019, it got a USD115 million (~S$150 million) glow-up, which added new waterslides , the revamped pool deck , and a bunch of new bars and restaurants . So while it’s not the newest ship on the block, it’s had serious work done.
Where does the cruise sail to from Singapore & how much does it cost?
Itineraries range from 2 to 13 nights , with most short trips heading to Malaysia and Thailand. The longer ones reach Vietnam, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, and Japan.

2-night cruise to nowhere means 0 leave needed
The Weekend Getaway leaves Singapore at 4pm on a Friday and is back by 7am on Sunday. That gives you a full sea day in between with nothing to do but work through the ship’s slides, shows, and buffet. It’s the cheapest way to find out whether cruising is your thing, or whether you get seasick looking at a bathtub.
Sailing is limited though. Only 2 dates were listed at the time of writing, including 26th March 2027, so lock one in early.
12- & 13-night cruises to Tokyo are one-way only
The longest sailings run one-way between Singapore and Tokyo , hitting Hong Kong, Taipei, and a string of Japanese ports along the way. The 12-night cruise departs on 13th February 2027, while the 13-night version leaves on 29th April 2027 and adds Ho Chi Minh City, Jeju, and Fukuoka.
Since these are one-way, you’ll need to book a flight home from Tokyo . Or extend your trip in Japan and pretend work doesn’t exist for a bit longer.
What are the signature attractions & highlights of the ship?
The Blaster is the longest waterslide at sea
This is the headliner. The Blaster is Royal Caribbean’s first aqua coaster, and at about 244m long, it’s billed as the longest waterslide at sea . You and a buddy ride a 2-person raft that gets shoved uphill by water jets, then sent through drops and dips, including a stretch that swings out over the side of the ship. Nothing quite like staring at the open ocean while hurtling along on a float.
Right next to it is Riptide , a headfirst mat-racer slide with a see-through tube. Together, the pair is called The Perfect Storm, which feels accurate for anyone who ate too much at the buffet beforehand.
A massive Caribbean-style pool deck & other signature attractions
The 2019 makeover gave Navigator a Caribbean-themed pool deck with double the surface area of the old one, so there’s actually space to lie down without fighting for a deck chair.
Adults who want peace and quiet can retreat to the Solarium , an adults-only pool area .

body:
Kallang Ice World: Ice skating rink in Singapore
It doesn’t matter if you’re trying to recreate Alysa Liu’s ice skating routine to Stateside . Kallang Ice World , right next to Stadium MRT Station, boasts competition-standard ice so you can zoom around in circles or perform tricks if you’re up for it. Here’s all you need to know before donning your down jackets and lacing up your pair of skates.
Where to go ice skating in Singapore
With The Rink in JCube being permanently closed since 2023, and Ice Penguin offering a synthetic ice skating experience in Clarke Quay, Kallang Ice World remains Singapore’s only rink with real ice, where you can glide around and live out your figure skating dreams.
Is online booking available at Kallang Ice World ?
No, there’s no online booking available at Kallang Ice World, so you’ll need to purchase your tickets in-person. Keep in mind, however, that there are only 150 spaces per ice skating session, so it’s a good idea to arrive early on weekends to make sure you get a spot.
However, they do host birthday parties and also offer private or group lessons, so you can call and enquire if you can make a booking in advance.
What are the prices for ice skating at Kallang Ice World ?
Image credit: @c2lingsquare via Instagram
Ice skating prices at Kallang Ice World start from $20 for adults and $18 for children aged 5-12 for a 2-hour session , with standard figure skates included as part of the admission fee. Visitors can also opt for ice hockey skates for an additional $2, bringing the total to $ 22 for adults and $20 for children.
If you’re bringing your own skates, rink admission goes down to $15 for adults and $13 for children aged 5-12. Gloves and socks are also mandatory, so bring your own or purchase a pair, priced at $2.50 for both adult and children’s sizes.
Kallang Ice World offers 5 public skating sessions daily.
• 1st slot: 9am to 11am
• 2nd slot: 11.20am to 1.20pm
• 3rd slot: 2pm to4pm
• 4th slot: 4.40pm to 6.40pm
• 5th slot: 7.20pm to 9.20pm
An additional late-night session from 9.40pm to 11.40pm is available on Fridays , Saturdays , and the eves of public holidays .
If you’re simply going to watch people skate and not partake in the activity, there is a $3 spectator fee for entering the viewing area.
Can I rent ice skating aids for beginners or kids?
Image credit: @shiela_matias via Instagram
Kids have a little help with balance here, with free support trainers available for use. For adults wobbling their way through the rink, you can either hold on tight to bae’s hand and cling to the rink’s bar or opt to rent an ice skating seal aid for $20 .
Image credit: @keeriyan via Instagram
Do note that there’s a limited quantity of 10 support trainers and 5 ice skating seal aids available. Otherwise, you can always keep our ice skating tips in mind and put them into practice.
Can I take part in classes at Kallang Ice World?
Image credit: Tripadvisor
Keen to level up your skating skills? Kallang Ice World offers ice skating lessons for beginners and experienced skaters alike. Newbies can pick up the basics of balancing, stopping, and gliding, while more advanced skaters can work on figure skating and ice hockey techniques.
There are group and private lessons available, both beginner and freestyle classes, so you can learn alongside other skaters or receive personalised coaching from an instructor. The rink also occasionally hosts holiday skating camps for children and youths looking to sharpen their skills during the school holidays.
Classes are only conducted on Tuesdays or Fridays . Remember to dress up appropriately for these classes! It is mandatory to wear gloves and long pants , and they strongly advise you to wear long and thick socks.
Classes are priced from $55 for a private coaching session to $41/pax for a group coaching session . Private lessons have an occupancy of up to 3 students , whereas you can expect up to 10 people in a group class. Keep in mind that children below the age of 5 are not allowed to skate.
What do I need to wear for ice skating in Singapore?
There’s no need to shop for winter coats like these.
Temperatures will be frigid to keep the ice frozen for skaters, but you won’t have to wear thick winter coats. Stick to long-sleeved layers that you can easily put on and take off so you won’t be sweating once you’re out of the rink.
Image for illustration purposes only.
Image adapted from: Uniqlo
It’s best to wear tighter-fitting clothes like jeans and sweaters instead of dresses and baggy pants, especially if you’re a newbie to ice skating. This will prevent loose fabric from getting caught in your skates. If you have them, it’s a good idea to wear protective gear like knee pads and elbow guards as well.

The most underhyped decoration in Singapore is the Christmas wreath. There, we said it. Sure, you can get a Christmas tree in Singapore and call it a day. But a wreath is an understated piece of decor that ties your festive home together. The best part is the fuss-free setup. You can hang it anywhere in your house, and it’ll look amazing. If you’re looking to go the extra mile with your decorations this year, here’s where to find the ideal Christmas wreath in Singapore.
Why trust this guide
Everyone talks about the Christmas tree, the festive dinners, and the log cakes. But who do you turn to when you need help with the lesser-talked-about details like a Christmas wreath? Us! We’re all about that Christmas flair at Honeycombers, and we believe your door (or dining table) deserves some yuletide lovin’ too. From fresh to preserved, these are the Christmas wreaths in Singapore we’ve got our eye on.
Where to buy Christmas wreaths in Singapore
1. Friday’s Garden
Photography: Friday’s Garden
These aren’t your typical Christmas wreaths in Singapore, but that’s exactly what makes them so special! A little festive with a lot of personality, we’re loving the O, Rest Ye Merry Gumnuts wreath, made from copper banksia, dried lime, and eucalyptus. If you need your wreath with a splash of red for Christmas, go for the Christmas Must Have Red wreath complete with velvety red ribbons.

Because how can we ever resist getting all the beautiful things to bring the right vibe into a space? All the decor sold here focuses on elevating everyday spaces, and that sentiment runs into its Christmas collection. With both artificial and living wreaths available, we’re sure you’ll find one suitable for your home. And if you’re on a budget, we recommend going for the mini wreaths that are both beautiful and budget-friendly.

Photography: Flower Addict
Elegant and opulent, Flower Addict will have your back with its classy Christmas wreaths. Made for the modern home, its wreaths are versatile. That means you can choose to use it at your dining table as a table setting, or hang it on your door or wall as a decoration. It stays fresh for about two weeks, and you can admire yours for way longer once it’s fully dried out.
Price: Wreaths start from $219

6. Blossoms by Rei
Photography: Blossoms by Rei
Decision paralysis, begone, because Blossoms by Rei keeps it direct with a single Christmas wreath option. You don’t have to worry about picking the best one because all the wreaths are thoughtfully made with fresh leaves and flowers. If you don’t want a hanging wreath, you can get a gorgeous table arrangement done instead for your dining table!

Where to buy: Blossoms by Rei , available online

Photography: Stems by Joan
For those who want the smell of pine without figuring out the logistics of delivering a Christmas tree to their home, snag one of the fresh pine Christmas wreaths from Stems by Joan (previously Fleuriste). Crafted with lush pine firs, natural pinecones, cotton, and additional decorations like baubles, dried fruit, and ribbons, they’re incredibly eye-catching. We love that these also come complete with fairy lights!

3-day Johor Bahru food itinerary
If planning a Johor Bahru trip to hit all the must-try food spots feels daunting, we’ve got you covered. From hearty bagel breakfasts to indulgent zi char feasts, this three-day JB food itinerary is packed with delicious stops to help you make the most of your trip.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.31 as of 25 November 2026.
Day 1
Breakfast: Palates & Bagels By T.A.M
Since you’re probably starving by the time you’ve crossed the border, we reckon your breakfast spot should be somewhere near the customs. But it’s also got to be somewhat filling to make up for all that space in your stomach. And so we’ve landed on Palates & Bagels By T.A.M , a cafe that’s a short 10-minute drive from the JB checkpoint.
They offer three signature bagels: Original (RM6++) , Parmesan Cheese (RM8++) , and Flavoured (RM7++) , which come with toppings such as Cranberry , Mixed Black Sesame , and Pumpkin Seeds . We’re a fan of their savoury bagels, specifically the Ah Seng (RM31.90++) . This rendition is stuffed with a thick prawn patty, egg, caramelised onions, and sliced cheddar.
Read our Palates & Bagels By T.A.M coverage .
Address: 10 Jalan Dhoby, Bandar Johor Bahru, 80000 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 8am to 6pm
Website

The best thing about Space Cafe is the extensive menu. Don’t miss the Caramel Biscotti Coffee (RM19++) , served with house-made honeycomb candy for added sweetness and crunch. Lunch: Shuu Cafe
Next, enjoy your lunch at this whimsical cafe that feels right out of a fairytale. Shuu Cafe is a quaint Korean-inspired cafe with a cottagecore vibe, specialising in choux pastries, caneles, and other artisanal bakes. The cafe is set in a rustic brick-and-wood cottage structure, the kind you’d stumble across in Seoul or rural Europe. There’s even a private garden decked out with aesthetic white garden furniture and picturesque views, making every corner perfect for the ‘gram.
The food and drinks were just as good. The Rosti Benny (RM36++) is a pan-fried rosti topped with a poached egg, garden salad, and drizzled with hollandaise sauce. It was crisp and golden on the outside with a soft, fluffy interior, which paired nicely with the perfectly poached egg. The hollandaise sauce also elevated the dish with its richness. We also had to try their signature choux pastries, available in a plethora of flavours, such as Chocolate (RM15++), Madagascar Vanilla (RM17++) , and Calamansi Guava (RM15++) . We understood the hype: the pastry was light and airy while the cream was rich and indulgent. It’s one of the best choux pastries we’ve had in a while!

For those with a sweet tooth, drop by Cheevit Cheeva , a Thai-famous dessert cafe with several outlets worldwide at the time of writing. Over at their Mount Austin JB outlet, you’ll find their signature bingsu and hearty shokupan toasts.
Their Royal Thai Tea Bingsu (from RM24) is a must-get if you’re here with friends; we found the Thai tea flavour rich and addictive. If you’re not a fan of bingsu, get the croffle instead. There are five variations to choose from, including Salty Egg Yolk (RM30) and Choco Nutella (RM30) .

It’s only been 6 months since Casa Vostra brought its authentic Italian cuisine to the east of Singapore . And just earlier this month, it also landed at Singapore’s premier shopping district – Orchard Road .
More than just another outlet in town that patrons can visit, Casa Vostra at Wisma Atria also offers exclusive menu items worth making the trip down for. We recently got to try some of these dishes, so keep reading to see our favourites.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
2 new menu items that might interest you are SquareCrunch pizzas (S$15) and Housemade Mascarpone gelato in za’atar cones (from S$9) . The former is a Roman-style crunchy square pizza, while the latter is a new way of enjoying gelato, thanks to a collaboration between Casa Vostra and Petra .
But that’s not all you can find at this Casa Vostra outlet.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
For me, the new Anchovy 2.0 (S$22) and Carbonara 2.0 (S$24) pizzas are must-tries. I wish I could tell you specifically which one I preferred, but the truth is – I tried both and liked both! So I guess it comes down to mood and personal taste.
I enjoyed Anchovy 2.0’s savoury, briny profile, combined with its creamy texture and aroma. The Carbonara 2.0 was crisp and meaty with pancetta, and rich with egg yolk – a combination that makes for satisfying bites each time.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
Another personal highlight would have to be the Ossobuco (S$30) , a generous slab of veal shank served over potato purée. While dining, we learned this dish is usually found in high-end Italian restaurants, so the team at Casa Vostra wanted to create their own, more accessible take on the traditional favourite.
And it was delicious. Slow-cooked for 4–6 hours, the meat turned out really tender. It also paired very well with the mashed potato underneath and the finely chopped herbs, citrus zest, and garlic that it’s seasoned with. Every mouthful was a rich and hearty delight.
Photos by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
When it comes to Italian food, you can’t skip talking about pasta. And I think it’s worth mentioning the new Orecchiette Salsiccia e Broccoli ($22) . For something with “broccoli” in its name, I did not expect to like it the way I did.
If you want a simple, tasty pasta dish that has balanced flavours throughout, you will love this. The combination of sausage, roasted broccoli, parmesan cheese, prosciutto crumble, fried basil, and ear-shaped orecchiette pasta worked perfectly to create pleasant, comforting flavours.
I especially enjoyed the texture the prosciutto crumble added to each bite. If you love your greens, definitely try this one.
Photo by Soh Zhen Wei (Confirm Good)
For me, Casa Vostra’s charm extends beyond the plate. The warm, cosy space, thoughtfully arranged seating, and open kitchen that invites you to watch pizzas and pastas being made – all make for an inviting experience for any occasion and date .
Can’t wait to dine at Casa Vostra at Wisma Atrium already? The good news is that for the first time, diners will be able to make reservations – only at this outlet. A limited number of reservations will be available on SevenRooms , starting in December 2026 .
Buon appetito!

Credit: Earle Swensen’s

And since no Swensen’s meal is complete without its iconic Banana Split, the classic gets a festive makeover with the Bruleed Banana Split (S$14) , featuring a trio of premium ice cream flavours.
Planning to host a Christmas gathering at home? Let Earle Swensen’s take care of the festive spread with its selection of Christmas takeaway creations , available for pre-order via the Swensen’s eStore.
For larger gatherings, the Jumbo Herb Roast U.S. Turkey (S$228) makes an impressive centrepiece, with plenty to go around. Hosting a more intimate group? As the year winds down and the invitations for 2026 year-end celebrations start streaming in, the annual headache of finding the perfect restaurant makes its return. Especially for those hosting larger groups, you’ll need a restaurant that caters to everyone’s palate while having sufficient space to comfortably accommodate the whole crew. Leave the headache of planning behind. For your convivial gatherings this year, we found eight restaurants in Singapore that fit the bill. Psst: remember to bring along your Citi Card ‘cos there are sweet dining deals up for grabs!
Restaurants for huge year-end celebrations in 2026
1. Noa Lounge
Photography: Noa Lounge
Meet Noa Lounge, a cosy dining spot tucked away in Mondrian Singapore Duxton. From its classic Spanish tapas to the richly textured interiors and buzzy ambience, this restaurant perfectly captures the lively spirit of Spain. Settle in over tapas, grilled meats and seafood, and wine with your loved ones, and watch the hours fly by.
Go for the monthly rotating lunch and dinner set menus, or pick your fancy from the a la carte menu. Order a round of tapas for the whole table, featuring standouts like the Noa bomba with spiced beef and pork, and bikini sobrasada (a toasted melty sandwich that’s utterly irresistible). For the main stars of the feast, pick from delicacies like the half suckling pig served with pork jus and grilled pineapple, and the ‘Rubia Gallega’ striploin dry-aged for 40 days.
Perk alert: enjoy 15% off the a la carte food menu when you pay with a Citi Card. Valid from now till 30 June 2027; T&Cs apply.
Must-try items: Bikini sobrasada; Noa bomba; half suckling pig
Price: Starters from $4; mains from $36
Opening hours: Monday to Saturday, 12pm to 2.30pm & 6pm to 10.30pm
Address: #01-01, Mondrian Singapore Duxton, 83 Neil Road, Singapore 089813
2. Yellow Pot
Photography: Yellow Pot
Classic Chinese cuisine gets an upgrade at Yellow Pot. This modern Chinese restaurant in Duxton Reserve Singapore, Autograph Collection beckons with a menu that feels both familiar and unexpected. The dishes are rooted in culinary traditions, but refined by contemporary techniques and inspired by the seasons.
Curate your spread with a la carte highlights like the Cantonese roasted duck with glossy, crisp skin and tender meat, the bold and tingling crispy Sichuan chicken, and steamed threadfin fish fillet topped with five-year-aged preserved radish. Or, trust the chef and go for the three- or five-course set menus, featuring braised kurobuta pork rib and a trio platter.
Perk alert: enjoy 15% off the a la carte food menu when you pay with a Citi Card. Valid from now till 30 June 2027; T&Cs apply.
Must-try items: Cantonese roasted duck; crispy Sichuan chicken; steamed threadfin fish fillet
Price: A la carte food from $9; set menus from $28 per guest
Opening hours: Daily, 12pm to 2.30pm & 5.30pm to 10.30pm
Address: Duxton Reserve Singapore, Autograph Collection, 83 Duxton Road, Singapore 089540
3. CÉ LA VI
Photography: CÉ LA VI
Take your 2026 year-end celebrations to new heights (literally) at CÉ LA VI. Perched 57 floors above ground level, this chic rooftop destination is made for gathering the whole crew. On Saturdays, celebrations kick off from 11.30am with East Meets Extra, a lively brunch pairing modern Asian cuisine with progressive beats, interactive entertainment and panoramic city views.
Settle in for a three-course menu featuring signature dishes such as line-caught red snapper and A4 Miyazaki striploin, alongside free-flow champagne, wines, beers, cocktails and spirits. Staying for dinner? The à la carte menu spotlights sustainably sourced ingredients across bold, modern Asian plates.
Perk alert: enjoy free-flow champagne and beverages at CÉ LA VI’s East Meets Extra Saturday Brunch for $128++ per person (U.P. $148++) when you pay with a Citi Card. Valid from now till 31 December 2026, with a minimum booking of 4 guests; T&Cs apply.
Must-try items: Pan-seared Hokkaido scallops; line-caught red snapper; A4 Miyazaki striploin
Price: À la carte food from $12++; East Meets Extra Saturday Brunch from $88++ per guest
Opening hours: Daily, 5.30pm to 12am; Saturday, 11.30am to 3pm
Address: Level 57, Marina Bay Sands, Hotel Tower 3, 1 Bayfront Avenue, Singapore 018971
4. Super Thai by Soi Aroy
Photography: Super Thai by Soi Aroy
Missing the Land of Smiles? Skip the three-hour flight and book a table at Super Thai by Soi Aroy. Available at three locations islandwide, this authentic Thai restaurant serves fiery dishes with a modern twist and creative Thai-inspired cocktails and shots. If you can’t take the heat, the chefs can tailor the spice level to your liking.

Dessert lovers, here is a deal that rewards the greedy: TOFU G topping bar now lets you pile on as many toppings as fit in your cup for a flat S$2. Singapore’s first tofu-based gelato brand has rolled out its new unlimited Build-Your-Own Topping Bar across five outlets: Suntec City, Waterway Point, Great World, Raffles City and VivoCity.
Image: TOFU G
How the TOFU G topping bar works
Pick any signature live-churned tofu gelato cup for S$8 , add the Topping Bar for a flat S$2 (S$10 for a fully loaded cup), and load up with as many toppings as the cup will hold. There is no weighing or counting. Every cup starts with tofu made in-house from premium soybeans and churned live at the counter, giving a light, creamy texture and a clean finish.
Image: TOFU G
The toppings: from injeolmi to tempeh chips
Four outlets (Suntec City, Waterway Point, Great World and Raffles City) carry a twelve-topping selection:
• Nuts: almond slices, pecans, walnuts, pistachio kernels, roasted peanut
• Korean snacks: injeolmi, joripong, rice crispy puffs, yakgwa
• Dried fruit: cranberries
• Soy-based: tempeh chips
• Sweet: marshmallow sprinkles (contains gelatin)
VivoCity has a six-topping selection, including pistachio kernels, injeolmi, joripong, yakgwa, mini chocolate chips and coconut flakes. As the bar is a shared, open-service station, guests with allergies or dietary requirements should check with staff first.
Image: TOFU G
Gelato flavours worth trying
Core flavours at all topping bar outlets include Vegan Tofu, Vegan High-Protein Tofu (limited daily quantity), Vegan Black Sesame, Rich Chocolate and Pistachio. Outlet exclusives include Chodang Sweet Corn (Waterway Point and Raffles City), Sweet Potato (Raffles City), Nurungji Tofu (Suntec City) and Pomegranate (Great World and VivoCity). Beyond gelato, the menu has Korean-inspired desserts such as Butter Tteok, Tofu Pudding and Tofu Tiramisu. If you enjoy new dessert spots, see our recent Xiao Jiao Tian Wisma Atria feature and our Sagye Lite VivoCity deal.
Image: TOFU G
Raffles City opening special
To mark its newest openings, TOFU G is offering complimentary toppings with any gelato purchase at Raffles City from 21 to 29 November 2026 . Follow @tofug.sg on Instagram, post a Story featuring the outlet props while tagging @tofug.sg, then show it to staff to redeem.
Image: TOFU G
Where to find TOFU G in Singapore
Raffles City outlet: 252 North Bridge Road, B1, Raffles City Shopping Centre, Singapore 179103. Open daily, 11am to 10pm. The topping bar is also available at Suntec City, Waterway Point, Great World and VivoCity.
Image: TOFU G
Our take: at S$10 for a fully loaded cup, the flat-rate topping bar is an easy way to turn a simple scoop into a dessert you design yourself. Images: TOFU G.

2-Day Mount Austin food itinerary
Mount Austin is usually non-negotiable for me whenever I visit Johor Bahru ; it’s chock-full of trendy cafes and things to do. If you’re heading down soon but aren’t sure what to do, this two-day Mount Austin food itinerary is jam-packed with delicious eats, aesthetic cafes, and fun activities so you can make the most of your trip.
PSA: If you’re looking to explore Johor Bahru beyond Mount Austin, check out our JB food itinerary instead.
The current exchange rate is RM1 = ~S$0.31 as of 26 November 2026.
Day 1
Breakfast: XY 80s Kopitiam
After crossing the border, head to XY 80s Kopitiam and start your day with a hearty breakfast . It’s located in Austin Heights, a 34-minute drive from JB customs. The whole space is practically a time capsule, packed with nostalgic decor and old-school memorabilia that’ll throw you back to the ‘80s: think vintage Chinese kitchen cabinets, retro posters, vinyl records, and even an old-fashioned TV set!
The vibe extends to the furniture, with old-school kopitiam chairs and tables refurbished from sewing machines. You can also help yourself to free-flow snacks and sweets, available near the entrance of the cafe.
The Nasi Lemak Fried Chicken with Egg (RM16.90++) is a main worth ordering if you’re hungry after the hour-long journey across the causeway. The standout is definitely the ayam berempah, crispy and well-seasoned with aromatic spices, pairing beautifully with fluffy, fragrant lemak rice.
If you can’t stomach a full breakfast, order the Black Sesame Mochi Trimmed Toast (RM9.90++) instead. Each slice of toast came with a generous spread of black sesame paste, a thick slab of butter, and stretchy, QQ mochi tucked inside. We particularly enjoyed how rich, nutty, and gao the black sesame paste was, which complemented the buttery toast well.
Round off the meal with a cup of Hor Ka Sai (RM9.90++) : a blend of Milo and kopi. It’s almost like a localised version of mocha, with the kopi adding an extra potent oomph.
Address: 32 & 36, Jalan Austin Heights 7/3, Taman Mount Austin, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor Darul Ta’zim, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 7:30am to 8pm
Website
XY 80s Kopitiam is not halal-certified.
20 JB Breakfast Spots To Eat At The Next Time You Cross The Causeway Early
Coffee: Kirin Coffee
Image credit: grassy via Google Maps
After a filling breakfast, head to an IG-worthy cafe for a second round of caffeine. What better way to pump yourself up for a full day of activities than to visit Kirin Coffee , a two-storey cafe branding itself as a “dopamine concept”? It’s slightly out of the way, so you’ll have to make a short detour, but you won’t want to miss this spot.
Image credit: Kirin Coffee via Google Maps
In here, the zaniness is amped up to the max. The space boasts a maximalist aesthetic that reminds me of Wiggle Wiggle in Korea, with a blood-red colour palette and wacky decor. Think Superman flying straight into a wall and Ted the bear donning a bikini. There are tons of photo spots as well, if you’re looking to add a pop of colour to your feed.
Image credit: Andrew Wtr via Google Maps
Their most popular item is the Coffee + Brush = Crush (RM20.90) : guava-flavoured coffee made with their signature coffee blend, served with a dollop of peppermint cream on a toothbrush—don’t brush your teeth with it, though! The Red Bean Cold Brew (RM21.90) is worth a try too, comprising a layer of coffee foam sitting on red bean-flavoured milk, served with a skewer of their house-made mini croissant.
Image credit: Chui Hui Lu via Google Maps
In the off chance that you get bored, there are also board and card games that you and your friends can play, including UNO and Monopoly.
Read our Kirin Coffee feature .
Address: G-03, Austin 18, Jalan Austin Perdana 3, Taman Austin Perdana, 81100 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 11pm
Website
Kirin Coffee is not halal-certified.
This JB Cafe Delivers Dopamine With Its Bizarre Decor And “Toothbrush” Coffee
Lunch: Principle Cafe
Image credit: Principle Cafe via Google Maps
You can’t go to Mount Austin without enjoying a cafe brunch , and Principle Cafe is a good spot for it. They have three outlets around Johor Bahru, with the Mount Austin outlet boasting a 4.7-star rating from over 2K Google reviews—pretty impressive given JB’s competitive cafe scene.
Image credit: Jessie Tan via Google Maps
If you’re a bread lover, you’re in luck: Principle Cafe is known for their focaccia, said to be soft and slightly chewy with a crispy crust. The Salmon Royale Focaccia Bar (RM22.90++) is a great way to enjoy it, topped with sour cream, smoked salmon, capers, and dill. Then there’s the Chicken Sliced & Cheese Focaccia Sandwich (RM24.90) , which takes the same focaccia and loads it with chicken ham, arugula, melted cheese, and sun-dried tomatoes.
Image credit: Chen Ying Chao Cherry via Google Maps
…
summary: This two-day Mount Austin food itinerary is jam-packed with delicious eats, aesthetic cafes, and fun activities to help you make the most of your trip.
title: 2-Day Mount Austin Itinerary: TikTok-Viral Bakery, Dachshund Cafe And More

Tanjong Pagar food guide
Tanjong Pagar is definitely an area where you’ll be spoilt for choice when it comes to food. Think CBD locale houses cafes and restaurants, spanning Asian cuisines to desserts. Here’s a list of the best Tanjong Pagar food places to visit if you’re around the area.
If you’ve been feeling the pinch, we’ve also got a guide to the best affordable lunch sets in the CBD from $18++ per person.
Best Tanjong Pagar food spots, in a nutshell:
• Best cafe in Tanjong Pagar : Fortuna Terrazza – Italian brunch cafe by popular pizzeria
• Best affordable restaurant in Tanjong Pagar : Hamburg Steak Keisuke – Hamburg steaks with free-flow salad bar
• Affordable dinner spot in Tanjong Pagar : Papi’s Tacos – Legit Mexican food by a native chef
• For supper cravings in the CBD : Hansik Dining Collective – 24/7 Korean restaurant with six concepts
Occasion restaurants
1 . Bottega Di Carna
Image credit: Mondrian Hotels
What is Bottega Di Carna? If you have a special occasion coming up, Bottega Di Carna might be the perfect spot to celebrate. Helmed by Chef Kenny Huang in collaboration with Tuscan butcher Dario Cecchini, the Italian restaurant specialises in steaks and wood-fired mains.
Image credit: Esther via Google Maps
Some signatures include the Stockyard Rib-Eye ($98++) and Westholme Wagyu Hanging Tender ($68++) . If you don’t want to break the bank, you can go for the pastas, such as the Linguine ($38++) and Oxtail Agnolotti ($38++) , which has black truffle and bone marrow. Popular sharing plates also worth considering are the Signature Steak Tartare ($32++) and Puglia Burrata ($28++).
Expect to pay: $ 50-100++ per person
What to order: Stockyard Rib-Eye ($98++), Oxtail Agnolotti ($38++), Signature Steak Tartare ($32++)
Address: 16A Duxton Hill, #03-01, Singapore 089970
Opening hours: Daily 7am to 11pm
Bottega Di Carne Website
Bottega Di Carne is not halal-certified.
2 . Chef Lam’s Sichuan Cuisine – Award-winning Sichuan restauran t
What is Chef Lam ’s Sichuan Cuisine? Another award-winning restaurant in Tanjong Pagar is Chef Lam ’s Sichuan Cuisine . The Chengdu-born brand has built a strong reputation for its legit Sichuan fare, drawing long queues back home and earning a loyal fanbase for its bold, flavour-packed creations . FYI, this outlet at Guoco Tower marks the brand’s first overseas venture !
One of the restaurant’s most popular dishes is the Gold Medal Kung Pao Chicken ($15.80++) , which we loved for its distinct smoky aroma and underlying sweetness. For those visiting in a group, Dongpo’s Golden Soup with Pickled Fish ($29.90++) is an ideal sharing dish served in a huge pot. You get melt-in-your-mouth fish slices submerged in a tangy-spicy broth with a strong suan cai flavour. Otherwise, go for the Chengdu Cold Noodles with Shredded Chicken ($9.90++) , which comes slathered in a numbing sauce with garlic, vinegar, cucumber, shredded chicken, and their house-made chilli oil.
Read our Chef Lam’s Sichuan Cuisine review .
Expect to pay: $20-$40++ per person
What to order: Gold Medal Kung Pao Chicken ($15.80++), Dongpo’s Golden Soup with Pickled Fish ($29.90++), Chengdu Cold Noodles with Shredded Chicken ($9.90++)
Address: 5 Wallich Street, #01-13, Guoco Tower, Singapore 078883
Opening hours: Daily 11am to 10pm
Chef Lam’s Sichuan Cuisine Website
Chef Lam’s Sichuan Cuisine is not halal-certifie d .
3. Bae Sik Dang – Late Night K-BBQ Spot
Image credit: @baesikdang1969
What is Bae Sik Dang? Tanjong Pagar is known for its wide variety of K-BBQ restaurants, including Bae Sik Dang , a new spot serving Jeju pork in a casual, K-drama-inspired setting. Better yet, it opens till 5am, which is perfect for any late-night supper plans.
Image credit: Irene H Lim via Google Maps
Their specialty item is the Flash-frozen Pork Belly ($32++ for 150g) , which is said to crisp up on the grill and goes well in ssam—Korean lettuce wraps for grilled meat. There’s also a wide variety of Korean side dishes to accompany your meal, such as their rolled omelette and fresh kimchi. To round off your meal in true Korean fashion, order their Fried Rice ($12++) , cooked in the residual pork belly fat for extra richness.
Read our Bae Sik Dang feature .
Expect to pay : $30-$45 per person
What to order: Flash-frozen Pork Belly ($32++), Fried Rice ($12++), Soybean Paste Stew ($22+)
Address: 48 Tanjong Pagar Road, Singapore 088469
Opening hours: Daily 5pm to 5am
Tel: 8127 6902
Bae Sik Dang Website
Bae Sik Dang is not halal-certified.
4 . Hamburg Steak Keisuke – Hamburg steaks with free-flow salad bar
What is Hamburg Steak Keisuke? Hamburg Steak Keisuke is one of the many Chef Keisuke’s restaurants in Singapore that sell tasty Japanese fare around the Tanjong Pagar locale. Here, you’ll find a delicious menu of beef hamburg steaks, all flambed right in front of you. Better yet, each set ordered comes with complimentary access to their free-flow salad bar and egg buffet!
…
summary: Discover plenty of Tanjong Pagar food options, including affordable traditional Chinese desserts, Korean knife-cut noodles and more.
title: Tanjong Pagar Food Guide: 20 Places For Korean Knife-Cut Noodles, KL Nasi Lemak And More

Beauty in The Pot’s new buffet at The Star has a headline price of S$23.90++ a person, and that figure belongs to one window only: weekend and public holiday afternoons from 2.31pm to 4.30pm.
Buffet prices at The Star by day and time, before service charge and GST. Image: Paradise Group
Paradise Group has opened Beauty in The Pot Buffet at #02-24 The Star, with a grand-opening offer that started on 25 November. The group bills it as Singaporeans’ favourite hotpot going buffet style: eight broths brewed fresh daily, more than 100 ingredients, unlimited international hot dishes and dim sum, and what it calls its largest dessert and pastry spread, with a live dessert station.
Three tiers, priced by day and hour
Every set runs 90 minutes from seating, with last orders 20 minutes before the end. All prices below are before service charge and prevailing GST, which are added to the bill.
Monday to Friday:
• Lunch, 11.30am to 2.30pm: Standard S$28.90, Deluxe Beef and Seafood S$39.90, Luxury Wagyu and Seafood S$56.90
• Hi-tea, 2.31pm to 4.30pm: S$15.90 for cooked food, desserts and drinks only, no hotpot, 60 minutes
• Dinner, 4.31pm to 10pm: Standard S$38.90, Deluxe S$48.90, Luxury S$69.90
Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays:
• Lunch, 11am to 2.30pm: S$32.90, S$43.90, S$59.90
• Happy hour, 2.31pm to 4.30pm: S$23.90, S$32.90, S$45.90
• Dinner, 4.31pm to 10pm: S$42.90, S$52.90, S$72.90
Last seating for dinner is 8.30pm on any day. Children aged 5 to 12 pay half on the hotpot sets, under-5s eat free, and students get S$3.90 off on weekdays before 2.30pm, except public holidays, on showing a valid student pass. Everyone at the table has to pick the same set.
The chocolate fountain and fruit at the dessert counter. Image: Paradise Group
What the extra money buys
The tiers differ only in the set-exclusive meats and seafood. Standard covers sliced pork belly, chicken, chicken thigh, pork collar and three pastes, including century egg fish paste. Deluxe adds US Angus chuck roll, Australian sirloin, US short plate, lamb, Kurobuta and Duroc pork, scallops, sea prawns, snakehead fish, prawn dumplings and drunken chicken. Luxury brings Japanese wagyu chuck eye roll, US wagyu karubi, Angus prime short rib, half-shell abalone, salmon, Iberico and Japanese pork.
All sets choose from four classic soups: tomato with sweet corn, pork bone, spicy, and cordyceps flower with mushroom. The four signature soups, including the Beauty Collagen base the chain built its name on, cost extra: S$15 for a single pot, S$10 each in a twin pot, S$5 each in a four-way pot. Food wastage is charged at S$10 per 100g.
Part of the dessert and pastry counter. Image: Paradise Group
Waffles made to order at the live dessert station. Image: Paradise Group
The opening upgrade
From 25 November to 1 December, Citi and OCBC credit or debit cardmembers and Paradise Gourmet Rewards members get a free one-tier upgrade on their buffet set. Snap the buffet line or the live dessert station, post it on a public TikTok, Instagram or RedNote account and show the post to staff. Each post, on a different account, upgrades one diner, and the upgrade has to be confirmed before dining starts. The offer cannot be combined with other discounts, promotions, vouchers or membership privileges.
Details
Beauty in The Pot Buffet, #02-24 The Star, 1 Vista Exchange Green. Tel: 6262 1692. Open daily from 11.30am on weekdays and 11am on weekends and public holidays, to 10pm. Buona Vista MRT is the nearest station.
summary: Beauty in The Pot Buffet is open at The Star with three 90-minute hotpot tiers. The S$23.90++ headline price applies only from 2.31pm to 4.30pm on weekends and public holidays; weekday lunch starts at S$28.90++ and weekend dinner at S$42.90++.
title: Beauty in The Pot Buffet opens at The Star, and its S$23.90 rate is for weekend and public holiday afternoons only

body:
Singapore is a melting pot of many different cultures and backgrounds, and nothing celebrates that unity more than fusion cuisine. In this case, Hainanese- Western fusion. British Hainan exists for this sole purpose: to celebrate both cultures under one roof.
They recently made a move to Tiong Bahru , introducing a new kopitiam-style setting. They soft-launched on 17 Nov 2026 , focusing on creating a casual, coffee-shop setting.
Credit – British Hainan
Those familiar with their former location at Kallang Way will know that the previous location focused on a vintage style, with all sorts of collectables decorating the interior. Their new location will lean more into the old-school kopitiam concept.
Credit – British Hainan
The new outlet has a very rustic interior with its wooden stools, simple wooden tables and chequered floor design. A lot of the metallic elements of their decor give the space an industrial feel that many customers might find familiar.
Credit – Google
What remains mostly unchanged is their menu. Their Oxtail Stew (S $32.90) and Hainanese Pork Chop (S$16.90) are still the crowd favourites and continue to satisfy new customers as well. Why fix what isn’t broken, right?
That being said, with their new opening, they may decide to add or discontinue certain dishes. For more information, keep an eye on their Instagram .
Credit – British Hainan
Another detail I personally thought was cool is their outdoor seating. They decorated the area with wooden barrels and local plants, as well as a view of the bustling street just in front of you. I can’t put my finger on it, but this scene definitely reminds me of a kampung where you’d eat on the side of the street.
Hock Gooi Hainanese Curry Rice: Loaded curry rice from $4 with crispy pork chop, braised pork & pork trotters
summary: British Hainan has moved to Tiong Bahru and opened in a rustic, kopitiam-style space after a soft launch on 17 Nov 2026. The Hainanese-Western menu stays largely the same, with the Oxtail Stew at S$32.90 and Hainanese Pork Chop at S$16.90 still the crowd favourites. It suits diners who knew the previous Kallang Way outlet or want old-school coffeeshop surroundings.
title: British Hainan – Hainanese-Western classics gets a new home in Tiong Bahru

The space of Si Yan spots a dark interior with a main dining hall and a couple of private rooms. The Food Rooted in traditional Teochew cooking, the restaurant places emphasis on carefully selected ingredients and time-honored preparation techniques. Key highlights from their menu include 15-year vintage preserved turnip and a Teochew marinated seafood series spanning lobster, crab, cockles and prawns, prepared using a traditional 38-year-old recipe. Beyond its signature seafood, the menu offers a wide selection of Teochew favourites, including braised dishes, lunchtime dim sum from S$8.80, noodles, rice dishes and traditional desserts. I started with one of their signatures – Teochew Marinated Red Cream Mud Crab (S$14 per 100g). The Teochew Marinated Red Cream Mud Crab is marinated in a house-made sauce for more than eight hours, and I must say it is delicious. body:
SingPost digital stamps
If you aren’t in the know, SingPost has been spending much of 2026 reinventing its services and operations. From opening a new Automated Parcel Sortation Facility to putting a posting box on Sentosa Island , the postal provider has been finding new ways to make traditional mailing more fun and convenient.
Keeping up with its efforts to modernise traditional mailing, SingPost has introduced digital stamps , which means no more stocking up on physical stamps just for the occasional letter day. Here’s how you can get your hands on digital stamps and send mail with just a few easy steps.
What are SingPost digital stamps?
View this post on Instagram
In celebration of World Post Day 2026 and following the successful rollout of SingPost@MyBlock , SingPost commenced the public trial of Asia’s 1st digital stamps on 8th August 2026 .
Gone are the days of making post office runs just for stamps; you can now pay for postage digitally from the comfort of your home, whenever you need it. But philatelists need not worry; physical stamps aren’t going anywhere. Digital stamps simply give you another option when it comes to traditional mailing.
The trial runs till 6th April 2027 , during which SingPost will gather feedback through surveys on its mobile app. This will help it improve the user experience and its automated systems.
What can I use my digital stamps on?
Image credit: SingPost
During the 6-month trial phase, digital stamps will cover letters , postcards , and printed paper items in paper envelopes . If you’re unsure whether your mail qualifies for digital stamps, refer to the mailing requirements on the SingPost website .
This service is only available domestically , and though there isn’t any end-to-end tracking on your digitally stamped mail, basic mail is expected to be delivered in 1 to 2 days .
How do I use digital stamps?
Step 1: Purchase digital stamps through the SingPost app
Screenshot: SingPost
Firstly, log in to the SingPost mobile app ( App Store | Google Play ) . If you don’t have an account, it takes less than 5 minutes to set one up.
Screenshot: SingPost
Next, navigate to the digital stamp section. Here, it’ll show you an overview of the active and used stamps in your collection. Currently, there are 2 types of stamps available for purchase: Standard Regular Mail and Standard Large Mail .
Once you’ve made your purchase, tap into your digital stamps to see the unique codes assigned to each of them.
Step 2: Write the unique code on the envelope
Image credit: SingPost
To make use of your digital stamps, simply write the code on the top-right corner of the envelope , where a stamp would otherwise go. Yes, it’s as easy as it sounds. Remember to mark on the app when a code has been used.
SingPost recommends you use a black or dark blue pen . This is to ensure that their optical character recognition (OCR) scanners can discern your handwritten codes as accurately as possible, to avoid any delivery mix-ups.
Step 3: Send your mail out for delivery
Image credit: SingPost
Once the code is written on the envelope, you’re all set. Head down to your nearest posting box or post office and drop your letters off, just like you normally would. You’ll receive a notification through the app once your mail has been processed.
View this post on Instagram
You can also mail letters out through the “Return Mail” slot at residential letterboxes introduced with the SingPost@MyBlock scheme. Just make sure that they fit through the slot before sending them on their way.
How much do digital stamps cost?
Screenshot: SingPost
Good news on the price front: SingPost’s digital stamps cost the exact same as their physical counterparts, with no additional fees. A Standard Regular Mail stamp costs $0.62 , while a Standard Large Mail stamp goes for $0.90 each.
However, you must purchase digital stamps in denominations of 5 , with a maximum of 50. This means at minimum, you’ll have to pay $3.10 for a set of 5 Standard Regular Mail stamps, and $4.50 for a set of 5 Standard Large Mail stamps. Digital stamps will also expire 24 months after the date of purchase .
During the trial period, each account can also purchase 1 set of each stamp type at a discounted price. This brings the price down to just $1 for a set of Standard Regular Mail stamps and $1.50 for a set of Standard Large Mail stamps. Do note that stamps purchased at these discounted prices will only be valid until 6th April 2027 .
What stamp designs are there?
61st National Day stamps set.
Image credit: Shop@SingPost
SingPost’s digital stamps launched with 2 designs , 1 for each stamp type. Standard Regular Mail stamps feature a 61st National Day-inspired design , while Standard Large Mail stamps sport the World Post Day otters .
There’s also a 3rd design featuring the Fullerton Building , Singapore’s first General Post Office. You can unlock this special design with every 15th stamp purchase .
…
summary: No need for post office runs when you can buy digital stamps on the SingPost app.
title: You Can Now Buy Postage Digitally & Send Letters Without Physical Stamps In Singapore – Here’s How
